JOINING DISSIMILAR MATERIALS IS A COMMON PRACTICAL PROBLEM IN THE AUTOMOTIVE, AEROSPACE AND MEDICAL DEVICE INDUSTRIES [1, 2]. THE MOST POPULAR AND MOST RECENTLY DISCUSSED MATERIALS FOR AEROSPACE AND AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRIES ARE LIGHTWEIGHT STRUCTURAL METALS: ALUMINUM (AL), TITANIUM (TI) ALLOYS AND FIBER-REINFORCED COMPOSITES [3]. COMPLEXITY OF FINE-TUNING AND MAXIMIZING PERFORMANCE OF MULTI-MATERIAL PARTS AS WELL AS NECESSITY OF THEIR COST REDUCTION DRIVE GREAT INTEREST TO INTEGRATED APPROACHES WHERE JOINING OF DISSIMILAR MATERIALS PLAYS SIGNIFICANT ROLE [1, 4-6].
MAGNESIUM (MG) IS THE LIGHTEST OF THE PRACTICAL, ENVIRONMENTALLY FRIENDLY METALS WITH HIGH SPECIFIC STRENGTH AND GREAT BIOCOMPATIBILITY. THERE IS TREMENDOUS INTEREST TO ADAPTATION OF MG-BASED ALLOYS TO AUTOMOTIVE, AEROSPACE, ENERGY, MEDICAL, CONSUMER AND MILITARY APPLICATIONS. MG-AL ALLOYS HAVE A GREAT POTENTIAL TO BE MATERIAL FOR THE AIRCRAFT'S WING SKIN, ENGINE, BATTERY HOUSING OR FRAMES. THE USE OF TI ALLOYS IS ALSO INCREASING DUE TO THEIR UNIQUE COMBINATION OF LIGHTNESS, HIGH STRENGTH, CORROSION RESISTANCE AND BIOCOMPATIBILITY. HIGH STRENGTH LIGHTWEIGHT TI ALLOYS ARE WIDELY USED IN THE AEROSPACE INDUSTRY AS STRUCTURAL FRAME MATERIALS. THEREFORE, JOINING MG AND TI RECENTLY BECAME THE HOT AREA OF RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT [6, 7]. HOWEVER, SATISFACTORY MG/TI JOINING WAS REPORTED ONLY FOR COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE FRICTION STIR WELDING AND DIFFUSION BONDING TECHNIQUES [8-13]. SINCE THESE METHODS OPERATE AT ABOVE CRYSTALLIZATION TEMPERATURE, THE MAIN PROCESSES OF IMPROVEMENT OF BONDING ARE CONNECTED WITH FORMATION OF INTERMETALLICS THAT SIMILAR TO FUSION PROCESSES. THERE ARE NO KNOWN PUBLICATIONS ON JOINING MG/TI BY IMPACT WELDING TECHNIQUES. IMPACT WELDING IS A COMPARATIVELY NEW APPROACH THAT HAS DEMONSTRATED MUCH POTENTIAL IN THE AGILE WELDING OF HIGH STRENGTH MATERIALS [14, 15].
BASED ON OUR REVIEW OF CURRENT STATUS OF DISSIMILAR JOINING OF MG AND TI ALLOYS, WE SUGGEST THE EXPLORATORY STUDY OF JOINING USING RELATIVELY NEW AND NOT COMMERCIAL VAPORIZING FOIL ACTUATOR WELDING (VFAW) IMPACT TECHNOLOGY ESTABLISHED AT OSU [16]. SINCE THICKNESS OF BONDING INTERFACE PRODUCED BY VFAW CAN BE JUST FEW NANOMETERS AND PROCESS GO THROUGH HIGH VELOCITY SURFACE CLEANING DUE TO JET PHENOMENA [17], THE ROLE OF INTRINSIC PROPERTIES OF MATERIALS IN BONDING STRENGTH IS INCREASED. SO, ALLOYING OF MG AND TI IS EXPECTED TO BE A MAJOR FACTOR OF IMPROVEMENT OF MG/TI JOINTS. THE ABILITY OF VFAW TECHNIQUE TO JOIN DISSIMILAR MATERIALS THROUGH FORMING HIGH STRENGTH BONDING AT ROOM TEMPERATURE IN MILLISECONDS WILL NOT ONLY LEAD TO NEW APPLICATIONS BUT MAY ALSO GIVE INSIGHT TO IMPORTANT SCIENTIFIC QUESTIONS REGARDING IMPACT WELDING SUCH AS
- WHAT IS ULTIMATE STRENGTH OF DISSIMILAR METALS BONDING? -	HOW MORPHOLOGY AND WIDTH OF INTERFACE FORMED BY BONDING WITH HIGH VELOCITY IMPACT CAN BE AFFECTED BY SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCE IN STRENGTH AND PLASTICITY OF DISSIMILAR MATERIALS?
-	HOW CRYSTALLOGRAPHIC ORIENTATION OF GRAINS AND GRAIN SIZE EFFECTS THE BONDING STRENGTH?
-	DOES PLASTIC DEFORMATION PLAY SIGNIFICANT ROLE IN VFAW PROCESS? CAN TWINNING OCCUR DURING IMPACT WELDING?
-	CAN WE EXPECT FORMATION OF NEW INTERMETALLIC COMPOUNDS AND THEIR PRECIPITATION DURING IMPACT WELDING?
-	CAN SURFACE MODIFICATION (COATING, IMPLANTATION, PLASMA TREATMENT, ETC.) BE A SIGNIFICANT FACTOR IN VFAW PROCESS?
-	HOW MUCH SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCE IN MECHANICAL PROPERTIES AND METALLURGICAL DISSIMILARITY PROMOTE CRACKING, SPALLATION AND OTHER DEFECTS IN VFAW PROCESS?
WE BELIEVE THAT EXPLORATORY STUDY OF JOINING MG AND TI ALLOYS WITH VFAW PROCESS WILL HELP TO GAIN DEEPER UNDERSTANDING THE JOINING OF DISSIMILAR METALS.

AGING AND OTHER DEGRADATION EVENTS AFFECT THE FUNCTIONS OF MPS IN RPE AND CAN LEAD TO DISEASES SUCH AS AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION (AMD). 5 MPS ARE HIGHLY HETEROGENOUS SUPRAMOLECULAR ASSEMBLIES THAT INCLUDE VARIOUS OLIGOMERIZED FORMS OF 5,6-DIHYDROXYINDOLE-2-CARBOXYLIC ACID (DHICA) AND 5,6-DIHYDROXYINDOLE (DHI) AS WELL AS PROTEINS. 6-8 OUR HYPOTHESIS IS THAT UNDERSTANDING THE PROTECTIVE FUNCTIONS OF MPS AS WELL AS THEIR DEGRADATION DEPENDS ON OUR ABILITY TO I) IDENTIFY THE PHOTOCHEMICAL, MORPHOLOGIC AND STRUCTURAL ROLE OF INDIVIDUAL MOLECULAR COMPONENTS THAT FORM THE INTACT MPS, II) CHARACTERIZE HOW THESE COMPONENTS CHANGE AS A RESULT OF DEGRADATION AND III) CHARACTERIZE THE EFFECTS OF OTHER DEGRADATION PRODUCTS SUCH AS LIPOFUSCIN ON THE COMPONENTS AND PROPERTIES OF MPS.
THE SCIENTIFIC SCOPE OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT INCLUDES
1)	TO IDENTIFY AND LINK MOLECULAR MARKERS WITHIN MPS (FROM RPE CELLS) TO SPECIFIC FUNCTIONS (I.E., STRUCTURAL, PHOTOCHEMICAL, ETC.),
2)	TO CHARACTERIZE HOW THESE MARKERS ARE AFFECTED BY AGING AND OTHER STRESSORS SUCH AS LASER DAMAGE,
3)	TO CHARACTERIZE THE DARK AND PHOTOINDUCED MECHANISMS THAT LEAD LIPOFUSCIN PRODUCTS TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEGRADATION OF MPS.
4)	TO CHARACTERIZE SYNTHETIC MELANINS (SMS) AS MODELS FOR THE MOLECULAR COMPOSITION OF MPS.
IN ADDITION A MAJOR SCOPE OF THE PROJECT IS TO PROVIDE RESEARCH TRAINING TO TWO GRADUATE (GR) AND TWO UNDERGRADUATE (UG) STUDENTS WHO WILL PERFORM SUMMER RESEARCH AT AFRL AS PART OF THE ML-RCP SUMMER INTERNSHIP PROGRAM.
OUR PROPOSED INVESTIGATION WILL LEAD TO IMPROVE CURRENT MODELS OF PHOTOCHEMICAL AND PHOTOTHERMAL LASER DAMAGE IN THE EYE AND IN THE SKIN WHICH IS A MAJOR TOPIC OF INTEREST WITHIN THE AFRL BIOEFFECT DIVISION (71 LHPW/RHD). THE PROJECT INCLUDES A MENTOR AT 71LHPW/RHD (DR. DENTON) WHO HAS BEEN STUDYING LASER-INDUCED DAMAGE IN RPE CELLS.
THE ABILITY TO CORRELATE INDIVIDUAL MOLECULAR COMPONENTS OF MPS AND SMS TO THE PARTICLES' PROPERTIES WILL ALSO CONTRIBUTE TO DEVELOP SM-BASED NANOMATERIALS THAT COULD BE DEPLOYED FOR BIOMEDICAL APPLICATION, SUCH AS THE RESTORATION OF FUNCTIONALITY TO RPE, OR BE APPLIED AS THERAPEUTIC OR DIAGNOSTIC TOOLS IN OTHER DISEASES.

PROJECT SUMMARY: THE CONCEPT OF ELECTRONIC TOPOLOGY AND THE ASSOCIATED TOPOLOGICALLY PROTECTED QUANTUM STATES AND DIFFERENT PROPERTIES IN TOPOLOGICAL INSULATORS (TIS) HAVE DRAWN ENORMOUS RESEARCH INTEREST. AMONG DIFFERENT TYPES OF EXOTICS QUANTUM STATES, THE DISCOVERY OF THE BERRY PHASE EFFECTS, AND NONLINEAR OPTICAL RESPONSES, SUCH AS SHIFT CURRENT, SECOND HARMONIC GENERATION (SHG), AND PHOTOVOLTAIC HALL EFFECT, BRINGS AN EXCELLENT OPPORTUNITY FOR DEVELOPING NEXT-GENERATION OPTOÃ‚Â­ ELECTRONIC DEVICES. RECENT THEORETICAL AND EXPERIMENTAL WORKS DEMONSTRATED THAT THE TIS DISPLAY A LARGE CIRCULAR PHOTOGALVANIC EFFECT (CPGE) AND STRONG SHG EFFECT. HOWEVER, ONE BIGGEST CHALLENGE HAVE BEEN UNDERSTANDING AND CONTROLLING THE UNIQUE OPTICAL PROPERTIES DRIVEN BY THE EXOTIC TOPOLOGICAL STATES. IT IS NECESSARY TO UNDERSTAND HOW SPIN-POLARIZED CURRENTS CAN BE MODULATED OR CONTROLLED IN TIS.

THE REQUIREMENTS TO OVERCOME CHALLENGES ARE THE FOLLOWING: (A) THE TOPOLOGICAL STRUCTURES SHOULD HAVE THEIR DIRAC/WEYL POINTS AND/OR ASSOCIATED FIELD-INDUCED MASS GAPS AT EF, OR BE READILY TUNABLE SO THAT THEY CAN BE PLACED AT EF VIA ELECTRIC FIELD GATING OR OTHER MEANS. (B) THE TOPOLOGICAL STRUCTURES AT FA SHALL NOT BE CONTAMINATED BY NON-TOPOLOGICAL (TRIVIAL) BANDS CROSS FA. HERE, WE PROPOSE FIRST-PRINCIPLES CALCULATIONS OF LIGHT-MATTER INTERACTIONS TO TUNE TOPOLOGICAL STATES AND ELECTRONIC TRANSPORT IN TOPOLOGICAL MATERIALS. MORE SPECIFICALLY, A MULTIPRONGED COMBINATION OF DENSITY FUNCTIONAL THEORY (DFT) PLUS TIGHT BINDING-BASED COMPUTATIONAL MODELING, BULK AND THINÃ‚Â­ FILM MATERIALS SYNTHESIS TECHNIQUES, AND DETAILED CHARACTERIZATION METHODS, INCLUDING ANGLEÃ‚Â­ RESOLVED PHOTOEMISSION SPECTROSCOPY (ARPES), SPIN-ARPES, X-RAY AND NEUTRON SCATTERING, MAGNETIZATION, AND TRANSPORT TO CREATE A CLOSED FEEDBACK LOOP BETWEEN THEORY, SYNTHESIS, CHARACTERIZATION, AND SPECTROSCOPY, ENABLING ITERATION AND IMPROVEMENT OF PREDICTIONS AND MATERIALS. RESISTIVE SWITCHING (RS) MATERIALS HAVE BEEN UNDER INTENSE STUDY IN THE PAST DECADE AFTER THE FIRST WORKING MODEL WAS CREATED BY THE HEWLETT PACKARD LABORATORY. THEY HAVE ATTRACTED INCREASINGLY LARGE ATTENTION DUE TO THEIR POTENTIAL APPLICATIONS IN NEXT-GENERATION ELECTRONICS INCLUDING FASTER READ/WRITE TIME, NON-VOLATILITY, AND SMALLER SIZES. MUCH OF THE RECENT RESEARCH HAS FOCUSED ON THE UNDERLYING PHYSICAL MECHANISMS THAT CAUSE THE REVERSIBLE CHANGES IN THE RESISTIVE STATE OF THE VARIOUS MATERIALS. PHYSICAL EXPERIMENTS HAVE BEEN CONDUCTED TO MEASURE THE EFFECTS OF DIFFERENT PARAMETERS, SUCH AS GEOMETRICAL VARIATIONS, MANUFACTURING PROCESSES, AND MATERIAL PARAMETERS. WHILE EXPERIMENTS PROVIDE NECESSARY DATA, THERE ARE CURRENTLY FEW COMPUTATIONAL MODELS THAT CAPTURE THE BEHAVIORS OF INTEREST IN RESISTIVE SWITCHING MATERIALS. EVEN FEWER COMPREHENSIVELY INCORPORATE THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS THAT DRIVE RESISTIVE SWITCHING. THE PROPOSED MODEL FOCUSES ON THE CONDUCTIVE FILAMENTS IN RS MATERIALS AND THEIR GENERATION/RUPTURE DUE TO ELECTRICAL BIASES, JOULE HEATING (SORET FORCES), AND FICK FORCES. AN ITERATIVE FINITE ELEMENT APPROACH WILL BE TAKEN TO MODEL THE MOVEMENT OF OXYGEN VACANCIES WITHIN THE MATERIAL AND THE OVERALL RESISTANCE IN THE ON/OFF STAGE WILL BE CALCULATED. FINALLY, THE HYSTERESIS LOOP WILL BE MODELED USING A BOUC-WEN MODEL AND A LIFE-CYCLE ANALYSIS WILL BE PERFORMED BASED ON EXPERIMENTAL DATA.

THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP COMPUTATIONALLY EFFICIENT MACHINE LEARNING (ML) SURROGATE MODELS USING
NEURAL NETWORKS FOR MULTI-PHYSICS ENGINEERING APPLICATIONS TO BE APPLIED TO LASER BIOEFFECTS PREDICTION THROUGH THREE
OBJECTIVES: 1) TEST PERTURBED DEEP OPERATOR AND PHYSICS INFORMED KERNEL NETWORKS; 2) INCORPORATE DISCONTINUITY OF
MODEL PARAMETERS BY TRAINING THE WEAK FORMATION OF MULTI-PHYSICS MODELS; AND 3) DEVELOP AN INVERSE NETWORK
FRAMEWORK FOR REDUCED-ORDER SURROGATE MODELING. WE WILL COMPUTATIONALLY INVESTIGATE THE EFFICACY, STABILITY
(CONVERGENCE AND CONSISTENCY), AND UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION OF THE PROPOSED DEEP LEARNING NEURAL NETWORK
ALGORITHMS. IDENTIFYING THE BOUNDARIES OF OPERATION FOR THE PROPOSED SURROGATE DEEP ML MODELS, PARTICULARLY KNOWING
WHEN THESE NETWORKS BREAK DOWN, IS CRITICAL FOR DETERMINING TRUST IN REAL-TIME RISK MANAGEMENT GUIDELINES ON THE
BATTLEFIELD. TO DO THIS, WE WILL EMPLOY PHYSICS INFORMED NEURAL NETWORKS (PINN [1,2]) AND DEEP OPERATOR NETWORKS
(DEEPONET [4]). WHILE THE DEEPONET ARCHITECTURE IS INSPIRED BY THE WELL-KNOWN UNIVERSAL APPROXIMATION THEOREM
(UAT [5]), STABILITY AND UNCERTAINTY ISSUES ARE NOT WELL UNDERSTOOD. WE WILL EXTEND RECENT WORK ON THE THEORETICAL
FOUNDATION FOR UNIVERSAL NONLINEAR OPERATOR APPROXIMATION BY SINGLE LAYER NEURAL NETWORKS [6] TO PRACTICAL MODELS,
SUCH AS PYTHON ABLATION CODE (PAC1D, [7]) AND SCALABLE EFFECTS SIMULATION ENVIRONMENT (SESE [8]), WHICH CAN SIMULATE
A MATERIAL'S TIME-DEPENDENT RESPONSE TO INCIDENT LASER RADIATION. MANY APPROACHES, INCLUDING PINN [1,2], FNO [3],
DEEPONET [4], AND PHYSICS INFORMED KERNEL NEURAL OPERATORS (PIKNO [9]) HAVE BEEN INVESTIGATED FOR PAC1D [9,10]
AND SESE [9], AND HAVE SUCCESSFULLY SURROGATED PDE MODELS; HOWEVER, STABILITY (CONVERGENCE AND CONSISTENCY) AND
UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION ARE STILL MAJOR ISSUES.
BUILDING ON OUR WORK WITH COLLEAGUES AT AFRL [9,10], INCLUDING OUR INVESTIGATIONS OF UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION FOR
PAC1D [11], WE WILL DEVELOP NOVEL ALGORITHMS TO FIND COMPUTATIONALLY EFFICIENT SURROGATES FOR PARTIAL DIFFERENTIAL
EQUATION MODELS OF LASER-HUMAN INTERACTIONS.

THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP AND DEMONSTRATE A SOFTWARE DEFINED RADIO-BASED SYSTEM THAT AUTOMATICALLY DETECTS AND CLASSIFIES VARYING RADAR AND COMMUNICATION WAVEFORMS DIRECTLY FROM THE COMPLEX RF DATA USING A NOVEL AND MORE INTERPRETABLE DEEP LEARNING FRAMEWORK.

CURRENT TECHNIQUES ON RF WAVEFORM RECOGNITION HEAVILY RELIES ON TRANSFORMING TO RAW COMPLEX RF DATA INTO A FEATURE SPACE SUCH AS TIME-FREQUENCY DOMAIN AND EXTRACTING ENGINEERED FEATURES AND UTILIZING PATTERN RECOGNITION AND MACHINE LEARNING APPROACHES ON THE FEATURE SPACE [1-2]. THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH TECHNIQUES IS HIGHLY LIMITED DUE TO THE LOW REPRESENTATION OF FEATURES COMPARED TO THE COMBINATORIAL POSSIBILITIES OF VARIOUS RF WAVEFORM FEATURES AND UNDERLYING SCENARIOS. IN ADDITION, SINCE THESE APPROACHES REQUIRE A TRANSFORMATION FROM RAW RADAR DATA TO A DOMAIN SUCH AS TIMEÃ‚Â­ FREQUENCY, THEY HAVE HIGH COMPUTATIONAL COMPLEXITY AND ARE NOT VERY SUITABLE FOR CLOSE REAL-TIME IMPLEMENTATIONS EASILY. RATHER TECHNIQUES THAT CAN DIRECTLY LEARN THE OPTIMAL FEATURES FROM THE UNDERLYING COMPLEX RAW DATA ARE NECESSARY. WHILE RECENT DEEP LEARNING (DL) FRAMEWORKS SUCH AS CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORKS (CNN) PROVIDE CAPABILITY TO LEARN DIRECTLY FROM THE DATA, THEIR PERFORMANCE ON RAW RADAR DATA ARE LOW AND CNNS GENERALLY SHOW BETTER PERFORMANCE WHEN APPLIED ON TIME-FREQUENCY IMAGES. IN ADDITION, THE UNDERLYING LEARNING ARCHITECTURE IS GENERALLY A BLACK BOX WITHOUT ENOUGH INTERPRETABILITY AND PHYSICAL UNDERSTANDING. COMBINING THE UNDERLYING PHYSICAL INFORMATION AND BRINGING ADDITIONAL INTERPRETABILITY TO DL ARCHITECTURES HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO RESPOND TO THE CHALLENGES IN LEARNINGÃ‚Â­ BASED RECOGNITION OF RF WAVEFORMS IN VARIOUS DYNAMIC ENVIRONMENTS.

WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A MORE INTERPRETABLE DL FRAMEWORK THAT CAN DIRECTLY WORK ON COMPLEX RF DATA LEADING TO CLOSE TO REAL TIME IMPLEMENTATIONS. PROPOSED DL FRAMEWORK WILL LEARN PARAMETRIZED SINE FILTERS THAT IMPLEMENTS BAND-PASS FILTERS. IN THIS CASE, ONLY THE LOW- AND HIGH-CUTOFF FREQUENCIES ARE THE LEARNABLE PARAMETERS, WHICH RESULT IN THE NETWORK, I.E., SINE-NET, FOCUSING ON HIGHER-LEVEL LEARNABLE PARAMETERS THAT HAVE CLEAR PHYSICAL MEANINGS. OUR INITIAL RESULTS APPLIED ON RADAR BASED HUMAN ACTIVITY RECOGNITION SHOWS INCREASED PERFORMANCE AND INTERPRETABILITY. WE WILL DEVELOP BOTH A RF DATA SIMULATION ENVIRONMENT AND A SOFTWARE DEFINED RADIO-BASED HARDWARE IN THE LOOP DEMONSTRATION TO VALIDATE
THE PROPOSED SOLUTION FOR RF WAVEFORM CLASSIFICATION.

ALONG THE LE OF THE OUTBOARD WING RESULTING IN STRONG FLOW OSCILLATIONS THAT MIGHT CAUSE FLUTTER. THE VORTEX
LIFTOFF CAN BE EASILY PRECIPITATED BY A LEADING-EDGE CRANK OR OTHER DISCONTINUITIES IN THE SHAPE OF THE LEADING
EDGE (DROOP, SNAG, VORTILON AND A FENCE). IT CAN ALSO BE DELAYED, AND ITS LOCATION CHANGED BY ACTIVE FLOW
CONTROL (AFC) BECAUSE A SINGLE SMALL JET APPROPRIATELY ORIENTED AND PLACED AFFECTED THE PITCH OF A TAILLESS
AIRCRAFT OVER A WIDE RANGE OF INCIDENCE ANGLES OF INTEREST. SINCE THE UNDERSTANDING OF THIS FLOW PHENOMENON
MAY PROVIDE THE ACTIVE MEANS TO CONTROL PITCH DEPARTURES AND FLUTTER, THEY MAY ALSO PROVIDE HIGHER USABLE LIFT
COEFFICIENTS THAT ARE CURRENTLY AVOIDED BY THOSE ADVERSE EFFECTS AND HENCE SHORTEN TAKEOFF DISTANCES
INCREASING AIRFIELD AVAILABILITY.

VARIOUS TECHNIQUES HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED TO SYNTHESIZE AND DESIGN MICROSTRIP BSFS. CONVENTIONALLY, A TRIBAND BSF CAN BE OBTAINED BY CASCADING THREE DIFFERENT BANDSTOP FILTERS OR BY CASCADING A DOUBLE BAND BANDSTOP FILTER AND ANOTHER BANDSTOP FILTER. THE SIDE EFFECT OF THIS TECHNIQUE IS AN INCREASE IN CIRCUIT SIZE. SIZE REDUCTION OF BSFS IS ALWAYS AN IMPORTANT RESEARCH TOPIC. IN THIS PROJECT, A DOUBLE STUB LOADED MICROSTRIP RESONATOR, HAVING THREE ATTENUATION POLES, IN FOUR FORMATS, IS PROPOSED. ITS CHARACTER IMPEDANCE IS DERIVED, AND ITS RESONANT CONDITIONS ARE FOUND. MATLAB PROGRAMS WILL BE MADE TO CALCULATE ALL THE ELECTRICAL LENGTHS OF THE FIVE MICROSTRIPS IN THE RESONATOR. FOUR FIRST ORDER BSFS AND FOUR SECOND ORDER BSFS WILL BE DESIGNED USING THE FOUR FORMATS OF THE RESONATORS RESPECTIVELY. ALL THE FILTERS WILL BE SIMULATED AND TUNED ON SONNET SUITE SOFTWARE. THE FOUR SECOND ORDER BSFS WILL BE FABRICATED AND MEASURED USING A MICROWAVE
NETWORK ANALYZER. THE SIMULATED AND THE MEASURED RESULTS WILL BE COMPARED.

THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVES OF THIS COMPREHENSIVE RESEARCH ENDEAVOR ARE THREEFOLD. FIRSTLY, IT INVOLVES THE
UTILIZATION OF SUBSPACE MODELING WITHIN THE EXTENSIVE HYPERSPACE OF SPACE DOMAIN AWARENESS (SDA) DATA TO ESTABLISH
OPERATIONAL TAXONOMIES AND SUPPORTIVE ONTOLOGIES, ENABLING THE EFFECTIVE RECOGNITION AND IDENTIFICATION OF HOSTILE ACTIONS
CONDUCTED BY ADVERSARIAL DIRECT ASCENT ANTI-SATELLITES (DA ASATS). THESE ACTIONS MAY INVOLVE INTRICATE AND DECEPTIVE
BEHAVIORS SUCH AS CAMOUFLAGED, CONTENTMENT, AND DECEPTION (CCD) BEHAVIORS, POSING POTENTIAL THREATS TO THE SAFETY OF
SATELLITES OPERATING IN BOTH LOW EARTH ORBIT (LEO) AND GEOSYNCHRONOUS ORBITS (GEO). THIS RESEARCH ENTAILS A METICULOUS
ANALYSIS OF REAL-WORLD, NON-CLASSIFIED SPACE DOMAIN AWARENESS (SDA) DATA ENCOMPASSING VARIOUS DATA TYPES, INCLUDING
BEHAVIORAL PATTERNS, ORBITAL PARAMETERS, PHOTOMETRIC DATA, RADAR CROSS-SECTION, RF EMISSIONS, INFRASONIC SIGNALS, GPS
TELEMETRY, AND ASSOCIATED LIGHT CURVES. THE PROCESS INVOLVES DATA VALIDATION, CORRELATION, DIMENSIONALITY REDUCTION THROUGH
GROUPING AND CLUSTERING, STATISTICAL AND PROBABILISTIC MODELING OF NOISY DATA, AND ENHANCEMENT OF DATA ENTROPY THROUGH
SENSOR FUSION TECHNIQUES SUCH AS MONTE CARLO FILTERING (E.G., KALMAN AND PARTICLE FILTERING). SECONDLY, THE RESEARCH AIMS
TO DEVELOP TECHNIQUES FOR DISCRIMINATING AND CLASSIFYING DA ASATS, PARTICULARLY THOSE CARRYING INTELLIGENCE PAYLOADS OR
WEAPONS, WHILE EMPLOYING CCD TACTICS TO MISLEAD DETECTION. IT ESTABLISHES A THEORETICAL ARCHITECTURAL FRAMEWORK TO
SYSTEMATICALLY DISCRIMINATE AND CLASSIFY DA ASATS, FACILITATING INFORMED DECISION-MAKING AND CONTRIBUTING TO NATIONAL
DEFENSE AND SPACE ASSET SAFETY. LASTLY, THE PROJECT INCLUDES PROOF-OF-CONCEPT DEMONSTRATIONS USING THE PRINCIPAL
INVESTIGATOR'S ELECTROMAGNETIC MODELING AND SIMULATION SOFTWARE AND DISSEMINATING RESEARCH OUTCOMES AT DEFENSE
CONFERENCES IN COLLABORATION WITH AFRL PROJECT TECHNICAL MONITORS. THE FINAL OBJECTIVE INVOLVES RECRUITING, ENGAGING,
AND TRAINING MINORITY AND UNDERREPRESENTED GRADUATE STUDENTS AS FUTURE ASSETS FOR THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE, ALIGNING
WITH AFRL'S ORACLE PROJECT IN THE L1-ZONE AND THE CUSTODY MAINTENANCE OF DETECTED RESIDENT SPACE OBJECTS (RSO) OF
INTEREST VIA DOD'S SPACE SURVEILLANCE NETWORK (SSN).

MOR AND SI ARE ESSENTIAL PROCESSES IN THE LOW- DIMENSIONAL APPROXIMATION OF LARGE-SCALE MULTI PHYSICS SYSTEMS, PROVIDING COMPUTATIONALLY EFFICIENT SURROGATE MODELS FOR SIMULATION, DESIGN, OPTIMIZATION, AND CONTROL. UNDER REALISTIC CONDITIONS, UNCERTAINTY IS ALWAYS PRESENT IN THESE MODELS. A NON-PROBABILISTIC SETTING FOR UQ WILL BE PURSUED BASED ON (I) SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS AND (II) ROBUSTNESS ANALYSIS USING A LINEAR FRACTIONAL TRANSFORMATION (LFT) SETUP THAT ALLOWS THE NOMINAL SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION AND MODEL REDUCTION TO BE PERFORMED IN PARALLEL WITH THE PARAMETER UNCERTAINTY REDUCTION. THE OBJECTIVE IS TO ASSESS THE RELATIVE IMPORTANCE OF THE UNCERTAIN PARAMETERS AND TO DEVELOP UNCERTAINTY BOUNDS FOR THE RESULTING LOW ORDER MODELS USING STRUCTURED ROBUSTNESS ANALYSIS. UQ IN MOR WILL BE EXAMINED IN PROJECTION-BASED KRYLOV SUBSPACE AND BALANCED TRUNCATION ORDER REDUCTION METHODS THAT ARE APPROPRIATE FOR OBTAINING LOW-ORDER MODELS OF LARGE-SCALE SYSTEMS. ALSO, UQ IN REGRESSION-BASED IDENTIFICATION METHODS WILL BE EXAMINED THAT PRODUCE REDUCED-DIMENSIONALITY MODELS FROM EXPERIMENTAL DATA OR FROM HIGH-FIDELITY SIMULATION DATA. BOTH LINEAR AND NON-LINEAR DYNAMIC PROCESSES WILL BE CONSIDERED WHERE NONLINEARITY WILL BE CAPTURED IN A LINEAR PARAMETER VARYING (LPV) FRAMEWORK THAT EMBEDS THE NONLINEAR SYSTEM IN A PARAMETRIZED FAMILY OF LINEAR MODELS. THE RLCAP: EXPLAINING RL USING LOGICAL RULES, CONSTRAINTS, AUTOMATA, AND PROGRAM SYNTHESIS PROJECT AIMS TO
CREATE A FUNDAMENTAL SCIENCE OF EXPLAINABILITY FOR DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING (DEEPRL) BY DEVELOPING
NEW ALGORITHMS USING LOGICAL RULES, CONSTRAINTS, AUTOMATA, AND PROGRAM SYNTHESIS. THE ULTIMATE OBJECTIVE IS
TO ENABLE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF DEEPRL ALGORITHMS. BY COMBINING FORMAL LOGIC WITH RECENT RESULTS IN
DEEP MULTI-MODAL LEARNING AND LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS, WE WILL DEVELOP A SUITE OF METHODS THAT CAN EXPLAIN
THE BEHAVIOR OF DEEPRL MODELS. WE PLAN TO DEMONSTRATE THESE METHODS ON TEXT-BASED AND VIDEO-ORIENTED
GAMES, WHICH ARE WIDELY USED AS BENCHMARKS IN THE FIELD. OUR METHODOLOGY WILL DRAW ON RECENT ADVANCES IN
THE FOLLOWING AREAS:
(I) CONTRASTIVE LEARNING FOR SHARED MULTI-MODAL REPRESENTATIONS (CHUANG ET AL., 2022);
(II) STABLE DIFFUSIONS FOR VERIFYING EXPLANATIONS (DE BORTOLI ET AL., 2021);
(III) LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS FOR REASONING (RADFORD ET AL., 2019);
(IV) AUTOMATA LEARNING SUCH AS L* FOR GENERATING EXPLANATIONS (ANGLUIN, 1987); AND
(V) PROGRAM SYNTHESIS (JHA ET AL., 2010).
THROUGH THIS RESEARCH, WE AIM TO ESTABLISH A FRAMEWORK FOR THE EXPLAINABILITY OF DEEPRL ALGORITHMS THAT CAN
BE APPLIED TO A WIDE RANGE OF DOMAINS.

FEATURES. 1) IT CAN SUPPORT A BROADER CATEGORY OF RANK-AWARE QUERIES, AND 2) IT CAN BE BUILT BY RESOURCECONSTRAINED
DATA OWNERS. ACCORDINGLY, THIS PROJECT EXPLORES TWO APPROACHES. 1) THE CONCEPT OF INFORMATION
ELEMENT. AN INFORMATION ELEMENT IS A BASIC UNIT OF RANK-AWARE INFORMATION IN THE FORM OF WHICH RECORD HAS
WHAT RANK IN WHICH SUBDOMAIN. BEING FINE-GRAINED, INFORMATION ELEMENTS CAN THEN BE USED TO COMPUTE
POTENTIALLY ARBITRARY TYPES OF INFORMATION COMPOUND. 2) THE CONCEPT OF VERIFIABLE ADS. THE IDEA IS TO ALLOW
THE CLOUD TO PERFORM THE HEAVY COMPUTATION (E.G., FINDING THE INTERSECTIONS OF A SET OF RANKING FUNCTIONS)
WHILE THE DATA OWNER SIMPLY VERIFIES AND SIGNS THE COMPUTATION RESULTS. THE PROPOSED SOLUTIONS WILL BE
IMPLEMENTED AND EVALUATED THROUGH COMPLEXITY ANALYSIS AND EXPERIMENTS.

WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP ADAPTIVE, RECONFIGURABLE, SAFE, AND RESILIENT FLIGHT CONTROL SYSTEMS ABLE
TO HANDLE SYSTEM FAULTS, AND OFF-NOMINAL ADVERSE AND HAZARDOUS FLIGHT CONDITIONS, UTILIZING A NOVEL COMBINATION
OF ROBUST-ADAPTIVE/LEARNING CONTROL ALGORITHMS AND RUN TIME ASSURANCE (RTA). THE PROPOSED DUAL-LOOP
CONTROL CONFIGURATION IS EXPECTED TO GUARANTEE SATISFACTORY FLIGHT PERFORMANCE, AND AT THE SAME TIME ACHIEVE
ROBUST FAULT-TOLERANT CLOSED-LOOP FLIGHT STABILITY AND SAFETY DURING AUTONOMOUS FLIGHT OPERATION. WE ENVISION A
CLOSED-LOOP CONTROL ARCHITECTURE CONSISTING OF AN INNER LOOP IN THE ATTITUDE DYNAMICS, AND AN OUTER LOOP FOR PATH
PLANNING. IN THE INNER LOOP, WE PROPOSE TO USE A LINEAR-PARAMETER-VARYING (LPV) CONTROLLER FOR SMOOTH DYNAMIC
FLIGHT CONDITION SCHEDULING THAT IS COUPLED WITH A DEEP NEURAL NETWORK-BASED OBSERVER FOR ESTIMATING THE
UNKNOWN DYNAMICS AND DISTURBANCES DUE TO OPERATING CONDITION CHANGES. IN THE OUTER LOOP, GIVEN A NOMINAL OR
DESIRED TRAJECTORY TO FOLLOW, WE PROPOSE A LEARNING-BASED MOTION PLANNER FOR THE GENERATION OF THE REFERENCE
TRAJECTORY THAT THE VEHICLE IS EXPECTED TO TRACK, AND RE-PLANNING OF THE TRAJECTORY IN CASE OF SUBSYSTEM OR
COMPONENT FAULTS (E.G., A DAMAGED ROTOR) SEEKING TO ENSURE CONTINUATION OF THE MISSION. RTA FILTERING OF THE
CONTROL INPUT WILL BE DESIGNED INDEPENDENTLY OF THE CONTROL TO ENSURE THAT THE PRIMARY CONTROLLER ACTION DOES NOT
VIOLATE PREDETERMINED SAFETY CONSTRAINTS IN THE FACE OF UNCERTAINTY AND POTENTIAL SYSTEM FAULTS. THE PROPOSED
RECONFIGURABLE AND SAFE AUTONOMOUS FLIGHT CONTROL CONFIGURATION WILL BE VALIDATED ON A UAV TESTBED AT THE
UNIVERSITY OF HOUSTON (UH).

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND:
OCCUPATIONAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL CHEMICAL EXPOSURE IN DEPLOYMENT AND TRAINING IS ONE OF THE MOST CHALLENGING ASPECTS OF DOD RISK MANAGEMENT. ONE PROBLEM THAT NEEDS TO BE BRIDGED IS THAT HEALTH RISK
ASSESSMENT OF CHEMICAL EXPOSURE IS GREATLY RELIANT ON ANIMAL STUDIES [1, 2]. ALTHOUGH THIS APPROACH IS
FOUNDATIONAL TO TOXICOLOGY, AND AS SUCH UNLIKELY TO BE ENTIRELY REPLACED, IT HAS SERIOUS DRAWBACKS IN THAT IT IS NON-HUMAN, EXPENSIVE, LOW THROUGHPUT, AND IMPRACTICAL FOR SCREENING LARGE NUMBERS OF POTENTIALLY TOXIC CHEMICALS. TO ADDRESS THESE PROBLEMS, THE AIR FORCE (AF) SURGEON GENERAL INVESTED IN A PROGRAM AT SANFORD BURNHAM PREBYS (SBP) TO DEVELOP THE CELLULAR SENTINELS OF TOXICITY PLATFORM (CSTP), WITH THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF IMPROVING RISK MANAGEMENT OF OCCUPATIONAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL CHEMICAL EXPOSURES. THE CSTP IS
A SUITE OF ASSAYS FOR CELLULAR PHENOTYPE AND PHYSIOLOGY THAT UTILIZE HUMAN-INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELL
(HIPSC)-DERIVED NEURONS, CARDIOMYOCYTES, AND HEPATOCYTES TO ASSESS POTENTIAL TOXICITY. THE VALIDATION OF THE CSTP AGAINST CHEMICAL LIBRARIES OF KNOWN TOXINS DEMONSTRATED THE UTILITY OF THIS APPROACH TO DETECT TOXIC AGENTS.
IN AN AF-FUNDED SBP FOLLOW-UP PROGRAM, ÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã…Â€ŒENHANCEMENT OF A PREDICTIVE TOXICOLOGY TOOLBOX VIA MULTI-PARAMETRIC DATA-INFORMED QSAR MODELING OF BENCHMARK TOXINSÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¯Â¿Â½, WE LEVERAGED THE NEURON MODULE
OF THE CSTP FOCUSING ON THE HIGH SUSCEPTIBILITY OF NEURONS TO DAMAGE FROM CHEMICAL AGENTS. OUR OBJECTIVES
WERE TO: 1) PERFORM SCREENS OF THE CSTP NEURON MODULE ON A DIVERSE COLLECTION OF SELECT BENCHMARK CHEMICALS TO GENERATE A PRECISION DATABASE, PROVIDING A HIGH QUALITY DATA FEED TO CURRENT QUANTITATIVE STRUCTURE ACTIVITY RELATIONSHIP (QSAR) [3] MODELS OF NEUROTOXICOLOGICAL EXPOSURES, THUS IMPROVING THEIR PREDICTIVE POWER; 2) ENHANCE UTILITY OF THE CSTP NEURON MODULE BY MODELING THE EFFECTS OF CHEMICAL EXPOSURE ON LEARNING AND MEMORY PROCESSING UNDER PILOT CONDITIONS, SUCH AS STRESS, AND STIMULANTS FOR
WAKEFULNESS, AND HYPOXIA AND 3) DEVELOP AN IN SILICO TOXICOLOGY PLATFORM PREDICTIVE OF CHEMICAL EXPOSURE
ON HUMAN NEURONAL CELL PHENOTYPE, PHYSIOLOGY, AND COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE.
OVER THE THREE-YEAR PROGRAM, WE DEMONSTRATED UTILITY OF THE PLATFORM FOR RAPID IDENTIFICATION OF POTENTIALLY TOXIC CHEMICALS, CORRELATION OF TOXIC CHEMICAL DATA SIGNATURES WITH CHEMICAL STRUCTURE, AND POTENTIAL FOR THE PLATFORM TO SERVE AS A FOUNDATION FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF MORE ADVANCED ASSAYS TO MODEL THE EFFECT OF POTENTIAL TOXIC CHEMICALS ON COGNITION, LEARNING, AND MEMORY.
BRIEFLY, IN COLLABORATION WITH AF RESEARCHERS, WE ASSEMBLED THE SBP-AF TOXIN LIBRARY OF A 220 BENCHMARK, ÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã…Â€ŒSELECTÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¯Â¿Â½ CHEMICALS WITH STRUCTURAL AND MECHANISTIC DIVERSITY TO PROVIDE A TEST SET TO DETERMINE THE PREDICTIVE VALUE OF QSAR MODELS. WE SCREENED THE SBP-AF TOXIN LIBRARY AGAINST CSTP NEURON
MODULE ASSAYS FOR CELLULAR PHENOTYPE AND PHYSIOLOGY ON HIPSC-DERIVED NEURONS: 1) IMAGE-BASED ANALYSES OF NEURITE MORPHOLOGY TO IDENTIFY TOXINS DETRIMENTAL TO NEURAL NETWORK FORMATION AND MAINTENANCE; 2) LIVE
CELL ANALYSES OF MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION, OFTEN ASSOCIATED WITH EXPOSURE TO NEUROTOXINS; 3) PHYSIOLOGICAL ANALYSES OF ELECTRICAL ACTIVITY AT BOTH SINGLE-CELL AND NETWORK LEVELS USING MULTI-ELECTRODE ARRAYS, AN ASSAY WHICH WE FURTHER DEVELOPED TO MODEL CHEMICAL EXPOSURE EFFECTS ON COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE UNDER CONDITIONS
OF PILOT STRESS. IN ADDITION, FOR A SELECT SUBSET OF CHEMICALS, WE PERFORMED TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSES TO LINK
POTENTIAL NEUROTOXIN TARGETS TO MOLECULAR INITIATING EVENTS IN ADVERSE OUTCOME PATHWAYS. PRELIMINARY QSAR

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND: 

DR. HOANGHA PIRNSTILL, 711 HPW/RHBAM WILL UTILIZE THE TECHNICAL EXPERTISE OF TSI INC/KENNETH FARMER, THE UNIVERSITY OF IOWA/TOM PETERS AND THE UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS AT CHICAGO (UIC)/MARGARET SIETSEMA TO MEET THE OBJECTIVES IDENTIFIED IN THE ABOVE REFERENCED STUDY. EACH SUBRECIPIENT WILL PURSUE COMPLETION OF THE WORK OUTLINED BELOW IN SUPPORT OF 711 HUMAN PERFORMANCE WING OBJECTIVES. 

INHALATION OF AIRBORNE PARTICULATE MATTER CAN POTENTIALLY LEAD TO SIGNIFICANT HEALTH PROBLEMS SINCE SOME OF THESE PARTICLES CAN REACH THE DEEPEST REGIONS OF THE LUNGS, POSING MAJOR HEALTH AND OPERATIONAL RISK CONCERNS IN SOME DEPLOYMENT ENVIRONMENTS. THE SIZE AND COMPOSITION OF PARTICULATE MATTER IS IMPORTANT FOR THE ACCURATE ASSESSMENT OF HEALTH RISKS FOR DEPLOYED PERSONNEL. PARTICLES WITH AN AERODYNAMIC DIAMETER 2.5 MICRONS OR SMALLER ARE OF INTEREST DUE TO THEIR ABILITY TO SETTLE OUT IN THE GAS EXCHANGE REGIONS OF THE LUNG AND REMAIN IN THE RESPIRATORY BRONCHIOLES CAUSING MOST OF THE ADVERSE HEALTH EFFECTS. THE ABILITY TO RAPIDLY MEASURE, ASSESS AND PREDICT THE IMPACT OF AIRBORNE HEALTH HAZARDS AND THREATS IN THE AIR FORCE OPERATIONAL ENVIRONMENT IS IMPORTANT TO SAFEGUARD OUR AIRMEN.

TSI INCORPORATED HAS DEVELOPED A NEW TECHNOLOGY FOR ASSESSING RESPIRATORY PROTECTION AT THE FINE OR ULTRA-FINE SCALE, CALLED WEARABLE RESPIRATORY PROTECTION ASSESSMENT SYSTEM (WRPAS). THIS REVOLUTIONARY DEVICE INCORPORATES TWO WATER-BASED CONDENSATION PARTICLE COUNTERS INTO A TINY, WEARABLE FORM FACTOR USED TO EVALUATE RESPIRATOR PROTECTION IN REALÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¯Â¿Â½TIME WHILE A WORKER PERFORMS OCCUPATIONAL TASKS.  THE TECHNOLOGY IS ALSO SUITABLE FOR DETECTING FINE AND ULTRA-FINE PARTICLES IN THE ENVIRONMENT TO ENABLE ASSESSMENT OF EXPOSURE TO ENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS SUCH AS SMOLDERING OR OTHER PARTICULATE SOURCES.

THE WORK FOR THIS CONTRACT IS THE CULMINATION OF SEVERAL YEARS OF RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT SPONSORED BY THE AIR FORCE THROUGH THE SBIR PROGRAM TARGETED AT DETECTING AND ASSESSING THESE HEALTH RISKS, WITH THE AIM OF ENABLING A SOLUTION TO BE BROUGHT TO COMMERCIAL FRUITION.

TSI INCORPORATED, TOGETHER WITH COLLABORATORS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF IOWA AND UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS AT CHICAGO WILL WORK WITH AIR FORCE RESEARCH LABORATORY (AFRL) TO MATURE AND EVALUATE THE WRPAS PROTOTYPE FOR MILITARY USE. THREE DESIRED CAPABILITIES/AIMS HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED FOR THIS WORK: (1) DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION IN OPERATIONAL ENVIRONMENT TO DRIVE WRPAS TO TRL 9 (FULL FIELD USAGE) FOR RESPIRATORY APPLICATIONS, (2) DEMONSTRATE USES BEYOND RESPIRATORY PROTECTION:  EMISSION DETECTION AND PERFORMANCE OF PROTECTIVE TECHNOLOGIES, AND (3) EVALUATE CAPABILITY FOR PARTICLE SIZE DISTINCTION/DETECTION.

1. SCOPE
WE WILL ENGINEER THE NTRAIN SYSTEM, A WIRELESSLY CONTROLLED BIOELECTRONIC/SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY
HYBRID IMPLANTED DEVICE THAT WILL REDUCE THE TIME NEEDED TO ADAPT TO NEW TIMEZONES OR DRASTIC

WILL SUPPORT AND ENHANCE CELL VIABILITY AND BIOLOGICS PRODUCTION. THE IMPLANT, DEPLOYED
SUBCUTANEOUSLY, WILL BE WIRELESSLY POWERED BY MAGNETO-ELECTRIC TRANSDUCERS AND TRANSMIT DATA BY
NEAR FIELD COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS TO A LOW PROFILE WEARABLE HUB. THE HUB WILL COMMUNICATE
EITHER DIRECTLY OR VIA A CUSTOM SMARTPHONE APPLICATION IN ORDER TO DIRECT THE WARFIGHTER TO TRIGGER
THE DELIVERY OF PEPTIDE THERAPEUTICS PRODUCED BY THE MAMMALIAN CELL FACTORIES. THIS PLATFORM FORMS
THE BASIS FOR A LIVING BIOELECTRONIC PHARMACY. THE IMPLANTABLE NTRAIN DEVICE IS MEANT TO BE
DEPLOYED VIA OUTPATIENT SUBCUTANEOUS IMPLANTATION, AND BE VIABLE FOR AT LEAST 60 DAYS, BUT IS BASED
ON TECHNOLOGY THAT ENABLES LONG TERM VIABILITY, WITH TRIGGERED DELIVERY POSSIBLE DURING ITS LIFETIME.
SURGICAL DEVICE EXPLANTATION OR ADMINISTRATION OF APPROVED SMALL MOLECULE DRUGS WHICH ACTIVATE A
KILL SWITCH IN THE CELL FACTORIES RENDER THE DEVICE INACTIVE. COMPONENT (CELL, COMMUNICATION, ETC.)
DEVELOPMENT WILL BE VALIDATED IN RODENT MODELS, WITH THE INTEGRATED BIOELECTRONIC AND HYBRID
SYSTEM TESTED FOR SAFETY AND EFFICACY IN NON-HUMAN PRIMATE (NHP) MODELS. WE HAVE ELECTED TO USE
NHPS DUE TO THEIR HIGH TRANSLATIONAL VALIDITY TO HUMAN SLEEP-WAKE STATES AND CIRCADIAN RHYTHM
PATTERNS, AS WELL AS IMPROVED CELL VIABILITY RESPONSE OF ALLOGENEIC OPTICALLY-INDICIBLE CELL-BASED
FACTORIES AND THEIR DELIVERED NATIVE PEPTIDES, AND WE HAVE MADE CONCERTED EFFORTS TO REDUCE THE
QUANTITY OF NHPS NEEDED (APPENDIX A). BIOELECTRONIC CARRIER/COMMUNICATION COMPONENTS WILL BE
TESTED FOR SAFETY IN PHASE 3 FIRST IN HUMAN CLINICAL TRIAL.
THE MECHANISTIC BASIS THAT WILL ENABLE A 50% REDUCTION IN ENTRAINMENT TIME IS THE TARGETING
OF BOTH CENTRAL AND PERIPHERAL CIRCADIAN CLOCKS AND MITIGATING THEIR DESYNCHRONY. WE WILL EMPLOY
NON-TRADITIONAL PEPTIDE-BASED THERAPIES GROUNDED IN SLEEP AND CIRCADIAN SCIENCE LITERATURE FOR
PRODUCTION BY CELL FACTORIES. WE WILL TARGET PEPTIDES WHICH WILL ACT ON BOTH THE CENTRAL
(HYPOTHALAMIC SUPRACHIASMATIC NUCLEUS) CLOCK AND ON PERIPHERAL CLOCKS IN CONCERT (INITIAL TARGETS:
GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1, GLP-1; OREXIN-A), WITH OTHERS NOTED IN RISK MITIGATION IN VOLUME I.
THESE THERAPIES ARE EXPECTED TO ACT SYNERGISTICALLY BY ACTING ON PATHWAYS ENGAGED IN SLEEP-WAKE
AND FEED-FAST CYCLES. QUANTIFYING THE TIMING OF THERAPEUTIC RELEASE WITH RESPECT TO CLOCK TIME, AS
WELL AS THE WARFIGHTERÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¢Â€ŽÂ¢S CURRENT PHASE (DETERMINED FROM A MINIMAL BASIS SET OF SENSORS) WILL ENABLE
PRECISION DOSE AND TIMING FOR EFFECTIVE ENTRAINMENT THERAPY. NTRAIN WOULD ENABLE ACCELERATED
ADAPTATION TO A NEW TIME ZONE OR SCHEDULE FOR WARFIGHTERS, SHIFT WORKERS, AND FIRST RESPONDERS, IN
ADDITION TO GARNERING BROAD SOCIETAL AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS. FURTHER, THE LIVING BIOELECTRONIC

THE EXISTENCE OF PRAGMATIC CONSTRAINTS, EITHER EXPLICITLY OR IMPLICITLY SPECIFIED, IS AN IMPORTANT USABILITY FACTOR WORTHING CAREFUL CONSIDERATION IN DESIGNING SYSTEMS FOR AUTOMATIC MODEL EXPLORATION. FULLY EXPLORING A COMBINATORIAL MODEL SPACE ASSUMING AN INFINITE AMOUNT OF TIME OR SYSTEM RESOURCE IS NOT REALISTIC, NOT ONLY INCURRING A PROHIBITIVELY EXPENSIVE COMPUTE COST BUT ALSO A PRACTICALLY INTOLERABLE Ã¢Â‚¬Å“SILENT RESPONSEÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ PERIOD FOR HUMAN EXPERTS TO START TO RECEIVE ANY DISCOVERED MODELS FOR PROVIDING FEEDBACK. WE ENVISION BUDGET-BASED MODEL DISCOVERY BEING FAR MORE RELEVANT AND PRAGMATIC Ã¢Â‚¬Â€? USERS SPECIFY A BUDGET (FOR EXAMPLE, IN TERMS OF COMPUTING TIME) FOR THE SYSTEM TO DISCOVER THE BEST MODEL AMONG CANDIDATES. THOSE CANDIDATES CAN BE RANDOMLY SELECTED FROM THE MODEL SPACE, OR THEY CAN BE THE OUTPUT OF THE META-LEARNING ALGORITHM. WE FORMULATE THIS TASK OF IDENTIFYING THE BEST MODEL AS IDENTIFYING THE BEST ARM IN A NON-STOCHASTIC MULTI-ARMED BANDIT (MAB). EACH ARM IS A CANDIDATE MODEL. HOWEVER, IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO TRAIN AND EVALUATE EVERY CANDIDATE EXHAUSTIVELY. THE KEY IDEA IS TO TERMINATE MODEL SEARCH PATHS (FOR EXAMPLE, TERMINATING ITERATIVE LEARNING PROCESSES ON CERTAIN MODELS, MUCH EARLIER THAN THE TYPICAL EARLY-STOPPING USED IN LEARNING METHODS) IF WE ARE ASSURED THAT THOSE MODELS ON THOSE PATHS WILL NEVER BECOME BETTER (THAN ALTERNATIVES). IN ESSENCE, WE DO NOT NEED (AND SHOULD NOT) WAIT UNTIL ALL MODELS CONVERGE BEFORE WE DECIDE A PARTICULAR SEARCH DIRECTION IN THE MODEL SPACE IS FUTILE. FOR EXAMPLE, THE PRELIMINARY WORK BY TALWALKAR ET AL [5] HAS SHOWN PROMISING RESULTS ON USING MAB TO TUNE HYPERPARAMETERS, GIVEN A BUDGET OF TRAINING TIME. THE KEY STRATEGY IS TO MAINTAIN A LARGE LIST OF POSSIBLE CONFIGURATIONS OF HYPERPARAMETERS AND THEN HALVE THE LIST BY DISCARDING THE BOTTOMHALF POORLY PERFORMING ONES, AFTER RUNNING LEARNING PROCEDURES FOR A VERY SHORT TIME. THE SURVIVING HALF IS THEN ALLOCATED MORE COMPUTING TIME AND THE HALVING PROCESS IS APPLIED AGAIN TO ELIMINATE THE BOTTOM HALF, RESULTING 1/4 OF THE ORIGINAL LIST. RECURSIVELY, THE FINAL (BUT STILL WITHIN THE BUDGET) SURVIVING CONFIGURATION OF HYPERPARAMETERS IS PROVABLY THE OPTIMAL ONE. WE PLAN TO BUILD ON THIS TYPE OF STRATEGY FOR OUR BUDGET-BASED MODEL SPACE EXPLORATION. MODERN MACHINE LEARNING SYSTEMS HAVE BECOME INCREASINGLY COMPLICATED. THEY ARE SYSTEMS OF SYSTEMS, WHICH ARE MADE OF HETEROGENEOUS SUBSYSTEMS AND ORGANIZED IN COMPLEX PIPELINES. FURTHERMORE, THEY CAN ALSO BE EMBEDDED AS A SUBSYSTEM IN A PIPELINE, CONNECTING WITH OTHER NON-MACHINE LEARNING PROCESSING COMPONENTS. CONVENTIONAL GRADIENTBASED OPTIMIZATION TECHNIQUES, APTLY USED BY DEEP LEARNING ARCHITECTURES FOR END-TO-ENDING LEARNING, ARE NO LONGER ADEQUATE FOR TWO REASONS: (1) NOT EVERY COMPONENT ADMITS GRADIENT COMPUTATION WITH RESPECT TO PARAMETERS OF ITS AND OTHERS; (2) IT IS COMPUTATIONALLY COSTLY TO DIRECTLY ESTIMATE THE JOINT GRADIENT OF ALL PARAMETERS IN THE SYSTEM. TO ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES WE PROPOSE A SET OF KEY TECHNIQUES THAT BUILD ON STATE-OF-THE-ART RESULTS IN OPTIMIZATION AND PROBABILISTIC INFERENCE

GA2O3 HAS A LOW THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY. AS THE MATERIAL HEATS UP, DEVICE PERFORMANCE DEGRADES DUE TO INCREASED SCATTERING. ADDITIONALLY, THE DEVICES MAY FAIL PREMATURELY IF THE HEAT IS NOT EFFICIENTLY REMOVED. TO ADDRESS THE THERMAL CHALLENGES, TWO APPROACHES ARE BEING TAKEN. FIRST, IS TO REDUCE THE AMOUNT OF HEAT PRODUCED IN THE FIRST PLACE. BY REDUCING THE RESISTANCE OF THE DEVICE, LESS HEAT IS PRODUCED. THIS WILL BE ACHIEVED BY REDUCING THE CONTACT RESISTANCE BETWEEN THE METAL AND THE GA2O3 THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN IN-SITU ETCH PROCESS.
THERE WILL INEVITABLY BE SOME RESISTANCE WHICH WILL RESULT IN SOME HEAT BEING PRODUCED. THAT HEAT IS MOVED FROM THE DEVICE CHANNEL TO THE BACKSIDE USING OUR PATENT-PENDING THERMAL SOLUTION. ONCE HEAT IS AT THE CHIP BACKSIDE, IT MUST BE SPREAD AND ALLOWED TO DISSIPATE THROUGH THE USE OF A HEATSINK OR OTHER HEAT SPREADING TECHNIQUES.
THE CORNELL TEAM WILL FOCUS ON THE IN-SITU ETCH DEVELOPMENT, WHILE GALLOX FOCUS ON THE PACKAGE DEVELOPMENT.

OBJECTIVES AND MILESTONES: 
OBJECTIVE 1: HYPERSPECTRAL UNMIXING IS THE PROCESS OF EXTRACTING UNDERLYING MATERIALS FROM REMOTELY SENSED SPECTROSCOPY, AVAILABLE NATIVELY FROM HSI. IN HSI, AN INDIVIDUAL PIXEL CONTAINS RADIANCE INFORMATION WHICH IS A FUNCTION OF BOTH THE REFLECTIVITY FROM MATERIAL PROPERTIES AS WELL AS ATMOSPHERIC EFFECTS. HYPERSPECTRAL UNMIXING CAN LEVERAGE SIMULATION OR DATA-DRIVEN METHODS. SIMULATION SUCH AS RAY-TRACING USES MONTE CARLO METHODS TO MODEL RANDOM RAY REFLECTION GIVEN AN UNDERSTANDING OF THE CANDIDATE MATERIALS GEOMETRY AND PHYSICAL PROPERTIES. DATA-DRIVEN APPROACHES USE MACHINE LEARNING TO EXTRACT THIS NONLINEAR RELATIONSHIP FROM GROUND TRUTH DATA ITSELF. RAY-TRACING TECHNIQUES LEND THEMSELVES TO SCENARIOS WHERE PHYSICAL PROPERTIES ARE EASILY MODELED, AND DATA-DRIVEN TECHNIQUES ARE EFFECTIVE FOR PROBLEMS WITH CONSIDERABLE GROUND TRUTH DATA. MILESTONE 1: FOR EACH APPLICATION, WE WILL BUILD RAY-TRACING AND DATA-DRIVEN TECHNIQUES THAT ARE SUITABLE FOR REAL-TIME PROCESSING AT THE EDGE BY LEVERAGING OUR EXPERIENCE WITH NEW LOW SWAP TENSOR PROCESSING UNITS FOR ACCELERATION. MILESTONE 2: FURTHERMORE, WE WILL INCORPORATE DR. BOUBINÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¢Â€ŽÂ¢S PRIOR WORK IN AUTONOMOUS UAV TO 1) POSITION COMPUTE ONBOARD UAV OR AT THE EDGE FOR MINIMUM LATENCY AND 2) AUTONOMOUSLY NAVIGATE ENVIRONMENTS TO QUICKLY BUILD ACCURATE MAPS OF PHENOMENA. METRICS: WE WILL TRACK BOTH THE ACCURACY AND INFERENCE TIME OF OUR UNMIXING TO ASSURE QUALITY AND SUITABILITY FOR REAL-TIME PROCESSING.  

OBJECTIVE 2: WE WILL TARGET OUR EVALUATION TOWARD TWO APPLICATIONS: SECURE WATERWAYS, AND SECURE FOOD SYSTEMS. WE WILL LEVERAGE THE EXPERTISE OF OUR COLLABORATOR DR. WIGDAHL AT SUNY FREDONIA, A LAKE ECOLOGIST, TO DETECT EARLY SIGNS OF HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS IN LAKES AND WATERWAYS. WE WILL ALSO LEVERAGE DR. BOUBINÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¢Â€ŽÂ¢S EXPERTISE TO DETECT CROP DISEASES AND PESTS IN CROP FIELDS USING HSI. THIS EVALUATION WILL PROVIDE A GENERAL DUAL USE SOLUTION RELEVANT TO NATIONAL PROTECTION OF WATERWAYS/AGRICULTURE AS WELL AS PROVIDING AN ANALOGOUS USE CASE TO SMALL OBJECT DETECTION IN DEFENSE PROBLEMS. PROJECT FOCUS:
THE FOCUS OF THIS WORK IS TO DESIGN AN IRS AT SUB-THZ FREQUENCIES WHERE THE DESIGN IS INFORMED
BY THE CHANNEL MODELING IN RELEVANT SCENARIOS. MORE SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL DEVELOP A
COMPREHENSIVE CHANNEL MODEL WHICH SPECIFIES THE DYNAMIC RANGE OF MULTIPATH SIGNALS, THE
SPECIFIC IMPACT OF THE NEAR FIELD, AND THE STRONGEST POINTS OF REFLECTED SIGNALS. THESE WILL THEN BE
EXPLOITED TO DESIGN AN IRS WHICH IS NOT AGNOSTIC TO THE CHANNEL CONDITIONS, BUT RATHER
STRATEGICALLY DESIGNED AND ORIENTED TO HELP INCREASE THE ROBUSTNESS OF THE SUB-THZ LINK. THE
PROJECT RELIES ON THE UNIQUE SYMBIOSIS OF THE PIÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¢Â€ŽÂ¢S EXPERTISE, AS WELL AS THEIR STRONG COLLABORATION

THIS PROJECT WILL ADDRESS THE NE IPM CENTER’S SIGNATURE PROGRAM: IPM AND ORGANIC SYSTEMS BY PROVIDING ORGANIC DRY BEAN FARMERS WITH VALUABLE INFORMATION ABOUT THEIR SAVED SEED THROUGH A SEED-BORNE DISEASE SCREENING. DRY BEAN PRODUCTION IN THE NORTHEAST IS LARGELY THROUGH ORGANIC FARMERS ON A SMALL-SCALE, WITH MANY FARMERS CHOOSING TO SAVE THEIR OWN SEED RATHER THAN PURCHASE NEW SEED AT THE START OF EACH SEASON. THE DECISION TO SAVE SEED IS IN-PART DRIVEN BY A LACK OF SEED SOURCES FOR HEIRLOOM OR SPECIALTY VARIETIES OF DRY BEANS THAT CONSUMERS PREFER. CROP ROTATION IS A CRUCIAL IPM STRATEGY FOR ORGANIC PRODUCERS. DRY BEANS SERVE A VALUABLE ROLE AS A ROTATIONAL CROP WITH SMALL GRAINS BY STOPPING DISEASE TRANSMISSION FROM YEAR TO YEAR BECAUSE LEGUMES LIKE DRY BEANS ARE NOT SUSCEPTIBLE TO THE SAME DISEASES AS CEREAL GRAINS. PLANTING CLEAN DISEASE-FREE SEEDS IS CRITICAL TO REDUCING THE RISK OF DISEASE OUTBREAK DURING THE SEASON. FARMERS THAT PURCHASE SEEDS CAN ENSURE CLEAN SEED BY BUYING CERTIFIED SEEDS, BUT FARMERS THAT ARE SAVING AND PLANTING THEIR OWN SEED MUST HAVE THEIR SEED TESTED BY A PLANT DIAGNOSTIC LABORATORY TO ENSURE THAT IT IS FREE OF SEED-BORNE PATHOGENS. FARMERS THAT PARTICIPATE IN THIS SEED-BORNE DISEASE SCREENING WILL NOT ONLY LEARN WHAT SEEDBORNE PATHOGENS ARE PRESENT IN THEIR SEED BUT WILL ALSO RECEIVE VALUABLE RESOURCES ON THE SPECIFIC PATHOGENS AND MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT WILL HELP REDUCE DISEASE INCIDENCE AND POTENTIAL CROP LOSS DURING THE GROWING SEASON.

THE NEW PI PROF. HAO ZHENG). PROF. EWETZ AND PROF. ZHENG WILL MEET ON A WEEKLY BASIS TO
ENSURE THAT TIMELY PROGRESS IS MADE ACCORDING TO THE PROJECT PLAN.
2. TASK 1 (PHASE 1): CREATE JOINT LATENT ENCODINGS OF SYMBOLIC AND NEURAL REPRESENTATIONS.
WE WILL DEVELOP ALGORITHMS TO ALIGN UNIVERSAL SCENE DESCRIPTION LANGUAGE AND IMAGES
USING CONTRASTIVE LEARNING. THE OBJECTIVE IS TO ALLOW IMAGES TO SEAMLESSLY BE CONVERTED
INTO TEXT AND THEN BACK INTO IMAGES AGAIN.
3. TASK 3 (PHASE 1): DECISION MAKING FROM TEMPORAL LOGIC SPECIFICATIONS USING GRAPH
NEURAL NETWORKS AND ALTERNATING AUTOMATA. THIS WILL INCLUDE DEVELOPING ALGORITHMS FOR
NAVIGATION BASED ON NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTIONS. WE WILL USE AN LLM TO CREATE CONTROL
ALGORITHMS AND GRAPH NEURAL NETWORKS USING THE LLMS INTRINSIC CODE GENERATION ABILITIES.
4. TASK 4 (PHASE 1): DEMO AND EXPERIMENTAL SUPPORT: THE UF TEAM WILL DEVELOP THE HYBRID
AI SYSTEM SOLUTION DUE TO DARPA IN OCTOBER 2024. THE SYSTEM WILL CONSIST OF AN
INTEGRATED MANEUVER AND PERCEPTION COMPONENT.
5. TASK 1 (PHASE 2): SCALABLE REASONING BY COMPUTING CONFIDENCE USING BAYESIAN HYPOTHESIS
TESTING WITH SPATIO-TEMPORAL PRIORS: WE WILL INVESTIGATE BAYESIAN HYPOTHESIS TESTING TO
COMPUTE THE CONFIDENCE OF A PREDICTION FROM OUR NEURO-SYMBOLIC APPROACH.
6. TASK 3 (PHASE 2): LEARNING ALTERNATING AUTOMATA AS SYMBOLIC REPRESENTATIONS OF
ENVIRONMENT AND MODEL CHECKING AGAINST TEMPORAL LOGIC SPECIFICATIONS: THIS WILL INCLUDE
CONVERTING NATURAL LANGUAGE SPECIFICATION INTO LINEAR TIME LOGIC (LTL) TO VERIFY THE PLAN
GENERATED BY THE LLM. WE WILL DESCRIBE THE BEHAVIOR OF AUTONOMOUS AGENTS USING
ALTERNATING AUTOMATA, TO ENABLE SWIFT VERIFICATION FOR HIGH ASSURANCE.
7. TASK 4 (PHASE 2): DEMO AND EXPERIMENTAL SUPPORT: THE UF TEAM WILL DEVELOP THE HYBRID
AI SYSTEM SOLUTION DUE TO DARPA IN PHASE 2 (DUE DATES TO BE DETERMINED). THE SYSTEM WILL CONSIST OF AN INTEGRATED MANEUVER AND PERCEPTION COMPONENT THAT WILL MEET REAL-
TIME SIZE, WEIGHT, AREA, AND POWER CONSTRAINTS.

IOWA STATE UNIVERSITY (ISU) IS EMBARKING ON A GROUNDBREAKING PROJECT AIMED AT REVOLUTIONIZING POSITION, NAVIGATION, AND TIME (PNT) CAPABILITIES FOR TACTICAL RADIO UNITS OPERATING IN GNSSDENIED ENVIRONMENTS. OUR INNOVATIVE APPROACH INVOLVES EMBEDDING A NAVIGATION SIGNAL DIRECTLY INTO THE TACTICAL RADIO SIGNAL, LEVERAGING THE ROBUST TRANSMISSION CAPABILITIES AND LOWER ORBITS OF THESE UNITS. THIS INTEGRATION ENHANCES OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY AND OPTIMIZES SPECTRAL UTILIZATION BY CAPITALIZING ON THE WIDEBAND CHARACTERISTICS OF BOTH THE TACTICAL RADIOCOMMUNICATION AND NAVIGATION SIGNALS, ALLOWING FOR EFFECTIVE SUPPRESSION OF MUTUAL INTERFERENCE THROUGH PROCESSING GAINS. THIS WORK WILL BE PERFORMED UNDER TASK 9 OF THE UNM OVERARCHING SOW. 1. COMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS: WE WILL CONDUCT AN IN-DEPTH ANALYSIS TO EVALUATE THE MUTUAL INTERFERENCE BETWEEN THE NAVIGATION SIGNAL AND THE TACTICAL RADIO SIGNAL. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL ASSESS THE DECODING ERROR PROBABILITY FOR BOTH PNT INFORMATION AND TACTICAL RADIO COMMUNICATION. THIS RIGOROUS ANALYSIS IS CRUCIAL TO ENSURE THE FEASIBILITY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF OUR PROPOSED SOLUTION. 2. INNOVATIVE DECODING APPROACH: WE WILL EXPLORE A NOVEL METHOD TO FIRST DECODE THE STRONG TACTICAL RADIO SIGNAL AND THEN CANCEL IT FROM THE RECEIVED SIGNAL. THIS WILL ENABLE THE NAVIGATION SIGNAL TO BE DECODED WITHOUT INTERFERENCE FROM THE TACTICAL RADIO SIGNAL, ENSURING UNADULTERATED PNT INFORMATION. WE WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE IMPACT OF IMPERFECT CANCELLATION DUE TO DECODING FAILURES, ENSURING A ROBUST AND RELIABLE SYSTEM. 3. ADAPTIVE JAMMING MITIGATION: PROBABILISTIC JAMMING POSES A SIGNIFICANT CHALLENGE DUE TO ITS RANDOM OR SEMI-RANDOM INTERFERENCE PATTERNS. TO ADDRESS THIS, WE WILL EMPLOY CUTTING-EDGE REINFORCEMENT LEARNING TECHNIQUES TO DYNAMICALLY ADAPT THE CARRIER FREQUENCY OF THE NAVIGATION SIGNAL. THIS ADAPTIVE APPROACH WILL SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCE THE ADVERSE EFFECTS OF PROBABILISTIC JAMMING, CONTRIBUTING TO MORE ROBUST AND SECURE NAVIGATION SIGNAL RECEPTION. 4. DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH FINDINGS: ISU WILL PROVIDE ANALYSIS, INSIGHT, AND RECOMMENDATIONS TO ADVANCE THE STATE-OF-THE-ART FOR COUNTERING GNSS DENIAL IN TACTICAL RADIO NETWORKS. THIS TASK WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED BY DISSEMINATING OUR RESEARCH FINDINGS THROUGH PRESENTATIONS TO THE SPONSOR, TECHNICAL PRESENTATIONS AT CONFERENCES, AND JOURNAL PUBLICATIONS. 5. MANAGEMENT: ISU WILL WORK IN COLLABORATION WITH THE UNM PI TO PERFORM A SUBSTANTIVE PORTION OF THE PROGRAMMATIC EFFORT ON AN AWARD. PROGRAM PROGRESS IS QUANTIFIED BY WRITTEN MONTHLY STATUS REPORTS AND QUARTERLY TECHNICAL STATUS REPORTS. WE MEET WITH THE COSMIAC PROGRAM MANAGER AND RELEVANT RESEARCHERS IN PERSON, AS POSSIBLE. ISU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SAME REGULATORY AND COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS AS UNM

RF SENSOR SOW FOR COLORADO SCHOOL OF MINES
BACKGROUND
THIS PROJECT FOCUSES ON PERFORMING FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH TO IMPROVE THE PERFORMANCE OF AN ELECTRO-OPTIC (EO)-BASED RADIO FREQUENCY (RF) SENSOR USING TARGETED ELECTRODE DESIGN. EO-BASED RF SENSORS OFFER WIDE INSTANTANEOUS RF SENSING BANDWIDTH, POTENTIALLY HIGH ELECTRIC FIELD SENSITIVITY, AND SMALL SIZE, WEIGHT, AND POWER. RECENT WORK FROM A NUMBER OF GROUPS, INCLUDING DR. SANTAMARIA BOTELLO’S GROUP AT THE COLORADO SCHOOL OF MINES, HAS SHOWN THE IMPORTANCE OF ELECTRODE DESIGN, INCLUDING ASSOCIATED COMPONENTS FOR IMPEDANCE MATCHING, TO ENHANCE THE SENSITIVITY OF EO-BASED RF SENSORS OVER A LARGE FREQUENCY RANGE. 
THE PURPOSE OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO DEVELOP HIGH-PERFORMANCE ELECTRODE DESIGNS FOR A SERIES OF EO PHOTONIC INTEGRATED CIRCUIT (PIC) ARCHITECTURES. BY LEVERAGING THE INTERNAL DESIGN, SIMULATION CAPABILITIES, AND SPECIALIZED PERSONNEL AT THE COLORADO SCHOOL OF MINES, THIS RESEARCH WILL DETERMINE THE POTENTIAL FOR SENSITIVITY IMPROVEMENTS. THIS WORK SUPPORTS THE BROADER RESEARCH GOALS UNDER THE COMPNT PROJECT, SPECIFICALLY ADDRESSING OVERLAPPING RESEARCH NEEDS IN RECONFIGURABLE COMMUNICATIONS, HIGH-FREQUENCY SENSING (UP TO V-BAND AND W-BAND), AND POSITIONING, NAVIGATION AND TIMING COMPONENTS.
OBJECTIVE
THE SUBRECIPIENT WILL DEVELOP THEORETICAL MODELS FOR ELECTRIC FIELD ENHANCEMENT IN RF ELECTRODES DRIVING ELECTROOPTIC STRUCTURES, ENGINEERED TO MAXIMIZE MODULATION EFFICIENCY. THIS WILL SUPPORT APPLICATIONS IN COMMUNICATIONS, SENSING, AND PNT, OVER A WIDE RANGE OF RADIOFREQUENCIES. SIMULATION WORK AND ANALYSIS WILL BE PERFORMED USING FULL-WAVE SOLVERS (ANSYS HFSS) AND IN-HOUSE CODE WRITTEN IN MATLAB OR PYTHON.
TASK 1: ELECTRODE ENHANCEMENT MODEL
DEVELOP A THEORETICAL MODEL FOR ELECTRIC FIELD ENHANCEMENT IN RF ELECTRODES ENGINEERED TO MAXIMIZE EO MODULATION EFFICIENCY IN AN EASILY USEABLE LANGUAGE SUCH AS MATLAB OR PYTHON. WHILE PREVIOUS WORK HAS SHOWN SUBSTANTIAL ENHANCEMENT FACTORS BY EMBEDDING RESONANT RF STRUCTURES IN EO MODULATORS (ARXIV:2510.06176, NATURE 637 (8048), 1096-1103), RESONATORS ARE NATURALLY NARROWBAND AND ARE TYPICALLY DESIGNED FOR REAL-VALUED MODERATE SOURCE IMPEDANCES (E.G., 50 OHM). IF THE EO RECEIVER IS COUPLED TO AN ELECTRICALLY SMALL ANTENNA, THIS WILL TYPICALLY PRESENT EXTREME SOURCE IMPEDANCES APPROACHING THE EDGE OF THE SMITH CHART. IT IS UNCLEAR TO WHAT EXTENT A CO-DESIGNED ANTENNA-ELECTRODE RESONANT STRUCTURE CAN ENHANCE THE MODULATION EFFICIENCY AND WITHIN WHAT BANDWIDTH. HOWEVER, IT IS EXPECTED THAT NON-RESONANT ELECTRODES WHEREBY THE DISTRIBUTED CAPACITANCE OF THE ELECTRODES IS MINIMIZED, WILL INCREASE THE ELECTRIC FIELD AT THE ELECTROOPTIC MEDIUM DUE TO THE REDUCED LOADING EFFECT OF THE ANTENNA. SIMILARLY, WHETHER SYNTHESIS OF COUPLED LUMPED RF RESONATORS OR ARTIFICIAL TRANSMISSION LINES USING EXTERNAL INDUCTORS/CAPACITORS COULD ENHANCE THE MODULATION EFFICIENCY OVER A BROAD FREQUENCY RANGE REMAINS AN OPEN QUESTION. THE FOLLOWING SUB-TASKS WILL BE CARRIED OUT:
SUB-TASK 1.1: DEVELOP A THEORETICAL MODEL FOR THE LIMITS OF RESONANT AND NON-RESONANT ELECTRIC FIELD ENHANCEMENT IN RF ELECTRODES FED BY AN ARBITRARY SOURCE IMPEDANCE. FIND IMPLICATIONS FOR ELECTRICALLY SMALL ANTENNAS AND HIGH-LEVEL CO-DESIGN RULES (E.G., OPTIMAL ELECTRODE CAPACITANCE-VPI*L TRADEOFF). 
SUB-TASK 1.2: THEORETICALLY INVESTIGATE NOVEL APPROACHES TO REALIZE BROADBAND ELECTRIC FIELD ENHANCEMENT IN ELECTRODES, SUCH AS THE USE OF EXTERNAL LUMPED INDUCTORS AND CAPACITORS TO SYNTHESIZE PHASE-MATCHED ARBITRARY NETWORKS OR ARTIFICIAL TRANSMISSION LINES THAT OPTIMIZE THE EO RESPONSE.
TASK 2: ELECTRODE CO-DESIGN FOR A GIVEN ANTENNA AND RING GEOMETRIES
FULL-WAVE SIMULATION SOFTWARE (ANSYS HFSS) WILL BE USED TO DESIGN ELECTRODES THAT MAXIMIZE THE EO MODULATION EFFICIENCY IN THIN FILM BARIUM TITANATE (TFBTO) RACETRACK RESONATORS, WITH VARIOUS PERIMETERS RANGING E.G., FROM 2MM TO 8MM. THE CALIFORNIA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY (CALTECH) IS STUDYING THE APPLICATION OF HIGH-Q ON-CHIP OPTICAL RESONATORS FOR APPLICATION TO SAGNAC GYROSCOPES IN PNT SYSTEMS. SUCH GYROCOPES COULD ENJOY THE ADVANTAGES OF INTEGRATION AND SCALABLE MANUFACTURING, AND WOULD OFFER RUGGED DESIGNS FOR OPERATION IN CHALLENGING ENVIRONMENTS. IN THIS PROGRAM, WE WILL COLLABORATE WITH OTHER TEAM MEMBERS TO EXECUTE THE PROGRAM OBJECTIVES AND DEVELOP AN ON-CHIP, HIGH-PERFORMANCE GYROSCOPE. SPECIFIC TASKS ARE AS FOLLOWS:

1.	GYROSCOPE RESONATOR DESIGN: WE WILL SIMULATE AND PROVIDE RESONATOR DESIGNS FOR APPLICATION AS RING-LASER GYROSCOPES. THIS DESIGN WORK WILL BE FOCUSED ON THE ULTRA-LOW-LOSS SILICON NITRIDE PLATFORM, AND THE RING-LASERS WILL USE THE STIMULATED BRILLOUIN PROCESS TO ACHIEVE ULTRA-LOW FREQUENCY NOISE FOR HIGH-SENSITIVITY ROTATION SENSING. DESIGN WORK WILL INCLUDE OPTIMIZATION OF Q FACTORS AND DESIGN OF EFFICIENT WAVEGUIDE COUPLERS TO FACILITATE PUMPING AND SIGNAL EXTRACTION.
2.	GYROSCOPE MEASUREMENTS AND ANALYSIS: WE WILL ADVISE AND ASSIST IN MEASUREMENTS AND CHARACTERIZATION OF RESONATORS AND RING LASER GYROSCOPES. WE WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN ANALYSIS AND INTERPRETATION OF DATA. IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT MULTIPLE DESIGN, MEASUREMENT AND INTERPRETATION CYCLES WILL BE NECESSARY TO OPTIMIZE DEVICES. RING LASER PUMPING THRESHOLD AND FREQUENCY NOISE WILL BE BASELINE MEASUREMENTS USED TO GUIDE GYROSCOPE PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION.
3.	GYROSCOPES BASED ON ULTRA-LOW-LOSS GERMANO-SILICATE RESONATORS: WE WILL EXPLORE A NOVEL GERMANO-SILICATE ON SILICON METHOD TO ACHIEVE ULTRA-HIGH-Q RESONATORS. THIS METHOD HAS ALREADY ACHIEVED RECORD-HIGH OPTICAL Q FACTORS IN THE VISIBLE AND NEAR VISIBLE BANDS, AND THEREBY OFFERS HIGHER POSSIBLE GYROSCOPE PERFORMANCE IN THESE BANDS. IT ALSO HAS A MUCH HIGHER POTENTIAL Q LIMIT IN THE TELECOM BANDS, THEREBY OFFERING THE POSSIBILITY OF BETTER GYROSCOPE PEFORMANCE COMPARED TO EXISTING INTEGRATED HIGH-Q PLATFORMS. DEVICES BASED ON THIS MATERIAL WILL BE OPTIMIZED FOR OPERATION AS RING-LASER GYROSCOPES. DESIGNS AND PROCESS IMPROVEMENTS FOR EVEN HIGHER OPTICAL Q FACTORS WILL BE INVESTIGATED. ALSO, THE POSSIBLE ADVANTAGES OF GYROSCOPE OPERATION IN THE NEAR VISIBLE BANDS (INCLUDING IMPROVED SAGNAC SIGNAL STRENGTH) WILL BE STUDIED. DESIGNS FOR EFFICIENT COUPLERS AND IMPROVED OPTICAL CLADDING WILL BE INVESTIGATED.
4.	DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH FINDINGS: CALTECH WILL PROVIDE ANALYSIS AND RECOMMENDATIONS TO ADVANCE THE STATE-OF-THE-ART FOR ON-CHIP SAGNAC GYROSCOPES. THIS TASK WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED BY DISSEMINATING OUR RESEARCH FINDINGS THROUGH PRESENTATIONS TO THE SPONSOR, TECHNICAL PRESENTATIONS AT CONFERENCES, AND JOURNAL PUBLICATIONS.
5.	MANAGEMENT: CALTECH WILL WORK IN COLLABORATION WITH UNM TO PERFORM A SUBSTANTIVE PORTION OF THE PROGRAMMATIC EFFORT ON AN AWARD. PROGRAM PROGRESS IS QUANTIFIED BY WRITTEN MONTHLY STATUS REPORTS AND QUARTERLY TECHNICAL STATUS REPORTS. WE WILL MEET WITH THE COSMIAC PROGRAM MANAGER AND RELEVANT RESEARCHERS BY ZOOM, AS POSSIBLE. CALTECH WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SAME REGULATORY AND COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS AS UNM.

DEVELOPING THE TAXONOMY WILL FIRST REQUIRE US TO CONSIDER ALL ASSETS PRESENT IN AN AL HARDWARE SYSTEM INCLUDING BOTH HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE LP, CONFIDENTIALITY OF SENSITIVE DATA, AND THE INTEGRITY AND AVAILABILITY OF THE AL SYSTEM. NEXT, WE WILL CONSIDER ATTACK SURFACES AND MAP ATTACK SURFACES TO VULNERABLE ASSETS TO GENERATE A TAXONOMY OF HARDWARE VULNERABILITIES IN AL SYSTEMS.
SUBTASK 1.2. AUTOMATED VULNERABILITY ASSESSMENT OF AL HARDWARE: WE PLAN TO DEVELOP A FRAMEWORK TO FACILITATE SECURITY-AWARE DESIGN OF AL ACCELERATORS, AS SHOWN IN FIGURE 2 AND 3. LN ORDER TO DO THIS, WE WILL FIRST USE FORMAL VERIFICATION TECHNIQUES TO CHECK FOR VULNERABILITIES IN AN AL MODULE.       WE       WILL      CHARACTERIZE
ACCELERATORS ACCORDING TO THEIR ARCHITECTURAL FEATURES AND CONSIDER THE WAYS THAT THOSE FEATURES CONTRIBUTE TO ASSET PROTECTION AND PROPAGATION, SIDE- CHANNEL EXPLOITATION, AND PHYSICAL ATTACKS. FOR EXAMPLE, A SYSTEM WHICH USES A GPU OR FPGA TO ACCELERATE INFERENCE MUST PROTECT MODEL WEIGHTS THAT ARE STORED IN EXTERNAL MEMORY, WHEREAS AN INTEGRATED COPROCESSOR MIGHT FEATURE HARD-WIRED MODEL PARAMETERS   WHICH   ARE   VULNERABLE  TO
INVASIVE IMAGING TECHNIQUES. ADDITIONALLY, WE PLAN TO DEVELOP METRICS TO QUANTIFY VULNERABILITIES IN AL ACCELERATORS. NEXT, WE WILL USE THE RESULTS OF OUR ANALYSIS TO DEVELOP RULES AND POLICIES AS WELL AS AUTOMATIC DETECTION MECHANISMS FOR ENSURING SECURITY, TRUST, AND INTEGRITY IN AL SYSTEMS. THESE RULES WILL ACCOUNT FOR DIFFERENCES IN POLICY REQUIRED FOR DIFFERENT TYPES OF ACCELERATORS. LN CONTRAST TO EXISTING AL PROTECTION METHODS, WHICH FOCUS ON THE DETECTION OF ADVERSARIAL INPUTS, OUR RULES AND POLICIES WILL FOCUS ON THE PROTECTION OF AL ACCELERATOR HARDWARE. MORE SPECIFICALLY, THE RULES AND POLICIES WILL BE DIVIDED INTO THREE CATEGORIES: 1) RESILIENCE AGAINST SIDE-CHANNEL ATTACKS THAT ATTEMPT TO RECOVER THE AL MODEL, 2) ACCELERATOR ARCHITECTURES THAT ARE RESILIENT AGAINST ATTEMPTS TO FORCE MISCLASSIFICATION, AND 3) AL ACCELERATOR STRUCTURES THAT COUNTER PHYSICAL PROBING ATTACKS.
SUBTASK 2.1 EXPERIMENTS AND EVALUATION OF VULNERABILITIES IN ACCELERATORS: WE PLAN TO START OUR EVALUATION OF HARDWARE VULNERABILITIES IN AL HARDWARE BY EXAMINING THE CASE OF AN EDGE AL PLATFORM WITH AN FPGA ACCELERATOR. FPGAS USUALLY REQUIRE LESS ENERGY THAN GPUS AND ARE RECONFIGURABLE, WHICH ALLOWS THEM TO IMPLEMENT ACCELERATORS TAILORED TO SPECIFIC NETWORK ARCHITECTURES. AND TO BE UPDATED AS THE STATE-OF-THE-ART IN AL RESEARCH EVOLVES. MAJOR FPGA VENDORS AND RESEARCHERS HAVE RELEASED TOOLCHAINS FOR QUICKLY IMPLEMENTING CUSTOM HARDWARE ACCELERATORS, PRUNING AND QUANTIZING MODELS, AND GENERATING ACCELERATOR BINARIES. EVALUATING AN FPGA WILL GIVE US OPPORTUNITIES TO EXPERIMENT WITH MULTIPLE VARIATIONS OF DIFFERENT ACCELERATOR HARDWARE AND IDENTIFY MAJOR CHARACTERISTICS (LIKE IDENTIFYING ACCESS WAYS TO AL ASSETS OR WAYS TO CAUSE MISCLASSIFICATION) THAT CONTRIBUTE TO THE ACCELERATOR'S SECURITY.
SUBTASK 3.2 BACKSIDE PROTECTION IN AL HARDWARE: VARIOUS HARDWARE PROTECTIONS, SUCH AS PROTECTIVE MESHES, SENSORS, AND SHIELDS, FOR INVASIVE ATTACKS ON THE FRONT SIDE OF INTEGRATED CIRCUITS. HOWEVER, THE BACKSIDE OF THESE LCS, WHICH IS TYPICALLY EASY TO ACCESS BECAUSE MANY MANUFACTURERS HAVE CONVERTED TO
A "FLIP CHIP" PACKAGING STYLE, IS NOT WELL-PROTECTED. ATTACKS ON THE BACKSIDE OF LCS MAY BE PERFORMED USING TOOLS SUCH AS FLB (FOCUSED LON BEAM) OR PHOTON-EMISSION. THIS COULD ALLOW ATTACKERS TO READ MODEL PARAMETERS, REVERSE-ENGINEER THE ACCELERATOR, OR INJECT FAULTS DURING INFERENCE TO CAUSE MISCLASSIFICATION  ATTACKS.  LN THE
CONTEXT OF EXPERIMENTS ON FPGAS, IT IS ALSO POSSIBLE TO USE BACKSIDE PROTECTION TO DEFEAT BITSTREAM ENCRYPTION AND AUTHENTICATION BY READING KEYS FROM BATTERY-BACKED RAM.

OUR LONG‐TERM VISION IS TO UNDERSTAND THE FUNDAMENTAL LIMITS OF HOW INFORMATION CAN BE USED TO ACHIEVE ASSURED AUTONOMY. TO MEET THE AFOREMENTIONED CHALLENGES, EFFORTS IN THIS COE WILL FOCUS ON RESEARCH DIRECTIONS THAT CENTER ON THE AVAILABILITY, INTEGRITY, AND EFFICIENT USE OF INFORMATION. A CENTRAL ELEMENT OF AUTONOMY IS THE ABILITY TO MAKE DECISIONS BASED ON AVAILABLE INFORMATION THAT HAS SOME LEVEL OF INTEGRITY. EFFORTS IN RESEARCH THRUST 1 (RT1) WILL EXAMINE FUNDAMENTAL CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH NONSMOOTH, INTERMITTENT, AND/OR ASYNCHRONOUS SENSOR/STATE/ACTUATOR INFORMATION AND METHODS TO ASSURE OR PROVIDE ROBUSTNESS AGAINST ADVERSARIAL EFFORTS TO DISRUPT, DENY, OR CORRUPT THE INFORMATION. BASED ON LOCALLY SENSED OR COMMUNICATED INFORMATION, AGENTS MAY ADJUST THE MISSION PLAN (E.G., IDENTIFYING A NEARBY ADVERSARY AND SWITCHING FROM A PATROL MODE TO A PURSUIT MODE). THAT IS, EACH AGENT IN A NETWORK WILL MAKE ONBOARD DECISIONS TO ENGAGE IN DIFFERENT BEHAVIORS, AND THE TIMING AND TRIGGER FOR EACH SWITCH WILL BE INFORMED BY DATA AN AGENT GATHERS ITSELF AND DATA IT RECEIVES FROM OTHER AGENTS IN THE NETWORK, ALL OF THEM LIKELY AT DIFFERENT TIME INSTANCES. TASKS
THE MISSOURI S&T EFFORT WILL FOCUS ON DENSIFICATION OF ZRB2-BASED CERAMIC COMPOSITIONS AND CHARACTERIZATION OF POWDERS, GREEN BODIES, AND DENSE CERAMICS. ALL TASKS WILL BE ACTIVE THROUGHOUT EACH OF THE THREE PROJECT YEARS.
TASK 1: CHARACTERIZATION
THE CHARACTERIZATION EFFORT WILL INCLUDE ANALYSIS OF STARTING POWDERS FOR SIZE, SHAPE, AND SIZE DISTRIBUTION ALONG WITH OXYGEN CONTENT AND LEVELS OF IMPURITIES INCLUDING FE, W, AND C. CHARACTERIZATION OF GREEN BODIES WILL DETERMINE THE UNIFORMITY OF GREEN DENSITY ALONG WITH THE SIZE, SHAPE, AND DISTRIBUTION OF PORES OR OTHER DEFECTS. FINAL CERAMICS WILL BE CHARACTERIZED TO DETERMINE RELATIVE DENSITY, THE AMOUNT OF POROSITY, AND THE SIZE OF PORES. IN ADDITION, FINAL LEVELS OF OXYGEN AND IMPURITIES WILL ALSO BE DETERMINED.
TASK 2: DENSIFICATION
DENSIFICATION BEHAVIOR OF MATERIALS WILL BE STUDIED USING THREE METHODS. INITIAL SINTERING STUDIES WILL BE CONDUCTED USING SPARK PLASMA SINTERING, WHICH ALLOWS FOR IN-SITU MONITORING OF THE TEMPERATURE FOR ONSET OF DENSIFICATION AND DENSIFICATION RATES AS A FUNCTION OF TEMPERATURE. THE INITIAL INFORMATION WILL BE USED FOR A STATISTICAL DESIGN OF EXPERIMENTS APPROACH TO EVALUATE THE EFFECTS OF PARTICLE SIZE, IMPURITY LEVELS, AND ADDITIVE CONTENTS ON DENSIFICATION BEHAVIOR. THE COMBINATION OF INITIAL SCREENING AND THE DESIGN OF EXPERIMENTS WILL RAPIDLY SCREEN THE LARGE PROCESS PARAMETER SPACE TO IDENTIFY SIGNIFICANT PARAMETERS. THE FINAL PART OF THE DENSIFICATION STUDY WILL BE TO DESIGN PRESSURELESS SINTERING METHODOLOGIES BASED ON THE INFORMATION FROM THE FIRST TWO STAGES TO ENABLE TRANSITION OF THE TECHNOLOGY TO A MANUFACTURING ENVIRONMENT.
TASK 3: MECHANICAL AND THERMAL PROPERTY TESTING
MECHANICAL AND THERMAL PROPERTIES WILL BE ANALYZED AT ROOM AND ELEVATED TEMPERATURES. THE MECHANICAL PROPERTIES OF INTEREST ARE STRENGTH AND FRACTURE TOUGHNESS. THERMAL PROPERTIES TO BE MEASURED INCLUDE THERMAL DIFFUSIVITY, HEAT CAPACITY, AND THERMAL EXPANSION COEFFICIENT, WHICH WILL ENABLE CALCULATION OF THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY.

STANDARD ULTRA-HIGH TEMPERATURE CERAMIC (UHTC) MANUFACTURING RESULTS IN COMPONENTS WITH LARGE DIFFERENCES IN PROPERTIES DUE TO VARIABILITY IN MICROSTRUCTURAL ÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã…Â€ŒCRITICAL FLAWÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¯Â¿Â½ DISTRIBUTIONS. CRITICAL FLAWS CAN BE ANY IRREGULARITY IN A COMPONENT, SUCH AS A SECONDARY PHASE, INCLUSION, CRACKS, PORES ETC. THIS IS PROBLEMATIC WHEN DESIGNING REPRODUCIBLE UHTC COMPONENTS FOR MACH 6 HYPERSONIC APPLICATIONS. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO BUILD PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTION FUNCTIONS (PDF) FOR PROCESS-STRUCTURE-PROPERTY (PSP) PARAMETERS AND LINK THEM AT EACH STAGE OF UHTC PROCESSING IN A WAY THAT ALLOWS FOR UNCERTAINTY PROPAGATION. THIS METHODOLOGY HAS NOT BEEN PERFORMED IN THE PAST DUE TO THE COMPLEX INTERRELATIONS OF UHTC PSP PARAMETERS THAT NEED TO BE DECONVOLVED. THUS, MULTI-FIDELITY PSP DATABASE DEVELOPMENT AND EFFECTIVE INTEGRATED COMPUTATIONAL MATERIALS ENGINEERING (ICME) COMBINED WITH STATISTICAL MODELING IS KEY TO MINIMIZE UNCERTAINTY DURING UHTC MANUFACTURING. THIS APPROACH WILL CONSIST OF THREE KEY INTEGRATED THRUSTS: THRUST I: MANUFACTURING AND RAPID MATERIALS CHARACTERIZATION: TO POPULATE A MULTI-FIDELITY PSP DATABASE USING A COMBINATION OF LOWER-FIDELITY IN-LAB EXPERIMENTS AND MODELING ALONG WITH HIGHER-FIDELITY SYNCHROTRON 3-D MICROSTRUCTURAL CHARACTERIZATION EXPERIMENTS. THRUST II: UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION: TO DEVELOP A PSP-ICME DATABASE IN TANDEM WITH MULTI-FIDELITY STATISTICAL MODELING USING A BAYESIAN NEURAL NETWORK APPROACH. THRUST III: VALIDATION OF THE MULTI-FIDELITY MODEL: TO VERIFY THAT THE STATISTICAL MODEL CAN REDUCE UNCERTAINTY IN UHTC MANUFACTURING IN TERMS OF PROPERTIES AND MICROSTRUCTURAL FLAWS. THE DENSIFICATION OF ZRB2 WILL BE USED AS A MODEL SYSTEM FOR THIS METHODOLOGY AS IT IS A PRIME CANDIDATE FOR CERAMIC MATRIX MATERIALS IN HYPERSONIC-READY CERAMIC MATRIX COMPOSITES (CMCS). THIS WORK WILL BE COMPLETED IN COLLABORATION WITH AIR FORCE RESEARCH LABORATORY (AFRL) IN DAYTON OHIO WITH THE GOAL OF ESTABLISHING STUDENT-PIPELINES TRAINED IN UHTC MANUFACTURING, MULTI-FIDELITY MATERIALS CHARACTERIZATION AND MODELING, AND UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION.

THE FOCUS OF THE MODELING EFFORT WILL BE THE DEVELOPMENT OF FAST, ROBUST, AND ACCURATE PREDICTION OF FLUID PROPERTIES AND MIXING. THE PROPOSED MODEL WILL LEVERAGE A MULTI-FLUIDÃƑÂ€ŠÃ‚Â­MIXING APPROACH THAT ALLOWS DEDICATED EQUATIONS OF STATE FOR EACH SPECIES. STATUS OF A MORAL AGENT, THAT IS, AN ACTOR THAT HAS CERTAIN GENERAL CAPACITIES AND ABILITY FOR ACTION UPON
ITS ENVIRONMENT, COUPLED WITH THE CAPACITY FOR MORALLY RELEVANT ACTION. ESTABLISHING WHEN, HOW, AND
WHY ROBOTS ARE MORAL AGENTS IS KEY FOR ADVANCING HUMAN-ROBOT INTERACTION (HRI), IN PART DUE TO THE
MULTI-FACETED, MULTI-DISCIPLINARY IMPLICATIONS OF SAID AGENCY. FOR INSTANCE, WHETHER OR NOT A ROBOT
IS CONSIDERED A MORAL AGENT HAS SIGNIFICANT IMPLICATIONS FOR HOW RESEARCHERS, DESIGNERS, AND USERS
CAN, SHOULD, AND DO MAKES SENSE OF ROBOTS AND WHETHER THEIR AGENCY IN TURN TRIGGERS OTHER SOCIAL
AND MORAL COGNITIVE AND BEHAVIORAL PROCESSES IN OTHERS. ROBOTIC MORAL AGENCY ALSO HAS SIGNIFICANT
IMPLICATIONS FOR HOW PEOPLE SHOULD AND DO HOLD ROBOTS MORALLY RESPONSIBLE, ASCRIBE BLAME TO
THEM, DEVELOP TRUST IN THEIR ACTIONS, AND DETERMINE WHEN THESE ROBOTS WIELD MORAL INFLUENCE.
THUS, BECAUSE OF THE CRITICAL SIGNIFICANCE OF ROBOTIC MORAL AGENCY, RESEARCHERS FROM SEVERAL DISCIPLINES HAVE STARTED TO INVESTIGATE HOW WE CAN DETERMINE WHETHER AND TO WHAT EXTENT ROBOTS CAN
BE DETERMINED TO BE MORAL AGENTS. FOR EXAMPLE, IN THE PSYCHOLOGY LITERATURE, RESEARCHERS HAVE
DEVELOPED MEASURES INTENDED TO CAPTURE HUMAN PERCEPTIONS OF MORAL AGENCY, THAT IS THE DEGREE TO
WHICH OBSERVERS PERCEIVE ROBOTS TO BE MORAL AGENTS. HOWEVER, THERE ARE SEVERAL PSYCHOLOGICAL AND
PHILOSOPHICAL CHALLENGES TO THE CONSTRUCTION OF THESE MEASURES, INCLUDING CONFLATING GOOD MORAL
COMPETENCE (E.G., OPERATING IN A WAY THAT IS MORALLY GOOD) WITH MORAL AGENCY, WHERE SIMPLY BEING
A MORAL ACTOR DOES NOT NECESSITATE THAT THE ACTOR IS A GOOD MORAL ACTOR.
FURTHER AND MORE FUNDAMENTALLY, THE COMMON APPROACH TAKEN IN THE EXISTING LITERATURE LIMITS
ROBOT MORAL AGENCY TO A PURELY PSYCHOLOGICAL CONSTRUCT RATHER THAN AN ONOTOLOGICAL STATE OF BEING. ALTHOUGH THIS DISTINCTION IS NUANCED, IT IS A CRITICAL ONE TO MAKE. FRAMING MORAL AGENCY AS
A PURELY PSYCHOLOGICAL CONSTRUCT WOULD IMPLY THAT HUMANS HAVE AN INTUITIVE UNDERSTANDING AND
MENTAL CONCEPTUALIZATION OF THE DEGREE TO WHICH A ROBOT OR OTHER AUTONOMOUS AGENT IS A MORAL
AGENT. CHANGES IN AND FEATURES OF ROBOT DESIGNS AND BEHAVIORS WOULD LIKELY INFLUENCE THE DEGREE
TO WHICH SUCH AGENCY IS ASCRIBED TO THE ROBOT FROM THE HUMAN MIND. AN ONTOLOGICAL FRAMING, ON
THE OTHER HAND, WOULD SUGGEST THAT (MOST) HUMANS DO NOT HAVE AN INTUITIVE UNDERSTANDING OF THE
PHILOSOPHICAL CONCEPT OF ROBOT MORAL AGENCY. TO ILLUSTRATE, ALTHOUGH ROBOT DESIGN INFLUENCES PERCEPTIONS OF THE CONSTITUENT PSYCHOLOGICAL CONSTRUCTS OF MORAL AGENCY, LIKE AUTONOMY AND ADAPTABILITY,
THESE WOULD NEED TO BE LOGICALLY COMBINED TO PRODUCE ARGUMENTS IN FAVOR FOR OR AGAINST ANY GIVEN
ROBOTÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¢Â€ŽÂ¢S ONTOLOGICAL STATUS AS A MORAL AGENT BY ANY GIVEN HUMAN. THAT IS TO SAY, (1) JUST BECAUSE
AN ARGUMENT FOR AGENCY DEPENDS ON HUMAN PERCEPTIONS OF THE BUILDING BLOCKS OF AGENCY, IT DOES
NOT GUARANTEE THAT HUMANS DIRECTLY PERCEIVE ROBOT MORAL AGENCY; AND (2) A QUANTIFICATION OF ROBOT
MORAL AGENCY REQUIRES SUBSTANTIALLY MORE CAREFUL ASSESSMENT OF THE ANTECEDENTS OF AGENCY, AS WELL
AS INFORMED APPROACHES FOR HOW EVIDENCE FOR THOSE ANTECEDENTS SHOULD BE LOGICALLY COMBINED TO
INFER WHETHER A ROBOT IS INDEED A MORAL AGENT.
TO ADDRESS THE CURRENT DEFICIENCY IN MORAL AGENCY CONCEPTUALIZATION AND MEASUREMENT, WE
PROPOSE TO DRAW UPON FIRST PRINCIPLES OF ROBOTIC MORAL AGENCY AS AN ONTOLOGICAL CATEGORY GROUNDED
IN PHILOSOPHY, AND SUPPORTED BY TECHNIQUES IN EXPERIMENTAL PSYCHOLOGY AND COGNITIVE SCIENCE.

full_descriptions: (DEPSCOR) INCOMMENSURATE MULTI-WALLED NANOTUBES: ELECTRONIC AND MECHANICAL PROPERTIES
(DEPSCOR-RC FY23) INCOMMENSURATE MULTI-WALLED NANOTUBES: ELECTRONIC AND MECHANICAL PROPERTIES

CARBON NANOTUBES HOLD STRONG PROMISE FOR MILITARY AND COMMERCIAL APPLICATIONS INCLUDING CLASSICAL COMPUTING, QUANTUM
COMPUTING, NANOSENSORS, AND OTHER ELECTRONIC DEVICES. DEVICE FABRICATION RELIES HEAVILY ON THE ABILITY TO TUNE MULTIPLE
PARAMETERS OF THE MATERIALS TO OBTAIN THE DESIRED TRANSPORT PROPERTIES. CARBON NANOTUBES CAN BE TUNED BY CHOICE OF
HELICAL WRAPPING, TWISTS, BENDING, AND MULTI-WALL LAYERING. MANY OF THESE FEATURES CAN MAKE THE SYSTEM INCOMMENSURATE,
OR NOT PERIODIC. THIS POSES A CHALLENGE AS TYPICALLY ELECTRONIC MODELS OF CARBON NANOTUBES REQUIRE PERIODICITY.
THE PROPOSED 3-YEAR-RESEARCH WOULD DEVELOP MODELS, COMPUTATIONAL TO

CARBON NANOTUBES HOLD STRONG PROMISE FOR MILITARY AND COMMERCIAL APPLICATIONS INCLUDING CLASSICAL COMPUTING, QUANTUM
COMPUTING, NANOSENSORS, AND OTHER ELECTRONIC DEVICES. DEVICE FABRICATION RELIES HEAVILY ON THE ABILITY TO TUNE MULTIPLE
PARAMETERS OF THE MATERIALS TO OBTAIN THE DESIRED TRANSPORT PROPERTIES. CARBON NANOTUBES CAN BE TUNED BY CHOICE OF
HELICAL WRAPPING, TWISTS, BENDING, AND MULTI-WALL LAYERING. MANY OF THESE FEATURES CAN MAKE THE SYSTEM INCOMMENSURATE,
OR NOT PERIODIC. THIS POSES A CHALLENGE AS TYPICALLY ELECTRONIC MODELS OF CARBON NANOTUBES REQUIRE PERIODICITY.
THE PROPOSED 3-YEAR-RESEARCH WOULD DEVELOP MODELS, COMPUTATIONAL TOOLS, AND NUMERICAL ANALYSIS TO STUDY THE ELECTRONIC
AND MECHANICAL PROPERTIES OF THE INCOMMENSURATE SYSTEMS. THE WORK WOULD ADAPT TOOLS AND METHODOLOGY FROM THE
INCOMMENSURATE LAYERED TWO-DIMENSIONAL MATERIALS LITERATURE, WHICH THE PI HAS WORKED WITH EXTENSIVELY. FOR ELECTRONIC
COMPUTATIONS, MOMENTUM SPACE APPROACHES, SIMILAR TO THE FAMOUS BISTRITZER-MACDONALD MODEL FOR TWISTED
BILAYER GRAPHENE, WILL BE INCORPORATED INTO THE CARBON NANOTUBE SYSTEMS USING TIGHT-BINDING MODELS. FOR MECHANICAL
DEFORMATION, WE WILL CREATE A CONTINUUM MODEL INFORMED BY QUANTUM MECHANICAL DATA DERIVED USING THE ATOMIC CLUSTER
EXPANSION MACHINE LEARNING AND LOCAL PERIODIC APPROXIMATIONS INFORMED BY DENSITY FUNCTIONAL THEORY DATA. THE
PROPOSAL COLLABORATOR WILL BRING HIS EXPERTISE ON CONTINUUM MODELING TO COLLABORATE ON THE MECHANICAL MODELING AND
COMPUTATION. THE PROPOSED WORK WOULD INCLUDE THE SUPPORT OF A GRADUATE STUDENT, AND SUPPORT THE MATERIAL SCIENCE FOCUS
IN THE MATHEMATICS DEPARTMENT AT LOUISIANA STATE UNIVERSITY. THE EXPECTED OUTCOME OF THE RESEARCH IS DIVIDED INTO TWO
PRINCIPLE COMPONENTS. FIRSTLY, WE WILL DEVELOP ALGORITHMS TO COMPUTE ELECTRONIC OBSERVABLES SUCH AS THE DENSITY OF STATES
AND TRANSPORT PROPERTIES FOR SINGLE-WALLED CURVED NANOTUBES AND MULTI-WALLED INCOMMENSURATE NANOTUBES. SECONDLY, WE
WILL DEVELOP NON-LINEAR PDE MODELS FOR PREDICTING NANOTUBE DISPLACEMENT UNDER VARIOUS BOUNDARY CONDITIONS AND THE
MECHANICAL RELAXATION PATTERN OF DOUBLE-WALLED INCOMMENSURATE CARBON NANOTUBES. THE DATA FROM THESE MODELS WE WILL
INCORPORATE INTO THE ELECTRONIC STRUCTURE METHODS. THE MODEL SEPARATION BETWEEN MECHANIC AND ELECTRONIC EFFECTS IS
JUSTIFIED VIA THE BORN-OPPENHEIMER APPROXIMATION, WHICH STATES THAT MECHANICAL AND ELECTRONIC EFFECTS ARE ON SIGNIFICANTLY
DIFFERENT TIME SCALES. HENCE MECHANICAL EFFECTS ARE SOLVED AND MODELED SEPARATELY, AND THEN THE RESULT INCORPORATED INTO
THE ELECTRONIC MODEL.

OBJECTIVE: THE GOAL OF THIS TASK IS TO DEVELOP THE METHODOLOGY TO GENERATE PHYSICAL PERTURBATIONS THAT ARE DIFFERENTIABLE. THESE PERTURBATIONS ARE NEEDED TO ACHIEVE THE ADVERSARIAL TRAINING OF TASK 1. FURTHER, THIS TASK AIMS TO ASSOCIATE EACH PHYSICAL PERTURBATION WITH A COST FUNCTION TO INCORPORATE WITHIN THE TASK 1.

TASK 3: ROBUST AUDIO CLASSIFICATION
OBJECTIVE: THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS TASK IS TO DEVELOP ROBUST AUDIO CLASSIFICATION, FOCUSING ON BIOMETRIC BASED AUTHENTICATION. THIS TASKS INVOLVES A SYSTEMATIC STUDY OF THE ADVERSARIAL ATTACKS ON AUDIO-BASED AUTHENTICATION. SIMILAR TO THE IMAGE CASE, THIS TASK MODELS THE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINTS FOR THE AUDIO SAMPLES TO EXTRACT ROBUST FEATURES WHICH ENABLE THE DESIGN OF ROBUST CLASSIFIERS.
PRIMARY ORGANIZATION: UNIVERSITY OF TORONTO
SUBTASK 3.1: TAXONOMIZING THE SPACE OF AUDIO ADVERSARIES THIS SUBTASK WILL PRODUCE A FINE-GRAINED TAXONOMY OF ADVERSARIES THAT CAPTURES BOTH POSSIBLE ADVERSARIAL GOALS AS WELL AS CAPABILITIES NEEDED TO MOUNT ATTACKS. THIS TAXONOMY INFORMS THE DESIGN OF PRINCIPLED DEFENSES THROUGH THE ENFORCEMENT OF PHYSICAL CONSTRAINTS. THE DETAILED SUBTASKS INCLUDE:
3.1.1: DEVELOP BASIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE ADVERSARIES IN THE AUDIO SPACE
3.1.2: SYSTEMATIZE BLACK-BOX ATTACKS ON AUDIO CLASSIFIERS WITH PARTIAL INFORMATION
3.1.3: SYSTEMATIZE BLACK-BOX ATTACKS ON AUDIO CLASSIFIERS THROUGH MODEL EXTRACTION
SUBTASK 3.2: MODELING PHYSICAL CONSTRAINTS FOR SEQUENTIAL AUDIO SAMPLES THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS SUBTASK TO MODEL THE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINTS IN THE AUDIO CASE. WE CONSIDER THREE TYPES OF INVARIANTS: ENVIRONMENT NOISE AND SENSOR ARTIFACTS, TEMPORAL DEPENDENCY AMONG THE AUDIO SAMPLES, AND THE MULTI-AUDIO STREAMS. THE SUBTASKS ARE AS FOLLOWS:
3.2.1: MODEL PHYSICAL EFFECTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL NOISE AND SENSOR ARTIFACTS
3.2.2: DEVELOP INVARIANTS FROM MULTI-SOURCE AUDIO
SUBTASK 3.3: ROBUST AUDIO CLASSIFICATION ARCHITECTURE THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS SUBTASK IS TO TRAIN STABLE ARCHITECTURES FOR ROBUST AUDIO CLASSIFICATION. THESE ARCHITECTURES ENFORCE THE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINTS DEVELOPED IN SUBTASK 3.2. BASE-STRUCTURE ENGINEERING DESIGN CONDUCT A PARAMETRIC DESIGN AND FEASIBILITY STUDY USING THE SEAHIVE SYSTEM BASED ON SITE CONDITIONS AND HYDRODYNAMIC INPUTS. RESEARCH AND DEVELOP SEAHIVE BASE-STRUCTURE VARIANTS CONSIDERING ENGINEERING CRITERIA SUCH AS STABILITY AND WAVE TRANSMISSION. REVIEW DESIGN ALTERNATIVES IN COLLABORATION WITH TA1, TA2, AND TA3 TEAMS AND DETERMINE ENHANCEMENTS TO INCREASE ENGINEERING PERFORMANCE (I.E., REDUCTION OF WAVE ENERGY TO MEET TARGET METRICS). PREPARE A TECHNICAL MEMORANDUM FOR THE PROPOSED SEAHIVE SYSTEM. PREPARE ENGINEERING PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS IN SUPPORT OF SEAHIVE DEPLOYMENT. SUPPORT PERMITTING, TECHNOECONOMIC ASSESSMENT TASKS, AND DEPLOYMENT IN RELATION WITH THE SEAHIVE SYSTEM.  DESKTOP DATA COLLECTION AND ALTERNATIVES ANALYSIS  THIS TASK INCLUDES COLLECTING DATA TO SUPPORT PERMITTING AND DESIGN OF THE PROJECT. PRIOR TO BEGINNING DATA COLLECTION, AECOM WILL COORDINATE WITH KNOWN PROJECT PARTNERS TO DEVELOP A PLAN TO CONDUCT A DESKTOP ANALYSIS FOR SITE CHARACTERIZATION. THE FIELD SURVEYS OF THE NEARSHORE DEPLOYMENT AREA WILL BE CONDUCTED BY OTHERS (E.G., IV&V TEAM).  SERVICES CONDUCTED UNDER THIS TASK SHALL INCLUDE A DESKTOP ANALYSIS OF READILY AVAILABLE ENVIRONMENTAL DATABASES AND MAPPING (E.G., NATIONAL WETLANDS INVENTORY, SUBMERGED AQUATIC VEGETATION, MANGROVE COMMUNITIES, CRITICAL HABITATS).  IN ADDITION, AECOM WILL CONDUCT AN ALTERNATIVES ANALYSIS. THIS TASK INCLUDES REVIEWING UP TO THREE DESIGN ALTERNATIONS PREPARED BY THE REEFS DESIGN TEAMS AND DETERMINING ENHANCEMENTS TO INCREASE ENGINEERING PERFORMANCE (I.E., REDUCTION OF WAVE ENERGY TO MEET DARPA TARGET METRICS). THE ALTERNATIVES ANALYSIS WILL ALSO BE USED TO SUPPORT PERMITTING TASKS.  AECOM WILL PREPARE A TECHNICAL MEMORANDUM FOR THE PROPOSED SHORELINE PROTECTION CONCEPT STRUCTURES. THE TECHNICAL MEMORANDUM WILL CONSIDER HOW EACH STRUCTURE/CONFIGURATION CONTRIBUTES TO WAVE ENERGY REDUCTION POTENTIAL (I.E., PROVIDING HYDRODYNAMIC MODELING SUPPORT, WITH HYDRODYNAMIC MODELING BEING CONDUCTED BY OTHERS) OR IMPACTS PROBABLE CONSTRUCTION COSTS. THE MEMORANDUM WILL MAKE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR HOW THE STRUCTURE MIGHT PERFORM WITH REGARDS TO REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS AND A RECOMMENDATION WILL BE GIVEN FOR PROCEEDING TO DETAILED DESIGN. A MINIMUM OF ONE CONCEPT-LEVEL EXHIBIT WILL BE PREPARED FOR EACH PROPOSED ALTERNATIVE STRUCTURE/CONFIGURATION. AECOM WILL WORK WITH PROJECT PARTNERS TO DETERMINE A RECOMMENDED ALTERNATIVE AND, PENDING PROJECT PARTNER APPROVAL, USE THE RECOMMENDED ALTERNATIVE IN COMPLETING OTHER AECOM TASKS. THE FIELD SITE CHANGED (FROM NAS KEY WEST TO ELLIOT KEY, FL) AND WE ARE RE-DOING A GREAT DEAL OF THE 2-D FIELD HYDRODYNAMIC MODELING (DOWNSCALING) TO ACCOUNT FOR THIS CHANGE. DOWNSCALING IS THE PROCESS OF TRANSFORMING AN OFFSHORE WAVE CLIMATE, GENERATED BY A LARGE, REGIONAL-SCALE COUPLED CLIMATE AND WAVE MODEL, INTO SHALLOW-WATER WAVES IN THE NEARSHORE. THIS PROCESS IS TIME CONSUMING (OFTEN 1-2 MONTHS) AS IT REQUIRES COLLECTING DATA FORM THE LARGE REGIONAL-SCALE MODEL, REGIONAL TO LOCAL-SCALE BATHYMETRY, DEVELOPING AND THEN RUNNING THE DOWNSCALING MODEL GRID TO TRANSFORM WAVES FOR A RANGE OF DIFFERENT OFFSHORE CONDITIONS.

WE ARE CONTINUING TO PROVIDE MUCH GREATER SUPPORT THAN ANTICIPATED TO THE DESIGN AND TESTING OF THE PROPOSED STRUCTURES INT EH FLUME AT THE US ARMY CORP ERDC TESTING FACILITY. ORIGINALLY, THE ROLE FOR THE UCSC TEAM WAS TO PROVIDE A SELECT FEW COMPUTATIONAL FLUID DYNAMICS (CFD) SIMULATIONS IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE PHYSICAL WAVE TANK TESTING OF THE ARTIFICIAL REEF STRUCTURES. OVER THE COURSE OF THIS PROJECT, IT BECAME CLEAR THAT THE CFD SIMULATIONS COULD ITERATE THROUGH STRUCTURE DESIGNS FASTER THAN WAS POSSIBLE WITH THE PHYSICAL EXPERIMENTS. AS A RESULT, OUR TEAM HAS SIMULATED ABOUT 200 INDIVIDUAL CFD.

THE PRESENT WORK AIMS TO DEVELOP EPIGENETIC MARKERS OF CORAL RESILIENCE. THESE MARKERS WILL BE IDENTIFIED BASED ON EXPERIMENTS INDUCING CORAL HARDENING EX-SITU (I.E., LABORATORY TANKS SUBJECT TO DIFFERENT THERMAL REGIMES) AND AT TEST BED STRUCTURES IN THE OCEAN (SIMULATING CONDITIONS OF THE DEPLOYED STRUCTURE IN THE PROJECT). ONCE IDENTIFIED, THESE MARKERS WILL BE USED TO IDENTIFY HARDENED COLONIES TO TRANSPLANT INTO THE EXPERIMENTAL STRUCTURE.

A. THE FIELD SITE CHANGED (FROM NAS KEY WEST TO ELLIOT KEY, FL) AND WE ARE RE-DOING A GREAT DEAD OF THE 2-D FIELD HYDRODYNAMIC MODELING (DOWNSCALING) TO ACCOUNT FOR THIS CHANGE. DOWNSCALING IS THE PROCESS OF TRANSFORMING AN OFFSHORE WAVE CLIMATE, GENERATED BY A LARGE, REGIONAL-SCALE COUPLED CLIMATE AND WAVE MODEL, INTO SHALLOW-WATER WAVES IN THE NEARSHORE. THIS PROCESS IS TIME CONSUMING (OFTEN 1-2 MONTHS) AS IT REQUIRES COLLECTING DATA FROM THE LARGE REGIONAL-SCALE MODEL, REGIONAL TO LOCAL-SCALE BATHYMETRY, DEVELOPING, AND THEN RUNNING THE DOWNSCALING MODEL GRID TO TRANSFORM WAVES FOR A RANGE OF DIFFERENCE OFFSHORE CONDITIONS.
