TITLE ÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¢Â‚¬Å“ IMPEDE: INHIBITING MOLDS WITH PROBIOTIC ENSEMBLES FROM DIVERSE ENVIRONMENTS.
1. SCOPE
BLACK MOLD AND ASSOCIATED FUNGAL CONTAMINATIONS POSE A LARGE RISK TO OPERATIONAL READINESS OF VARIOUS DOD ASSETS
AND MILITARY PERSONNEL. THE END PRODUCT OF THE IMPEDE PROJECT IS A FIELD-READY ROBUST MULTI-SPECIES MICROBIAL
CONSORTIA THAT CAN BE APPLIED TO VARIOUS DOD-RELEVANT SURFACES AND ENVIRONMENTS TO REPEL THE GROWTH OF BLACK
MOLD FOR MORE THAN 6 MONTHS. BY AMASSING TENS OF THOUSANDS STRAINS FROM DIVERSE ENVIRONMENTS AND
CHARACTERIZING AND MODELING MILLIONS OF INTER-SPECIES AND BACTERIA-FUNGAL INTERACTIONS, WE WILL ASSEMBLE A STABLE
AND RESILIENT CONSORTIUM OF MOLD-REPELLING PROBIOTIC STRAINS. IN GENERATING THIS ANTI-MOLD CONSORTIA, WE WILL
LEVERAGE NEXT-GENERATION TECHNOLOGIES IN HIGH-THROUGHPUT SYSTEMS MICROBIOLOGY, GENOMICS, AND QUANTITATIVE
MODELING THAT ARE UNIQUELY AVAILABLE TO OUR GROUP, INCLUDING ROBOTIC STRAIN ISOLATION, HIGH-THROUGHPUT INTERROGATION
OF MICROBIAL PHENOTYPE AND GENOMES, MACHINE-LEARNING MODELS OF POPULATION DYNAMICS, AND SCALABLE TESTBEDS
THAT REPLICATE FIELD CONDITIONS AND PERTURBATIONS. TECHNICAL AREA 1 WILL FOCUS ON DEVELOPING THE EXPERIMENTAL
TESTBEDS OF MOLD-CONTAMINATION IN DOD-RELEVANT SETTINGS, ISOLATING AND CHARACTERIZING MOLD-ASSOCIATED STRAINS,
AND MODELING POPULATION STABILITY AND DYNAMICS. TECHNICAL AREA 2 WILL FOCUS ON ASSEMBLING STRAINS INTO ROBUST
AND POTENT ANTI-MOLD CONSORTIA, MODELING THEIR BEHAVIORS UNDER LABORATORY AND IN-FIELD CONDITIONS AND
DISTURBANCES, GENETICALLY ENHANCING THE POTENCY OF THE CONSORTIA WITHOUT TRIGGERING ADDITIONAL REGULATORY
REQUIREMENTS OF GENETICALLY-MODIFIED MICROBES (GMM) FOR FIELD USE, AND FORMULATION INTO FIELD-READY SPRAYS OR
PAINTS. THE IMPEDE PROJECT WILL BE LED BY WORLD-CLASS RESEARCHERS AND EXPERIENCED PAST DARPA PERFORMERS
WITH KEY DOMAIN EXPERTISE IN MYCOLOGY AND MICROBIOLOGY, SYSTEMS AND SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY, COMPUTATIONAL AND
ECOLOGICAL MODELING, AND COATING AND POLYMER SCIENCE. THIS FOUR-YEAR TWO-PHASE PROJECT IS POISED TO MAKE KEY
BREAKTHROUGHS THAT WILL HAVE IMMEDIATE IMPACT ON NUMEROUS DOD APPLICATION AREAS WHERE MICROBIAL
AUGMENTATION AND PROTECTION CAN INCREASE PERFORMANCE AND LONGEVITY OF DOD ASSETS. THE TEAM WILL BE LED BY DR.
HARRIS WANG (PI) AT COLUMBIA UNIVERSITY AND WILL INCLUDING PERFORMERS AND EXPERTS FROM MIT (VOIGT), UWMADISON
(VENTURELLI) AND USM (KUEHN) IN ALL ESSENTIAL AREAS IN ENVIRONMENTAL MICROBIOLOGY AND MYCOLOGY,
QUANTITATIVE ECOLOGICAL MODELING, AND SYSTEMS AND SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY. FURTHERMORE, WE REQUEST PARTICIPATION BY
MEMBERS BELONGING TO AFRL (VARALJAY, BUHRMASTER) AND AFCEC (DILTZ) TO ENHANCE DOD RELEVANCE OF OUR OVERALL
EFFORT.
1.1. BACKGROUND
CONTAMINATION AND DEGRADATION OF DOD ASSETS DUE TO GROWTH OF MOLD IS A PERVASIVE CHALLENGE THAT CAN LEAD TO LOSS
OF FUNCTION AND HEALTH RISKS FOR SERVICE MEMBERS. WE PROPOSE TO CREATE PROTECTIVE BIOFILMS COMPOSED OF MIXED
MICROBIAL COMMUNITIES THAT PROTECT SURFACES AGAINST COLONIZATION BY SPECIES OF BLACK MOLD. WE WILL CATALOGUE
MICROBES THAT NATURALLY POPULATE MATERIAL SURFACES (SEATS, FLOORBOARDS, STRAPS) AND IDENTIFY CRITICAL SPATIAL AND
TEMPORAL STEPS OF BLACK MOLD COLONIZATION. USING THIS INFORMATION, WE WILL IDENTIFY INDIVIDUAL COMMUNITY
MEMBERS THAT HAVE THE CAPACITY TO INHIBIT MOLD FORMATION. THEIR NATURAL INHIBITORY FUNCTION WILL BE ENHANCED BY:
1) USING DATA-GUIDED SIMULATIONS AND MICROFLUIDICS TO IDENTIFY AND VALIDATE MINIMAL SUBSETS OF MICROBES THAT ARE
STABLE TO FLUCTUATIONS IN AUSTERE ENVIRONMENTS, AND 2) APPLYING TECHNIQUES FOR RAPID DISCOVERY OF ENHANCING
GENOME MODIFICATIONS THAT DO NOT REQUIRE REGULATORY APPROVAL AS A GENETICALLY-MODIFIED MICROBE (GMM) FOR FIELD
USE. THESE COMMUNITY PROBIOTICS WILL BE EVALUATED AS SPRAYS AND EMBEDDED IN MATERIALS USING A LABORATORY SYSTEM
THAT CAN ACCURATELY RECREATE FIELD CONDITIONS AND COLONIZATION DYNAMICS ON RELEVANT MATERIALS. THE APPLICATION
TECHNOLOGIES WILL BE DEVELOPED AND TESTED WITH EXPERT INPUT REGARDING MATERIAL COATINGS. WORKING WITH THE IV&V
TEAM(S), WE WILL DEMONSTRATE PHYSICAL REPULSION OF MOLD FORMATION ON DIFFERENT DOD-RELEVANT SURFACES FOR UP TO
6 MONTHS. THE DEVELOPMENT OF MICROBIAL PROTECTIVE BIOFILMS AGAINST BLACK MOLD FORMATION WILL IMPROVE SERVICE
LIFE OF ASSETS AND DECREASE RISK OF HEALTH COMPLICATIONS IN WARFIGHTERS.

KEVIN KUEHN, PHD IS A PROFESSOR IN THE SCHOOL OF BIOLOGICAL, ENVIRONMENTAL AND EARTH SCIENCES AT
THE UNIVERSITY OF SOUTHERN MISSISSIPPI. DR. KUEHN IS A FUNGAL ECOLOGIST WHO IS AN EXPERT IN
QUANTIFYING THE ROLE OF FUNGI IN BIOGEOCHEMICAL CYCLES AND THEIR POTENTIAL INTERACTIONS WITH OTHER
MICROBIAL GROUPS. HE WILL LEAD TESTBED EFFORTS TO ASSESS THE EFFICACY OF PROBIOTIC CONSORTIA TO
REPEL BLACK MOLD FORMATION ON DOD MATERIALS IN SIMULATED ENVIRONMENTS.

CYBER PROTECTION TEAMS (CPTS) DEFEND TACTICAL NETWORKS AGAINST ADAPTIVE AND PERSISTENT CYBER ADVERSARIES USING SECURITY ORCHESTRATION, AUTOMATION, AND RESPONSE (SOAR) SYSTEMS. THESE SYSTEMS HELP DETECT, PRIORITIZE, AND MITIGATE CYBER INCIDENTS AS PER THE VARIOUS PHASES OUTLINED IN THE SANS PICERL CYBERSECURITY FRAMEWORK [1]. AS OPERATIONAL ENVIRONMENTS BECOME MORE DYNAMIC AND ADVERSARIES INCREASINGLY LEVERAGE AUTOMATION AND AI, SOAR SYSTEMS ARE EVOLVING TOWARD AUTONOMOUS, MULTI-AGENT AI ARCHITECTURES [2, 3], WHERE SPECIALIZED AGENTS COORDINATE THREAT DETECTION, RESPONSE SELECTION, AND REMEDIATION ACTIONS.

WHILE THESE MULTI-AGENT AI-ENABLED SOAR SYSTEMS OFFER SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENTS IN SPEED, SCALABILITY, AND ADAPTABILITY, THEY ALSO INTRODUCE NEW RISKS. AUTONOMOUS AGENTS MAY PURSUE CONFLICTING OBJECTIVES, DEVELOP OPAQUE DECISION-MAKING PROCESSES, OR EXPLOIT GAPS IN OVERSIGHT, LEADING TO LOSS OF CONTROL, UNINTENDED SYSTEM BEHAVIOR, OR MISSION IMPACT. THESE SOAR SOLUTIONS LACK FORMAL ASSURANCE MECHANISMS THAT CAN GUARANTEE SAFE COORDINATION, EXPLAINABILITY, AND BOUNDED AGENT BEHAVIOR UNDER ADVERSARIAL CONDITIONS, INCLUDING AGAINST ADAPTIVE, LEARNING- ENABLED ATTACKERS.

IN MISSION-CRITICAL TACTICAL ENVIRONMENTS, MAINTAINING TRUST, HUMAN-ON-THE-LOOP (HOTL) AUTHORITY, AND OPERATIONAL INTEGRITY IS ESSENTIAL. ADDRESSING THESE GAPS REQUIRES NEW APPROACHES THAT ASSURE AI BEHAVIOR AND PREVENT LOSS OF CONTAINMENT WHILE PRESERVING THE AGILITY BENEFITS OF AUTONOMOUS CYBER DEFENSE AND REMAINING ROBUST TO ADVERSARIAL ATTACKS.

PROJECT GOALS:
THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP AN ASSURANCE AND CONTAINMENT FRAMEWORK FOR AI-ENABLED, MULTI-AGENT SOAR SYSTEMS SUPPORTING CPTS. THE AIM OF THE FRAMEWORK IS TO ENSURE THAT AUTONOMOUS SOAR AGENTS REMAIN SAFE, PREDICTABLE, EXPLAINABLE, AND HUMAN-GOVERNABLE, EVEN UNDER ADVERSARIAL CONDITIONS AND OPERATIONAL UNCERTAINTY. SPECIFICALLY, THIS RESEARCH PROJECT SEEKS TO: (I) PREVENT LOSS OF CONTROL AND UNSAFE EMERGENT BEHAVIORS IN HIERARCHICAL, MULTI-AGENT SOAR SYSTEMS, WHILE ENSURING AI ACTIONS REMAIN ALIGNED WITH MISSION INTENT AND OPERATOR AUTHORITY AND ENABLING ADAPTIVE AUTONOMY THAT IMPROVES RESPONSE TIME AND MISSION AGILITY WITHOUT SACRIFICING SAFETY OR TRANSPARENCY, AND (II) EVALUATE SYSTEM ROBUSTNESS AGAINST ADAPTIVE ADVERSARIES, INCLUDING THOSE EMPLOYING LEARNING-BASED ATTACK STRATEGIES.

PROJECT TASKS:
THE RESEARCH WILL BE ORGANIZED INTO TWO MAIN TASKS. EACH TASK WILL PRODUCE TANGIBLE ARTIFACTS THAT FEED SUBSEQUENT TASKS, REDUCING TECHNICAL RISK AND SUPPORTING INCREMENTAL TRANSITION.

TASK 1: FORMAL MODELING AND DESIGN-TIME ASSURANCE OF MULTI-AGENT AI SOAR SYSTEMS
TASK 2: ADVERSARIAL RED-TEAM EVALUATION OF MULTI-AGENT AI SOAR SYSTEMS

STATEMENT OF WORK:
WE PROPOSE A 24-MONTH PHASE I PROGRAM TO DEVELOP ACCELERATED MATERIAL TESTING METHODS AND DATA
REDUCTION PROTOCOLS (FA1 IN THE METALS BAA), TOGETHER WITH AN OPTIMAL DESIGN APPROACH TO
CONTINUOUSLY VARY MATERIAL PROPERTIES WITHIN AN ENGINEERING STRUCTURE (FA2 IN THE METALS BAA). IN AN
OPTIONAL PHASE II PROGRAM, WE WILL APPLY THESE TOOLS TO THE REDESIGN OF A STAGE-4 BLISK FOR A HONEYWELL
INTERNATIONAL 7000 SERIES AIRCRAFT ENGINE AND DEMONSTRATE A 100 O
C INCREASE IN USE TEMPERATURE AND 50%
REDUCTION OF A MATERIAL CRITICALITY INDEX. IN THE OPTIONAL PHASE III PROGRAM, THE BLISKS WITH CONTINUOUSLY
GRADED MATERIALS WILL BE FABRICATED AND EVALUATED IN SPIN-PIT TESTS. ALL TASKS TO BE PERFORMED UNDER THIS
PROGRAM CONSIST ONLY OF FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH.
TASK 1. DESIGN FRAMEWORK FOR CONTINUOUS MATERIAL OPTIMIZATION: THIS TASK ADDRESSES FOCUS AREA 2
(FA2). ITS OBJECTIVE IS TO CREATE A DESIGN OPTIMIZATION FRAMEWORK FOR CONTINUOUS MATERIAL PLACEMENT
WITHIN A GIVEN COMPONENT. THE MACHINE LEARNING (ML) BASED CONSTITUTIVE MODEL WITH COMPOSITION Ã¢Â‚¬Â€Œ
PROPERTY RELATIONSHIPS WILL FORM THE INPUT.
SUBTASK 1.1. SIMPLIFIED FRAMEWORK: THE OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP A SIMPLIFIED OPTIMIZATION FRAMEWORK
ENABLING USE OF A NONLINEAR ML ELASTIC CONSTITUTIVE MODEL IN THE OPTIMIZATION LOOP. A CONTINUOUS MATERIAL
SPACE WILL BE EMPLOYED WHERE THE CONSTITUTIVE PARAMETERS VARY WITH DESIGN VARIABLES (E.G., COMPOSITION)
THAT ALSO SERVE AS INPUT TO THE ML MODEL. ONE-WAY COUPLED THERMOMECHANICAL PHYSICS WITH A SINGLE LOAD
CASE WILL BE CONSIDERED. THE FORMULATION EXPLOITS THE ABILITY TO PREDICT DESIGN PERFORMANCE, AND COMPUTE
GRADIENTS OF THE OBJECTIVE AND CONSTRAINT FUNCTIONS EFFICIENTLY TO UPDATE THE DESIGN. THIS IS CRITICAL TO
ACHIEVE THE GOAL OF A CONTINUUM SOLUTION IN LESS THAN 12 HOURS ON AN ENGINEERING WORKSTATION.
INCREMENTALLY INCREASING THE LEVEL OF COMPLEXITY WILL FACILITATE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPROVEMENT OF THE
STRATEGY FOR CONTINUOUS MATERIAL DESIGN TO ACHIEVE THE GOAL OF A CONTINUUM SOLUTION IN LESS THAN 12 HOURS
ON AN ENGINEERING WORKSTATION. MILESTONE 7.1: DESIGN OPTIMIZATION CODE WITH ML MODEL INPUTS.
DELIVERABLE: REPORT AT END OF Q2 WITH THE DETAILS OF A SIMPLIFIED THERMOMECHANICAL MATERIAL OPTIMIZATION
PROBLEM AND DESIGN SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE.
SUBTASK 1.2. CONTINUOUS MATERIAL PARAMETERIZATION SCHEME: THE OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP APPROPRIATELY
SMOOTHED DESIGN OPTIMIZATION INPUTS. TO ENABLE CONTINUOUS MATERIAL OPTIMIZATION, THE WEIGHT-PERCENT OF
IMPORTANT, UNIQUELY IDENTIFYING CHEMICAL CONSTITUENTS WILL BE PARAMETERIZED IN ADDITION TO AN INDICATOR
VARIABLE ACCOUNTING FOR VARIOUS MANUFACTURING PROCESSES (E.G., HEAT TREATMENT). THESE PARAMETERS ALSO
SERVE AS INPUT TO THE ML MODELS OF TASK 6. MILESTONE 7.2: OPTIMIZATION TOOL FOR THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF
A SINGLE MATERIAL PROPERTY (E.G., MODULUS). DELIVERABLES: REPORTS AT END OF Q2 AND Q6 DESCRIBING THE
SINGLE PROPERTY OPTIMIZATION SCHEME AND DESIGN SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT PLAN.
SUBTASK 1.3. INTEGRATION AND VERIFICATION USING A SIMPLIFIED PROBLEM: THE OBJECTIVE IS TO IMPLEMENT
SIMPLIFYING ASSUMPTIONS TO MEET THE 12-HOUR DESIGN TIME CRITERION ON AN ENGINEERING WORKSTATION.
SIMPLIFICATIONS INCLUDE: (I) USE OF SIMPLE STEADY-STATE CONDUCTIVE HEAT TRANSFER ANALYSIS FOR DETERMINING
THE TEMPERATURE DISTRIBUTION THROUGHOUT THE SOLID; (II) WEIGHTED SUMMATION OF MATERIAL CONSTITUENT MASS
WITH WEIGHTS CHOSEN IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE SELECTED MATERIAL CRITICALITY INDEX; (III) AN APPROPRIATE STRESS
MEASURE CONSTRAINED TO REMAIN BELOW THE YIELD STRENGTH DURING NORMAL OPERATION AND (IV) OXIDATION
THICKNESS OF EACH SURFACE ELEMENT WILL BE KINETIC MODEL APPROXIMATED AND CONSTRAINED TO REMAIN BELOW AN
ACCEPTABLE LEVEL. MILESTONE 7.3: OPTIMAL BLISK DESIGN TOOL FOR SPATIAL GRADIENTS OF MULTIPLE MATERIAL
PROPERTIES. DELIVERABLE: A REPORT AND SOFTWARE FOR MULTI-PROPERTY OPTIMIZATION WITHIN A COMPONENT WITH
DEMONSTRATED CONVERGENCE TIME OF UNDER 12 HOURS.

R. TWO PARALLEL APPROACHES WILL BE CONDUCTED. ONE POSES A GENERAL ELASTIC-VISCOPLASTIC MULTIAXIAL CONSTITUTIVE MODEL WHOSE UNKNOWN COEFFICIENTS WILL BE ESTABLISHED FROM DATA WHILE THE SECOND IS BASED UPON A NEW (BAYESIAN) RECURRENT NEURAL NETWORK SCHEME. SUBTASK. PURELY DATA-DRIVEN CONSTITUTIVE LAW MODEL FOR KNOWN STRESS-STRAIN DATA: USING THE DATA FROM A FINITE ELEMENT SIMULATION OF THE TEST SELECTED IN TASK 6.1 CONDUCTED FOR A KNOWN CONSTITUTIVE LAW, WE WILL TRAIN A RECURRENT NEURAL NETWORK TO LEARN THE PATH-DEPENDENT CONSTITUTIVE BEHAVIOR OF THE MATERIAL FROM THE SINGLE SPECIMEN TEST. NOTE THAT IN THIS TASK, THE CONSTITUTIVE LAW OF THE MATERIAL IS ALREADY KNOWN, BUT THE DATA-DRIVEN MODEL IS TRAINED WITHOUT THIS KNOWLEDGE. THIS INTERMEDIATE STEP IS DEEMED NECESSARY TO ENSURE THE FEASIBILITY OF THE PROPOSED APPROACH. WE HIGHLIGHT THAT THIS TASK IS AKIN TO WHAT CO-PI BESSA AND CO-WORKERS DID WHEN THEY FIRST DEMONSTRATED THAT RECURRENT NEURAL NETWORKS COULD LEARN THE PLASTICITY CONSTITUTIVE BEHAVIOR OF HETEROGENEOUS REPRESENTATIVE VOLUME ELEMENTS OF MATERIALS. HOWEVER, UNLIKE WHAT WAS DEMONSTRATED THEN, IN THIS CASE THE STRAIN SPACE IS NOT SAMPLED EXHAUSTIVELY. INSTEAD, IT IS LIKELY TO HAVE VAST REGIONS WITHOUT STRAIN DATA. RESEARCH. INVESTMENTS FOR NEW STIMULUS DEVELOPMENT (E.G., VIDEO RECORDINGS),

THE MICHIGAN CONTRIBUTION TO THIS BRC INCLUDES COMPUTATIONS (THRUST 1, JOHNSEN) AND EXPERIMENTS (THRUST 2, XU). AS PART OF THRUST 1 (COMPUTATIONAL/THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK FOR CAVITATION SIMULATIONS IN SOFT MATERIALS), THE JOHNSEN GROUP WILL DEVELOP A MODEL FOR SPHERICAL BUBBLE DYNAMICS IN GENERAL VISCOELASTIC MEDIA, AND INCORPORATE THE MOST RELEVANT CONSTITUTIVE MODEL INTO THE NUMERICAL METHOD FOR NON-SPHERICAL BUBBLE DYNAMICS. FIRST, WE WILL INCORPORATE COMPREHENSIVE MASS TRANSPORT TO ACCOUNT FOR NON-EQUILIBRIUM PHASE CHANGE AND GAS DIFFUSION INTO THE BUBBLE. SECOND, WE WILL EXPAND THE CONSTITUTIVE MODELING TO INCLUDE MORE COMPLEX EFFECTS, SUCH AS RATE- AND TEMPERATURE-DEPENDENCE AND PLASTIC BEHAVIOR. 
THE RESULTING MODEL WILL ENABLE RAPID CALCULATIONS OF SPHERICAL BUBBLE DYNAMICS. THIRD, WE WILL DEVELOP A 1D PDE MODEL TO CHARACTERIZE THE IMPORTANCE OF COMPRESSIBILITY. FINALLY, WE WILL ANALYZE THE STABILITY OF BUBBLES IN SOFT MATERIALS TO NON-SPHERICAL PERTURBATIONS. BASED ON INCLUDE THE MOST RELEVANT CONSTITUTIVE MODEL INTO THE COMPUTATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR SIMULATIONS OF NON-SPHERICAL BUBBLE DYNAMICS (EFFORT LED BY COLONIUS AT CALTECH). WE WILL HAVE STRONG INTERACTIONS WITH THE OTHER THRUSTS: WE WILL USE THE EXPERIMENTS IN THRUST 2 FOR CALIBRATION AND VALIDATION, AND BASED ON OUR MODEL WILL 
GUIDE THE EXPERIMENTS; WE WILL LEVERAGE THE MODELING EFFORT OF THRUST 3 TO TEST VARIOUS RELEVANT CONSTITUTIVE MODELS; AND OUR EFFORT WILL FORM THE BASIS FOR THE RHEOMETRY TOOL TO BE DEVELOPED IN THRUST 4. AS A MAJOR PART OF THRUST 2 (EXPERIMENTAL), THE XU GROUP WILL CREATE INDIVIDUAL CAVITATION BUBBLES IN THE TARGET MATERIAL USING ULTRASOUND, AND THREE IMPORTANT CAVITATION PARAMETERS WILL BE MEASURED IN THE PROPOSED ULTRASOUND EXPERIMENTS IN THREE STEPS. 
FIRST, INDIVIDUAL CAVITATION BUBBLES WILL BE GENERATED BY A SINGLE MICROSECOND-LENGTH ULTRASOUND PULSE IN THE TARGET MEDIUM WITHOUT USING ANY INJECTED EXTERNAL CAVITATION NUCLEI. THE ULTRASOUND FOCAL PRESSURE AMPLITUDE, TEMPORAL WAVEFORM, AND SPATIAL PRESSURE PROFILE WILL BE MEASURED USING A FIBER OPTIC HYDROPHONE. SECOND, THE ULTRASOUND-INDUCED CAVITATION BUBBLES CAN GROW FROM NANO-METERS TO HUNDREDS OF MICRONS AND COLLAPSE WITHIN FIVE HUNDRED MICROSECONDS. IMAGES OF THE CAVITATION BUBBLES WILL BE RECORDED USING AN ULTRAFAST CAMERA, AND THE SIZE AND SHAPE OF THE BUBBLES WILL BE EXTRACTED AS A FUNCTION OF TIME. THIRD, THE SURROUNDING MATERIAL DISPLACEMENT WILL BE EXPERIMENTALLY OBTAINED BY EMBEDDING TRACKING PARTICLES IN THE TARGET MATERIAL AND MAPPING THE DISPLACEMENT OF THE PARTICLES VIA PIV. THE ULTRASOUND PRESSURE AND CAVITATION DYNAMIC DATA OBTAINED WILL PROVIDE THE CRITICAL AND NECESSARY EXPERIMENTAL VALIDATION TO THE COMPUTATIONAL CAVITATION SIMULATION FRAMEWORK IN THRUST 1. IN ADDITION, THE MATERIAL DISPLACEMENT MAPPING WILL PROVIDE DATA ESSENTIAL TO CHARACTERIZE AND VALIDATE THE MATERIAL MODEL IN THRUST 3. FOR THE TARGET MATERIAL, WE WILL START FROM THE HOMOGENEOUS, ISOTROPIC SOFT MATERIAL AND EXPEND TO MULTI-LAYERED, HETEROGENEOUS COMPLEX MATERIALS.

2.	USING THE SPECIFICATIONS OF THE ENVIRONMENT, THE ACOUSTIC FIELD WILL BE MODELED BY THE TEAM AS A FUNCTION OF POSITION AND TIME. THE UNCERTAINTY IN THE ENVIRONMENT WILL BE TRANSFORMED IN TO THE UNCERTAINTY IN THE ACOUSTIC FIELD.
3.	GIVEN THE ACOUSTIC FIELD, SYSTEM ARRAY ALGORITHM PERFORMANCE WILL BE MODELED BY THE TEAM INCLUDING TIME VARIABILITY AND NON-STATIONARITY. THE UNCERTAINTY IN THE ENVIRONMENT AND ACOUSTIC FIELD WILL BE TRANSFORMED INTO UNCERTAINTY IN ARRAY PROCESSING ALGORITHM PERFORMANCE. CALIBRATION BY SUB-SPACE FITTING MAY ALLOW SONAR ARRAYS TO BE CALIBRATED IN SITU. THE PERFORMANCE OF WAVEFRONT CURVATURE RANGING IN SHALLOW WATER IS OF INTEREST. IN ADDITION, AUTOMATED SCREENING, ANALYSIS AND EXPLOITATION OF TRANSIENT OR SHORT DURATION SIGNALS USING MACHINE LEARNING MAY BE ENABLED IF SHALLOW WATER PROPAGATION IS BETTER UNDERSTOOD. OUR TEAM PROPOSES TO USE THE ACOUSTIC DATA COLLECTED, MODELING ADVANCES, AND ANALYTICAL DEVELOPMENTS TO ASSESS THE EFFECTIVENESS OF SIGNAL PROCESSING ALGORITHMS IN SHALLOW WATER AND EXPLOIT THIS KNOWLEDGE FOR SYSTEM PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENTS.
4.	A TOOL WILL BE DEVELOPED BY THE TEAM TO EFFECTIVELY COMMUNICATE THE RESULTS OF THE ENVIRONMENT SPECIFICATION, ACOUSTIC MODELING, AND ARRAY SYSTEM PERFORMANCE MENTIONED ABOVE TO NAVY USERS BASED ON A JUPYTER NOTEBOOK OR EQUIVALENT. LEONARD LAB: BIOLOGICALLY INSPIRED, DIRECTED PERCEPTION FOR ROBUST AUTONOMY WORK IN THE LEONARD LAB WILL EXPLOIT THE STRONG INTERPLAY BETWEEN LOCATION/POSE INFORMATION AND OBJECT RECOGNITION, EXPLOITING THE INTERCONNECTS BETWEEN THE WHERE VS. THE WHAT INFORMATION FOR IMPROVING NAVIGATION AND SPATIAL AWARENESS. WE WILL DEVELOP DIRECTED PERCEPTION METHODS BY WHICH AVS CONTROL WHERE TO LOOK AND WHERE TO MOVE TO MAXIMIZE INFORMATION GAIN TO MEETING MISSION OBJECTIVES WHILE CONCURRENTLY MINIMIZING POSE UNCERTAINTY. ROY LAB: AUTONOMY VIA UNIFIED KNOWLEDGE REPRESENTATION, PLANNING AND LEARNING CONVENTIONAL APPROACHES TO AUTONOMOUS NAVIGATION HAVE RELIED ON PRIOR CONSTRUCTION OF DETAILED METRIC MAPS, AND COMPUTATIONALLY INTENSIVE TRAJECTORY OPTIMIZATION TO MOVE THROUGH THOSE MAPS. HOWEVER, THERE IS CONSIDERABLE EVIDENCE THAT BIOLOGICAL SYSTEMS USE HYBRID REPRESENTATIONS, WHERE LOCAL METRIC REPRESENTATIONS ARE RELATED TO EACH OTHER THROUGH PERCEPTUALLY DISTINCT FEATURES. BY USING PERCEPTUAL-DRIVEN FEEDBACK POLICIES TO NAVIGATE GLOBALLY, BUT USING LOCALLY ACCURATE METRIC REPRESENTATIONS FOR LOCAL CONTROL, A SYSTEM CAN NAVIGATE NEAR-OPTIMALLY OVER LONG DISTANCES WITHOUT INCURRING THE COMPUTATIONAL COST OF CONSTRUCTING A GLOBALLY CONSISTENT DENSE METRIC MAP. IF THE PERCEPTUAL FEATURES ARE ALSO TIED TO NOTIONS OF EXECUTION OR CONTROL COST (E.G., MOVING OUT OF A ROOM, GOING INDOORS OR OUTDOORS), THE SAME FEATURES CAN BE USED TO GUIDE THE AUTONOMOUS AGENT IN CHOOSING A NAVIGATION STRATEGY. BY HAVING PERCEPTUAL FEATURES THAT PREDICT THE FUTURE, SUCH AS SEMANTIC FEATURES, THE AUTONOMOUS AGENT CAN USE THESE FEATURES TO KNOW BOTH WHERE IT IS AND HOW TO MAKE PROGRESS TOWARDS A GOAL. PROFESSORS LEONARD AND ROY WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE PROJECT BY LEADING THE EFFORTS DESCRIBED ABOVE IN THE RESPECTIVE LABORATORIES, AND ALSO BY COLLABORATING THE OTHER MEMBERS OF THE MURI TEAM AT BOSTON UNIVERSITY. LEONARD AND ROY WILL PARTICIPATE IN REGULARLY SCHEDULED PROJECT MEETINGS AND ANNUAL REVIEWS HELD BY ONR, AND THEY WILL ALSO CONTRIBUTE TO THE ANNUAL AND FINAL PROJECTS REPORTS FOR THE PROJECT. LEONARD AND ROY WILL PERFORM COLLABORATIVE EXPERIMENTS WITH THE OTHER PARTNERS, AND WILL HELP MENTOR VARIOUS MEMBERS OF THE PROJECT TEAM PARTICIPATING IN THE MURI BOTH AT MIT AND AT BU.

TASK 1: MULTI-UXV COORDINATED SEARCH (UCONN: PATTIPATI) 
IN THIS TASK, UCONN WILL INVESTIGATE THE PROBLEM OF MIXED-INITIATIVE COORDINATED UXV  AND SUBMARINE ROUTE PLANNING, AND COORDINATED SEARCH BY A TEAM OF UXVS TO MAXIMIZE THE PROBABILITY OF DETECTION OF TARGETS BY CONSDERING THE PROBABILITY OF ACTIVITY (POA) SURFACE(S) OF THREATS, METEOROLOGICAL AND OCEANOGRAPHIC (METOC) CONDITIONS,  BATHYMETRY, OBSTACLES, CLOUDS, FOG, BATTERY ENDURANCE, CAMERA CHARACTERISTICS (FIELD OF VIEW, RESOLUTION), AND HEIGHT/DEPTH OF THE UXV.   THE KEY DECISIONS TO BE MADE INCLUDE: THE NUMBER OF UXVS REQUIRED TO SEARCH THE TARGET AREA OR THE MAXIMUM OBTAINABLE DETECTION PROBABILITY FOR THE UXVS AVAILABLE, DRIFT MODELING OF FLOATING CAPSULES THAT HOLD THE UXVS, BAYESIAN UPDATE OF PROBABILITY OF ACTIVITY, COORDINATED MULTI-UXV SEARCH PLAN TO MAXIMIZE THE PROBABILITY OF TARGET DETECTION, SUBMARINE ROUTE PLAN FOR UXV DROP-OFF AND SUBMARINE ASSIGNMENT AREA TO MAINTAIN COMMUNICATION WITH UXVS DURING SEARCH.  WE PLAN TO FORMULATE THE PROBLEM AS A PARTIALLY OBSERVED MARKOV DECISION PROCESS (POMDP) AND EXPERIMENT WITH ROLL-OUT BASED APPROXIMATE DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING TECHNIQUES WITH SEQUENTIAL BAYESIAN UPDATE OF THE POA SURFACES AND REINFORCEMENT LEARNING (RL) TO DEAL WITH UNKNOWN ENVIRONMENTS.  OUR FORMULATION WILL INCLUDE THE  IMPACT OF WEATHER ON UXV SEARCH, UXV DYNAMIC MODELS AND SENSOR MODELS.  
TASK 2: PLANNING COVERAGE PATHS FOR BATHYMETRY MAPPING (UCONN: PATTIPATI) 
THE COVERAGE PATH PLANNING PROBLEM, WHICH IS INTEGRAL TO MANY UXV APPLICATIONS (E.G., DEMINING), DETERMINES PATHS OF UXVS THAT PASS OVER ALL POINTS OF AN AREA OR VOLUME OF INTEREST WHILE AVOIDING OBSTACLES. IN THIS TASK, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE PROBLEM OF COVERAGE PATH PLANNING FOR RAPID HIGH-RESOLUTION LOCAL BATHYMETRY MAPPING UNDER VARYING DEPTH CONDITIONS, TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE TIME REQUIRED FOR THE UUVS TO MAKE DEPTH CHANGES AND THE CAPABILITIES OF THE IMAGING SENSORS, E.G., CAMERA OR A SONAR.  BY REPRESENTING THE OCEAN FLOOR BY A GRID OF UNIFORM SQUARE OR TRIANGULAR CELLS, UCONN WILL FORMULATE THE COORDINATED MAPPING PROBLEM BY MULTIPLE UXVS  AS A  DYNAMIC OPTIMIZATION PROBLEM WITH THE GOAL OF MINIMIZING THE TOTAL TRAVEL DISTANCE TRAVELLED WHILE SATISFYING THE MINIMAL REQUIRED COVERAGE IN EACH CELL AND ACCOUNTING FOR UXV DYNAMICS AND SENSOR CONSTRAINTS.  THE ALGORITHMÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S PERFORMANCE WILL BE EVALUATED IN TERMS OF COVERAGE QUALITY AND COMPUTATION TIME.   
TASK 3: BATHYMETRY MAPPING SYSTEM (URI: STEPHEN LICHT)  
IN THIS TASK, URI WILL CONSTRUCT AND DEPLOY A SHALLOW WATER BAYTHMETRY MAPPING SYSTEM BASED ON AN EXISTING OPEN SOURCE DESIGN, UPGRADE AND MODIFY IT AS NECESSARY TO FACILITATE COORDINATED DEPLOYMENT OF AERIAL, SURFACE, AND UNDERWATER ROBOTS.  URI WILL SUPPORT THE FIELD TESTING OF COORDINATED MAPPING ALGORITHMS DEVELOPED AS PART OF TASK 2 AND, IF TIME PERMITS, THE SEARCH ALGORITHMS OF TASK 1.    
TASK 4: MODELING AND SIMULATION OF UUVS (URI: VINCENT) 
IN THIS TASK, URI WILL CONDUCT A MODELING AND SIMULATION STUDY OF A UUV OPERATING IN SHALLOW COASTAL WATERS WITH UNCERTAIN BATHYMETRY AND CURRENTS, TO BE COUPLED WITH MODELS OF AN EXISTING NAVIGATION SYSTEM, DOPPLER VELOCITY LOG (DVL) AND OFF-BOARD AIDING (E.G., INTERMITTENT TRANSPONDER RANGES).  A NEW PARTICLE FILTER APPROACH TO NAVIGATION IN UNCERTAIN ENVIRONMENTS WILL BE DEVELOPED, EVALUATED AND COMPARED TO FIELD DATA. 
TASK 5:  MISSION PLANNING FOR UUVS (URI: SODHI) 
IN THIS TASK, URI WILL DEVELOP NEW MODELS AND ALGORITHMS FOR MISSION PLANNING FOR UUVS.  MATHEMATICAL MODELS WILL BE FORMULATED AND CODED IN COMMERCIAL MATRIX GENERATION LANGUAGES, AND THESE WILL BE EVALUATED FOR COMPUTATIONAL TRACTABILITY.  HEURISTICS FOR SOLVING PROBLEMS OF LARGER DIMENSIONS WILL BE DEVELOPED AND TESTED.  THE DELIVERABLE WILL BE THE MODELS DEVELOPED AND ALGORITHMS AND COMPUTATIONAL DETAILS.

CO-I   TORN   WILL   CONTRIBUTE   TO   THE   PROJECT   BY   APPLYING   THE   ENSEMBLE-BASED
SENSITIVITY TECHNIQUE TO REAL-TIME ENSEMBLE FORECAST OUTPUT THAT WILL BE AVAILABLE DURING POTENTIAL 
 FIELD  PHASES,  WHICH  WILL  HELP  GUIDE  POTENTIAL  AIRCRAFT  FLIGHT  PLANS.   THIS  WORK BUILDS 
UPON THE STRATEGY USED WITHIN THE NOAA SHOUT EXPERIMENT, HAS BEEN TESTED IN A REAL-TIME FRAMEWORK 
WITH THE NATIONAL HURRICANE CENTER (NHC), AND IS CURRENTLY BEING TRANSITIONED INTO A NHC PRODUCT 
VIA THE JOINT HURRICANE TESTBED (JHT).  DURING YEARS 1- 3, CO-I TORN WILL USE HIS ENSEMBLE-BASED 
SENSITIVITY SOFTWARE TO COMPUTE THE SENSITIVITY OF FUTURE TC INTENSITY FORECASTS TO VARIOUS 
KINEMATIC AND THERMODYNAMIC FIELDS THAT COULD BE SAMPLED BY AIRCRAFT OBSERVATIONS AT THE TIME OF 
POTENTIAL MISSIONS.   THE CALCULATION WILL BE  CARRIED  OUT  ON  ANY  AVAILABLE  ENSEMBLE  OUTPUT,  
INCLUDING  OUTPUT  FROM  THE  GLOBAL ECMWF  AND  FV3  MODELS;  HOWEVER,  THESE  MODELS  HAVE  
LIMITED  ABILITY  TO  RESOLVE  TC INTENSITY  CHANGE  DUE  TO  THEIR  HORIZONTAL  RESOLUTION.     IN 
 ADDITION,  WE  WILL  COMPUTE SENSITIVITY  FOR  REGIONAL  HURRICANE  WEATHER  RESEARCH  AND  
FORECASTING  (HWRF)  AND COAMPS-TC ENSEMBLE, IF AVAILABLE.   SEVERAL FORECAST METRICS WILL BE 
TESTED, INCLUDING TC  INTENSITY  AT  A  SINGLE  TIME  (GENERALLY  24  H  AFTER  A  FLIGHT),  AS  
WELL  AS  PRINCIPLE COMPONENTS  OF  THE  ENSEMBLE  EMPIRICAL  ORTHOGONAL  FUNCTIONS  (EOFS)  OF  TC 
 INTENSITY FORECAST VARIABILITY OVER A PERIOD OF TIME, OR THE EOFS OF THE 10 M TC WIND FIELD NEAR 
THE STORM,  WHICH  PROVIDES  A  MEASURE  OF  THE  TC  WIND  FIELD,  ESPECIALLY  WITH  THE  LOWER 
RESOLUTION MODELS.  SENSITIVITY WILL BE COMPUTED WITH RESPECT TO SEVERAL DIFFERENT FORECAST FIELDS 
AT THE TIME OF POTENTIAL FLIGHTS, INCLUDING THE WIND FIELD, TEMPERATURE, AND MOISTURE FIELD.   
REGIONS OF LARGE SENSITIVITY IN THESE FIELDS WILL ALLOW US TO EVALUATE THE PROCESSES THAT 
CONTRIBUTE TO RI FOR EACH STORM.
PRIOR TO ANY FIELD OPERATIONS, CO-I TORN WILL WORK WITH PI DUNION, CO-PIS ROGERS, ZAWISLAK,  AND  
CIONE,  CO-I  SELLWOOD,  AND  ANY  OTHER  INTERESTED  DRI  PARTICIPANTS  TO DETERMINE  THE  
APPROPRIATE  SET  OF  FIGURES  THAT  WILL  BE  NEEDED  FOR  FLIGHT  PLANNING.     IN ADDITION, CO-I 
TORN WILL MAKE ANY NECESSARY MODIFICATIONS TO HIS SENSITIVITY SOFTWARE FOR THE NEW FORECAST METRICS 
OR FIELDS. WITH THIS OUTPUT, LOCATIONS OF LARGE SENSITIVITY TO THESE FIELDS  WILL  INDICATE  
LOCATIONS  WHERE  ADDITIONAL  OBSERVATIONS  WOULD  REDUCE  TC  INTENSITY FORECAST VARIABILITY.   
CO-I TORN WILL PROVIDE THIS OUTPUT IN ADVANCE OF THE DAILY MISSION PLANNING MEETINGS AND WILL 
PROVIDE A SUMMARY OF THE OUTPUT DURING THE MEETING.  DURING YEARS 4 AND 5, CO-I TORN WILL CONTINUE 
TO PROVIDE REAL-TIME MISSION SUPPORT IF NEEDED. OTHERWISE,  CO-I  TORN  WILL  WORK  WITH  OTHER  
TCRI  PARTICIPANTS  TO  PROVIDE  TAILORED ENSEMBLE  SENSITIVITY  OUTPUT  FOR  USE  IN  
UNDERSTANDING  THE  SOURCES  OF  UNCERTAINTY  AND SENSITIVITY IN THE SPECIFIC MODELS AND WHY IT 
MIGHT BE IMPORTANT FOR TC INTENSITY CHANGE
VIA SETS OF TARGETED DATA ASSIMILATION OR INITIAL CONDITION PERTURBATION EXPERIMENTS."

1.0	SCOPE.

MACHINE LEARNING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) HAVE BEEN INCREASINGLY INVOLVED IN SEQUENTIAL DECISION MAKING IN OUR DAILY LIFE. IN THE IDEALIZED, CLEAN AND SIMPLE SCENARIO, MACHINE LEARNING
 
ALGORITHMS CAN AUTONOMOUSLY COMPUTE AND EXECUTE THE OPTIMAL POLICY USING STANDARD TECHNIQUES SUCH AS REINFORCEMENT LEARNING. INDEED, WE HAVE SEEN AN INCREASING NUMBER OF APPLICATIONS OF AUTOMATIC SEQUENTIAL DECISION MAKING, FROM DETERMINING WHICH ADVERTISEMENTS USERS SEE ONLINE, TO OPERATING ROBOTIC ENTITIES, TO NAVIGATING UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLES.

DESPITE THE SUCCESS OF AUTOMATIC DECISION MAKING IN THESE APPLICATIONS, IN SITUATIONS WHEN THE STAKE IS HIGH OR WHEN THE LEARNING MODELS/OBJECTIVES ARE TOO COMPLICATED TO BE ACCURATELY SPECIFIED, SUCH AS IN GOVERNMENT POLICY MAKING OR IN MILITARY APPLICATIONS, FULLY AUTOMATIC DECISION MAKING HAS NOT ACHIEVED THE LEVEL OF BEING FULLY TRUSTED AND MAY LEAD TO SUBOPTIMAL OUTCOMES. THEREFORE, HUMANS ARE OFTEN BROUGHT INTO THE LOOP TO MAKE THE FINAL CALL ON WHAT POLICY TO EXECUTE. IN THIS TYPE OF HUMAN-AI DECISION MAKING FRAMEWORKS, LEARNING ALGORITHMS MAKE RECOMMENDATIONS BASED ON THE CALCULATED OPTIMAL POLICY, AND HUMAN DECISION MAKERS DECIDE ON WHAT POLICY TO DEPLOY, BASED ON THE RECOMMENDED POLICY. HERE THE GOAL OF MACHINE LEARNING AND AI IS TO AUGMENT, INSTEAD OF REPLACING, HUMANS IN THE LOOP OF DECISION MAKING.

AS A SUBCONTRACTOR, UCSC TEAM WILL HELP DEVELOP ALGORITHMIC RESPONSES TO THIS SEQUENTIAL DECISION MAKING WITH HUMAN BIAS SETTING IN ALL FOLLOWING THREE THRUSTS:

1.	FORMALIZE THE HUMAN-AI SEQUENTIAL DECISION MAKING FRAMEWORK THAT INCORPORATES HUMAN DECISION BIASES. QUANTIFY THE EFFECTS OF HUMAN BIASES AND DESIGN INTERVENTIONS (E.G., WHAT INFORMATION TO SHOW TO HUMAN DECISION MAKER) TO HELP IMPROVE THE OUTCOME OF THE POLICY.

2.	DESIGN STRATEGIES THAT DETECT AND EXPLOIT THE BIASES OF OPPONENT DECISION MAKER. DEVELOP APPROACHES THAT LEARN DECISION MAKER'S PAYOFF FUNCTIONS FROM THEIR ACTIONS (E.G., USING TECHNIQUES FROM INVERSE REINFORCEMENT LEARNING). QUANTIFY THE AMOUNT OF INFORMATION LEAK FROM REVEALED ACTIONS (E.G., HOW MUCH THE ENEMY CAN LEARN FROM THE COMMANDER'S OBJECTIVE FROM OBSERVING ACTIONS TAKEN BY THE COMMANDER).

3.	DEVELOP STRATEGIES THAT ARE ROBUST TO EXPLOITATION. DEVELOP SEQUENTIAL DECISION MAKING ALGORITHMS THAT ARE ROBUST TO ENEMY EXPLOITATION. FORMALIZE THE TRADEOFFS OF MINIMIZING THE INFORMATION LEAK AND MAXIMIZING THE DECISION MAKER'S UTILITY.

THIS DOCUMENT DESCRIBES MIT'S STATEMENT OF WORK FOR ITS SUBCONTRACT TO THE UNIVERSITY OF 
PENNSYLVANIA FOR THE PROJECT "UNCERTAINTY-BASED ACTIVE SELF-LEARNING FOR PERCEPTION" BEING 
SUBMITTED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF PENNSYLVANIA.

SELF-LEARNING AS INFERENCE OF NOVEL ABSTRACTIONS

IN THE ROY LAB, WE PROPOSE TO BUILD ON OUR PREVIOUS WORK WHERE WE SHOWED THAT A ROBOT COULD 
INCORPORATE BACKGROUND CONCEPTUAL KNOWLEDGE ENCODED AS A MARKOV LOGIC NETWORK ENCOMPASSING SEMANTIC 
ATTRIBUTES, RELATIONSHIPS, AFFORDANCES ETC. CAN BE USED TO INFER "MISSING" PLAN CONSTITUENTS (SUCH 
AS ACTION SUBJECTS OR GOAL LOCATIONS) BASED ON STATISTICAL CORRELATIONS AND TAXONOMIC AFFINITIES. 
TO REDUCE COMPUTATIONAL COMPLEX-ITY, AN ONLINE CONTEXT-DRIVEN APPROACH CAN BE USED THAT 
HYPOTHESIZES THE POTENTIAL FOR MISSING KNOWLEDGE COMPONENTS BY INTEGRATING EVIDENCE FROM THE VISUAL 
OBSERVATIONS OF THE WORLD STATE. THE ABILITY TO INFER LATENT PLAN COMPONENTS ENABLES THE ROBOT TO 
TAKE INFORMATION GATHERING ACTIONS SUCH AS VISUAL EXPLORATION OR ENGAGING IN DIALOGUE WITH THE 
HUMAN TO REPLENISH ITS KNOWLEDGE GAP AND ENABLE PLAN SYNTHESIS.

PROBLEMS THAT ARE LONG-HORIZON AND HIGH DIMENSIONAL ARE USUALLY INTRACTABLE FOR END-TO-END LEARNING 
PRO-CESSES. THE STRATEGY IS TO RENDER THESE PROBLEMS TRACTABLE BY EXPLOITING STRUCTURE IN THE 
PROBLEM, INCLUDING FACTORING INTO WEAKLY INTERACTING SUB-COMPONENTS (POSSIBLY INVOLVING DIFFERENT 
ASPECTS OF THE STATE SPACE OR DIFFERENT TEMPORAL SUB-REGIONS), AND "LIFTING" OR ABSTRACTING OVER 
ARBITRARY SETS OF ENTITIES IN THE DOMAIN. THE REPRESENTATIONS THAT HAVE EFFECTIVELY ENABLED 
COMPACTNESS AND EFFICIENT REASONING IN VERY LARGE PROBLEMS ARE LOGICS, INCLUDING PROPOSITIONAL 
LOGIC, FIRST-ORDER LOGIC, GRAPHICAL MODELS (WHICH CAN BE VIEWED AS A PROBA-BILISTIC VERSION OF 
PROPOSITIONAL LOGIC) AND TEMPORAL LOGICS. THE PRIMARY VIRTUE OF LOGICAL REPRESENTATIONS IS THAT 
THEY ALLOW COMPOSITIONALITY -  A LOGICAL REPRESENTATION PROVIDES A SYSTEM OF RULES THAT ALLOW 
SYNTACTIC MANIPULATIONS TO CREATE NEW REPRESENTATIONS WHILE PRESERVING THE SEMANTICS OF THE MODEL. 
CONCRETELY, PARTS OF THE MODEL CAN HAVE INDEPENDENT SEMANTICS, ALLOWING THEM TO BE LEARNED 
INDEPENDENTLY AND THEN COMPOSED USING LOGICAL OPERATIONS TO INFER THE SEMANTICS OF A COMBINED 
MODEL, PROVIDING A PARTICULARLY AGGRESSIVE AND USEFUL FORM OF GENERALIZATION.

MODELING UNCERTAINTY

A CRUCIAL ABILITY FOR LONG-TERM AUTONOMY IS THE ABILITY TO INTROSPECT, AND RECOGNISE WHEN ITS 
INTERNAL MODEL IS ACCURATE AND WHEN IT IS UNCERTAIN. IT IS IMPORTANT TO DISTINGUISH BETWEEN TWO 
TYPES OF UNCERTAINTY: ALEATORIC UNCERTAINTY THAT CAPTURES STOCHASTICITY IN SENSORS, ACTUATORS AND 
THE ENVIRONMENT, AND EPISTEMIC UNCERTAINTY THAT RESULTS FROM AN INCOMPLETE MODEL OF THE WORLD. HIGH 
ALEATORIC UNCERTAINTY IMPLIES THAT EXPECTED RISK CAN BE CALCULATED ACCURATELY, WHEREAS EPISTEMIC 
UNCERTAINTY MEANS THAT THERE ARE PARTS OF THE SENSOR DATA THAT THE VEHICLE CANNOT ACCURATELY MODEL. 
SEPARATING ALEATORIC AND EPISTEMIC UNCERTAINTY ALLOWS FOR A PROCESS OF MODIFYING RISK PROFILES WHEN 
NO FEASIBLE PLAN IS FOUND, POTENTIALLY INCREASING THE TOLERANCE FOR RISK DUE TO ALEATORIC 
UNCERTAINTY UNTIL A FEASIBLE PLAN IS FOUND.

WE PROPOSE TO LEVERAGE OUR PREVIOUS WORK IN ANOMALY DETECTION (ALSO REFERRED TO AS 
OUT-OF-DISTRIBUTION OR OOD DETECTION). IN NOVEL ENVIRONMENTS, UNCERTAINTY ESTIMATES CAN BE 
DIFFICULT TO CALIBRATE AND, AS A RESULT, OOD REJECTION CAN BE USED TO REPLACE OR IMPROVE UPON 
EPISTEMIC UNCERTAINTY ESTIMATES AS A WAY TO REDUCE THE IMPACT OF ERRONEOUS OUTPUTS FROM 
'UNEXPECTED' SENSOR DATA. OUR PAST WORK HAS INVESTIGATED ANOMALY 
DETECTION VIA AUTOENCODERS AND VIA LEARNED REPRESENTATIONS OF BELIEF. LEVERAGING OUR EXPERIENCE 
WITH BOTH OOD REJECTION AND DEEP MODELS OF ALEATORIC AND EPISTEMIC UNCERTAINTY, WE PROPOSE TO 
INVESTIGATE SEVERAL AVENUES OF UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION IN AN EFFORT TO DETERMINE A ROBUST 
APPROACH FOR SEMANTIC PERCEPTION.

PROPOSED EXPERIME

1. BACKGROUND
THE OFFICE OF NAVAL RESEARCH (ONRÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S) OCEAN BATTLESPACE AND EXPEDITIONARY ACCESS
DEPARTMENT (CODE 32) EXPLORES SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY IN THE AREAS OF OCEANOGRAPHIC AND
METEOROLOGICAL OBSERVATIONS, MODELING AND PREDICTION IN THE BATTLESPACE ENVIRONMENT;
SUBMARINE DETECTION AND CLASSIFICATION (ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE); AND MINE WARFARE
APPLICATIONS FOR DETECTING AND NEUTRALIZING MINES IN BOTH THE OCEAN AND LITTORAL
ENVIRONMENT.
IN PREPARATION FOR A MULTI-DOMAIN OPERATIONS (MDO) READY FORCE THE US NAVY REQUIRES
MORE SENSITIVE TOOLS TO DETECT INTRUSIONS INTO SECURE FACILITIES, DETECT LOW MAGNETIC
SIGNATURE SUBMARINES, AND SEA MINES. THE ABILITY TO DETECT THESE TARGETS WITH RECENTLY
DEVELOPED LOW COST, LOW POWER CONSUMPTION, HIGH SENSITIVITY SOLID STATE MAGNETICS AND
ACOUSTICS SENSORS WILL PROVIDE THE NAVY WITH ENHANCED CAPABILITY, PARTICULARLY IN THE
LITTORAL ZONE.
IN SUPPORT OF NAVY UNCREWED SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT, DESIGN, AND TEST & EVALUATION, USM
IS ESTABLISHING A TEST AREA IN THE MISSISSIPPI SOUND, MISSISSIPPI BIGHT, AND OFFSHORE OF
THE GULF OF MEXICO. IN THIS TEST AREA, USM CAN SUPPORT ALL OF NAVYÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S MISSIONS, EXCEPT
ARTIC OPERATIONS AND THE AREA IS VERY ANALOGOUS TO SOUTHEAST ASIS. UNDER THIS AWARD,
USM WILL ESTABLISH A MAGNETIC COMPONENT FOR THE OCEAN CUBE. THIS OCEAN CUBE
FUNCTIONALITY WILL ALLOW USM AND ITS PARTNERS TO TEST & EVALUATE NEW MAGNETIC AND
POTENTIALLY GRAVITY SENSORS IN A COASTAL ENVIRONMENT. USM AND ITS PARTNERS WILL INTEGRATE
THE SELECTED SENSORS IN VARIOUS UUV AND USV PLATFORMS/VEHICLES AND TEST & EVALUATE
THEIR PERFORMANCE AGAINST TARGETS OF INTEREST. USM HAS PARTNERED WITH SYSTEMS INTEGRATED,
GOVERNMENT SERVICES DIVISION (SI-GSD) FOR THE DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, AND INTEGRATION
METHODOLOGY FOR THIS PROJECT.
2. APPROACH
USM/SI-GSD WILL PARTNER TO ENHANCE THE FUNCTIONALITY OF THE OCEAN CUBE BY FOLLOWING A
TYPICAL V METHODOLOGY THAT PROGRESSES THROUGH A PROCESS OF DESIGN, DEVELOP, AND
INTEGRATE AN OCEAN CUBE NETWORK. SI-GSD IS A LEADER IN TECHNOLOGY SOLUTIONS IN
ENGINEERING AND SPECIFICALLY AS IT APPLIES TO MAGNETIC ENVIRONMENTS. BY PARTNERING WITH
USMÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S ROGER F. WICKER CENTER FOR OCEAN ENTERPRISE, THE NAVY WILL BE ABLE TO LEVERAGE
RECENT ADVANCES IN SENSOR DESIGNS, AND ON-BOARD PROCESSING TO TEST PLATFORM AGNOSTIC
MAGNETIC AND ACOUSTIC SENSORS TO BETTER PREDICT CONDITIONS AND EXECUTE MANEUVERS IN
LITTORAL ZONES FASTER AND MORE ACCURATELY, AS WELL AS MAP/AVOID MINES, PROVIDING A
SUSTAINED STRATEGIC ADVANTAGE.

"PROJECT OVERVIEW:
THE CONVERGENCE OF GAME THEORY, ALGORITHMS, AND LEARNING HAS LED TO SIGNIFICANT ADVANCEMENTS
IN UNDERSTANDING AND PREDICTING STRATEGIC INTERACTIONS AMONG RATIONAL AGENTS. THIS PROJECT AIMS
TO FURTHER EXPLORE THE DYNAMIC INTERPLAY OF THESE FIELDS IN THE CONTEXT OF COMPLEX STRATEGIC
GAMES (CSGS). CSGS ENCOMPASS SCENARIOS WITH MULTIPLE PLAYERS OF DIVERSE TYPES, EVOLVING
PARAMETERS, MULTI-OBJECTIVE PAYOFF FUNCTIONS, INCOMPLETE INFORMATION, COALITION FORMATION,
INFORMATION GATHERING, DECEPTION, AND NONZERO-SUM INTERACTIONS. THE PROJECT SEEKS TO DEVELOP
BOTH THEORETICAL FOUNDATIONS AND PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS FOR MULTI-AGENT DECISION-MAKING AND
LEARNING IN CSGS.
PROJECT GOALS:
1. THEORETICAL FOUNDATIONS:
X ANALYZE AND DISSECT THE WAYS IN WHICH CSGS TRANSCEND EXISTING GAME THEORY
MODELS.
X DEVELOP NEW SOLUTION CONCEPTS, WITH A FOCUS ON BAYESIAN EQUILIBRIUM, TO
ACCOUNT FOR THE COMPLEXITIES OF CSGS.
X INVESTIGATE DYNAMIC AND REPEATED ASPECTS OF CSGS, INCLUDING THE DEVELOPMENT
OF STOCHASTIC GENERALIZATIONS AND REGULARIZATIONS OF REPLICATOR DYNAMICS.
X EXPLORE NOVEL APPROACHES TO HANDLE INCOMPLETE AND INCONSISTENT INFORMATION, AS
WELL AS THE CHALLENGES OF INCORRECT INFORMATION AND INFORMATION UPDATING IN A
DYNAMIC SETTING.
X STUDY THE IMPACT OF PLAYER DECEPTION ON ANALYSIS AND PREDICTION IN CSGS.
2. PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS:
X APPLY THE DEVELOPED THEORETICAL FOUNDATIONS TO EMBLEMATIC CSGS, SUCH AS
GENERALIZED DIPLOMACY AND STRATEGO.
X EXPLORE INNOVATIVE STRATEGIES FOR INFORMATION SHARING, COALITION FORMATION, AND
DECEPTION IN CSGS.
X DEVELOP ALGORITHMS AND LEARNING TECHNIQUES TAILORED TO ADDRESS THE COMPLEXITIES
OF CSGS, WITH A FOCUS ON MULTI-AGENT REINFORCEMENT LEARNING AND GAME-SPECIFIC
ADAPTATIONS.
X INVESTIGATE THE COMPUTATIONAL TRACTABILITY OF ANALYZING AND SOLVING CSGS,
CONSIDERING BOTH COOPERATIVE AND COMPETITIVE SCENARIOS.
X DEMONSTRATE THE POTENTIAL REAL-WORLD APPLICATIONS OF CSG ANALYSIS AND DECISIONMAKING, PARTICULARLY IN MILITARY CONTEXTS INVOLVING VARIOUS PLAYER ROLES AND
OBJECTIVES.
PROJECT SCOPE:
X CONDUCT AN IN-DEPTH LITERATURE REVIEW TO IDENTIFY EXISTING RESEARCH IN GAME THEORY,
ALGORITHMS, AND LEARNING AS THEY RELATE TO CSGS.
X ORGANIZE REGULAR TEAM MEETINGS TO FOSTER COLLABORATION AND KNOWLEDGE EXCHANGE AMONG
EXPERTS FROM DIVERSE DOMAINS.
X DEVELOP MATHEMATICAL MODELS AND FORMALISMS TO REPRESENT THE COMPLEXITIES OF CSGS,
INTEGRATING CONCEPTS FROM GAME THEORY, ALGORITHMS, AND LEARNING.
X IMPLEMENT AND REFINE ALGORITHMS FOR ANALYZING CSGS, LEVERAGING INSIGHTS FROM BOTH
THEORETICAL DEVELOPMENTS AND PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS.
X DESIGN EXPERIMENTS AND SIMULATIONS TO EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF PROPOSED
APPROACHES IN ADDRESSING THE CHALLENGES POSED BY CSGS.
X APPLY THE DEVELOPED METHODOLOGIES TO SPECIFIC CSG SCENARIOS, EMPHASIZING THE
ADAPTATION OF STRATEGIES FOR MILITARY CONTEXTS.
X DOCUMENT RESEARCH FINDINGS, METHODOLOGIES, ALGORITHMS, AND RESULTS IN TECHNICAL REPORTS
AND SCHOLARLY PUBLICATIONS. "

DECEPTION, AND NONZERO SUM IN BOTH DIRECTIONS --- WIN-WIN AND LOSE-LOSE --- DEPENDING ON THE 
COMBINATION OF PLAYERS AND STRATEGIES.

A.	DESIGN & DEVELOPMENT SPECIFICATIONS FOR THE OCEAN CUBE TEST AND EVALUATION SOFTWARE.
THE MAIN EMPHASIS IN THIS STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW), IS TO EXPAND THE EXISTING OCEAN CUBE TEST AND EVALUATION SOFTWARE SUCH THAT IT CAN INGEST AND VISUALIZE NEW SENSOR NETWORK OBSERVATION DATA AND PROVIDE NEAR REAL-TIME OVERLAY OF AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE (I.E. OCEAN AERO) POSITION DATA, AS WELL AS, ENVIRONMENTAL DATA TRANSMITTED OR DELAYED-MODE DATA FROM THE VEHICLE. TYPES OF DATA FROM THE VEHICLE MAY INCLUDE: POSITIONS, ACOUSTICS, TEMPERATURE, SALINITY, CURRENT PROFILES, MARINE RADAR, AIS, AND CAMERA. IN ADDITION, THERE IS A NEED FOR THE CAPABILITY TO SUPPORT FROM ONE TO THREE HRTAS WITHIN THE EXISTING OCEAN CUBE RANGE EXTENT THAT WILL BE HEAVILY INSTRUMENTED USING THE SENSOR NETWORKS DESCRIBED ABOVE. NOT ONLY WILL THE INGEST AND DISPLAY OF THE NETWORK SENSOR DATA BE NEEDED, BUT THE CAPABILITY OF VISUALIZING VERY HIGH-RESOLUTION NUMERICAL MODEL DATA FOR THESE SPECIFIC AREAS WILL NEED TO BE DEVELOPED ALONG WITH THE USER INTERFACE SUPPORT. ALSO, A TOOL WILL BE DEVELOPED FOR THE VISUALIZATION OF THE FULL RESOLUTION DATA THAT WILL BE UPLOADED FROM THE AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE POST OPERATIONS.
B.	SOURCE CODE AND DOCUMENTATION OF OCEAN CUBE TEST AND EVALUATION SOFTWARE. ALL NECESSARY SOFTWARE CODE FOR THE COMPONENTS OF A WORKING OCEAN CUBE TEST AND EVALUATION SYSTEM SHALL BE DELIVERED AND DEMONSTRATED TO PERFORM SATISFACTORILY. IN-CODE DOCUMENTATION WILL CONSIST OF MODULE DESCRIPTIONS AT THE BEGINNING OF EACH MODULE DESCRIBING THE PURPOSE OR FUNCTION OF THE MODULE ALONG WITH A DESCRIPTION OF ANY INPUT AND/OR OUTPUT PARAMETERS. AFTER THE INITIAL DELIVERY, ADDITIONAL COMMENTS WILL INCLUDE ANY CHANGES MADE TO THE MODULE ALONG WITH THE DATE AND PERSON RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CHANGES MADE.  COMMENTS WILL BE MADE WITHIN THE BODY OF THE MODULE TO SUFFICIENTLY DESCRIBE THE PROCESSES AND DATA FLOW.
C.	OCEAN CUBE TEST AND EVALUATION SOFTWARE MAINTENANCE MANUAL.
THE EXISTING OCEAN CUBE TEST AND EVALUATION SOFTWARE DOCUMENTATION WILL BE EXPANDED TO INCLUDE THE FEATURES AND ADDITIONAL CAPABILITIES THAT ARE DESCRIBED ABOVE.  SPECIFICALLY, SECTIONS OF THE DOCUMENTATION WILL BE EXPANDED FOR THE DESCRIPTION OF THE AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE DATA INGESTED AS NEW DATA BECOME AVAILABLE AND FOR THE INCLUSION OF NETWORK SENSOR OBSERVATION DATA. ALSO, THE STEPS NECESSARY FOR THE ADDITION OF NEW OR REPOSITIONED HRTAS WILL BE DESCRIBED.
D.	OCEAN CUBE TEST AND EVALUATION SOFTWARE OPERATING PROCEDURES MANUAL.
THE EXISTING OCEAN CUBE TEST AND EVALUATION SOFTWARE USER GUIDE DOCUMENTATION WILL BE EXPANDED TO INCORPORATE THE INCLUSION OF THE NEW DATA SOURCES (OCEAN AERO) ALONG WITH ANY NEW CAPABILITIES THAT ARE DEVELOPED FOR VISUALIZING THESE DATA.  ANON-LINE DATA DICTIONARY DESCRIBING THE VISUALIZED DATA PARAMETERS WILL BE ACCESSIBLE VIA THE OCEAN CUBE USER INTERFACE. 

E.	METHODOLOGY FOR DATA INGEST AND DATA DICTIONARY FOR OCEAN CUBE APPLICATIONS THE METHODOLOGY FOR DATA INGEST OF THE AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE AND NETWORK SENSOR DATA WILL BE DEVELOPED.  AS THE DATA INGEST PROCESS OF EACH NEW VEHICLE OR INSTRUMENT DATA IS DEVELOPED THE EXISTING OCEAN CUBE DOCUMENTATION WILL BE UPDATED TO INCLUDE PROVISIONS DESCRIBING THESE NEW DATA SOURCES.
F.	ALL SOFTWARE MANUALS AND DESCRIPTIONS WILL BE DELIVERED ON THE OCEAN CUBE WEBSITE.
ALL MANUALS DELIVERED WILL BE IN A FORM THAT IS EASILY ACCESSIBLE VIA WEBSITE DOWNLOAD.  APPROPRIATE LINKS WILL BE MADE WITHIN THE APPLICATION TO ALLOW FOR THE USER TO ACCESS THE MANUALS AND DOCUMENTATION.

THE ALIGN PROJECT SEEKS TO DEVELOP OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE FOR ANALOG/MIXED-SIGNAL CIRCUIT LAYOUT TO BUILD A HIERARCHICAL, MACHINE LEARNING (ML) DRIVEN PHYSICAL LAYOUT GENERATOR. FOUR CLASSES OF ANALOG/MIXED SIGNAL CIRCUITS ARE CONSIDERED: LOW-FREQUENCY CIRCUITS, WIRELINE SYSTEMS, WIRELESS SYSTEMS, AND POWER DELIVERY CIRCUITS. THE PHILOSOPHY OF ALIGN IS TO IDENTIFY A SET OF BUILDING BLOCKS FROM AN INPUT NETLIST AND TO HIERARCHICALLY BUILD LAYOUTS FOR THESE BLOCKS FROM THE CELL LEVEL TO THE SYSTEM LEVEL. ALIGN GENERATES PARAMETERIZED LAYOUTS FOR THE LOWEST-LEVEL CELLS, COMPOSES THESE CELLS INTO LARGER SUB-CIRCUITS THROUGH FLOOR PLANNING/PLACEMENT STRATEGIES, AND PERFORMS PERFORMANCE-AWARE ROUTING. AT EACH STEP, ALIGN COMPREHENDS DESIGN RULE CONSTRAINTS AND ELECTRICAL CONSTRAINTS AND TRANSLATES THESE TO DIRECTIVES FOR EACH LAYOUT STEP. THE APPROACHES USE A MIX OF GRAPH-BASED TECHNIQUES AND ACCELERATED PHYSICAL DESIGN METHODS, COUPLED WITH MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES THAT ENABLE FAST DESIGN OPTIMIZATION.

SUBTASK 1.1.1.2	DEVICE DEVELOPMENT OF NIRS SUBSYSTEM 

THE NIRS SYSTEM CONSISTS OF A SENSOR TO BE APPLIED ON THE DURA AT THE SITE OF SPINAL CORD INJURY DURING THE SURGICAL DECOMPRESSION/FUSION, AND A CONTROLLER WHICH DRIVES THE NIR LIGHT EMISSION AND COLLECTS THE INFORMATION ABOUT ABSORPTION THAT WILL BE TRANSLATED BY THE CONTROLLER SOFTWARE TO BLOOD OXYGENATION AND BLOOD FLOW.   THE DESIGN OF THE SENSOR AND CONTROLLER WILL BE AN EXTENSION OF THE WORK ALREADY PERFORMED BY DRS. SHADGAN AND KWON (UBC) TO DEVELOP AN IMPLANTABLE NIRS SENSOR, AND WILL BE DEVELOPED IN CONJUNCTION WITH DR. VEFAGH OF PATHONIX WHO WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE NIRS CONTROLLER. TELIATRY WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR BUILDING THE PROTOTYPE.   THE DEVICE WILL MEET DARPA SPECIFICATIONS (E.G SENSOR ACCURACY AND PRECISION, MRI COMPATIBLE, ETC) AND WILL MEET OR EXCEED FDA REQUIREMENTS FOR BIOCOMPATIBILITY, MECHANICAL AND ELECTRICAL SPECIFICATIONS FOR EVENTUAL IMPLANTATION INTO  HUMAN SUBJECTS. THE NIRS CONTROLLER WITH HARDWARE TO DRIVE THE EMITTER AND RECEIVE SIGNALS FROM THE PHOTODETECTOR WILL BE BUILT FOR IMPLANTATION INTO THE ANIMAL   DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS INCLUDE THE ABILITY TO EVENTUALLY COMMUNICATE WITH THE TESS_HEMO PLATFORM AND COMPATIBILITY FOR MRI SCANNING.
 REQUIREMENTS FOR THE NIRS SUBSYSTEM DEVELOPMENT
1.	REDUCE FOOTPRINT OF THE SENSOR TO ALLOW FOR 14 DAY IM-PLANTATION.
2.	SENSOR CASING COMPATIBLE WITH FIXATION SYSTEM. 
3.	UP TO 5 LED EMITTERS (EMITTER ARRAY) WITH DIFFERENT WAVELENGTH AND A SINGLE PHOTODETECTOR POSITIONED 15-16 MM AWAY FROM THE EMITTER FOR AN INTER-OPTODE DISTANCE (IOD) OF 7.5-8.0 MM.    
4.	SENSOR CONTROLLER CONTAINS SOFTWARE THAT PARAMETERIZES LIGHT PULSES FROM EMITTER (PULSE WIDTH, PULSE DURATION, AMPLITUDE, ETC) AND MANAGES DATA STREAM FROM SENSOR TO NEUROCOMMANDER 
5.	MEDICAL GRADE DEVICE MANUFACTURED ACCORDING TO FDA BIOCOMPATIBILITY AND SAFETY STANDARDS, INCLUDING HUMAN BIOCOMPATIBILITY OF SENSOR MATERIALS, ELECTRICAL SAFETY STANDARDS (SPECIAL CARE THAT EMITTERS DO NOT EXCEED HEAT GENERATION STANDARDS)
6.	3T MRI COMPATIBILITY FOR IMPLANTABLE SUBCOMPONENTS.
7.	POWER IS AVAILABLE TO RUN THE DEVICE FOR 14 DAYS
8.	NON-INVASIVE NIRS SYSTEM ACCURACY OF MEASURING O2HB AND THB (OXYGENATED AND TOTAL HEMOGLOBIN AS MEASURES OF O2 AND BLOOD VOLUME/FLOW IN THE SCI PENUMBRA) WITHIN 20% ACCURACY OF INVASIVE OXYFLOW MEASURES OF OXYGEN AND BLOOD FLOW IN THE SCI PENUMBRA.
9.	NIRS SYSTEM SENSOR PRECISION WITHIN 20% OF COV DUR-ING BASELINE RECORDING.

1.1.1.3.2	ESTABLISH FIXATION METHOD FOR NIRS SENSOR

THE METHOD FOR NON-RIGIDLY SECURING THE NIRS SENSOR ON THE SPINAL CORD WILL BE DEVELOPED TO ACCOMMODATE THE NEW DESIGN OF THE SENSOR MANUFACTURED BY TELIATRY.  HERE WE WILL UTILIZE LATERAL CONNECTORS FROM PRE-EXISTING SPINAL STABILIZATION SYSTEMS THAT ARE CURRENT STANDARDS OF SURGICAL CARE, SO THAT WHEN THE NIRS SENSOR/WIRE/INIRS-C ARE PULLED OUT THROUGH THE SKIN, THE SYSTEM THAT SECURES THE NIRS SENSOR TO THE DURA CAN REMAIN IN PLACE AS PART OF THE SPINAL FIXATION CONSTRUCT.   THE ADVANTAGE OF THIS IS THAT THERE WILL THEN BE ONE LESS APPROVAL TO OBTAIN TO LEAVE AN IMPLANTABLE DEVICE IN A HUMAN, PLUS, THE NIRS SENSOR WILL NOT BE DEPENDENT UPON A PARTICULAR COMPANYÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¢Â€ŽÂ¢S FIXATION SYSTEM (RECOGNIZING THAT DIFFERENT INSTITUTIONS WILL USE DIFFERENT COMPANIES).   EVERY SPINAL IMPLANT COMPANY MAKES LATERAL CONNECTORS, AND MOST CERVICAL SYSTEMS USE RODS IN THE 3.2-3.5 MM RANGE - HENCE, THE DORSAL SURFACE OF THE SENSOR NEEDS TO MANUFACTURED IN SUCH A WAY THAT THE TIP OF A LATERAL CONNECTOR CAN ÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã…Â€ŒDOCKÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¯Â¿Â½ INTO THE SENSOR TO PROVIDE DORSAL STABILITY TO THE SENSOR ON THE DURA WITHOUT PREVENTING IT FROM BEING PULLED OUT THROUGH THE SKIN WHEN NIRS MONITORING CONCLUDES.   IMPORTANTLY, THIS THEN OBVIATES THE NEED TO RE-OPEN THE SURGICAL WOUND TO REMOVE THE SENSOR.    

TO ACHIEVE THIS, KWON AND SHADGAN WILL USE THE STRATEGIES THEY HAVE DEVELOPED WITH LATERAL CONNECTORS AND CROSS CONNECTORS FROM THE MEDTRONIC VERTEX CERVICAL FIXATION SYSTEM, WHICH THEY HAVE OBTAINED ALREADY FROM MEDTRONIC.  THE USE OF THESE LATERAL CONNECTORS HAS ALREADY BEEN SHOWN TO WORK AS FOR A 7D FIXATION STRATEGY IN THE PIGS POST-SCI, AND SO IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT SLIGHT MODIFICATIONS TO ACCOMMODATE THE NEW SENSOR HEAD DESIGN WILL RESULT IN AN EFFECTIVE FIXATION SYSTEM.   HERE, SPECIFIC ANIMALS ARE NOT BUDGETED FOR, AS THE KWON LAB EXPECTS THAT THEY WILL HAVE OTHER ANIMAL EXPERIMENTS ONGOING (OR CADAVERIC PIGS POST-EXPERIMENTATION) IN WHICH TO TEST THE FIXATION SYSTEM.    FOR THIS REASON, IN THESE 9 MONTHS IT IS EXPECTED THAT THE FIXATION SYSTEM WILL BE ESTABLISHED.   

THE FIXATION METHOD WILL BE CONFIRMED BY THE FOLLOWING CRITERIA:

1.  COMBINATION OF LATERAL CONNECTOR APPLYING DORSAL PRESSURE TO THE SENSOR AND TISSEAL AROUND THE SENSOR EXCLUDES EPIDURAL BLOOD FROM SEEPING UNDER THE SENSOR OVER A 4 HOUR PERIOD (I.E. SECURING THE SENSOR ON THE DURA)
2.  PULLING ON THE EXTERNALIZED SENSOR WIRE ALLOWS FOR THE DISENGAGEMENT OF THE SENSOR FROM THE DURA AND FOR THE SENSOR TO BE PULLED THROUGH THE MUSCLE AND SKIN (I.E. ALLOWING FOR REMOVAL AFTER NIRS MONITORING IS COMPLETE AT ~14D)

THIS EXPERIMENT IS A NON-SURVIVAL STUDY (N=5) IN WHICH THE RECIPIENT SHALL ANATOMICALLY DISSECT THE OVERLYING TISSUE AND PERFORM A LAMINECTOMY TO EXPOSE THE SPINAL CORD BETWEEN THE T6 AND L2 SPINAL LEVELS. THE RECIPIENT SHALL THEN STIMULATE THE SPINAL CORD AT EACH LEVEL TO DETERMINE THE PRESSOR RESPONSE TO STIMULATION AT EACH SEGMENT. ADDITIONALLY, THE RECIPIENT SHALL RECORD EMG RESPONSES FROM THE TRUNK AND ABDOMINAL MUSCLES FOR LATER USE IN SUB-SUBTASK 1.1.2.1.3. PRIOR TO THE SURGERY, THE RECIPIENT SHALL COLLECT HIGH-RESOLUTION MRI OF EACH MINIPIG USING NEWLY DEVELOPED MRI SEQUENCES THAT ALLOW US TO VISUALIZE THE POSTERIOR AND VENTRAL ROOTS OF THE SPINAL CORD WITH UNPRECEDENTED SHARPNESS. THE RECIPIENT SHALL EXPLOIT THESE SCANS TO GENERATE COMPUTATIONAL MODELS OF THE MINIPIGSÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¢Â€ŽÂ¢ THORACIC SPINAL COLUMNS. THE RECIPIENT SHALL THEN PERFORM SIMULATIONS TO DETERMINE RELEVANT
ELECTRODE CONFIGURATIONS TO TARGET THE POSTERIOR ROOTS OF THE THORACIC AND LUMBAR SPINAL CORD. THESE PREDICTIONS SHALL BE USED TO DESIGN AND FABRICATE	1-12
 

	DISPOSABLE E-DURA ARRAYS THAT SHALL ENABLE THE MAPPING OF PRESSOR RESPONSES. AFTER THE EXPERIMENTS, THE ANIMAL SHALL BE TERMINATED. THE RECIPIENT SHALL THEN DISSECT THE SPINAL CORD AND VERTEBRA TO MEASURE THE ROSTROCAUDAL AND LONGITUDINAL LOCATIONS OF THE POSTERIOR ROOTS, WHICH SHALL SERVE TO CONFIRM AND UPDATE THE MODELS. THESE ANATOMICAL MEASUREMENTS SHALL COMPLEMENT THE DATA OF THE MAPPING TO DESIGN THE PIG_HEMO_LEAD.

NOTE: THIS SHALL BE AN ALL-DAY EXPERIMENT THAT DOES REQUIRE THE T2 SCI TO DISRUPT THE PHYSIOLOGIC BAROREFLEX. THE MRI SHALL BE FAIRLY LABOR INTENSIVE BUT ARE DO-ABLE (THE IMAGING FACILITY IS ABOUT 1 MILE FROM THE ANIMAL FACILITY, AND IS A HUMAN 3T MRI). IT SHALL REQUIRE THE PHILLIPS AND COURTINE TEAMS TO COME TO VANCOUVER TO SUPPORT THE EXPERIMENTS AND ANALYZE THE DATA. NOTE: THE COURTINE/PHILLIPS TEAM HAVE ALREADY PERFORMED SIMILAR VALIDATION STUDIES OF THIS DEVICE IN RODENTS AND MONKEYS AND THEREFORE EXPECT THIS STEP TO BE RELATIVELY STRAIGHT FORWARD, ALBEIT TIME CONSUMING. IT SHALL ALSO BE NECESSARY TO COLLECT MRI DATA TO INFORM THE DESIGN OF ELECTRODE ARRAYS TARGETING THE CARDIOVASCULAR HOTSPOTS.

RISK MANAGEMENT: KWON LAB MAY RECORD MRIS OF LESS THAN FIVE PIGS. WHILE MRIS OF FIVE PIGS ARE SPECIFIED TO GENERATE THE SPINAL STIM MAP, THIS MAP CAN BE GENERATED USING ANY NUMBER OF SPINAL MODELS. THE MORE SPINAL MODELS ARE USED, THE MORE REPRESENTATIVE THE MAP BECOMES OF THE WHOLE YUCATAN MINIPIG POPULATION. WE SPECIFIED 5 AS A TRADEOFF BETWEEN THE TIME AND EFFORT INVESTED TO GENERATE INDIVIDUAL MODELS AND HOW REPRESENTATIVE THE MAP WOULD BE OF THE WHOLE POPULATION. USING THE LOWER NUMBER OF MODELS TO GENERATE THE MAP SHALL STILL ALLOW US TO PROCEED WITH THE ARRAY DESIGN (1.1.2.1.3), BUT MAY MAKE THESE ARRAY DESIGNS LESS EFFECTIVE WHEN APPLIED TO OTHER PIGS THAT MAY HAVE DIFFERENT SPINAL ANATOMY. THIS RISK CAN BE FURTHER MINIMIZED BY SELECTING MINIPIGS THAT SHARE THE SAME GENERAL ANATOMICAL FEATURES (WEIGHT, LENGTH, ETC.) AND, IF NECESSARY, BY EXAMINING THEIR MRI SCANS TO DETERMINE HOW SIMILAR THEIR ANATOMY IS TO THE PIGS USED TO MAKE THE DESIGN BEFORE INITIATING THE IMPLANTATION SURGERY.

RISK MANAGEMENT (COVID): SOME ASPECTS OF THIS SUB-SUBTASK CAN BE ACHIEVED REMOTELY BY CONDUCTING THE IMAGING AT UBC (VANCOUVER) AND SENDING THESE IMAGES TO EPFL/CHUV (SWITZERLAND). BUT THE IN-VIVO EXPERIMENTATION SHALL REQUIRE INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL FOR THE EPFL TEAM TO COME TO VANCOUVER. COVID-RELATED TRAVEL RESTRICTIONS MAY THEREFORE BECOME PROBLEMATIC. PROGRESS SHALL BE SLOWED IF THE COURTINE TEAM CANNOT TRAVEL TO VANCOUVER TO SUPPORT THESE IN VIVO EXPERIMENTS. ONCE THE DATA IS PREPROCESSED, THE NEXT STAGE IS SCENARIO RECONSTRUCTION, WHICH INVOLVES CREATING
A COMPREHENSIVE AND ACCURATE DIGITAL TWIN OF THE DRIVING ENVIRONMENT. MULTI-MODAL DATA FROM
CAMERAS, LIDAR, RADAR, AND OTHER SENSORS WILL BE FUSED TO BUILD A HIGH-FIDELITY 3D REPRESENTATION
OF THE SCENE USING THE 3D GAUSSIAN SPLATTING TECHNIQUE. THIS RECONSTRUCTION WILL NOT ONLY CAPTURE
THE GEOMETRY OF THE ENVIRONMENT BUT ALSO ENABLE SEMANTIC LABELING, WHERE OBJECTS SUCH AS
VEHICLES, PEDESTRIANS, TRAFFIC SIGNS, AND LANE MARKINGS WILL BE IDENTIFIED AND CLASSIFIED. SUCH
SEMANTIC CLASSIFICATION IS VITAL FOR UNDERSTANDING THE CONTEXT AND BEHAVIOR OF DYNAMIC AGENTS
WITHIN THE SCENE. IN PARALLEL, THE SYSTEM WILL EXTRACT THE TRAJECTORIES OF ALL DYNAMIC AGENTS, SUCH
AS VEHICLES AND PEDESTRIANS. THESE TRAJECTORIES PROVIDE A TEMPORAL RECORD OF HOW EACH AGENT
MOVES THROUGH THE ENVIRONMENT, FORMING THE BASIS FOR REALISTIC SCENARIO MODELING AND ANALYSIS.
III. EDGE CASE GENERATION VIA NATURAL LANGUAGE INTERFACE TO FURTHER ENRICH SIMULATION SCENARIOS AND TEST THE ROBUSTNESS OF AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS, EDGE
CASE GENERATION WILL BE ENABLED THROUGH LARGE VLMS. THE SYSTEM WILL ALLOW USERS TO DESCRIBE
DESIRED MODIFICATIONS OR RARE EVENTS IN PLAIN ENGLISH. FOR EXAMPLE, A USER MIGHT SPECIFY, “ADD A
JAYWALKING PEDESTRIAN AT THE NEXT INTERSECTION.” THE VLM WILL INTERPRET THESE INSTRUCTIONS AND
AUTOMATICALLY GENERATE THE CORRESPONDING MODIFICATIONS TO THE SCENARIO, SUCH AS PLACING NEW
OBJECTS, ALTERING ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS, OR INTRODUCING RARE AND CHALLENGING EVENTS.
IV. SCENARIO VIRTUALIZATION
WITH THE RECONSTRUCTED SCENE AND AGENT TRAJECTORIES IN HAND, THE WORKFLOW WILL ADVANCE TO
SCENARIO VIRTUALIZATION. HERE, THE DETAILED 3D SCENES AND EXTRACTED AGENT MOVEMENTS WILL BE
CONVERTED INTO FORMATS COMPATIBLE WITH LEADING SIMULATION PLATFORMS, SUCH AS CARLA. THIS
CONVERSION ENSURES THAT ALL SPATIAL, TEMPORAL, AND SEMANTIC DETAILS ARE PRESERVED FOR HIGH-FIDELITY
SIMULATION. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROCESS WILL ENSURE COMPATIBILITY WITH STANDARD SCENARIO DESCRIPTION
LANGUAGES LIKE OPENSCENARIO [10] AND OPENDRIVE [11], WHICH ARE WIDELY USED FOR DEFINING ROAD
NETWORKS, TRAFFIC FLOWS, AND AGENT BEHAVIORS IN SIMULATION ENVIRONMENTS.

WE PROPOSE EXTENSIONS TO PROJECTGL’S MODELING AND SIMULATION FRAMEWORK, RELYING ON CRUXGL CORE AND

EXPLORATION OF ALTERNATIVE COMMAND ARCHITECTURES (E.G., DOCTRINAL PLANNING VS. BIDDING-BASED DECISION
SYSTEMS) TO EVALUATE DECISION-MAKING EFFECTIVENESS IN HUMAN-MACHINE TEAMS (HMT).
AN INTEGRATED AGENT-BASED MODELING LAYER SIMULATES HUMAN AND AUTONOMOUS ACTORS (E.G., SQUADS, UAS

GENERATION AND INTERACTION UNDER DEGRADED OR CONTESTED CONDITIONS, WITH FULL LOGGING OF DECISIONS,
COMMUNICATIONS, AND STATE TRANSITIONS FOR ANALYSIS.
THE TESTBED INCORPORATES CYBER, ELECTRONIC WARFARE (EW), AND INFORMATION OPERATIONS TO EVALUATE
RESILIENCE IN CONTESTED ENVIRONMENTS. SIMULATED C2 TRAFFIC RUNS OVER A REALISTIC NETWORK BACKBONE,
ENABLING INJECTION OF CYBER EFFECTS (E.G., SPOOFING, JAMMING, MALWARE).
WE USE A MISSION ENGINEERING APPROACH GROUNDED IN ARMY DOCTRINE (FM 3-0, ATP 3-90, JP 3-12).
SCENARIOS ARE ENCODED USING SYSML/LML TO TRACE TASKS TO DOCTRINAL SOURCES. FOR EXAMPLE, A COMBINED
ARMS ASSAULT INCLUDES RECONNAISSANCE, FIRES, MANEUVER, AND CONSOLIDATION PHASES LINKED TO AUTHORITATIVE
GUIDANCE. INNOSLATE FLAGS PROCEDURAL DEVIATIONS USING MODEL LOGS.
THE TESTBED SUPPORTS RIGOROUS EVALUATION OF HMT TTPS USING THE FOLLOWING METRICS:
• TTP EFFECTIVENESS: MISSION SUCCESS RATE, TIME TO OBJECTIVE, ATTRITION.
• COORDINATION: COMMUNICATION FREQUENCY, TEAMWORK GRAPHS, TASK HANDOFF METRICS.
• HUMAN-AI TRUST: OPERATOR SURVEYS, OVERRIDE RATES, TRUST CALIBRATION INDICES.
• ADAPTABILITY: RE-PLANNING TIME, MISSION RECOVERY AFTER DISRUPTIONS.
• CONTESTED PERFORMANCE: IMPACT OF EW/CYBER ACTIONS ON MISSION OUTCOMES.
MACHINE LEARNING AND DATA MINING ARE APPLIED TO LOG DATA TO DISCOVER PATTERNS OF EFFECTIVE HMT
BEHAVIOR. RESULTS ARE VISUALIZED IN DASHBOARDS AND AFTER-ACTION REPORTS, ENABLING CONTINUOUS REFINEMENT OF TTPS AND DOCTRINAL ASSUMPTIONS.

APPLICABILITY, SPECIFICALLY FOR AUTONOMOUS GROUND VEHICLES OPERATING IN OFF-ROAD ENVIRONMENTS FOR THE U.S.
ARMY, ARC, AND GVSC. THIS FRAMEWORK, KNOWN AS THE NEURAL MEMORY ORGANIZATION SYSTEM (NEMOSYS),
INTEGRATES TWO DISTINCT COMPONENTS: EPISODIC MEMORY (EM) AND SEMANTIC MEMORY (SM). DESPITE THEIR
FUNDAMENTAL DIFFERENCES, THESE SYSTEMS WORK IN TANDEM TO UNDERSTAND TEMPORAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN
SEMANTIC ENTITIES (FROM SM TO EM) AND ENHANCE KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIFIC SCENARIOS BY RECOGNIZING REPEATED
TEMPORAL DEPENDENCIES (FROM EM TO SM). THIS FEEDBACK LOOP WILL ENABLE AUTONOMOUS GROUND VEHICLES TO
CATEGORIZE THEIR EXPERIENCES INTO A FUNDAMENTAL SET OF UNIQUE SCENARIOS AND TRACK TEMPORAL PATTERNS
WITHIN EACH CATEGORY. WE BELIEVE THAT THIS SYMBIOTIC INTERACTION WILL ALLOW AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS TO BE
TRAINED LIKE SOLDIERS PROGRESSING THROUGH TRAINING CAMP, WHERE THEY RECALL SPECIALIZED KNOWLEDGE AND
STRATEGIES FOR DISTINCT SCENARIOS ENCOUNTERED IN THE BATTLEFIELD. MORE SPECIFICALLY, NEMOSYS WILL ENABLE THE
AGENTS TO REFLECT ON PAST EXPERIENCES, IMPROVING THEIR UNDERSTANDING OF CURRENT OPERATING CONDITIONS AND
OPTIMIZING THEIR PERFORMANCE BASED ON THE SPECIFIC SCENARIO (SM) AND THEIR EXPECTATIONS OF FUTURE EVENTS
(EM). NEMOSYS WILL BE DEVELOPED WITH TRADITIONAL HARDWARE IN MIND, SUCH AS VON NEUMANN PROCESSORS OR
GRAPHICS PROCESSING UNITS. THEREFORE, WE DO NOT AIM TO USE ANY SPECIALIZED NEUROMORPHIC HARDWARE THAT
COULD LIMIT THE APPLICABILITY OF NEMOSYS IN BATTLEFIELD ENVIRONMENTS WHERE HARDWARE MUST BE RIGOROUSLY
DEVELOPED AND VALIDATED BEFORE DEPLOYMENT.

RQ1: CAN AN AUTONOMOUS AGENT MAKE VERIFIABLE PLANNING DECISIONS AT OPERATIONAL SPEEDS? IF A SYSTEM
IS GOING TO BE DEPLOYED IN REAL-WORLD MISSIONS, ITS DECISIONS NEED TO BE COMPUTATIONALLY TRACTABLE FOR THE
SIZE, WEIGHT, AND POWER (SWAP) CONSTRAINTS OF THE AUTONOMOUS SYSTEM. WHILE UGVS ARE LESS SWAPCONSTRAINED
THAN SMALL UAS, THEY CANNOT UTILIZE AS MUCH COMPUTATIONAL POWER AND TIME AS GRID- OR CLOUDBASED
OPTIMIZERS OFTEN LEVERAGE. THEREFORE, WE SEEK A NEW METHOD FOR CASTING THESE DECISION PROBLEMS
THAT IS AMENABLE TO SOLVING ON LOW-SWAP HARDWARE AT HIGH SPEEDS.
RQ2: CAN THE DECISION PROCESS INCORPORATE DYNAMIC UPDATES TO THE ENVIRONMENT AND THE MISSION? IN
ADDITION TO BEING FAST TO COMPUTE, SOLUTIONS NEED TO EASILY INCORPORATE DYNAMIC INFORMATION AT RUN TIME,
AS OPERATING CONDITIONS CHANGE. WHILE PURELY SYMBOLIC METHODS MAINTAIN A GRAPH OBJECT THAT CAN BE
INCREMENTALLY UPDATED, ADDING INCREMENTAL UPDATES TO AN OPTIMIZATION PROBLEM CAN REQUIRE AN ENTIRELY
NEW SOLUTION PROCESS. THUS, A SOLUTION METHOD THAT CAN BE INCREMENTALLY UPDATED IS CRITICAL.

OCCUR WITH SINGLE-CHANNEL PROCESSING. XR TECHNOLOGIES ENABLE THE ABILITY TO MANIPULATE: 1) THE SENSORY
CHANNELS AVAILABLE TO A USER DURING A TASK, 2) THE TYPE OF INFORMATION TO BE DELIVERED ON THE SENSORY

TYPE, AND LEVEL OF PROCESSING REQUIRED OF THE INFORMATION FOR EACH SENSORY CHANNEL, WE CAN IMPROVE
INDIVIDUAL TASK PERFORMANCE AND, THEREBY, OVERALL TEAM PERFORMANCE BY ALLOCATING TASKS CONTINGENT ON
INDIVIDUAL MEMBER SENSORY PROCESSING BURDEN.

THE MAIN SOURCE OF INFORMATION FOR A BIOMEDICAL MODEL IS EXTRACTED BY TEXT MINING TOOLS IN A FORM OF
INDEX CARDS. UNFORTUNATELY, INDEX CARDS CAN CONTAIN CONTRADICTORY INFORMATION. USING THE INFORMATION
FROM THE INDEX CARD, WE PLAN TO UTILIZE BAYESIAN PROBABILITY THEORY TO CALCULATE THE LIKELIHOOD OF A
STATEMENT EXTRACTED FROM THE LITERATURE BY TEXT MINING TO DESCRIBE A TRUE EVENT IN NATURE. IN THE FIRST
INSTANCE WE WILL IDENTIFYING WHAT PROBABILITIES MAY BE OBTAINABLE BASED ON THE INFORMATION SUPPLIED.
PROVENANCE PROBABILITY: PROBABILITY THAT ANY STATEMENT EXTRACTED FROM A JOURNAL, J, IS TRUE IN NATURE.
HERE WE CAN ESTIMATE THE VALUES FOR EVERY JOURNAL USING THEIR AVERAGE JOURNAL IMPACT FACTOR FROM THE
SCIENCE CI- TATION INDEX WHICH IS DOWNLOADABLE FROM THE WEB OF SCIENCE.

ACCURATELY EXTRACTED. AN EXAMPLE OF AN EVENT IS Ã¢Â‚¬ËŒGENE EXPRESSIONÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢.
GROUND PROBABILITY: PROBABILITY THAT THE PARTICIPANTS IN A STATEMENT EXTRACTED BY TEXT MINING (USUALLY
A PROTEIN/GENE AND A DRUG) CAN BE GROUNDED. WE CAN CONFIRM THIS BY TRYING TO GROUND THE PARTICIPANTS.
TEXTUAL PROBABILITY: PROBABILITY THAT A STATEMENT HAS BEEN ACCU- RATELY EXTRACTED FROM A PAPER BY TEXT
MINING.

BERKELEY WILL FOCUS ON PROVIDING BIOLOGICAL INSPIRATION FOR THE DESIGN OF MOBILE ROBOTS THAT ARE 
CAPABLE OF DYNAMIC TRANSITIONS BETWEEN DIFFERENT LOCOMOTION MODES. THE RESEARCH AT BERKELEY
WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE FOLLOWING TASKS:
TASK 1. ANIMAL USE OF MORPHOLOGICAL COMPOSITION.
OUR MORPHOLOGICAL AND BEHAVIORAL REDUCTIONS EXPOSE DESIGN OPPORTUNITIES IN NEW AND OFTEN COMPLEX 
WAYS WHOSE SURFACE WE HAVE MERELY SCRATCHED IN [14]. THESE RELATIONSHIPS SUGGEST VARIOUS POSSIBLE 
DESIGN SYNERGIES WHEREBY THE MORPHOLOGY OF THE OVERALL SYSTEM BEST FACILITATES COEXISTENCE OF THE 
COMPOSED CONTROLLERS AND/OR MAXIMIZES THE ACCURACY OF THEIR PARALLEL AND SEQUENTIAL COMPOSITION. 
THIS NEW EFFORT BRINGS THESE QUESTIONS TO THE FOREFRONT SINCE THE MECHANICAL COMPLEXITY OF 
SELF-RIGHTING NECESSITATES OUR SEEKING TO RECOGNIZE, ISOLATE EXTRACT AND MODEL PARALLEL AND 
SEQUENTIAL COMPOSITIONS OF TEMPLATES THAT DO NOT INTUITIVELY ADMIT A SINGLE TEMPLATE 
REPRESENTATION. OUR POLYPEDAL LABORATORY HAS A LONG HISTORY OF LEADERSHIP ON METHODOLOGIES FOR SUCH 
IDENTIFICATION AND MODELING, STARTING FROM, HISTORICALLY, THE VERY FIRST SUCH WORK IN THE 
LITERATURE - ON THE SLIP AND LLS RUNNING MODELS - AND CONTINUING TO THE PRESENT DAY, NOW DEVELOPING 
MORE RAPIDLY WITH THE RISE OF OUR GROWING COHORT OF TRAINEES. OUR EFFORT WILL ATTEMPT AS WELL TO 
INTEGRATE THIS SEARCH FOR TEMPLATE PRIMITIVES ACROSS DIFFERENT SPECIES AS IN SO AS TO DERIVE 
CLUES ABOUT THEIR NECESSARILY DISTINCTIVE MORPHOLOGICAL (AND
BEHAVIORAL) REDUCTIONS.
TASK 2. MULTIFUNCTIONALITY AND EQUIVALENCE IN ANIMAL REORIENTATION
WE HAVE A WEALTH OF KINEMATICS, FORCE, AND MORPHOMETRICS DATA FOR LIZARDS (AGAMA AGAMA) PERFORMING 
NON-STEADY MANEUVERS IN BOTH THE SAGITTAL AND HORIZONTAL PLANES, ALONG WITH ANCHOR MODELS OF THE 
LIZARDS IN BOTH PLANES. AS AN IMMEDIATE FIRST EXPLORATION OF AIMS 1 & 2, WE WILL ANCHOR EXISTING 
TEMPLATE MODELS OF INERTIAL REORIENTATION IN THE SAGITTAL PLANE AND TURNING IN THE HORIZONTAL PLANE 
TO EXPLAIN THE DESIGN TRADEOFFS WITH RESPECT TO DIFFERING TASKS.

TASK 3. PARALLEL AND SEQUENTIAL COMPOSITION IN ANIMAL REORIENTATION
WE HAVE RECENTLY BEGUN A COMPARATIVE STUDY ON RIGHTING TO ENUMERATE THE MANY POSSIBLE RIGHTING 
STRATEGIES AND ADVISE ON THE DESIGN OF MOBILE ROBOTS IN THIS NEW PROJECT, WE WILL USE EXISTING DATA 
AND NEW EXPERIMENTS TO EXAMINE THE ROLE OF MORPHOLOGY IN DETERMINING EFFICACIOUS STRATEGIES FOR THE 
DIVERSE SPECIES OF STUDY (LIZARDS AND CRABS) AND HOW MULTIPLE STRATEGIES MIGHT BE COMPOSED
TO INCREASE PERFORMANCE OR OVERCOME TERRAIN CHALLENGES.

PREVIOUS WORK IN OUR POLYPEDAL LABORATORY ON INSECTS REVEALED A DIVERSITY OF RIGHTING
STRATEGIES AS VARIED AS THE ANIMALS THEMSELVES. EACH OF THREE SPECIES OF COCKROACH HAS A DIFFERENT 
PREFERRED STRATEGY THAT APPEARS TIED TO ITS MORPHOLOGICAL AFFORDANCES (WINGS, LONG LEGS, ETC.). BY 
CONTRAST, INDIVIDUAL LIZARDS MAY EXHIBIT MANY STRATEGIES EVEN IN THE SAME SETTING. WHY WOULD AN 
ANIMAL EXHIBIT SO MANY SOLUTIONS TO THE SAME BEHAVIOR? WE HYPOTHESIZE THREE ADVANTAGES. FIRST, BODY 
SHAPE CAN CHANGE SUBSTANTIALLY OVER A LIFETIME, PARTICULARLY DUE TO APPENDAGE LOSS (E.G. TAIL 
AUTOTOMY). SECOND, STRATEGIES MAY VARY IN EFFICACY WITH RESPECT TO INITIAL CONDITIONS (POSTURE).
THIRD, TERRAIN FEATURES MAY DICTATE DIVERSE STRATEGIES. WE WILL TEST EACH OF THESE THREE HYPOTHESES

EXPERIMENTALLY IN OUR ANIMAL AND ROBOT MODEL SYSTEMS AND USE THE RESULTS TO REFINE OR REFUTE 
PUTATIVE TEMPLATE COMPOSITIONS. WE WILL CATEGORIZE OBSERVED RESPONSES BY TEMPLATE AND MEASURE THE 
PERFORMANCE (RIGHTING DURATION, PROBABILITY OF FAILURE, SENSITIVITY TO TERRAIN) OF EACH MODE.
WE HYPOTHESIZE AT LEAST THREE GENERAL, PHYSICALLY DISTINCT STRATEGIES ACROSS ALL SPECIES STUDIED SO 
FAR. APPENDAGES MAY GENERATE RIGHTING TORQUES BY CONTACTING THE SUBSTRATE FAR FROM THE CENTER OF 
MASS (PUSHING WITH THE TAIL OR WITH A LEG). APPENDAGES SWUNG RAPIDLY IN THE AIR CAN INDUCE INERTIAL 
TORQUES AS IN AERIAL RIGHTING (TAIL SWEEPING). BODIES CAN CHANGE SHAPE TO MO

IN THE PROPOSED HETEROGENEOUS DIVERSE TEAM COMPOSED OF ROBOTS AND HUMANS ENGAGED IN A COMPLEX MISSION, IT IS INEVITABLE THAT ASSETS WILL DEGRADE OR FAIL, FOR EXAMPLE, DUE TO COMMUNICATION FAILURE, GPS OUTAGE OR JAMMING, DEGRADED VISUAL CONDITIONS, FOR A SUBSET OF THE AGENTS. THIS TASK FOCUSES ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF A FORMAL MATHEMATICAL FRAMEWORK WHERE HETEROGENEOUS CAPABILITIES OF A SWARM, INCLUDING AUTONOMOUS AGENTS, COMPUTATIONAL RESOURCES, AND HUMAN TEAMMATES AND DECISION MAKERS, CAN BE ENCODED USING COMPUTATIONALLY MANIPULABLE ABSTRACTIONS. THESE ABSTRACTIONS WILL PROVIDE THE FRAMEWORK FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF ARCHITECTURES AND ALGORITHMS WHERE SWARM AUTONOMY CAN BE COMPOSED BY COMBINING AND ASSEMBLING
PERCEPTION-ACTION-COMMUNICATION LOOPS THROUGHOUT AN AUTONOMOUS NETWORK TO SATISFY TASK REQUIREMENTS.

REQUIREMENTS AS A FUNCTION OF AGENT TRAITS, THIS TASK APPLIES THESE MODELS TO PERFORM ONLINE, DECENTRALIZED, TASK ALLOCATION AND PLANNING FOR THE COLLECTIVE."

OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO PRODUCE ACTION PLANS AND TASKS THAT CAN BE EXECUTED IN A DECENTRALIZED MANNER BY MULTIPLE AGENTS WITH HETEROGENEOUS (AND POSSIBLY TIME-VARYING) CAPABILITIES, WITH THE ABILITY TO EXPLORE COST VERSUS PERFORMANCE TRADE-OFFS, AND ANALYSE THE IMPACT OF HETEROGENEITY.

SCOPE OF WORK:
 DEVELOPMENT OF GRAPH NEURAL NETWORK-BASED METHODS FOR MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS ENGAGED IN
COMPLEX COORDINATION TASKS.
 DEVELOPMENT OF METHODOLOGY THAT FACILITATES THE TRANSFER OF GRAPH NEURAL NETWORK-BASED POLICIES
FROM SIMULATED ENVIRONMENTS TO THE REAL WORLD.
 APPLICATION OF LEARNT COORDINATION POLICIES TO MULTI-AGENT PATH PLANNING, NAVIGATION AND
COLLABORATIVE MAPPING TASKS. INTEGRATION OF METHODS THAT FACILITATE FIRST-PERSON VIEW NAVIGATION.
 DEVELOPMENT OF METHODS THAT FACILITATE THE USAGE OF LEARNT COORDINATION POLICIES IN HETEROGENEOUS
TEAMS, WITH AN INITIAL FOCUS ON HETEROGENEOUS COMMUNICATION CAPABILITIES.
 EXPLORATION OF THE IMPACT OF HETEROGENEOUS AGENT CAPABILITIES ON TEAM PERFORMANCE WITH RESPECT TO
DYNAMIC CHANGES IN MISSION REQUIREMENTS AND ADVERSARIAL CONDITIONS."

"RESEARCH CONDUCTED AT UC BERKELEY WILL CONTRIBUTE TO THE FOLLOWING RESEARCH AREAS DISCUSSED IN DETAIL IN THE MAIN PROJECT PROPOSAL. THIS IS A FUNDAMENTAL RESEARCH PROJECT THAT IS NOT EXPECTED TO PRODUCE ANY
DEVELOPMENTAL ITEMS. SHOULD ANY DEVELOPMENTAL ITEMS RESULT FROM THIS WORK, THEY WILL HAVE BOTH CIVILIAN AND MILITARY APPLICATIONS.
RA 1.1: HIERARCHICAL AND COMPOSABLE PERCEPTION AND LEARNING
THIS TASK WILL FOCUS ON DESIGNING LEARNING ALGORITHMS THAT ARE MODULAR AND COMPOSABLE. WE WILL DEVELOP ANALYTIC MODULES THAT CAN BE INCORPORATED INTO A LEARNING SYSTEM VIA A MODULAR FRAMEWORK, FORCING THE LEARNED MODULES TO ADAPT TO THE BEHAVIOR OF THE ANALYTIC MODULES AND THEREBY ENSURING GOOD PERFORMANCE OF THE ENTIRE SYSTEM. THESE MODULES WOULD BE COMPOSED TO ACCOMPLISH MISSION PARAMETERS ON DEMAND, AND WOULD COOPERATE BOTH WITH OTHER MODULES WITHIN A SINGLE VEHICLE, AND ACROSS DIFFERENT VEHICLES IN SWARMS AND HUMAN-ROBOT TEAMS. OUR APPROACH WILL INCORPORATE HETEROGENEOUS AND DYNAMICALLY
RECONFIGURABLE STRUCTURE AND BOTH LEARNED MODULES AND DIFFERENTIABLE ANALYTIC MODULES SUCH AS MOTION PLANNERS, EFFECTIVELY HYBRIDIZING LEARNING AND MODEL-BASED DECISION MAKING ON SCALES RANGING FROM
REACTIVE CONTROL TO MISSION-LENGTH PLANNING.
RA 3.2 DATA RESILIENT MACHINE LEARNING
THIS TASK WILL FOCUS ON A RIGOROUS FUSION OF PROBABILISTIC GENERATIVE MODELS WITH DEEP NEURAL NETWORKS AND OTHER DISCRIMINATIVE MODELS. THE EXPRESSIVE POWER OF DISCRIMINATIVE MODELS COMBINED WITH PROBABILISTIC
PRIORS FROM GENERATIVE MODELS WILL ALLOW THE SWARM TO RELY ON LEARNED MODELS IN UNEXPECTED OR EVEN ADVERSARIAL CONDITIONS WITHOUT EXHIBITING SIGNIFICANTLY DEGRADED PERFORMANCE OR UNEXPECTED BEHAVIOR. WE
WILL BUILD LEARNING SYSTEMS THAT ARE RESILIENT AND ROBUST TO OUT-OF-DOMAIN INPUTS, ADVERSARIAL PERTURBATION, AND SUBSTANTIAL CHANGES OVER TIME IN NONSTATIONARY SETTINGS. WE CAN CATEGORIZE UNEXPECTED PERTURBATIONS
INTO THREE CATEGORIES: (1) OUT-OF-DOMAIN INPUTS THAT WERE NOT SEEN DURING TRAINING; (2) ADVERSARIAL INPUTS THAT ARE INTENTIONALLY DESIGNED TO CONFUSE OR DEGRADE THE LEARNING SYSTEM; (3) SYSTEMATIC CHANGES IN THE
ENVIRONMENT THAT REQUIRE EXPLICIT ADAPTATION (AS OPPOSED TO SIMPLE DISTURBANCE REJECTION). WE WILL ADDRESS (1) THROUGH THE USE OF PROBABILISTIC MODELS THAT ESTIMATE THE CONFIDENCE OF THE LEARNED MODEL.
WE WILL ADDRESS (2) THROUGH ADVERSARIAL TRAINING, INCLUDING NOVEL ADVERSARIAL REINFORCEMENT LEARNING TECHNIQUES. TO ADDRESS (3), WE WILL DEVELOP FAST ADAPTATION TECHNIQUES FOR AUTONOMOUS BEHAVIOR BASED
ON META-LEARNING."

USING VISUAL INFORMATION CAN ALSO LEAD TO EXTRA ROBUSTNESS IF THE WIRELESS COMMUNICATION
CHANNEL MIGHT TURN TOO NOISY OR EVEN COMPROMISED BY ADVERSARIES.
WE ARE HENCE MOTIVATED TO STUDY WHETHER VISUAL INPUTS CAN BE INTEGRATED TO ENHANCE THE
DAGNN-BASED DECENTRALIZED CONTROLLER LEARNING WITH LOCAL SPARSE COMMUNICATIONS. OUR GOAL IS
TO COMBINE THE BEST OF BOTH WORLDS : STRIKING A MORE FAVORABLE BALANCE BETWEEN EFFECTIVENESS
(THROUGH MULTI-MODALITY FUSION) AND EFFICIENCY (THROUGH ONE-HOP ONLY COMMUNICATION). OUR
RESEARCH AGENDA WILL BE UNFOLDED INTO THREE OBJECTIVES, WHOSE DETAILS ARE EXPANDED NEXT:

OBJECTIVE 1 AIMS TO CONSTRUCT THE MAIN PIPELINE FOR FUSING VISUAL AND STATE INPUTS IN THE DAGNN
FRAMEWORK. WE WILL START BY USING DRONENET [7] TO EXTRACT HIDDEN FEATURES FROM EACH DRONES
VISUAL INPUTS. AT EACH TIME, EACH DRONE COMMUNICATES THE FEATURES TO ITS ONE-HOP NEIGHBOR,
WHICH AGGREGATES THOSE FEATURES WITH ITS OWN VISUAL FEATURES, USING ELEMENT-WISE AVERAGE OR
MAX POOLING. THE AGGREGATED VISUAL FEATURES WILL THEN BE FED TOGETHER WITH THE STATE FEATURES
INTO DAGNN TO LEARN THE DECENTRALIZED CONTROLLER, AS DESCRIBED IN [4].
BUILT ON THIS NAIVE BASELINE (WHICH COULD BE CONSIDERED AS EARLY FUSION [9] IN COMPUTER
VISION), WE WILL INVESTIGATE DIFFERENT KINDS OF FUSION STRATEGIES, E.G., PROGRESSIVE FUSION, AS BOTH
VISUAL AND STATE INPUTS CAN BE HANDLED BY CNNS AND MIGHT THUS PARTIALLY SHARE THEIR FEATURE
EXTRACTION BACKBONE TO BE OPTIMIZED FOR A COMMON LATENT FEATURE SPACE.
OBJECTIVE 2 AIMS TO IMPROVE THE PIPELINE ADAPTIVITY AND ROBUSTNESS BY INJECTING CONFIDENCE/
UNCERTAINTY AWARENESS INTO THE FUSION PROCESS. SPECIFICALLY, MULTIPLE SOURCES CAN GIVE RISE TO
CONFLICT INFORMATION, AND NOT ALL INPUTS ARE EQUALLY TRUSTWORTHY AT ALL MOMENTS. FOR EXAMPLE, THE
VISUAL PERCEPTION MIGHT NOT BE VERY RELIABLE, IF TWO DRONES ARE VERY DISTANT AWAY SUCH THAT EVEN
RECOGNITION/LOCALIZATION OF EACH OTHER BECOMES HARD. THEREFORE, IT IS IMPORTANT TO QUANTIFY AND
MONITOR THE CONFIDENCE OF EACH INPUT, BASED ON WHICH WE COULD PERFORM ADAPTIVE FUSION THAT
ALWAYS WEIGHS MORE ON THE MORE CONFIDENT MODALITY AT THE MOMENT. THE BASELINE APPROACH
COULD BE IMPLEMENTED BY UTILIZING THE CURRENT FEATURE BACKBONES PREDICTION ENTROPY (E.G., FOR
DRONENET WITH SOFTMAX OUTPUT), AS WELL AS THE PREDICTION VARIANCE IN THE PAST TRAJECTORY. FOR
MORE ADVANCED OPTIONS, WE MIGHT CONSIDER THE TOOL OF BAYESIAN UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION [10].

HIERARCHICAL NET-MARS WILL BE MODELED AS A MULTILAYER COEVOLVING ADAPTIVE GRAPH TO
CAPTURE THE INTRA-TEAM AND INTER-TEAM ORGANIZATION OF THE MULTIAGENT SYSTEM, IN ORDER TO ENABLE
EFFECTIVE CHARACTERIZATION OF THE SYSTEM BEHAVIOR. THE MULTILAYER MODEL HAS THREE LAYERS: (1)
COMMUNICATION MULTIGRAPHS, (2) INFORMATION MULTI GRAPHS, AND (3) COLLABORATION MULTIGRAPHS. EACH
OF THESE LAYERS CONSISTS OF (1) AGENT-LEVEL GRAPH AND (2) ONE OR MULTIPLE TEAM-LEVEL GRAPHS. THE
AGENTS IN EACH TEAM ARE PROJECTED TO A NODE IN A HIGHER-LEVEL, SO EACH NODE IN THE HIGHER LAYER
REPRESENTS ONE OF THE TEAMS. TWO TEAMS ARE CONNECTED IF THERE IS A LINK BETWEEN THEIR CONSTITUENT
NODES IN THE LOWER LEVEL, OR IF THEY ARE IN DELTA-PROXIMITY OF EACH OTHER AND CAN ESTABLISH A
COMMUNICATION LINK AS A TEAM WITH THE OTHER TEAMS BY SWARM-TO-SWARM BEAMFORMING. THE
COMMUNICATION GRAPH WILL BE MODELED AS A -PROXIMITY GRAPH, AND THE INFORMATION GRAPH WILL BE
MODELED AS AN UNDIRECTED MULTIGRAPH WITH WEIGHTS CORRESPONDING TO INTRA AND INTER TEAM ATTRACTION

BY INTEGRATING RETRIEVAL AUGMENTED GENERATION (RAG) AND HIERARCHICAL SCENE GRAPHS, THIS FRAMEWORK WILL ENHANCE COORDINATION, PLANNING, AND SITUATIONAL AWARENESS IN UNPREDICTABLE ENVIRONMENTS SUCH AS DISASTER RESPONSE. 2. PROBLEM STATEMENT CURRENT MULTI-AGENT COORDINATION SYSTEMS RELY ON DIRECT EXCHANGES OF BASIC DATA, SUCH AS MAPS OR PLANS, WHICH LIMIT THE ABILITY TO DYNAMICALLY ADAPT TO CHANGING ENVIRONMENTS AND SHARED KNOWLEDGE ACROSS AGENTS. MOREOVER, THE LACK OF COMMON GROUND FOR DIALOGUE AND TASK COORDINATION BETWEEN AGENTS RESTRICTS AUTONOMY AND FLEXIBILITY. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THESE LIMITATIONS BY CREATING A SYSTEM THAT GROUNDS CONCRETE, ABSTRACT, AND FUNCTIONAL PROPERTIES IN A SHARED, QUERYABLE FRAMEWORK. AGENTS WILL BE ABLE TO PLAN, COMMUNICATE, AND UPDATE THEIR KNOWLEDGE AUTONOMOUSLY IN A DECENTRALIZED MANNER, SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVING THE EFFICIENCY AND ADAPTABILITY OF MULTI-ROBOT TEAMS IN COMPLEX ENVIRONMENTS. 3. T2C2A: ADAPTIVE TASK ALLOCATION FOR HETEROGENEOUS MULTI-ROBOT TEAMS
WE WILL PRODUCE A COMPUTATIONALLY EFFICIENT AND ADAPTIVE FRAMEWORK FOR DEPLOYING HETEROGENEOUS RESOURCES TO CARRY OUT A SET OF TASKS. KEY TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF SUCH A FRAMEWORK WILL BE THE OBSERVATION THAT A LOCAL, INTROSPECTIVE, REAL-TIME EVALUATION OF HOW WELL A PARTICULAR AGENT IS CARRYING OUT A PARTICULAR TASK ALLOWS FOR A RESILIENT AND ADAPTIVE GOOD ENOUGH TASK ALLOCATION STRATEGY. ONE PARTICULAR MANIFESTATION OF THIS IDEA WILL BE THAT A PARTICULAR AGENTS SPECIALIZATION TO A PARTICULAR TASK SHOULD EVOLVE OVER TIME BY COMPARING THE MODELLED PROGRESSION TOWARDS THE COMPLETION OF THE TASK TO THE ACTUAL PROGRESSION. IF THE AGENT IS DOING BETTER THAN EXPECTED, ITS SPECIALIZATION GOES UP. IF IT IS DOING WORSE, THE SPECIALIZATION GOES DOWN.
T2C2C: COVERAGE CONTROL AND BOUNDARY PROTECTION WITH HETEROGENEOUS CAPABILITIES
WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW TO UNDERSTAND HETEROGENEITY IN THE CONTEXT OF COVERAGE CONTROL, VIEWED AS A CANONICAL PROBLEM FROM WHICH A NUMBER OF OTHER PROBLEMS CAN BE DERIVED, SUCH A PERIMETER-DEFENSE OR AREA EXPLORATION. IN PARTICULAR, WE WILL INVESTIGATE HETEROGENEITY IN TERMS OF DIFFERENT SENSING AND MOBILITY MODALITIES. THE DEVELOPED ALGORITHMS WILL BE IMPLEMENTED ON TEAMS OF MOBILE ROBOTS.
T2C3G: RAPID LEARNING OF MULTI-ROBOT STRATEGIES FROM HUMAN OPERATORS BASED ON COORDINATED CONTROLS PRIORS
MULTI-ROBOT SYSTEMS ARE TYPICALLY ORGANIZED AROUND SETS OF STANDARDIZED AND WELL-UNDERSTOOD COORDINATED MOTION PRIMITIVES, SUCH AS GEOMETRIC FORMATION CONTROL, COVERAGE CONTROL, FLOCKING AND SWARMING, CYCLIC PURSUIT, RENDEZVOUS, OR BOUNDARY PROTECTION. BY CURATING A LIBRARY OF SUCH COORDINATED MOTION PRIMITIVES, IT SHOULD BE POSSIBLE TO LEARN HOW TO COMBINE THESE PRIMITIVES BY COMPARING HOW EXPERT OPERATORS ENGAGE WITH A TEAM OF ROBOTS. THIS WILL BE DONE AS PART OF THIS TASK, THEREBY BYPASSING THE HIGH-COMPLEXITY LEARNING TASKS OF LEARNING FULL-BLOWN CONTROL POLICIES FROM DATA.
T3C3A - HETEROGENEITY FOR RESILIENCE: TOPOLOGY AND NETWORK ROBUSTNESS
WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW ROBOTS IN A HETEROGENEOUS TEAM, WORKING TOGETHER BY SHARING RESOURCES, CAN BE MADE RESILIENT AS A TEAM TO FAILURES OF INDIVIDUAL COMPONENTS. FOR INSTANCE, IF AN AGENT LOSES A PARTICULAR SENSING MODALITY, THE ENABLING IDEA IS THAT THIS MODALITY CAN BE BORROWED FROM A NEIGHBORING AGENT. OR, BY COMBINING RESOURCES FROM NEIGHBORING AGENTS. OR, BY COMBINING NEIGHBORING RESOURCES WITH THE AGENTS OWN REMAINING RESOURCES. AS SUCH, CENTRAL TO THIS INVESTIGATION WILL BE A FORMAL NOTION OF HOW TO CHARACTERIZE SUCH RESOURCE COMBINATIONS AS WELL AS TYING THEM TO THE UNDERLYING NETWORK TOPOLOGY

THIS TASK THAT I AM INVOLVED WITH ADDRESSES ADVERSARIAL TEAM BEHAVIORS, WITH A SPECIAL FOCUS ON
DECEPTION. ITS GOAL (WHICH I WILL BE DIRECTLY CONTRIBUTING TO) IS TO DEVELOP STRATEGIES FOR TEAM
BEHAVIOR IN MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS, THAT INCLUDE DECEPTION, INCORPORATION OF MODELS OF IMPERFECT
INFORMATION, AND BRIDGING OF THE DIVIDE BETWEEN POPULATION MODELS, MODELS WITH A DISCRETE NUMBER
OF UNIDENTIFIED AGENTS, AND MODELS WITH LABELED/IDENTIFIED AGENTS. IN OUR CONTEXT, DECEPTION IS
DEFINED AS STRATEGIC INFORMATION TRANSMISSION IN WHICH A SENDER SHARES INFORMATION EITHER DIRECTLY
(COMMUNICATION) OR INDIRECTLY (PERCEPTION) WITH A RECEIVER, WITH HOWEVER THE TWO SIDES NOT
SHARING THE SAME OBJECTIVE. THE UNDERLYING DECISION PROBLEM IS THEN A NONZERO-SUM GAME, WHICH
IS DYNAMIC BECAUSE THE RECEIVERS INFORMATION DEPENDS ON THE SIGNAL OR MESSAGE GENERATED BY
THE SENDER. SINCE THE GAME ENTAILS AN INHERENT ASYMMETRY IN THE ROLES OF THE AGENTS, WE TREAT IT
AS A STACKELBERG (LEADER-FOLLOWER) GAME (OR SO-CALLED BAYESIAN PERSUASION) WITH THE SENDER ACTING
AS THE LEADER AND THE RECEIVER ACTING AS THE FOLLOWER. WITHIN THE CONTEXT OF THIS PROJECT, THE
RECEIVER IS VIEWED AS THE ADVERSARY (OR ADVERSARIAL TEAM) TO BE DECEIVED, AND THE GOAL IS TO CRAFT
THE INFORMATION THAT COULD BE AVAILABLE TO THE ADVERSARY TO CONTROL ITS PERCEPTION OF THE
UNDERLYING STATE OF THE SYSTEM AS A DEFENSIVE MEASURE. SINCE A RATIONAL ADVERSARY WOULD MAKE
DECISIONS BASED ON THE INFORMATION AVAILABLE TO IT, THE STRATEGIC CRAFTING OF THE SIGNAL THAT IS SHARED
WITH THE ADVERSARY, OR THE ADVERSARY CAN HAVE ACCESS TO, WILL BE EFFECTIVE IN THAT RESPECT.
THEREFORE, OUR GOAL IS TO DESIGN THE INFORMATION FLOWING FROM THE INFORMED SENDER AGENT TO THE
POSSIBLY UNINFORMED RECEIVER AGENT WHO NEEDS THAT INFORMATION TO TURN IT INTO ACTION, AND TO DO
THIS DECEPTIVELY ALIGNED WITH THE OBJECTIVE OF THE SENDER.

DR. DAIGO SHISHIKA AND HIS PH.D. STUDENT GOUTAM DAS WILL STUDY DISTRIBUTED CONTROL OF AUTONOMOUS AGENTS IN HIGHLY-DYNAMIC ADVERSARIAL ENGAGEMENT. MORE SPECIFICALLY, THEY CONSIDER A SITUATION WHERE THE BLUE-TEAM AGENTS ARE TASKED WITH GUARDING A HIGH-VALUE-TARGET (HVT) THAT IS MOVING THROUGH THE ENVIRONMENT. THE DYNAMICS OF THE HVT BRINGS ADDITIONAL CHALLENGES TO THE WELL-STUDIED VERSION WITH STATIONARY TARGETS. TO OBTAIN EFFECTIVE BLUE-TEAM STRATEGIES WITH PERFORMANCE GUARANTEES, WE FORMULATE THE SCENARIO AS DIFFERENTIAL GAMES AND SEEK TO FIND THE OPTIMAL / EQUILIBRIUM STRATEGIES. BASED ON THE GAME-THEORETIC STRATEGIES WITH STRONG PERFORMANCE GUARANTEES, LEARNING-BASED APPROACHES WILL BE LEVERAGED TO RELAX THE ASSUMPTIONS MADE ON THE INFORMATION STRUCTURE (I.E., SENSING AND COMMUNICATION CAPABILITIES). THE EXPECTED OUTCOME INCLUDES: (I) FORMATION TO BEST PREPARE AGAINST YET UNSEEN RED-TEAM AGENTS, (II) COOPERATIVE DEFENSE STRATEGY TO BEST REACT TO THE DETECTED RED-TEAM AGENTS, AND (III) DECENTRALIZED ALGORITHM THAT CAN PERFORM UNDER LIMITED FIELD OF VIEW AND COMMUNICATION RANGE. THE RESULTS OF THIS RESEARCH WILL PUSH THE STATE-OF-THE-ART IN MULTI-AGENT DIFFERENTIAL GAMES, AND THEY ARE ALSO HIGHLY RELEVANT TO MILITARY OPERATIONS WHERE AN EXPENSIVE, HIGH-CAPABILITY ASSET MUST BE ESCORTED TO ITS DESTINATION PROTECTED BY LOW-COST AUTONOMOUS AGENTS.
