WE ADDRESS A FUNDAMENTAL CHALLENGE OF DETERMINING OPTIMAL STRATEGIES OF COOPERATIVE MULTI-AGENT TEAMS AGAINST PHYSICAL ADVERSARIES IN THE ENVIRONMENT.
BACKGROUND: COOPERATIVE MULTI-AGENT AND ROBOT SYSTEMS REFER TO SYSTEMS OF ENTITIES WORKING TOGETHER TO REASON, PLAN, SOLVE PROBLEMS, THINK ABSTRACTLY, COMPREHEND THE SITUATION, AND LEARN ACCORDINGLY [1]. HERE, INTEGRATING AGENTS' INFORMATION AND STATE TO REASON COLLECTIVELY IS A KEY CHALLENGE IN ATTACKING OR DEFENDING AGAINST ADVERSARIES, ESPECIALLY IN A MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM WITH MANY HETEROGENEOUS AGENTS (E.G., AIR/GROUND VEHICLES) POSSESSING FUNCTIONALLY UNIQUE CAPABILITIES. FURTHER, MULTI-AGENTS COLLECTIVELY MAKING A SUITABLE REAL-TIME DECISION TO ADAPT TO THE CURRENT SITUATION BECOMES CRUCIAL IN ACHIEVING HIGHER SUCCESS PROBABILITIES AND LOWER AGENTS COSTS FOR A MISSION [2]. FURTHERMORE, COOPERATIVE DECISION-MAKING IS ESSENTIAL TO ADDRESS THE THREATS POSED BY PHYSICAL ADVERSARIES OR DETERMINE TRADEOFFS IN TACTICAL NETWORKS [3]. HERE, ADVERSARIES REFER TO AN ENEMY AGENT WHICH CONSCIOUSLY AND ACTIVELY IMPAIRS THE AGENT'S CAPABILITIES. THE EXISTING COOPERATIVE DECISION-MAKING MODELS USE THE MARKOV DECISION PROCESS AND ITS VARIANTS, GAME-THEORETIC METHODS, AND SWARM INTELLIGENCE. CURRENT RESEARCH APPROACHES MAINLY USE REINFORCEMENT LEARNING, OPTIMIZATION, OR MACHINE LEARNING TO FIND OPTIMAL OR SUBOPTIMAL ACTION SEQUENCES BASED ON CURRENT AND PREVIOUS STATES FOR ACHIEVING INDEPENDENT OR TRANSFERRED KNOWLEDGE OF DECISION-MAKING POLICIES. TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES WE ORGANIZE OUR APPROACH INTO TWO TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES THAT ADDRESS THE CHALLENGE OF ENABLING EFFECTIVE ADAPTIVE NAVIGATION BEHAVIORS:

TECHNICAL OBJECTIVE 1: EVALUATE EXISTING TECHNIQUES FOR HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP ROBOT LEARNING (E.G., TAMER [24], LEARNING FROM DEMONSTRATION [35], AND CYCLE-OF-LEARNING [33, 9]) FOR LEARNING ADAPTIVE NAVIGATION BEHAVIORS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL (A) DEVELOP EXPERIMENTAL PLATFORMS - BOTH USING SIMULATORS AND REAL ROBOTIC PLATFORMS - WITH APPROPRIATE NAVIGATION CAPABILITIES AND INTERFACES FOR HUMAN TRAINERS, (B) DEVELOP RELEVANT EXPERIMENTAL SITUATIONS - BOTH IN SIMULATION AND IN REAL 
PHYSICAL SPACES - INVOLVING DYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT CHANGES (E.G., SPECIFYING SPECIFIC OBJECTS OR TERRAIN TO AVOID AFTER THE EXPERIMENT HAS STARTED), AND (C) PERFORM EXPERIMENTS IN THESE SITUATIONS 
TO MEASURE THE EFFICACY OF EXISTING TECHNIQUES FOR ENABLING ADAPTIVE NAVIGATION BEHAVIORS BY ROBOTS.

TECHNICAL OBJECTIVE 2: IMPROVE THESE EXISTING TECHNIQUES FOR HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP ROBOT LEARNING BY DEVELOPING A UNIFIED FRAMEWORK CAPABLE OF LEARNING SIMULTANEOUSLY FROM PRESPECIFIED ENVIRONMENT 
REWARD, HUMAN DEMONSTRATION INFORMATION, AND HUMAN FEEDBACK SIMULTANEOUSLY. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL (A) MODEL AND PROTOTYPE MODIFIED LEARNING FRAMEWORKS THAT UTILIZE ALL OF THE ABOVE-MENTIONED 
SOURCES OF TRAINING INFORMATION (USING, E.G., IDEAS SUCH AS [22, 23] THAT HAVE NOT YET BEEN TESTED ON ROBOTIC PLATFORMS), AND (B) EVALUATE THESE MODIFIED TECHNIQUES IN THE SAME EXPERIMENTAL ENVIRONMENTS SPECIFIED ABOVE. MOREOVER, WE WILL EMPLOY MODERN, EXPRESSIVE FUNCTION APPROXIMATION TECHNIQUES (E.G., DEEP NEURAL NETWORKS) TO MODEL QUANTITIES SUCH AS THE AUTONOMOUS BEHAVIOR POLICY, HUMAN BEHAVIOR POLICIES, AND PREDICTIVE MODELS OF HUMAN FEEDBACK.

APPROACH: FORAGING, AN ANIMALS KEY COGNITIVE NEUROMECHANICAL BEHAVIORAL SUITE, ILLUSTRATES THE
DIVERSITY OF LENGTH AND TIME SCALES OVER WHICH FIT SPECIES PURSUE SURVIVAL TASKS. ANIMAL
MORPHOLOGIES SUPPORT THESE EMBODIED PROBLEM-SOLVING CAPABILITIES THROUGH HIERARCHICAL
INFORMATION PROCESSING AUGMENTED BY STRONG COUPLING BETWEEN HIGHLY DISTRIBUTED SENSING AND
ACTUATION, MATERIAL PROPERTIES, AND PHYSICAL DYNAMICS. NO ENGINEERED SYSTEM HAS EVER COME CLOSE
TO THE EXPLOITATION OF NONLINEARITY, INNOVATIVE MEMORY USE, AND SEEMING INFINITE DIMENSIONAL
LEARNING, ADAPTATION, DEVELOPMENT AND EVOLUTION THAT UNDERLIES SUCH EMBODIED AUTONOMY.
WE PROPOSE A NARROW, BUT INTEGRATED FOCUS, ON KEY RANGES ALONG THIS NEWLY ACCESSIBLE,
SWEEPING SPECTRUM OF ANIMAL LEARNING, WHEN INFORMED BY OUR TOPOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK FOR TRACING
THE NATURE OF AND CONSTRAINTS ON ENERGY AND INFORMATION FLOWS, HAS THE POSSIBILITY TO BREAK OPEN
NEW FOUNDATIONS OF MACHINE AUTONOMY. SPECIFICALLY, WE PROPOSE TO STUDY THE NEUROMECHANICS OF
INTACT, FREE-RUNNING SPECIES (SQUIRRELS) IN ARTIFICIAL FORAGING ENVIRONMENTS WHOSE NAVIGATION
THROUGH EXTREME MOTOR CHALLENGES (DENSELY OBSTRUCTED OR SEVERELY CRATERED PATHWAYS  THE SORT OF
UNSTRUCTURED AND RAPIDLY CHANGING ENVIRONMENTS THAT CONFOUND CONTEMPORARY ROBOTICS). WE WILL
STUDY THE HOW NOVEL AGILE MANEUVERS (E.G., SUDDEN PARKOUR GAP-CROSSING INNOVATIONS) ARISE
ACROSS BODY TYPES (DIFFERENT DEVELOPMENTAL STAGES IN THE SAME SPECIES) AND EVOLUTIONARY HISTORIES
(DIFFERENT ANIMAL GROUPS WITH SIMILAR HABITAT). IN TURN, WE WILL STUDY THE HOW ANIMALS VARIED
MECHANICAL PERFORMANCE CAPABILITIES AND ACCESS TO DIFFERENT SENSORY MODALITIES INTERACT WITH THEIR
NAVIGATIONAL STRATEGIES.
WE WILL STUDY JUVENILE FOX SQUIRRELS FOR THREE REASONS. FIRST, AS IN OTHER MAMMALS, TREE
SQUIRRELS MUST DEVELOP THEIR MOTOR SKILLS IN THE COMPLEX (AND RISKY) 3D ENVIRONMENT OF THE TREE
CANOPY. PERHAPS FOR THIS REASON, TREE SQUIRREL PHYSICAL AND COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT IS SLOWER THAN
THAT SEEN IN GROUND SQUIRRELS, SUCH AS CHIPMUNKS, WHO MOVE PRIMARILY IN 2D; TREE SQUIRRELS ALSO
HAVE RELATIVELY LARGER BRAINS THAN GROUND SQUIRREL.
YEAR 1-3. OUR GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY THE EFFECT OF PRIOR KNOWLEDGE ON THE FORM OF INNOVATION IN
FOX SQUIRRELS, COMPARING THE DEVELOPMENT OF SOLUTIONS TO DIFFERENT MOTOR TASKS IN GROUPS WITH
DIFFERENT PRIOR KNOWLEDGE OF THE PROBLEM. WE WILL UTILIZE THREE BEHAVIORS THAT ARE KNOWN TO BE
HYBRIDS OF KNOWN INNATE MOTOR PATTERNS (LEAPING, NUT OPENING, CACHE BURYING). BECAUSE THE
INNATE COMPONENTS OF THESE BEHAVIORS HAVE BEEN DESCRIBED, WE CAN PRECISELY IDENTIFY THE NOVEL,
LEARNED COMPONENTS. SECOND, THESE THREE BEHAVIORS OCCUR AT DIFFERENT SPATIAL SCALES AND HENCE
INVOLVE DIFFERENT MUSCLE GROUPS, FROM THE SMALLEST SCALE MOVEMENTS (NUT OPENING), TO MEDIUM
SCALE MOVEMENTS (GAP LEAPING) AND FINALLY LARGE SCALE MOVEMENTS (DISTRIBUTING CACHES). TO TEST

3.1. PATHOGENIC ASSESSMENT PIPELINE
3.1.1. INTEGRATION OF EXTERNAL DATA RESOURCES (MS AND JH). WHILE THERE IS CURRENTLY NO SINGLE COMPREHENSIVE EXTERNAL RESOURCE, THERE ARE MANY SPECIFIC RESOURCES AND JOURNALS THAT CATALOGUE BACTERIA PHENOTYPES. WE WILL BUILD A SINGLE DATABASE THAT MERGES DATA FROM RESOURCES SUCH AS BACDIVE AND FAPROTAX WITH LITERATURE DATA COMPILED AND CURATED FROM BACTERIAL PHENOTYPE JOURNALS SUCH AS THE INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SYSTEMATIC AND EVOLUTIONARY MICROBIOLOGY. THIS DATASET WILL PROVIDE A WEALTH OF INFORMATION TO HELP 1) DETERMINE THE OPTIMAL EXPERIMENTS FOR SEPARATING BACTERIA BY PHENOTYPE AND 2) INTEGRATE LITERATURE INFORMATION INTO OUR ALGORITHMS FOR DETERMINING BACTERIAL PATHOGENICITY. IN ADDITION, WE WILL BUILD A CATALOGUE OF ALL BACTERIAL GENE SEQUENCES THAT HAVE BEEN LINKED TO PATHOGENESIS.

3.1.3. PROBABILISTIC PATHOGEN CLASSIFICATION (MS, JP, SR, AND JH, PARTLY IN COLLABORATION WITH DI). WE WILL INTEGRATE EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS FROM 1.4.2 (E.G. GROWTH DATA, MORPHOLOGY, AUTO FLUORESCENCE, AND DYE BINDING) AND TA2 (3 DISTINCT PATHOGENIC TRAIT ASSAYS), WITH LITERATURE DATA (3.1.1), AND OMICS DATA (3.2). DATA FROM THESE FOUR INPUTS WILL INITIALLY BE COLLECTED FOR OUR PANEL OF 2:10 PATHOGENIC AND 2:10 NON-PATHOGENIC STRAINS (TA2) AND THEN BE EXPANDED TO INCLUDE ALL 2:20 STRAINS PROVIDED BY THE IV&V TEAM (2.1 AND 2.2). THIS DATA WILL SERVE AS INPUT FOR MULTIPLE DIFFERENT TYPES OF MACHINE LEARNING/CLASSIFICATION APPROACHES SUCH AS SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINES, NAVE BAYES CLASSIFIERS, RANDOM FORESTS, NEURAL NETS, PERCEPTRONS, AND CLUSTERING. IF TWO CLASSIFIERS PERFORM COMPARABLY, PREFERENCE WILL BE GIVEN TO CLASSIFIERS THAT CAN EASILY BE EXPANDED TO INCLUDE NEW DATASETS AS LONG AS IT DOES NOT RESULT IN IMPRACTICAL SCALING OF DATA PROCESSING TIME. THIS WORK WILL ALSO MAKE USE OF ANY GENETIC PRE-SCREENING DATA OBTAINED FOR BACTERIA IN MICRO-CHAMBERS (1.5). IN ADDITION, WE WILL DETERMINE THE EXTENT TO WHICH THESE RESULTS CONFIRM THE PATHOGENICITY PHENOTYPES AS DETERMINED BY HUMAN ORGAN CHIP TECHNOLOGY (2.3). WE WILL ALSO DETERMINE WHETHER INCORPORATION OF LOW THROUGHPUT PHENOTYPING FROM THE HUMAN ORGAN CHIP CAN BE USED TO IMPROVE THE PATHOGENICITY ALGORITHMS.

THE PAULSSON LAB UNDER DARPA FRIEND OR FOE (FOF) PROGRAM HAS DEVELOPED AN INTEGRATED PLATFORM FOR IN-DEPTH, HIGH-THROUGHPUT INTERROGATION OF CELLS, TRACKING UP TO A MILLION SEPARATE CELL LINEAGES FOR HUNDREDS OF GENERATIONS WITH MANY CELLS PER LINEAGE, TOTALING A BILLION IMAGED CELL DIVISIONS PER EXPERIMENT. EACH MUTANT LINEAGE IS PHYSICALLY SEPARATED FROM THE OTHERS, ANY CELLS OF INTEREST CAN BE PRISTINELY RETRIEVED AFTER IMAGING - MUCH LIKE A FLUORENSCENCE ACTIVATED CELL SORTER (FACS)NBUT SORTING AFTER EXTENSIVE TIME- LAPSE MOVIES OF NUMEROUS INDIVIDUAL CELLS FROM EACH MUTANT LINEAGE TO OBSERVE SPATIOTEMPORAL DYNAMICS AND COLLECT STATISTICAL INFORMATION. THE LOCAL CONDITIONS CAN BE EXCEPTIONALLY WELL CONTROLLED, WITH THE ABILITY TO CHANGE THE ENVIRONMENT IN TIME OR MIMIC COMPLEX GROWTH SITUATIONS. CELLS CAN ALSO BE RAPIDLY GENOTYPED IN SITU ON CHIP, FOR GENOTYPE-TO-PHENOTYPE MAPPING OF EVERY LINEAGE EVEN FOR LARGE POOLED MUTANT LIBRARIES. THE PLATFORM WILL HAVE THE ABILITY TO PERFORM MULTIPLE TERMINAL ASSAYS ON THE SAME INDIVIDUAL LINEAGES, BY SACRIFICING ONLY A FEW CELLS PER LINEAGE. IT WILL HAVE THE ABILITY TO RUN 96-WELL FORMAT CHIPS FOR INTEGRATED DRUG SCREENS. THE PLATFORM BEATS EXISTING TECHNOLOGIES BY ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE IN BOTH THROUGHPUT AND RESOLUTION, AND IS INEXPENSIVE AND EASY TO BUILD AND RUN. LIKE FLOW CYTOMETERS OR MICROSCOPES, THE PLATFORM IS NOT DESIGNED FOR ONE PARTICULAR APPLICATION, BUT RATHER TO EMPOWER BIOENGINEERING AND BIODETECTION BROADLY.

THIS WORK SCOPE AIMS TO DEVELOP TECHNIQUES AND METHODS TO ENSURE THAT THE FEEDSTOCK MATERIALS AND THE AM MACHINE ARE TAMPER-PROOF AT THE USER SITE. AN INNOVATIVE APPROACH IS TO DESIGN A "TEST PAGE" TO SELF-TEST ITS STRENGTH, AN INDICATOR OF FEEDSTOCK QUALITY AND AM PROCESS CORRECTNESS, WITHOUT MECHANICAL TESTING. FOUR SUPPORTING SUB-TASKS ARE DEVELOPED AND LISTED BELOW.
1. FEEDSTOCK MATERIALS (VALIDATE, INSPECTION TECHNIQUES ARE TAMPER-PROOF)
THE OVERALL GOAL IS TO DEVELOP AN INSPECTION SYSTEM TO EXAMINE THE FEEDSTOCK WIRE DURING THE MELTING PROCESS OF WAAM (WIRE-ARC ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING). THE METHOD USES A HIGH-RESOLUTION SCANNING CAMERA TO IDENTIFY THE VAPORIZATION IMPACT ON THE PHASE TRANSFORMATION AND ITS CONSEQUENT VARIANT OF COMPOSITION AND PHYSICAL PROPERTIES. THE INITIAL RESULTS FROM THE YEAR-1 EXIT INVESTIGATION USING AN AUTOMATED MICROSCOPE SYSTEM AND IMAGING PROCESSING ARE TO BE USED IN DESIGNING THE APPARATUS IN AN EXISTING WAAM SYSTEM. IN ADDITION, A PHENOMENOLOGICAL MODEL WILL BE TESTED AND CALIBRATED BASED ON THE MEASUREMENT. YEAR-2 WILL FURTHER IMPROVE THE SENSITIVITY OF THE MEASUREMENT'S EFFICIENCY AND ENHANCE THE MODEL PREDICTION TO ESTIMATE THE ELEMENTAL VAPORIZATION. THE PROCESS WINDOW TO FACILITATE SUCH A RAPID DETECTION OF ELEMENTAL LOSS WILL BE IDENTIFIED.
2. MACHINE COMPLIANCE
MACHINE COMPLIANCE IS THE OPERATION OF A MACHINE FOLLOWING WHAT IT IS DESIGNED FOR, SUCH AS A RULE, STANDARD, OR SPECIFICATION. FOR A WAAM MACHINE, THE KEY SPECIFICATIONS INCLUDE POWER, FEED RATE, SCANNING SPEED, GAS FLOW, ETC. TO VERIFY A WAAM SYSTEM FOR COMPLIANCE, THE TECHNICIAN FROM THE MACHINE MANUFACTURER WOULD RUN SEVERAL DIAGNOSTIC TESTS, WHICH WOULD TAKE DAYS TO COMPLETE. TO MORE EFFICIENTLY DETECT NON-COMPLIANCE ISSUES, THE TEAM WILL DEVELOP A MULTI-SENSOR-BASED MONITORING SYSTEM TO TRACK A MACHINE ONLINE BY INSPECTING THE DIFFERENT SIGNATURES RELATED TO WIRE-ARC SCANS DURING THE WAAM PROCESS. THE MONITORING SYSTEM WILL COMPRISE A CO-AXIAL SINGLE-CAMERA TWO-WAVELENGTH IMAGING PYROMETER MEASURING THE MELT POOL MORPHOLOGY AND TEMPERATURE, AN OFF-AXIS INFRARED (IR) CAMERA MEASURING THE HEAT INTENSITY OVER THE ENTIRE BUILD ENVELOPE SURFACE, AN OFF-AXIS CAMERA MONITORING THE PRINTING SCAN LOCATION AND SPATTER, AND A FRINGE PROJECTION PROFILOMETRY MEASURING THE LAYER-WISE POWDER BED SURFACE CONDITION AND SURFACE TOPOGRAPHY. MACHINE LEARNING-BASED IMAGE PROCESSING AND ANALYSIS ALGORITHMS WILL BE DEVELOPED TO ENHANCE THE MELT POOL, LAYER SURFACE, AND SPATTER MEASUREMENT ACCURACY AND ROBUSTNESS.
3. TEST PROCEDURES FOR VALIDATION/VERIFICATION OF MACHINE PERFORMANCE
THE MULTI-SENOR-BASED IN-SITU MONITORING SYSTEM WILL BE UTILIZED TO COLLECT DATA ON TEST PRINTS (SEE NEXT TASK). DEEP LEARNING NEURAL NETWORKS WILL BE TRAINED USING BENCHMARK MONITORING DATA TAKEN ON TEST PRINTS IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE MACHINE MAINTENANCE IS CONDUCTED. AN ONLINE MACHINE MONITORING TOOL WILL BE DEVELOPED BY INTEGRATING THE MULTI-SENSOR DATA ACQUISITION AND ANALYTICS CODES WITH THE TRAINED NEURAL NETWORK MODELS INTO A SOFTWARE PACKAGE. THE MONITORING SYSTEM AND SOFTWARE TOOLS WILL BE USED TO MEASURE SUBSEQUENT BUILDS AND DETECT ABNORMAL ARC SCANS AND POWDER SPREAD IN THE MACHINE. 
4. GENERALIZED DESIGN OF EXPERIMENTS
THE OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP A GENERALIZED DESIGN OF EXPERIMENTS (DOE) FOR THE TEST PRINTS TO VERIFY MACHINE COMPLIANCE. THE TEST PRINT IS EXPECTED TO CONTAIN SEVERAL FEATURES, SUCH AS OVERHANGS, BRIDGES, THIN WALLS, AND LATTICE STRUCTURES. IN ADDITION, IT WILL INCLUDE FEATURES SUCH AS BRIDGES AND CANTILEVER BEAMS
THAT ARE DESIGNED TO FAIL UNDER RESIDUAL STRESS WHEN THE MACHINE IS IN COMPLIANCE; THEREFORE, WHEN THE MACHINE OR FEEDSTOCK POWDER IS COMPROMISED, MORE FEATURES THAN USUAL WOULD FAIL. THE TEAM WILL DESIGN THE TEST PRINT TO BE EFFICIENT AND EFFECTIVE. PROCESS SIMULATION WILL BE USED TO PREDICT RESIDUAL STRESS FROM THE BUILD.

IN THIS RESEARCH, WE MODEL A FORENSIC EVENT NETWORK AS A WEIGHTED TEMPORAL LOCALITY GRAPH OF THE CRIME EVENTS (REPRESENTED AS NODES/VERTICES) AS FOLLOWS: THE COORDINATES OF A NODE IN THE GRAPH WILL CORRESPOND TO THE LATITUDE AND LONGITUDE OF THE LOCATION ATTRIBUTE AND THERE IS AN EDGE BETWEEN ANY TWO NODES (I.E., THE WEIGHTED TEMPORAL LOCALITY GRAPH IS A COMPLETE GRAPH BASED ON THE CONNECTIVITY OF THE NODES). THE DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO NODES IS THE EUCLIDEAN DISTANCE BETWEEN THE COORDINATES OF THE NODES. HOWEVER, THE WEIGHT OF AN EDGE IN THE GRAPH IS QUANTIFIED USING THE TIME ATTRIBUTE, PER ONE OF THE FOLLOWING THREE DIFFERENCE MEASURES: ABSOLUTE REAL-TIME DIFFERENCE MEASURE, DAILY-CYCLE MEASURE (ABSOLUTE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO TIME INSTANTS MOD 86400, WHICH IS THE NUMBER OF SECONDS IN A DAY) AND WEEKLY-CYCLE MEASURE (ABSOLUTE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO TIME INSTANTS MOD 14515200, WHICH IS THE NUMBER OF SECONDS IN A WEEK). IN ADDITION, THE NODES (CRIME EVENTS) IN THE LOCALITY GRAPH ARE WEIGHTED: THE WEIGHT OF A NODE/CRIME EVENT IS REPRESENTED AS A VECTOR OF THE METRIC SPACES CONSIDERED FOR THE OFFENDER(S) AND VICTIM(S) ATTRIBUTES. THE NOTION OF WEIGHTED TEMPORAL LOCALITY (WTL) GRAPH IS A UNIQUE MODELING APPROACH THAT HAS BEEN HITHERTO NOT EXPLORED IN THE LITERATURE AND IT IS PROPOSED WITH THE INTENTION OF INTEGRATING (FORENSIC MODEL FUSION) THE DYNAMICS OF THE CRIME EVENTS CAPTURED WITH RESPECT TO ALL THE FIVE ATTRIBUTES. WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING RESEARCH TASKS (INVOLVING VARIOUS NETWORK SCIENCE TECHNIQUES) TO BE CONDUCTED ON THE WTL GRAPH TO EXTRACT EVENT SIGNATURES THAT WOULD BE HELPFUL FOR INVESTIGATION.

AS A RESULT, WE WILL BE ABLE TO ANSWER QUESTIONS SUCH AS: ARE ANY TWO CRIME EVENTS MORE LIKELY TO HAPPEN AROUND THE SAME TIME OF THE DAY OR THE SAME TIME OF A WEEK (EVEN IF THEY HAPPENED ON DIFFERENT DAYS), REFERRED TO AS "BURNING TIMES" [1] IN THE CRIMINOLOGY LITERATURE?

IN THIS PURSUIT, WE WILL SUBJECT THE ORIGINAL WTL GRAPH TO A TRANSFORMATION WHEREIN WE WILL RETAIN AN EDGE BETWEEN TWO CRIME EVENTS ONLY IF THE NORMALIZED VALUES FOR THE METRIC SPACES CONSIDERED ARE WITHIN A THRESHOLD. WE WILL DEVELOP A BINARY SEARCH ALGORITHM TO DETERMINE THE MINIMUM VALUE FOR THIS THRESHOLD (COULD BE CONSTRUED AS A MEASURE OF SIMILARITY) THAT WOULD KEEP THE TRANSFORMED WTL GRAPH CONNECTED. IN THIS PURSUIT, WE WILL DEVELOP AN ALGORITHM FOR SPATIAL CRIME CASCADE BASED ON THE ASSUMPTION THAT CRIME EVENTS HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO SPREAD TO LOCATIONS THAT ARE WITHIN A THRESHOLD DISTANCE (SIMILAR TO CASCADABILITY OF INFORMATION IN SOCIAL NETWORKS [10]) AND THEREBY FURTHER SPREAD TO THE ENTIRE AREA (REFERRED TO AS GLOBAL CASCADE) THAT IS BEING COVERED UP FOR INVESTIGATION. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO SYSTEMATICALLY UNDERSTAND THE IMPACT OF TRANSIENCE ON MMWAVE
LINKS AND TO DESIGN BEAM ADAPTATION AND MANAGEMENT TECHNIQUES CUSTOM-TAILORED FOR TRANSIENT
TOPOLOGIES IN MILITARY SETTINGS. THE EXPLORATION WILL BE DIVIDED INTO THREE TASKS: (1) THE FIRST TASK
WILL BE TO ANALYTICALLY STUDY BEAM COHERENCE TIME AND LOS PROBABILITY OF MMWAVE LINKS WITH
RESPECT TO VEHICULAR MOBILITY, DENSITY, AND PRESENCE OF TRANSIENT BLOCKAGES. THE STUDY WILL BE
FOLLOWED BY AN INVESTIGATION ON HOW TRANSIENT REFLECTIONS FROM OTHER VEHICLES CAN BE PREDICTED AND
EXPLOITED IN REAL-TIME WITH LIMITED BEAMSEARCHING. (2) WHILE THE VEHICULAR REFLECTIONS ARE HELPFUL IN
LOW TO MODERATE DENSITY AND BLOCKAGE, THE SECOND TASK WILL EXPLORE THE USE OF AMBIENT REFLECTORS TO
MAINTAIN THE LINK CONNECTIVITY. GIVEN THAT EXISTING METHODS OF BEAMSEARCHING ARE NOT SUFFICIENT FOR
SHORT-LIVED, TRANSIENT CONNECTION DURATIONS, THIS TASK WILL INCLUDE EXPLORING THE CAMERA IMAGERY AND
USE OF MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES TO IDENTIFY, LOCATE AND LEVERAGE THE REFLECTORS FOR MAINTAINING
MMWAVE LINKS. (3) THE EXISTING METHODS OF INTERFERENCE ESTIMATION AND MEDIUM ACCESS IN PRESENCE
OF BEAMSEARCHING ARE INEFFECTIVE FOR MMWAVE V2V NETWORKS. TO ADDRESS THIS PROBLEM, INTERFERENCE
ESTIMATION TECHNIQUES WITH LOW MEASUREMENT OVERHEAD WILL BE DESIGNED. THESE TECHNIQUES WILL BE
INTEGRATED INTO TWO TYPES OF MEDIUM ACCESS PROTOCOLS. IN THE FIRST PROTOCOL, THE LINK INTERFERENCE
INFORMATION WILL BE SHARED OVER A LOW-FREQUENCY BACKBONE, WHILE IN THE SECOND PROTOCOL, A
COMPLETELY DISTRIBUTED, RANDOM ACCESS WITH SPATIAL BACKOFFS ON DIFFERENT MMWAVE PATHS WILL BE
INVESTIGATED, REQUIRING NO MEDIUM ACCESS COORDINATION BETWEEN VEHICLES. THE THREE TASKS WILL CREATE
A COMPREHENSIVE SOLUTION SPACE THAT CAN REALIZE THE TRUE POTENTIAL OF MMWAVE WIRELESS IN TRANSIENT
NETWORK TOPOLOGIES.

full_descriptions: AI-BASED CHARACTERIZATION OF TRUST AND DOMINANCE FOR TEAM PERFORMANCE

DESPITE ITS IMPORTANCE, A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW TRUST IS BUILT AND ITS RELATIONSHIP
TO TEAM PERFORMANCE REMAINS ELUSIVE. EXISTING RESEARCH SUGGESTS FACTORS BEYOND VERBAL COMMUNICATION, INCLUDING NONVERBAL DOMINANCE AND INTERPERSONAL SYNCHRONY, AFFECT TRUST.  HOWEVER, THERE IS A GAP IN UNDERSTANDING HOW THESE FACTORS DYNAMICALLY INTERACT AND CONTRIBUTE TO TRUST FORMATION IN HUMAN TEAMS. WITH THIS INTERDISCIPLINARY PROPOSAL, WE AIM TO EMPIRICALLY INVESTIGATE THE MODERATORS OF THE TRUST-PERFORMANCE RELATIONSHIP IN A MULTI-SESSION TEAM STUDY. DESPITE ITS IMPORTANCE, A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW TRUST IS BUILT AND ITS RELATIONSHIP
TO TEAM PERFORMANCE REMAINS ELUSIVE. EXISTING RESEARCH SUGGESTS FACTORS BEYOND VERBAL COMMUNICATION, INCLUDING NONVERBAL DOMINANCE AND INTERPERSONAL SYNCHRONY, AFFECT TRUST.  HOWEVER, THERE IS A GAP IN UNDERSTANDING HOW THESE FACTORS DYNAMICALLY INTERACT AND CONTRIBUTE TO TRUST FORMATION IN HUMAN TEAMS. WITH THIS INTERDISCIPLINARY PROPOSAL, WE AIM TO EMPIRICALLY INVESTIGATE THE MODERATORS OF THE TRUST-PERFORMANCE RELATIONSHIP IN A MULTI-SESSION TEAM STUDY. WE COMBINE THE DYADIC POWER THEORY (DPT) AND THE INTEGRATED SPIRAL MODEL OF TRUST (ISMT) TO EXPLAIN THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN POWER, NONVERBAL BEHAVIOR AND TRUST IN TEAMS. TO THIS END, WE DEVELOP MACHINE LEARNING MODELS TO DETECT TRUSTWORTHINESS AND DOMINANCE BY TRACKING INDIVIDUAL 
BEHAVIORS AND TEAM DYNAMICS. THE MAIN AIMS OF THIS PROPOSAL ARE: (1) IDENTIFYING KEY DETERMINANTS OF TRUST AND DOMINANCE THROUGH THE ANALYSIS OF SYNCHRONY AND CONVERGENCE IN TEAMS; (2) EXPLORING
THE FORMATION OF TRUST IN TEAMS AND ITS IMPACT ON PERFORMANCE OVER TIME BY MANIPULATING AUTHORITY
AND SKILL DIFFERENTIATION; (3) DEVELOPING INNOVATIVE GRAPH NEURAL NETWORKS TO MEASURE CRITICAL DIMENSIONS LIKE POWER, DOMINANCE, AND TRUST. THE RESEARCH WILL BE AMONG THE FIRST TO EMPIRICALLY VALIDATE A THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK FOR CONSTRUCTING AND MAINTAINING TRUST IN TEAMS AND WILL ADDRESS
ARO’S PRIORITIES OF THE DEVELOPMENT OF THEORIES AND MODELS THAT CAPTURE PROCESSES LEADING TO TRUST
AND IMPROVED PERFORMANCE IN TEAMS. WORK WILL PRODUCE NOVEL TOOLS FOR THE AUTOMATIC CODING OF TEAM INTERACTIONS. ADVANCING THE SCIENCE OF TEAM MEASUREMENT AND TRUST FORMATION WILL CONTRIBUTE TO DEVELOPING STRATEGIES FOR FORMING AND FOSTERING STRONG AND EFFECTIVE TEAMS.

REAL-TIME STRUCTURAL HEALTH MONITORING (SHM) OF RIVER NAVIGATION ASSETS HAS PROMISING POTENTIAL IN AVOIDING CATASTROPHIC FAILURES AND REDUCING THE OPERATION COSTS OF RIVER NAVIGATION. BY LEVERAGING THE RICH INFORMATION OF PHYSICS-BASED HIGH-FIDELITY COMPUTER SIMULATION MODELS, PHYSICS-INFORMED SHM TECHNIQUES ALLOW US TO NOT ONLY DETECT A DAMAGE (E.G. GATE GAP), BUT ALSO AUTOMATICALLY DETERMINE THE LOCATION AND SIZE OF THE DAMAGE. THE FRAMEWORK WILL ADDRESS THE CHALLENGING SHM ISSUES RELATED TO MODELING ISSUES, NONLINEAR STRAIN RESPONSE, HIGH COMPUTATIONAL COST, AND VARIOUS UNCERTAINTY SOURCES, BY INTEGRATING FINITE ELEMENT SIMULATION, MACHINE LEARNING, UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION, AND DESIGN OPTIMIZATION WITH BAYESIAN STATE ESTIMATION TECHNIQUES. THE INTEGRATION OF THESE METHODS ENABLES US TO MINIMIZE THE REQUIRED NUMBER OF STRAIN GAGES IN SHM, AND TO DETECT AND LOCATE THE DAMAGE IN REAL TIME.

Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢	REPRESENT STRAIN DISTRIBUTION ON THE ASSETSÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ SURFACE AS A RANDOM FIELD WITH BOTH SPATIAL AND TIME CORRELATION.

Ã¢Â‚¬Â¢	EXPLORE METHODOLOGIES LIKE THE NONLINEAR AUTOREGRESSIVE WITH EXTERNAL INPUT GAUSSIAN PROCESS SURROGATE MODELING (GP-NARX) TO IMPROVE ACCURACY OF SURROGATE MODELING IN LOAD MODELING AND STRAIN RESPONSE PREDICTION.

1. OVERVIEW:
BUILDING ON WORK THAT BEGAN IN FIRO PHASE ONE, THE FOCUS OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH
WOULD BE ON THE DETERMINATION OF THE STRUCTURE AND EVOLUTION OF PERSISTENT WEATHER REGIMES
ASSOCIATED WITH THE OCCURRENCE OF EXTREME WEATHER IN CALIFORNIA. THE PERSISTENT WEATHER
REGIMES OF MOST INTEREST WOULD BE THOSE ASSOCIATED WITH EXTENDED DRY AND WET PERIODS ON
INTRASEASONAL-TO-SEASONAL TIME SCALES. THE PHYSICAL PROCESSES THAT GOVERN BOTH WEATHER
REGIME PERSISTENCE AND WEATHER REGIME CHANGES BETWEEN EXTENDED DRY AND WET PERIODS WILL
BE ESPECIALLY TARGETED FOR FURTHER RESEARCH. THE PROJECT AS CURRENTLY ENVISIONED WOULD
PROVIDE SUPPORT FOR ONE PH.D. STUDENT (TYLER LEICHT) BEGINNING IN JULY 2020. THE PROPOSED
RESEARCH WILL TARGET THE STRUCTURE AND EVOLUTION OF PERSISTENT FLOW ANOMALIES OVER NORTH
PACIFIC OCEAN. WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW EAST ASIAN COLD SURGES, THE MADDEN-JULIAN
OSCILLATION, AND THE EL NINO-SOUTHERN OSCILLATION COLLECTIVE IMPACT THE STRUCTURE AND
EVOLUTION OF THE NORTH PACIFIC JET STREAM THROUGH ROSSBY WAVE BREAKING, AND POTENTIAL
VORTICITY STREAMER DEVELOPMENT, CUTOFF CYCLONE FORMATION. A CRITICAL COMPONENT OF THE
RESEARCH WILL BE DETERMINING THE RELATIONSHIP THE NORTH PACIFIC JET STREAM NPJ AND
ATMOSPHERIC RIVERS, A RELATIONSHIP THAT NEEDS TO BE BETTER UNDERSTOOD IN ORDER TO PREDICT WEST
COAST WEATHER REGIMES. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL BE CONDUCTED BY MEANS OF
CLIMATOLOGICAL, COMPOSITE, AND CASE STUDY ANALYSES OF WEST COAST WEATHER REGIMES AND
ATMOSPHERIC RIVERS IN CONJUNCTION WITH SELECTED NUMERICAL INVESTIGATIONS OF THE ABOVEMENTIONED WEATHER PHENOMENA. THESE RESEARCH EFFORTS WILL BE DONE IN COLLABORATION WITH
RESEARCH SCIENTISTS AND GRADUATE STUDENTS AT THE CENTER OF WESTERN WEATHER AND WATER
EXTREMES AT THE SCRIPPS INSTITUTION OF OCEANOGRAPHY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA-SAN
DIEGO. A VERY IMPORTANT PRACTICAL GOAL OF THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO TRANSFER THE RESEARCH
FINDINGS INTO OPERATIONS TO BENEFIT WATER MANAGERS AND EMERGENCY MANAGERS WITH RESPECT
TO ANTICIPATING THE POTENTIAL FOR SEVERE FLOODING

A. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION The Public Diplomacy Section of the U.S. Embassy in Bangkok announces an open competition for a cooperative agreement under the Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative (YSEALI) to develop and implement the YSEALI AI FutureMakers Regional Workshop – a six-day workshop in Thailand (inclusive of arrival and departure days) on exploring the transformative power of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in driving social innovation. Please note that this award is subject to availability of funding. Please carefully follow all instructions below. Priority Region: Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Laos, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, and Timor-Leste. Program Objectives: YSEALI (yseali.state.gov) is the U.S. government’s signature initiative to engage emerging leaders in Southeast Asia. The program aims to create a network of young Southeast Asian leaders who work across national borders to address common problems. Through a variety of programs and engagements, YSEALI seeks to build the leadership capabilities of youth in the region, strengthen ties between the United States and Southeast Asia, and develop a community of leaders addressing regional concerns. YSEALI is open to young leaders ages 18-35 who are both citizens and residents of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member countries (Brunei, Burma, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam) or Timor-Leste. YSEALI programs focus on four themes (Economic Growth, Sustainable Development, Education, and Civic Engagement) because youth in the region identified them as priorities. YSEALI also organizes annual Regional Workshops across Southeast Asia on strategic topics. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a transformative technology with profound implications for society, government, the economy, and the environment worldwide. Within ASEAN, governmental, societal, and economic actors are actively engaged in discussing the applications of this technology and the role of regulation, for example in the ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics approved at the 4th ASEAN Digital Ministers Meeting (ADGMIN) on February 2, 2024. Development of AI within Southeast Asia is complicated by the wide variation in economic development and technological capacity between member states, and 2025 is an opportune time to engage the YSEALI community in efforts to leverage AI to foster shared, sustainable, and inclusive growth throughout the Indo-Pacific Region. The YSEALI AI FutureMakers Regional Workshop will convene young people from throughout Southeast Asia to leverage the power of science, technology, and active civil society participation to address critical challenges and expand opportunities in Southeast Asia. The workshop will emphasize the importance of strengthening people-to-people connections, ensuring that technological advancements benefit not just economies, but societies at large, reinforcing the bridge between innovation and human-centric development. Through this workshop, the participants will not only address immediate challenges but will also lay the groundwork for long-term partnerships and collaborations that will drive positive change and development across the region. This workshop will bring together 60 YSEALI members from ASEAN countries and Timor Leste with a keen interest in leveraging technology to address regional and global challenges. It will offer a unique opportunity for YSEALI leaders to delve deeply into the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI), with a focus on at least one of the YSEALI’s core themes: economic empowerment, civic engagement, education, and environmental sustainability. Participants will engage in comprehensive discussions and hands-on activities aimed at harnessing AI for sustainable change. Within the realm of economic empowerment, the proposal should explore how AI technologies can catalyze socio-economic growth by creating new opportunities for entrepreneurship, enhancing livelihoods, and fostering inclusive economic development. Through case studies and interactive sessions, participants should gain insights into innovative AI-driven business models and strategies that promote equitable access to resources and opportunities. For civic engagement, the proposal should explore how AI can be used to bridge societal gaps and empower marginalized communities. Participants will consider successful AI projects that increase citizen access to information and political participation, while examining the risks of AI perpetuating inequalities that exist within training data and other source material and strategies to mitigate these risks. In the field of education, the proposal should create space for participants to explore how AI can improve access and quality of education, including language learning among Southeast Asia’s diverse populations; enhanced virtual resources; and/or teacher training in remote or rural communities, along with the ethical challenges of AI generated content and promoting critical thinking skills to detect and resist misinformation. In the context of environmental conservation, the proposal should highlight the potential of AI for monitoring and managing natural resources, protecting wildlife, and mitigating the impacts of climate change. Through interactive discussions and fieldwork at AI-driven organizations specializing in environmental conservation, participants should explore cutting-edge technologies and data-driven approaches that support sustainable environmental stewardship and biodiversity preservation. Through a combination of theoretical insights, practical case studies, hands-on activities, and collaborative discussions, the YSEALI AI FutureMakers Regional Workshop should equip participants with the knowledge, skills, and tools they need to harness the transformative potential of AI for building sustainable, inclusive, and equitable communities throughout Southeast Asia. The proposal should include workshop follow-on activities such as virtual collaborative work, projects funded through small seed grants, and/or ongoing mentorship. The follow-on activity should be included in the monitoring and evaluation plan. The proposal should include a pre and post workshop survey to measure the overall effectiveness of the workshop as well as any changes to the participants’ knowledge of the workshop topic. Workshop speakers/facilitators/mentors should be citizens of the United States, an ASEAN member country, or Timor-Leste. The workshop should also include a cultural or community service component that promotes ASEAN unity, and the United States as a partner to ASEAN. The recipient is expected to develop syllabus materials and an event program with participant and speaker biographies, as well as design banners, backdrops, and other printed materials. The recipient is expected to design a digital engagement strategy for workshop participants and social media audiences, including live video or live online engagement during the program. No new website specific to the event should be created or launched. Domain hosting and build costs will not be covered. Participants and Audiences: The recipient will coordinate with U.S. Embassy Bangkok and with the U.S. embassies in ASEAN and Timor-Leste to recruit and select the final 60 participants. Participants will be between the ages of 18-35 and a keen interest in leveraging AI technology to address and solve one of the following issues: economic empowerment, civic engagement, education, and environmental sustainability, as well as collaborating with others from diverse backgrounds and building networks for future initiatives. The recruitment process should ensure that the pool of applicants reflect different regions of the country, not just capital cities. All participants must be proficient in written and spoken English. All programs must include participants from all ten ASEAN member countries and Timor-Leste. The workshop will be conducted in English. The recipient will be responsible for arranging and using cooperative agreement funds to cover all elements related to participant and staff travel including international and domestic flights, visas, travel to and from airports, visas, accommodations, per diem, meals during the program, insurance, COVID-19 testing, etc. B. FEDERAL AWARD INFORMATION Length of performance period: September 2024 to December 2025 Number of awards anticipated: One Award amounts: Award may range from a minimum of $150,000 to a maximum of $250,000. Total available funding: $250,000 Type of Funding: FY24 Public Diplomacy Funds Anticipated program start date: September 2024 This notice is subject to availability of funding. Funding Instrument Type: Cooperative agreement The U.S. Embassy Bangkok will have substantial involvement in the development, content, and schedule of the workshop. In consultation with U.S. Embassy Bangkok, the award recipient must actively engage all relevant U.S. embassies related to the recruitment and selection process as well as communication with the participants. Working closely with U.S. Embassy Bangkok, the recipient of this cooperative agreement shall develop a robust program for the workshop; schedule the event at a mutually agreed upon location; manage the application and selection process through a secure portal; develop the agenda and content for the workshop; recruit speaker(s); manage all travel logistics for participants and speakers; and generate content for social media and other publicity. The recipient is expected to provide all design files, photos and video recorded, as well as a promotion-ready, U.S. Embassy-approved photo album and a video series of the workshop after completion. Regular, transparent communication via email, phone and video conference calls and face-to-face meetings (as appropriate) with the Grants Officer, Grants Officer Representative, and Program Officer throughout the period of performance is critical to the success of this cooperative agreement. All major elements of the program and its content require advance approval by U.S. Embassy Bangkok, including, but not limited to: Choices of dates, venue, accommodations, and menus; Final selection of participants, mentors, and speakers (from the United States, an ASEAN member country, or Timor-Leste); Titles, format, and content of workshop sessions and other program activities; Design and content of all marketing materials, publicity, and media products. Program Performance Period: Proposed programs should be completed in 12 months or less. The workshop must be a minimum of six full days, including travel days. C. ELIGIBILITY INFORMATION 1. SynopsisA. Program DescriptionBackground:Information has become a domain of warfare that now extends well beyond compromising or disabling the data-handling platforms, and into subtler forms of content manipulation, in order to elicit specific psychological and sociological responses. The existence of systemic campaigns of disinformation is now well established, conducted or supervised by malicious state and non-state actors, using the cover of widespread social media outlets. These rely on automated software agents (“bots”), designed and engineered with increasing levels of sophistication, as well as trained human agents who can control the bot deployment, adjust the network, and refine the strategies. Modern technology greatly facilitates Internet-based programs of social hysteria propagation, propaganda, disinformation, and influence operations, and as technological capabilities improve, the threat will grow accordingly. In an environment of widespread information uncertainty, open societies lose coherence and risk disorderly devolvement, the ultimate objective of the adversaries. Relying on various, authoritative tools of data analysis and network science, the forensic evidence of this social manipulation is undeniable. Even so, this is far from an optimal situation: detection of such campaigns can be difficult and inaccurate when dealing with an adversary who can quickly adapt strategies, and finding a-posteriori evidence of malicious disinformation yields little opportunity for timely and effective counter-measure. Thus, there is a critical need for an ability to: a) detect and counteract disinformation in real-time, especially if the adversary is able to rapidly adapt, as well as; b) predict future strategies and tactics of information warfare in order to design the appropriate defenses.Given the rapidly growing complexity of the information networks for ubiquitous access to information, as well as the pervasive deployment of malicious bots with fast expanding learning capabilities, these detection and prediction tasks can only be achieved by intelligent software, armed with highly efficient algorithms and operating on modern computing platforms. However, disinformation also relies on subtle factors, based on the study of emotional and cognitive processes inherent to the human targets. Those cannot be modeled as rational actors when under such influences, vastly increasing the uncertainty of predictive scenarios. Therefore, it is equally essential to incorporate this knowledge into the models and methods for detection and prediction of malign influence operations.Program Objective: The overarching goal of this research program is to enhance and extend the understanding of the theoretical underpinnings of future information warfare, towards rapid detection, tracking and prediction of attempts at social manipulation. The problem requires the deep integration of two, currently distinct scientific fields, mathematics and social sciences. While modern mathematical methods are often and well-used in social science studies, this research program is going well beyond the state of the art and is calling for the development of a new mathematical foundation for describing, analyzing and predicting human social behavior at multiple scales and in complex and dynamic environments, thus laying the groundwork for a new field.The first aspect concerns the mathematical understanding of the threat and the environment, leading to the design of efficient counter-measures. One must deal, especially, with the critical problems of malicious activity detection and inference of their sources in a very dynamic environment. The growing employment of Machine Learning (ML) methods, as well as other mathematical techniques for data analytics (e.g. topological data analysis – TDA, manifold reconstruction, etc.), provides some formidable capabilities, but is far from sufficient. For example, these tools deal with static data, not adversarial agents who can quickly adapt their strategies, effectively changing the rules of the game. The behavioral dynamics also evolve over a complex multi-layer network that includes cyber, media and a multitude of social dimensions. The true nature and scaling properties of these real-life networks may still be elusive, possibly disrupting an accurate interpretation of measurements, and these networks will evolve rapidly as technology and social conditions change. These are fundamental and unresolved problems for which current techniques are insufficient.The social dimension is the second aspect of the problem. It is already well appreciated how different forms of communication influence individual and group understandings of knowledge and behavior, but the acceleration of cyber influence by sophisticated software agents could have significant implications for social trust and how people live, learn, and communicate. Questions range up to the fundamental issues of how manipulating information at greater speeds and with greater specificity and customizability affects the social relations on which society relies. With the advent of 5G technology and beyond, people may be instantaneously exposed to a deluge of information, from the geo-political to the trivial. How does this accelerated information and network complexity impact social relations across micro, meso, and macro scales? Are new ways of manipulating opinion, even subtler than before, made accessible, and could we detect them? Who then become the principal agents of manipulation, whether complicit or unwitting?While relying on fundamental and exploratory studies in their respective fields, these two directions must eventually be integrated, as the mathematical models of the network, their agents, and the social behavior, must be based on realistic models at multiple scales of aggregation. The comprehensive basic research being sought-after in this opportunity should provide the basis for a unique ability to detect and predict evolving malign social influence, in realistic and ever-changing conditions.Research Areas:The fundamental science behind the objective of this topic covers multiple, coupled areas, thus requiring a combination of expertise, for example: computer science and machine learning, mathematics, cognitive psychology and sociology, network theory and/or game theory. Some specific research topics to be addressed in this undertaking may include, but are not limited to, the following:1) Carefully designed mathematical abstractions based on behavioral science for modeling the agent’s psychological and social variables, e.g.: emotional and cognitive states, human intent and belief, and group dynamics. These models should include approaches to multi-scale clustering for accurate comprehension and modeling of aggregate behavior, e.g. individual – group – nation.2) Game-theoretical and Machine Learning concepts, e.g. multi-agent reinforcement learning (RL) or distributional RL, as well as other innovative ideas that can consider a hybrid distribution of irrational and rational agents, including artificial ones (e.g. bots).3) Efficient mathematical methods and algorithms to detect malicious intent and learn agent behavior and objectives from limited and noisy observations.4) Concepts and methods for strategy optimization (inverse design), which may include counter-messaging, network-based intervention, or other means.The list above is not exhaustive and is only intended to provide examples of research directions. Strong emphasis is placed on the novelty of suggested approaches, their potential for generalizability and scaling, and their rigorous underpinnings. A generative approach that considers a dual evolutionary co-design of threat and defense strategies is particularly welcome, in order to enhance the ability at some future time to predict threat scenarios and verify the defensive posture.Proposals should aim to produce novel conceptual frameworks that present disruptive ways of thinking about the fundamental scientific problems described above. IN ADDITION, WARFIGHTERS LACK RELIABLE COMMUNICATIONS IN THE NORTHERN LATITUDES.
THIS WORK BUILDS ON THE SUCCESS OF THE 2014-2015 COALITION WARFARE PROGRAM AND COLLABORATIVELY INVESTIGATE THREE CLASSES OF TECHNIQUES FOR RANGE-COINCIDENT CLUTTER MITIGATION THAT LIMIT HF SURVEILLANCE SYSTEMS IN THE ARCTIC: (1) TWO-DIMENSIONAL ARRAYS, (2) ADVANCED RADAR WAVEFORMS, AND (3) MULTI-SITE SPATIAL DIVERSITY. A FOURTH OBJECTIVE INCLUDES EXPERIMENTATION USING HF RADAR COMPONENTS AS A POTENTIAL MEANS FOR DELIVERING EMBEDDED HF COMMUNICATIONS IN THE NORTHERN LATITUDES ABOVE 65 NORTH.

EMBEDDED WITHIN THE TWSC IS THE FLIGHT TEST SERVICES DIVISION, A DIVISION OF THE TEST DIRECTORATE.  THE DIVISION PROVIDES END-TO-END FLIGHT TEST PLANNING DESIGN DEVELOPMENT INTEGRATION AND TEST EXECUTION AS WELL AS FLEXIBLE LAUNCH PLATFORMS AND UNIQUE LOW-COST TARGET SOLUTIONS. THIS EFFORT IS DIRECTLY RELATED TO THE GOALS OF THE DIRECTORATE IN THAT IT SUPPORTS PROJECTS THAT APPLY STATE-OF-THE-ART TECHNOLOGIES TO CORRECT DEFICIENCIES IN DOD T&E CAPABILITIES.

DATA. MINED XAI HAS DEVELOPED DEEP TOPOLOGICAL MODELING CAPABILITIES BY EXTENDING DIMENSIONALITY

THE UNIVERSITY OF CONNECTICUT (UCONN), RTX TECHNOLOGY RESEARCH CENTER (RTRC) AND RAYTHEON (LEGACY RAYTHEON MISSILES AND DEFENSE (RMD)) PROPOSE THE MANUFACTURING RESEARCH FOR HYPERSONIC AIR-BREATHING WEAPONS (MRPHAW) PROGRAM, A 47-MONTH EFFORT TO INCREASE THE MANUFACTURING READINESS OF ADVANCED AIRFRAME WELDMENTS THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF TOOLS AND MATERIAL UNDERSTANDING FOR NICKEL-BASED ALLOYS (E.G., INCONEL 718 AND 625, HAYNES 230 AND 282).
MRPHAW WILL DEVELOP, PROTOTYPE AND TRANSITION LEADING-EDGE RESEARCH TO ADDRESS HISTORICAL CHALLENGES IN: (I) ELECTRON-BEAM WELD MODELING; (II) CRACKING IN AND AROUND WELDMENTS; AND, (III) MATERIAL SOURCING-DRIVEN WELD VARIATIONS. MRPHAW WILL DEVELOP WELD PARAMETER AND HEAT TREAT SOLUTIONS FOR AM TO WROUGHT JOINTS TO PREVENT WELD CRACKING AND HAVE HIGHER FIDELITY ANALYSIS FOR NEW DESIGNS.

OBJECTIVES - NEW RESEARCH IS NEEDED TO ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING IN: (A) THE CHARACTERISTICS, BEHAVIORS AND MODELING OF DISSIMILAR ALLOY WELDS; (B) THE PREDICTION AND MITIGATION OF HOT CRACKING, DISTORTION, AND RESIDUAL STRESSES; AND, (C) THE IMPACTS OF SOURCE MATERIAL VARIATIONS WELDED COMPONENTS. MRPHAW ADDRESSES THESE CHALLENGES BY THROUGH FOUR MAIN THRUSTS: (I) WELD PROCESS MAPPING TO GAIN UNDERSTANDING OF HIGH NICKEL ALLOY WELD CHARACTERISTICS; ; (II) WELD STRATEGIES TO MITIGATE DISTORTIONS; (III) PREDICTION AND MITIGATION OF HOT CRACKING; AND, (IV) RESEARCH TO PREDICT AND MITIGATE THE IMPACT OF SOURCE MATERIAL VARIATIONS ON WELD CHARACTERISTICS.

SCOPE OF WORK - RTX WILL SUPPORT MRPHAW EXECUTION ACROSS FIVE TASKS. THE PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE IS FROM SEPTEMBER 30, 2023 TO AUGUST 20, 2027 (47 MONTHS).

TASK 1: WELD PROCESS MAPPING - THIS TASK SHALL FOCUS ON COMBINATIONS OF NI-BASED ALLOYS TO INCLUDE INCO 625, INCO 718, HAYNES 230 AND HAYNES 282.
- RTRC SHALL PROVIDE PERMUTATIONS OF MATERIAL COMBINATIONS, WELD METHOD & PARAMETERS, JOINT
CONFIGURATIONS, & PLATE THICKNESSES MOST RELEVANT TO CRACKING ISSUES.
- RTRC SHALL FACILITATE JOINING OPERATIONS BY PROVIDING WELDED SAMPLES AND ACCOMPANYING WELD
PARAMETER DATA THAT BRACKET ACTUAL AEROSTRUCTURE ASSEMBLY PROCESSES.
- RTRC SHALL ASSIST WITH GENERATION OF CRITICAL MATERIALS DATA FOR FINITE ELEMENT (FE) MODEL
REFINEMENT.
- RTRC SHALL ASSIST W/ CREATION OF WELD PROCESS MAPS AS A FUNCTION OF BOTH WELD PARAMETERS
& DISSIMILAR WELD ALLOY COMPOSITIONS, TO PINPOINT REGIONS PRONE TO RESIDUAL STRESS, DISTORTION, & CRACKING FOR FE MODEL CALIBRATION.
TASK 2: INTEGRATED FE AND EXPERIMENTAL WELDING STUDIES
THIS TASK SHALL DELIVER AND DEMONSTRATE WELD PROCESS OPTIMIZATION TOOLS THAT INCREASE YIELD.
- RTRC SHALL ASSIST WITH: (I) REFINEMENT AND CALIBRATION OF THERMAL FE MODELS; (II) VALIDATION OF STRESS FE MODELS W/ RESIDUAL STRESS, DISTORTION, AND CRACK FORMATION DATA; AND (III) CREATION OF RESIDUAL STRESS AND DISTORTION PREDICTION MAPS FOR VARIOUS SETS OF WELDING CONDITIONS USING THE VALIDATED FE MODEL.
TASK 3: PREDICTION & MITIGATION OF HOT CRACKING - THIS TASK SHALL PRODUCE A UNIFIED ANALYTICAL-COMPUTATIONAL-EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH FOR HOT CRACKING THAT ENABLES ACCURATE PREDICTION & MITIGATION OF THIS PHENOMENON.
- RTRC SHALL INTEGRATE: (I) COMPUTATIONAL FLUID DYNAMICS ANALYSIS TO PREDICT MELT POOL
CHARACTERISTICS; (II) PHASE FIELD (PF) MODELING METHOD TO SIMULATE SOLIDIFICATION W/ CORRESPONDING MICROSTRUCTURE & (III) CRACK PROPAGATION & ARRESTÃ¢Â‚¬Â€�LEVERAGING PAST WORK.
TASK 4: MATERIAL SOURCING-RELATED VARIATIONS - THIS TASK SHALL DETERMINE & RATIONALIZE VARIATIONS IN WELD CHARACTERISTICS BECAUSE OF DIFFERENCES IN SOURCE MATERIAL.
- RTRC SHALL PROVIDE GUIDANCE ON THE ALLOYS, WELDING TECHNIQUES, & MATERIAL FORM FACTORS
CURRENTLY EMPLOYED IN THE ASSEMBLY OF HYPERSONIC PLATFORMS.
- RTRC SHALL PROVIDE SUITABLE MATERIALS & WELDMENTS FOR ANALYSIS OF MICROSTRUCTURES &
THERMOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES AT UCONN. MATERIALS SHALL INCLUDE PLATES, OR SHEETS & AM POWDERS.
TASK 5: PROGRAM MANAGEMENT - RTRC SHALL PARTICIPATE IN PROGRAMMATIC DISCUSSIONS W/ AFRL/
WELDMENT RESEARCH AND PROTOTYPING FOR HYPERSONIC AIR-BREATHING WEAPONS AND ADVANCED MATERIAL MANUFACTURING RESEARCH

THE B-52 PROGRAM OFFICE REQUIRES THE SERVICES OF TWO (2) SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS (SMES) TO DEVELOP AND EXECUTE THE RADAR MODERNIZATION PROGRAM. THE COMBINATION OF THE TWO SMES MUST DEMONSTRATE COMPREHENSIVE EXPERIENCE AND KNOWLEDGE OF THE SUBJECT MATTER INTENDED AND SHALL POSSESS THE FOLLOWING:

2.1.1	CHIEF ENGINEERING EXPERIENCE WITH ACAT 1 PROGRAMS
2.1.2	SYSTEMS ENGINEERING AND AIRWORTHINESS CERTIFICATIONS PROCESSES

2.5 KBRWYLE WILL SUPPORT PROGRAM OFFICE EVALUATION OF MONTHLY EARNED VALUE MANAGEMENT (EVM) DATA PROVIDED BY THE OEM AND SUPPLIERS AND PROVIDE ASSESSMENTS OF THE DATA AND THE PROGRAM STATUS.

2.1.1	THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL GATHER AND REVIEW EXISTING STUDIES, ASSESSMENTS, AND ANALYSIS TO INCLUDE WAR GAME REPORTS; TECHNOLOGY DEMONSTRATION/EXPERIMENTATION RESULTS; AND OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY OF DEFENSE, JOINT STAFF, SERVICE CHIEF, COMBATANT COMMANDER, FEDERALLY FUNDED RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT CENTER (FFRDC) STUDIES, ANALYSIS, AND ASSESSMENTS.  THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DEVELOP OR ADAPT METHODOLOGIES AS REQUIRED TO IMPLEMENT AND EXPLORE APPLICATIONS OF NEW TECHNOLOGIES.
2.1.2	BASED ON THE RESULTS OF THE EXISTING ANALYSIS AND REPORTS AND ADDITIONAL STUDY OUTCOMES, THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL MAKE RECOMMENDATIONS AND EVALUATE THE STAND UP AND EXECUTION OF IDENTIFIED PROGRAMS AS PART OF THE AIR FORCEÂ€™S STRATEGIC DEVELOPMENT PLANNING, PLANNING FOR DEVELOPMENT, AND EXPERIMENTATION.  
2.1.3	THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE ANALYSIS AND RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THE COORDINATION OF COMPREHENSIVE STUDIES OF CAPABILITIES REQUIRED TO OVERCOME THE CURRENT AND ANTICIPATED STRATEGIC, OPERATIONAL, AND TACTICAL ENVIRONMENTS.  THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE ANALYSIS OF STUDIES, DEMONSTRATIONS, AND EXPERIMENTS TO DETERMINE AND FILL PRIORITIZED CAPABILITY GAPS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL IDENTIFY APPROPRIATE CAPABILITY AREAS FOR FURTHER STUDIES AND ANALYSIS PLUS MAKE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THE APPROPRIATE AGENCY OR INSTITUTION TO STUDY IDENTIFIED AREAS.

2.1.6	THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE ANALYSIS AND RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF TEST AND EXPERIMENTATION CAMPAIGNS TO TEST HYPOTHESES AND DEMONSTRATE CAPABILITY. 
2.1.7	THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE RECOMMENDATIONS TO SUPPORT FUTURE CAPABILITY DEVELOPMENT FROM APPROPRIATE/RELEVANT CONFERENCES, WAR GAMES, PROGRESS REVIEWS, PLANNING MEETINGS, SEMINARS, ETC. 
2.1.8	THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL ASSESS EXISTING AND PLANNED CAPABILITIES RELATIVE TO THE ANTICIPATED THREAT; DEVELOP ACQUISITION AND BUDGETARY RECOMMENDATIONS, TO INCLUDE SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATIVE RESEARCH (SBIR) INITIATIVES.

2.2.2	PROVIDE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR MODEL BASED SYSTEMS ENGINEERING SOLUTIONS INTO EXISTING PROCESSES

THE PRIMARY PURPOSE OF THE APLSS IS TO DEMONSTRATE THAT A COMBINATION OF DIGITAL BREATHING REGULATOR AND PHYSIOLOGICAL DATA FROM HUMAN-MOUNTED MONITORING DEVICE CAN DECREASE THE RISK OF DEVELOPING THE SYMPTOMS OF A PHYSIOLOGIC EPISODE BY DETECTING THE ONSET OF A PHYSIOLOGIC EVENT IN ORDER TO SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASE CREW MEMBER SAFETY.  THE FCT PROPOSES TO COMBINE COBHAMÂ€™S DIGITAL BREATHING REGULATOR (SMART REGULATOR) WITH COBHAMÂ€™S INHALATION SENSOR BLOCK (ISB) AND EXHALATION SENSOR BLOCK (ESB), AND ELBITÂ€™S/CANARY INTEGRATED PHYSIOLOGICAL MONITORING SYSTEM. THIS RUDIMENTARY SYSTEM WILL FORM THE FOUNDATION FOR AN AUTONOMOUS LIFE SUPPORT SYSTEM THAT CAN BE USED TO DETECT, WARN, AND MITIGATE PHYSIOLOGICAL EVENTS (PES) THAT ARE BEING EXPERIENCED BY PILOTS TODAY.
 3.0 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS - APLSS SHOULD BE OF AN OPEN ARCHITECTURE DESIGN AND USE COMMONLY AVAILABLE INTERFACES.  THE EQUIPMENT SHALL COMPLY WITH THE FOLLOWING REQUIREMENTS:

3.1 FORM AND FIT  
ALL COMPONENTS SHALL INTEGRATE INTO EXISTING OR COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE OFF-THE-SHELF MBU-20/P MASKS.
3.2	SENSING  
3.2.1	COBHAM SHALL PROVIDE A SENSOR SUITE COMPRISED OF THE ISB AND ESB.  NO CHANGES TO THE CURRENT ISB AND ESB ARE ENVISIONED FOR THIS PROJECT
3.2.2	ELBIT SHALL PROVIDE A STANDARD HGU-55/P HELMET WITH  INTEGRATED CANARY SENSOR AND INTERFACE SYSTEM, WHICH WILL BE CONNECTED TO A PC APPLICATION THAT PRESENTS DATA IN REAL-TIME AND RECORDS DATA (IN PARALLEL TO THE COMMUNICATION WITH COBHAMÂ€™S REGULATOR). CANARY INTERFACE SYSTEM MAY ALSO BE USED TO INTERFACE THE REGULATOR IF NEEDED. CANARY DATA WILL ALSO BE RECORDED ON THE HELMET ITSELF. 
3.3	SMART REGULATOR
COBHAMÂ€™S SMART REGULATOR (SR) SHALL PROVIDE TYPICAL PERFORMANCE (SIMILAR TO CRU-98 OR CRU-103) UNDER NORMAL CONDITIONS.  IN ADDITION, THE REGULATOR SHALL DEMONSTRATE AUTONOMOUS ADJUSTMENT OF OXYGEN BASED ON PHYSIOLOGICAL INPUTS.  THE SR WILL INTERFACE WITH THE ISB, ESB, AND CANARY SENSOR AND BE ABLE TO STORE SYSTEM PERFORMANCE DATA FOR FOLLOW-ON PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS.  THIS OXYGEN ADJUSTMENT WILL BE CONTROLLED BY A NEW ALGORITHM BEING DEVELOPED UNDER THIS EFFORT.  

3.3.1	INTERFACE DEVELOPMENT.  THIS PROJECT WILL  DEFINE INTERFACES BETWEEN:
Â€¢	SR AND ISB, ESB SENSING
Â€¢	SR AND THE HELMET Â€“ MOUNTED CANARY SENSOR.
O	THIS INCLUDES MESSAGE FORMATS AND RATES THAT WILL BE AGREED UPON BETWEEN COBHAM AND ELBIT
Â€¢	UPDATES FOR CANARY SENSOR - MONITOR INTERFACES TO INCLUDE RELEVANT REGULATOR PARAMETERS PRESENTATION ON THE MONITOR

3.3.2	ALGORITHM DEVELOPMENT.  THE OXYGEN CONTROL ALGORITHM WILL BE PART OF THE SR.  THE ALGORITHM WILL BE DESIGNED TO REACT TO CERTAIN CONDITIONS BASED ON RECOMMENDATIONS AGREED TO BY NAMRU-D AND COBHAM SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS (SMES).  FOR THIS PROJECT THE ALGORITHM WILL AUTONOMOUSLY SHOW REACTION TO A SPECIFIED NUMBER OF INPUT CONDITIONS.

3.4	SYSTEM CALIBRATION.  THE SENSORS SHALL BE CALIBRATED TO AN ESTABLISHED STANDARD THAT ENCOMPASSES THE PERFORMANCE RANGES BEFORE THEY ARE INTEGRATED INTO THE SYSTEM. CALIBRATION MUST ACCURATELY TAKE INTO ACCOUNT THE DYNAMICS OF PILOT BREATHING.

3.4.1	CALIBRATION STANDARD.  COBHAM AND ELBIT SHALL COORDINATE EFFORTS WITH THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT TEAM TO DEVELOP AND APPROVE A STANDARD FOR SENSOR CALIBRATION THAT DEFINES THE EXPECTED SYSTEM PERFORMANCE CAPABILITIES.
I.	THE CONTRACTORS MAY REQUEST THE ASSISTANCE AND SUPPORT OF GOVERNMENT TEAM MEMBERS TO REFINE AND EVALUATE THE CONTRACTORÂ€™S CALIBRATION EFFORTS.
II.	THE CONTRACTORS SHALL REACH A CONSENSUS WITH GOVERNMENT TEAM MEMBERS REGARDING THE CALIBRATION STANDARD PRIOR TO ITS IMPLEMENTATION.
3.4.2	CALIBRATION MAINTENANCE.  THE CONTRACTORS SHALL DETERMINE HOW LONG THEIR RESPECTIVE SENSORS WILL HOLD CALIBRATION TO PROVIDE REPRODUCIBLE AND ACCEPTABLE PERFORMANCE. 

3.5	SYSTEM VERIFICATION.  THE APLSS WILL UNDERGO FOUR LEVELS OF VERIFICATION: 1) BASIC SR PERFORMANCE CHARACTERIZATION, 2) APLSS PROTOTYPE TESTING, 3) APLSS UNMANNED TESTING, 4) APLSS MANNED CENTRIFUGE TESTING, AND 5) APLSS MANNED ALTITUDE TESTING

I.	THE SR WILL BE ASSESSED TO MAKE SURE THAT IT PROVIDES PERFORMANCE SIMILAR (AT A MINIMUM MEET THE FLOW, ALTITUDE AND G-COMPENSATION REQUIREMENTS) OVER ALTITUDE AND PRESSURE TO A CRU-93 OR CRU-103.  IT IS ENVISIONED THAT THIS TESTING WILL BE INITIALLY PERFORMED AT COBHAM AND THEN SUBSEQUENTLY AT NAMRU-D.
II.	THE PROTOTYPE (TRL 4) TESTING WILL BE THE PRELIMINARY INTEGRATION OF THE COBHAM COMPONENTS (SR, ISB, ESB) WITH THE ELBIT CANARY SENSOR AND WILL OCCUR AT COBHAMÂ€™S ORCHARD PARK, NY FACILITY.  THIS TESTING WILL SHOW COMMUNICATION BETWEEN THE COMPONENTS AND RUDIMENTARY CONTROL OF OXYGEN.
III.	THE UNMANNED TESTING (TRL 5) WILL DEMONSTRATE DEVELOPED PACKAGED COMPONENTS INTEGRATED TOGETHER WITH THE APLSS FULLY FUNCTIONING (I.E., DETECT AND CONTROL) TO THE TEST CONDITIONS OF TABLE 1.  THIS TESTING IS TO ENSURE THAT THE APLSS IS ROBUST ENOUGH TO ENTER THE MANNED TESTING PHASE.  THE FINAL TESTING IS ENVISIONED TO BE PERFORMED ON A ROBD/E OR EQUIVALENT BY NAMRU-D.
IV.	THE MANNED CENTRIFUGE TESTING WILL DEMONSTRATE APLSS PERFORMANCE UNDER STRESSFUL CONDITIONS THAT MAY BE ENCOUNTER DURING A MISSION.   IT IS ENVISIONED THAT THIS TESTING WILL BE PERFORMED TWICE AT KBRWYLE LABORATORIES.  AFTER THE FIRST TEST, APLSS PERFORMANCE WILL BE ANALYZED AND POTENTIAL MODIFICATIONS IDENTIFIED, IMPLEMENTED, AND RETESTED IN AN ITERATIVE FASHION.

3.5.1	SYSTEM VERIFICATION PLAN.  APLSS VERIFICATION SHALL INCLUDE TESTING THAT REPLICATES THE DESIRED INPUT CONDITIONS AND THE DESIRED RESPONSES AS DEFINED IN TABLE 1. COBHAM SHALL PROVIDE A WRITTEN PLAN FOR SYSTEM VERIFICATION TESTING AND COORDINATE THAT PLAN WITH ELBIT AND THE GOVERNMENT PRIOR TO STARTING VERIFICATION TESTING.  

3.6	REAL-TIME DATA (RTD) ACCESS.  APLSS, VIA THE SR, SHALL PROVIDE A MEANS FOR WIRED REAL-TIME OUTPUT OF PARAMETERS TO BE MUTUALLY AGREED UPON TO INCLUDE AT A MINIMUM: SPO2, PPCO2, PPO2, BREATHING RATE, CABIN PRESSURE, BIT STATUS (BOTH), AND MASK LEAKAGE/PRESSURE.

3.6.1	RTD OUTPUT.  THE FORMAT OF THE DATA STREAM SHALL BE MUTUALLY AGREED UPON BY THE GOVERNMENT AND COBHAM/ELBIT.  COBHAM/ELBIT SHALL PROVIDE DOCUMENTATION FOR THE APPLICATION PROGRAMMING INTERFACE (API).  THIS DATA OUTPUT SHOULD RUN CONCURRENTLY WITH ANY OTHER MODE OF OPERATION AND DATA STORAGE.
I.	DOCUMENTATION SHALL BE PROVIDED TO DESCRIBE THE DATA FORMAT OUTPUTTED FOR THIS REAL-TIME ACCESS.  ANY DATA STREAMS SHALL HAVE A TIME-STAMP FOR SYNCHRONIZATION.
II.	THE FORMAT OF THE REAL-TIME DATA STREAM SHALL NOT REQUIRE ANY PROPRIETARY OR NON-OPEN SOURCE SOFTWARE TO DECRYPT, DECODE, OR OTHERWISE ACCESS THE DATA, OTHER THAN SOFTWARE THE GOVERNMENT ALREADY POSSESSES (I.E., MATLAB, LABVIEW, R, SAS, OR SPREADSHEET PROGRAM).
III.	COBHAM/ELBIT SHALL MUTUALLY AGREE WITH THE GOVERNMENT ON THE OUTPUT RATE OF THE REAL-TIME DATA STREAM, WITH THE MAXIMUM OUTPUT RATE NOT EXCEEDING THE LIMITS OF A 100MBAUD RT-UDP.
3.7	 BUILT-IN TEST.  COBHAM/ELBIT SHALL PROVIDE A BUILT IN TEST (BIT) OR ALTERNATE RAPID METHOD THAT VERIFIES EACH SENSOR IS OR IS NOT WARMED UP AND EACH SENSOR IS OR IS NOT OPERATING PROPERLY PRIOR TO EXTENDED DATA COLLECTION.

3.7.1	IN-OPERATION BIT REQUIREMENTS:
I.	THE BIT NEEDS TO MONITOR IF SENSORS ARE OPERATING CORRECTLY AND AS EXPECTED (E.G., NOT 0MMHG FOR INHALE O2, NOR 0MMHG FOR CABIN/AMBIENT PRESSURE).
II.	THE BIT NEEDS TO CHECK IF DATA IS BEING SAVED TO A FILE.
III.	THE BIT NEEDS TO PROVIDE AN ALERT UPON SYSTEM OR SENSOR FAULT.
3.8	EVENT MARKER.  AN EVENT MARKER THAT ALLOWS TEST PERSONNEL TO MARK SIGNIFICANT EVENTS IN RECORDED DATA WILL BE AVAILABLE WITH THE ELBIT CANARY SENSOR DATA RECORDING.
3.9	GUIDANCE ON PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS.  A GUIDELINE WILL BE INCLUDED WITH THIS STATEMENT OF WORK THAT PROVIDES A REFERENCE FOR APLSS SPECIFICATIONS AND PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS RELATED TO THE CONTENT OF SECTION 3. 4.1	BATTLE MANAGER DEVELOPMENT
THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL EXTEND PREVIOUS DEVELOPMENTS IN BATTLE MANAGEMENT SIMULATION TO FURTHER ENHANCE BATTLE MANAGEMENT CONTROL OF SYSTEMS PROTECTING AIR BASES.  THESE EXTENSIONS SHALL MEET THE FOLLOWING REQUIREMENTS: 
1.	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL EXPLORE THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES TO IMPROVE BATTLE MANAGEMENT DECISIONS AND SIMULATION OUTCOMES. THESE TECHNIQUES INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO, LIMITED LOOK AHEAD AND ADVERSARIAL SEARCH. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL EXTEND OR DEVELOP NEW SCHEMES AND ALGORITHMS AND REPORT ON PERFORMANCE, CONSTRAINTS, AND LIMITATIONS. 
2.	THE BATTLE MANAGER SIMULATION CAPABILITY SHALL MAKE ASSIGNMENTS COUNTERING DIVERSE THREATS USING DIVERSE DEFENSIVE ASSETS.  THE THREATS MAY INCLUDE ATTACK FIGHTERS, BOMBERS, CRUISE MISSILES (SUBSONIC, SUPERSONIC), AND BALLISTIC MISSILES.  DEFENSIVE ASSETS MAY INCLUDE PILOTED AND UNPILOTED AIR VEHICLES, SURFACE TO AIR MISSILES (SAMS), AIR TO AIR MISSILES (AAMS), SURFACE DIRECTED ENERGY (DE) WEAPONS, AIRBORNE DE WEAPONS, AND WILL VARY IN TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT RANGE AND CAPACITY.
3.	THE BATTLE MANAGER SHALL BE FLEXIBLE ENOUGH TO EXERCISE A WIDE VARIETY OF COMBINATIONS OF LEGACY AND ADVANCED CONCEPTS ACROSS THE TRADE SPACE.  FOR EXAMPLE, THE MAKEUP OF IAMD SYSTEMS OF SYSTEMS IN TERMS OF NUMBERS AND PLACEMENT MUST BE AN INPUT INTO THE MISSION VIGNETTE.
4.	THE BATTLE MANAGEMENT SOLUTION SHALL BE COMPATIBLE WITH AFSIM (SPECIFIC VERSION IS TO BE DETERMINED).
5.	THE BATTLE MANAGEMENT SOLUTION SHALL SUPPORT CONSTRUCTIVE SIMULATION (I.E., THERE IS NO HUMAN IN THE LOOP).
6.	THE BATTLE MANAGEMENT SOLUTION SHALL EXECUTE FASTER THAN REAL TIME WHEN OPERATING IN THE FULL MISSION VIGNETTE.
7.	THE SOLUTION MAY ENTIRELY REPLACE OR RE-USE ELEMENTS OF THE RULE-BASED BATTLE MANAGER.  CURRENT RULE-BASED BATTLE MANAGEMENT PRIMARILY ASSIGNS ASSETS THAT CAN ENGAGE ON A FIRST IN, FIRST OUT (FIFO) BASIS.  THE CURRENT BATTLE MANAGEMENT SCHEME DOES SIMPLE TARGET DE-CONFLICTION TO AVOID OVER ALLOCATION (ONLY ONE SHOT PER THREAT AT A TIME).  THE CURRENT RULE-BASED BATTLE MANAGEMENT SCHEME DOES NOT ACCOUNT FOR COST.
8.	THE BATTLE MANAGEMENT SOLUTION MAY ASSUME THAT TARGET SENSING AND TRACKING IS SUFFICIENT TO SUPPORT ENGAGEMENTS OUT TO THE FULL RANGE OF ALL WEAPON TYPES.
9.	THE BATTLE MANAGEMENT SOLUTION MAY ASSUME COMMUNICATIONS DATA LINKS HAVE SUFFICIENT BANDWIDTH AND THROUGHPUT TO SUPPORT ENGAGEMENTS OUT TO THE FULL RANGE OF ALL WEAPON TYPES.
10.	IT IS DESIRABLE THAT THE BATTLE MANAGEMENT SOLUTION BE IMPLEMENTED IN AN UNCLASSIFIED MISSION VIGNETTE OF SUITABLE COMPLEXITY.
4.2	AFSIM AIR COMBAT MODELING
THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP AN AIR COMBAT MODELING CAPABILITY, LEVERAGING MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES.  THIS IS A CONTINUATION OF THE EFFORT STARTED UNDER A PREVIOUS RAST TASK ORDER (TASK ORDER 13). THE MODELING CAPABILITY SHOULD BE EXPANDED TO ANSWER THE FOLLOWING RESEARCH QUESTIONS:  
1.	CAN TRANSFER LEARNING BE USED TO TRAIN AN AGENT IN A NON-AFSIM SIMULATION ENGINE AND PORTED TO AFSIM?
2.	CAN LEVERAGING PREVIOUS MANEUVER LEARNING POLICIES SHORTEN TRAINING TIME WHEN ADDING IN NEW (WEAPON) CAPABILITIES? SIMILARLY FOR MULTI-AGENT TACTIC EXPLORATION FOR AGENTS ON THE SAME SIDE? 
3.	HOW DOES ONE ACCOUNT FOR THE IMPERFECT STATE KNOWLEDGE, PARTIAL OBSERVABILITY, AND LIMITED PLATFORM CAPABILITY FOR AIR-TO-AIR COMBAT IN A MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHM?
4.	HOW CAN ONE INCORPORATE MISSION OBJECTIVES (OR DEGREE OF DEFENSIVENESS) INTO AGENT MODEL?  THAT IS, AN OPERATOR MAY EMPLOY BANZAI TACTICS IN DCA MISSIONS AS OPPOSED SKATE TACTICS IN OCA MISSIONS.
5.	WEAPON (MISSILE) EMPLOYMENT:
A.	HOW DOES INCORPORATING A MISSILE MODEL CHANGE THE UNDERLYING LEARNING AGENT?
B.	WOULD CURRICULUM LEARNING SUPPORT THE INTRODUCTION OF MISSILE MODELS?
C.	HOW DOES ONE ACCOUNT FOR TEMPORAL EFFECTS OF A MISSILE FLY-OUT?
D.	CAN AI LEVERAGE PREDICTED WEZ (LAUNCH COMPUTER) TO EXPEDITE LEARNING?
E.	CAN AI LEVERAGE PREDICTED THREAT WEZ?
F.	WHAT ARE THE RAMIFICATIONS OF CHANGING WEAPON PLATFORMS ON THE AGENT (I.E., CHANGE MISSILE CHARACTERISTICS SUCH AS +/- 25% MAXIMUM RANGE)? IS THERE A GENERIC SOLUTION OR IT IS UNIQUE TO EACH MISSILE PLATFORM?

3.1  RESEARCH IS NEEDED TO DEVELOP GUIDELINES FOR A Ã¢Â‚¬Å“TEAMMATE SELECTION TOOLÃ¢Â‚¬Ï¿½ FOR COMPOSING FLUID TEAMS.  ONE CRITICAL TASK IS TO IDENTIFY INDIVIDUAL TEAM MEMBER APTITUDES, SKILLS, AND EXPERIENCES THAT CONTRIBUTE TO BOTH EFFECTIVE TASKWORK (THE TASK-SPECIFIC CAPABILITIES REQUIRED TO PERFORM THE TASK) AND TEAMWORK (THE TEAM COORDINATION AND TEAMWORK BEHAVIORS THAT FACILITATE EFFECTIVE TEAM PERFORMANCE), SO THAT THESE ASSETS CAN BE QUICKLY IDENTIFIED, SELECTED, AND FORMED INTO EFFECTIVE TEAMS.  A FIRST STEP TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL IS TO CONDUCT A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF RESEARCH ON THE FORMATION AND PERFORMANCE OF FLUID TEAMS, IN ORDER TO LEVERAGE AND EXTEND THIS RESEARCH TO MEET THE CURRENT REQUIREMENT.
RESEARCH TASKS INCLUDE:
3.1.1 IDENTIFY THE FACTORS THAT WILL PREDICT FUTURE SUCCESS IN FLUID TEAMS. INTEGRATE EXISTING RESEARCH TO IDENTIFY THE SKILLS, APTITUDES, AND RELATED FACTORS THAT UNDERLIE EFFECTIVE PERFORMANCE IN DYNAMIC, FLUID TEAMS. IDENTIFY FACTORS (SUCH AS THE TYPE OF TASK) THAT MAY MODERATE THESE EFFECTS. IDENTIFY OTHER APPROACHES TO SUPPORT EFFECTIVE FLUID TEAM PERFORMANCE (E.G., TEAMWORK TRAINING). REVIEW EXISTING TEAM RESEARCH IN COGNATE FIELDS SUCH AS AVIATION (FLIGHT CREWS) AND HEALTHCARE (SURGICAL TEAMS) TO EXTRACT AND LEVERAGE PRIOR RESEARCH ON FLUID TEAMS.
3.1.2 EXAMINE WHAT BIOGRAPHICAL DATA ON INDIVIDUALS (E.G., SKILLS, APTITUDES, JOB EXPERIENCE) CAN BE DRAWN FROM EXISTING RECORDS AS WELL AS WHAT OTHER POTENTIALLY USEFUL DATA MAY BE NEEDED. EXAMINE HOW THIS INFORMATION CAN BE INTEGRATED, CONDENSED, AND PRESENTED TO THE END USER IN A FORM THAT IS EASILY ACCESSIBLE AND USABLE FOR SELECTION GUIDANCE. 
3.1.3 IDENTIFY METHODS THAT MAY ENHANCE THE PERFORMANCE OF FLUID TEAMS AFTER INITIAL FORMATION TO SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF SWIFT TRUST, COMMON GROUND, AND EFFECTIVE COORDINATION OF TEAMWORK BEHAVIORS.  
3.1.4 PROVIDE GUIDELINES AND RECOMMENDATIONS FOR RESEARCH TO SUPPORT THE SELECTION AND FORMATION OF FLUID TEAMS, AS WELL AS RESEARCH GAPS IN THE EXISTING LITERATURE.

AS WE MOVE INTO JOINT ALL DOMAIN OPERATIONS, CONSIDERATION FOR ACTIONS BEYOND VEHICLE MOVEMENTS IS DESIRED.  SPECIFICALLY, THE INCORPORATION OF CYBER ACTIONS INTO THE DECISION SPACE ADDS NEW DIMENSIONALITY TO CECEP.  THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS WORK IS TO INCORPORATE AND OPTIMALLY PRESENT TO THE DECISION MAKER INFORMATION ABOUT CYBER ACTIONS INTO THE REASONING AGENT (ALONG WITH THE CURRENT VEHICLE ACTIONS) FOR OPTIMAL ACTION RECOMMENDATION CONSIDERATION.  AS THE DOD MOVES TOWARD JOINT ALL DOMAIN C2, THE ABILITY TO CONSIDER CYBER OPTIONS WITH, OR INSTEAD OF, AIR OPTIONS AS VIABLE COURSES OF ACTION IS CRITICAL.  THE SPECIFIC TECHNICAL TASKS TO BE ACCOMPLISHED UNDER THIS EFFORT INCLUDE:

3.2	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL DETERMINE FAST TRAC SCENARIO USE CASES IN WHICH CYBER PLAYS ARE APPLICABLE
3.3	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL DETERMINE APPLICABLE METRICS FOR ASSESSING PLAY FIT (PSUCCESS, PSTEALTH, PBURN, ETC).
3.4	THE SUBCONTRACT SHALL WORK WITH THE CECEP TEAM TO DETERMINE A REASONABLE LEVEL OF ABSTRACTION OF CURRENT METRICS, WAYS TO CONSIDER HETEROGENEOUS METRICS, AND WEIGHTS OF METRICS FOR SCENARIO USE CASES.
3.5	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH THE AFSIM/WARLOCK TEAM TO SCRIPT CYBER ACTIONS INTO THE FAST TRAC SCENARIO.
3.6	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH THE IMPACT/WARLOCK TEAM TO DESIGN AND DEVELOP VISUALIZATIONS/INTERFACES TO DEPICT CYBER ACTIVITY.
3.7	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH THE FAST TRAC TEAM TO STORY BOARD DEMONSTRATION OF NEW CECEP CAPABILITIES.  
3.8	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH THE E-MS&A GROUP TO DETERMINE OTHER CYBER ACTIONS TO INCORPORATE INTO CECEP/IMPACT TO ENSURE A ROBUST TOOL FOR THE E-MS&A TOOLKIT.
3.2	MEDUSA. 
3.2.1	THE SUBCONTRACTOR WORK WITH THE ENHANCED IMPACT/MEDUSA C2 TEAM TO IDENTIFY AND REFINE HMI REQUIREMENTS TO SUPPORT OPERATOR INTERACTIONS IN SUPPORT OF BASE DEFENSE AND CSUAS OPERATIONS. 
3.2.2	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH THE ENHANCED IMPACT/MEDUSA C2 TEAM TO DEVELOP UX DESIGNS FOR THE ENHANCED IMPACT/MEDUSA C2 HMIS ACROSS THE VARIOUS OPERATOR INTERFACE PLATFORMS (E.G., DESKTOP CONSOLE SYSTEM, ATAK, ETC.). DESIGN WIREFRAME CONCEPTS WILL BE DEVELOPED WITHIN A DESIGNATED UX APPLICATION SUCH AS ADOBE XD OR BALSAMIC. SUBCONTRACTOR WILL COORDINATE WITH SYSTEM DEVELOPERS ON INTERFACE CONCEPTS TO DETERMINE FEASIBILITY, SUSTAINABILITY, AND SUPPORTABILITY OF ENVISIONED CONCEPTS.
3.2.3	THE SUBCONTRACT SHALL SUPPORT QUICK-LOOK DEMONSTRATIONS, HMI ASSESSMENT AND SIMULATION EVALUATIONS AS WELL AS POTENTIAL FIELD EXERCISE AS REQUIRED.

2.1	SBR&D REQUIREMENTS
FOR EACH OBJECTIVES 2.2 AND 2.3 BELOW:
2.1.1	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL IDENTIFY THE SBR&D REQUIREMENTS TO EFFECTIVELY TEST AND DEMONSTRATE THE TECHNOLOGY; THE REQUIREMENTS SHALL INCLUDE THE TYPE OF ANALYSIS AND MODEL FIDELITY REQUIRED. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP AND COORDINATE A SIMULATION REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT WITH THE PRIME AND AFRL.
2.1.2	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL RESEARCH CURRENT SBR&D CAPABILITIES AND ASSESS THEIR APPLICABILITY TO MEET THE REQUIREMENTS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL ASSESS BOTH IN-HOUSE (AFRL/RQQ) TOOLS AND CANDIDATE THIRD-PARTY CAPABILITIES; THE ASSESSMENT SHALL CONSIDER THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF THE TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT AND TEST, AS WELL AS SCHEDULE AND RESOURCE AVAILABILITY AND SHALL DETERMINE WHAT SBR&D CAPABILITIES CAN BE LEVERAGED AND WHAT CAPABILITIES MUST BE DEVELOPED. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP AND COORDINATE A SOFTWARE DESIGN DESCRIPTION AND SIMULATION ARCHITECTURE WITH THE PRIME AND AFRL.
2.1.3	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP THE SPECIFIC AUTONOMOUS CONTROL TECHNOLOGIES, AS OUTLINED BELOW, BASED ON THE DESIGN AND APPROACH PLAN; THE TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT SHALL BE BASED ON A SPIRAL DEVELOPMENT APPROACH AND SHALL INCORPORATE QUANTITATIVE TECHNOLOGY ASSESSMENTS TO DETERMINE THE MILITARY VALUE OF THE TECHNOLOGY BEING RESEARCHED AND DEVELOPED.
2.1.4	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP THE SBR&D TESTBED BASED ON THE DESIGN AND APPROACH PLAN. THE SBR&D TESTBED MAY INCLUDE DESKTOP M&S TOOLS, CONSTRUCTIVE SIMULATION, VIRTUAL SIMULATION, HARDWAREÃ‚Â­ IN-THE-LOOP SIMULATION, AND FLIGHT TEST ASSETS. THE TESTBED MAY LEVERAGE SBR&D CAPABILITIES IN THE AFRL/RQQ AEROSPACE VEHICLE TECHNOLOGY ASSESSMENT SIMULATION LAB AND/OR THE CREW SYSTEMS INTEGRATION LAB. THE SBR&D TESTBED SHALL ALLOW FOR: 1) MODELING OF VARIOUS LEVELS OF FIDELITY AND ABSTRACTION; 2) A SIMULATION ARCHITECTURE THAT PROVIDES FOR A COMPREHENSIVE AND FLEXIBLE CAPABILITY ACROSS ALL SBR&D HARDWARE; AND 3) A TRANSITION PATH TO HIGH-FIDELITY TESTING OR TRAINING SIMULATORS AND FLIGHT TEST ASSETS.
2.1.5	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL INTEGRATE AUTONOMOUS CONTROL TECHNOLOGIES INTO THE SBR&D TESTBED. THE TECHNOLOGIES REQUIRING INTEGRATION MAY BE DEVELOPED BY THE SUBCONTRACTOR, THE GOVERNMENT, OR OTHER SUBCONTRACTORS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL DESIGN EXPERIMENTS TO TEST THE INTEGRATED MANNED-UNMANNED AIRCRAFT TEAMING TECHNOLOGIES. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL DISCLOSE THE DESIGNS OF THEIR EXPERIMENTS TO THE PRIME AND GOVERNMENT FOR REVIEW PRIOR TO CONDUCTING ANY TESTS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL CONDUCT TESTS IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) THE DESIGNED EXPERIMENTS. FINALLY, THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL ANALYZE THE RESULTS OF THE TESTS AND REPORT THE FINDINGS TO THE PRIME AND GOVERNMENT.
2.1.6	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PURSUE PARTNERSHIPS WITH LEADING EXPERTS IN THE AUTONOMOUS CONTROL INDUSTRY AND ACADEMIA AND COLLABORATE CLOSELY WITH THE PRIME AND AFRL CUSTOMER TO PRODUCE RESULTS SUITABLE FOR PUBLICATION WHEN APPLICABLE.
2.2	AUTOMATIC COLLISION AVOIDANCE TECHNOLOGY
	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL DESIGN AND TEST AUTOMATIC COLLISION AVOIDANCE ALGORITHMS USING SBR&D. THE SBR&D SHALL PRIMARILY INVOLVE VIRTUAL SIMULATION, BUT MAY INCLUDE CONSTRUCTIVE SIMULATION. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE FOR AN INDEPENDENT ENGINEERING ANALYSIS AND TECHNICAL ASSESSMENT OF AUTOMATIC COLLISION AVOIDANCE ALGORITHMS.
2.3	SIMULATION CAPABILITY CONFIGURATION AND MAINTENANCE ACTIVITIES
	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT SBR&D ACTIVITIES TO PREPARE AND/OR CONFIGURE VARIOUS AVTAS SIMULATORS AND ASSOCIATED SIMULATION CAPABILITIES, ESPECIALLY THOSE INVOLVING THE VIRTUAL (PILOT-INÃ‚Â­THE-LOOP) SIMULATORS; SUCH AS OCTONIANS, TRITONS, MULTI-CREW, AND LAMARS. SPECIFIC TASKS MAY INCLUDE: STICK AND THROTTLE CONFIGURATION OR SWAP OUT; VIDEO SYSTEM STARTUP AND CONFIGURATION; CONTROL LOADER AND/OR FEEL-SYSTEM CONFIGURATION AND OPERATION; SIMULATOR MOTION SYSTEM CONFIGURATION AND OPERATION, PARTICULARLY WITH REGARD TO THE LAMARS SIMULATOR; VIDEO WALL STARTUP AND CONFIGURATION IN THE AVTAS CONTROL ROOM; SIMULATOR CUSTOMIZATIONS TO ENABLE MODIFICATION OR INTEGRATION OF NEW HARDWARE COMPONENTS (AS REQUIRED FOR ANY GIVEN PROJECT); AND MODIFICATIONS TO SIMULATOR COMPONENT WIRING AND/OR NETWORK CONNECTIONS.

1.3.2	MODEL BASED SYSTEMS ENGINEERING (MBSE) FOR MULTI-DOMAIN CAPABILITY ENHANCEMENT

	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE TO THE AUTONOMOUS COLLACORATION OF HETEROGENEOUS AIRCRAFT FOR MISSION PROSECUTION (ACHAMP) PROGRAM.  THIS ACTIVITY MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO PROVIDING OPERATIONAL EXPERTISE FOR SMALL UAS (SUAS), AS WELL AS OTHER CROSS-DOMAIN EXPERTISE TO INCLUDE COMMAND AND CONTOL (C2), AND JOINT TERMINAL ATTACK CONTROLLERS (JTAC) AS APPROPRIATE.

	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF CONCEPTS OF OPERATION (CONOPS) FOR SUAS, SPECIFICALLY TO ACHIEVE ACHAMP PROGRAM OBJECTIVES.
2.2	AUTONOMY TEST, EVALUTION AND TRANSITION
	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE TEST AND EVALUATION OF AUTONOMOUS CONTROL SYSTEMS TECHNOLOGIES. THIS EFFORT MAY INCLUDE CONSTRUCTIVE AND VIRTUAL SIMULATION, SOFTWARE- AND HARDWARE-IN-THE-LOOP SIMULATION, INTEGRATION, AND FLIGHT DEMONSTRATION/TESTING.  THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE TO COLLECT, ASSESS, AND DECOMPOSE OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS TO INFORM TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT FOR OPERATIONAL RELEVANCY, SUITABILITY AND TRANSITION TO THE WARFIGHTER.  
2.3	FLIGHT TEST
	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL HELP TO PLAN, DESIGN, COORDINATE, AND EXECUTE FLIGHT TEST AND FLIGHT TEST RISK REDUCTION ACTIVITIES IN ORDER TO EVALUATE AND DEMONSTRATE ADVANCED TECHNOLOGY CAPABILITIES ON ACTUAL FLIGHT SYSTEMS. THESE FLIGHT SYSTEMS MAY INCLUDE SUAS, ALSUAS, SURROGATE AIRCRAFT, LARGE UAS, OR MANNED AIRCRAFT.  SPECIFIC AREAS OF SUPPORT MAY INCLUDE FLIGHT TEST DESIGN, FLIGHT TEST RISK REDUCTION SIMULATIONS, PLANNING AND INTEGRATION OF RELEVANT FLIGHT SYSTEM AND SUBSYSTEM HARDWARE/SOFTWARE CONFIGURATIONS, INTEGRATION OF COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS, FLIGHT TEST RISK ASSESSMENT, PREPARATION OF REQUIRED FLIGHT TEST APPROVAL DOCUMENTATION, PARTICIPATION IN FLIGHT TEST APPROVAL REVIEWS, PREPARATION OF FLIGHT TEST CARDS, TRAVEL AND PARTICIPATION IN FLIGHT TEST EVENTS, DATA COLLECTION, DATA SYNCHRONIZATION AND ARCHIVING, DATA REDUCTION, AND RESULTS ANALYSIS, VALIDATION AND REPORTING.
2.4	TECHNOLOGY TRANSITION
	THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE TRANSITION OF AUTONOMOUS CONTROL TECHNOLOGIES TO CUSTOMER ORGANIZATIONS. NEEDS INCLUDE AIDING IN CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT TO IDENTIFY CAPABILITY GAPS AND SHAPE TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT, AIDING IN CUSTOMER DEVELOPMENT OF CONCEPTS OF OPERATION (CONOPS), CONCEPTS OF EMPLOYMENT (CONEMP), AND TACTICS, TECHNIQUES AND PROCEDURES (TTPS) FOR NEW CONTROL SYSTEM TECHNOLOGIES.

DESIGN ACTIVITIES SHALL INCLUDE A REVIEW OF THE RELEVANT LITERATURE; CONSIDERATION OF APPROPRIATE SOFTWARE AND HUMAN FACTORS STANDARDS, GUIDELINES, AND BEST PRACTICES; COGNITIVE TASK ANALYSIS, OPERATOR INTERVIEWS, AND A REVIEW OF TRAINING, TACTICS, TECHNIQUES, AND PROCEDURES MATERIAL FOR REQUIREMENTS DEVELOPMENT; AND THE CREATION OF INTERFACE MOCKUPS AS APPROPRIATE. DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES SHALL INCLUDE THE SOFTWARE AND HARDWARE TASKS REQUIRED TO CREATE A TESTABLE PROTOTYPE. THESE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPMENT OF A SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE, SOFTWARE CODING, SOFTWARE TESTING, THE PURCHASE OF HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE COMPONENTS, AND HARDWARE INTEGRATION. FOR SIMULATION EFFORTS IT FURTHER INCLUDES CONSTRUCTING THE SIMULATOR, SIMULATION ENVIRONMENT, AND VALIDATING THEY WORK AS INTENDED. FOR LIVE TEST EFFORTS IT INCLUDES WORKING WITH COTS/GOTS UXSS AND MAY INCLUDE WORKING WITH THE MANUFACTURER TO MODIFY THE UXS TO MEET TEST OBJECTIVES.
4.1.3 TEST AND DEMONSTRATION
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONDUCT TESTS AND/OR DEMONSTRATE ADVANCED UXS HUMAN-MACHINE TEAMING CONTROL STATION INTERFACE TECHNOLOGIES. THESE TESTS AND DEMONSTRATIONS SHALL FOLLOW THE SPIRAL DEVELOPMENT APPROACH IDENTIFIED WITHIN THE PROJECT PLAN DEVELOPED UNDER 4.1, AND SHALL BE PLANNED AND EXECUTED BY THE CONTRACTOR IN COORDINATION WITH THE GOVERNMENT TEAM. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONFORM TO THE AFRL (OR OTHER DESIGNATED) FLIGHT OR GROUND TEST PLANNING PROCESS BY ATTENDING MEETINGS WITH THE RELEVANT TEST OFFICE; GATHERING OR CREATING THE REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION; PRESENTING MATERIAL TO THE TEST APPROVAL AUTHORITY; AND SUPPLYING THE TEST EVENT WITH SOFTWARE, HARDWARE, LOGISTIC, SUBJECT MATTER EXPERT, UXS OPERATOR, AND DATA COLLECTION PERSONNEL AND SUPPORT, AS WELL AS AUDIO-VISUAL DOCUMENTATION OF THE TEST FOR REPORTING OR MARKETING EFFORTS.
