IN ORDER FOR OFFICERS IN OUR MILITARY TO BE ABLE TO DEFEND AGAINST CYBER-ATTACKS, REGARDLESS OF OCCUPATION, THERE NEEDS TO BE A FUNDAMENTAL SHIFT IN THE WAY SECURITY IS TAUGHT IN UNIVERSITIES. ALL OFFICERS IN THE MODEM ERA ARE EXPECTED TO HAVE AN AWARENESS OF SECURITY, AND CYBER HAS BECOME THE KEY SECURITY ELEMENT IN ALMOST ALL SYSTEMS. STUDENT CADETS ARE OFTEN LEFT OUT OF CURRICULUM RELATED TO SECURITY DUE TO THEIR CHOICE OF MAJOR. COMPUTER SCIENCE, COMPUTER ENGINEERING AND INFORMATION SYSTEMS STUDENTS ROUTINELY ARE EXPOSED TO CONCEPTS AND TECHNIQUES RELATED TO CYBER SECURITY, HOWEVER STUDENT-CADETS WHO CHOOSE OTHER CURRICULUM DO NOT GET EXPOSED TO TOPICS IN SECURITY. EVEN WHEN THE CURRICULUM INCLUDES AN OPTION WITH SECURITY, STUDENT-CADETS CAN CHOOSE TO FOCUS ON OTHER AREAS, THEREBY FORGOING THE POTENTIAL EXPOSURE TO SECURITY TOPICS. THIS PROPOSAL STRENGTHENS THE ACADEMIC ENVIRONMENT FOR ROTC STUDENT-CADETS BY OFFERING A HANDS-ON TEACHING AND RESEARCH EXPERIENCE IN DEVELOPING AND SECURING CPS USING PARROT BEBOP DRONES AND PRIVATE CLOUD. THIS PROPOSAL FULFILLS THE JOINT URGENT OPERATIONAL NEEDS (JUON) 3A AND 3B. RUON STATEMENT 3 IS THE USE OF RED AND BLUE TEAMS TO ATTACK AND DEFEND CYBER NETWORKS. STATEMENT 3A STIPULATES BLUE TEAM FORCES WILL SEARCH FOR WAYS TO IDENTIFY WEAKNESSES AND IMPROVE THE PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL SECURITY OF THEIR SYSTEMS. STATEMENT 3B STIPULATES THAT WHEN RED TEAMS ATTACK, BLUE TEAMS WILL IDENTIFY THE THREAT AND RESPOND IN REAL TIME. BOTH OF THE JUON SCENARIOS FORM THE CENTRAL MISSION OF THIS PROPOSAL. THE ROTC STUDENT-CADETS WILL LEARN NOT ONLY HOW TO ANALYZE A PHYSICAL CYBER-SYSTEM FOR EXPOSED VULNERABILITIES AND WEAKNESSES AND RESPOND TO ATTACKS IN REAL TIME, BUT ALSO TEACHES HOW TO DESIGN AND CONSTRUCT A COMPLEX CPS. THIS EXPERIENCE WILL GIVE ROTC STUDENT-CADETS PRACTICAL KNOWLEDGE OF THE FUNDAMENTAL PROPERTIES OF DESIGNING AND SECURING A CPS, SUCH AS THE CLOUD-CONTROLLED AIRÂ­BASED DRONE SYSTEM OF THIS PROPOSAL. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO EXPOSE AND TRAIN UTSA-ROTC STUDENT CADETS IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND SUBSEQUENT SECURITY ANALYSIS OF CYBER-PHYSICAL SYSTEMS (CPS). THE CADETS WILL BE EXPOSED TO THE PROGRAMMING ENVIRONMENT USED TO ENABLE ROBOT DRONES (PARROT BEBOP QUAD-COPTERS) TO COMMUNICATE THROUGH MULTIPLE NETWORK INTERFACES TO A CONTROLLER HOSTED IN A CLOUD-COMPUTING ENVIRONMENT. THE CADETS WILL LEARN HOW TO DESIGN THE END-TO-END CPS COMPRISED OF THE DRONES AND THE BACK-END CLOUD-SERVICES, WILL USE NETWORK DISCOVERY TOOLS TO ENUMERATE THE EXPOSED APIS AND SERVICE END-POINTS, AND WILL USE ETHICAL HACKING TECHNIQUES TO ATTACK AND DEFEND THEIR CPS. THE GOAL OF THE RED TEAM ATTACKS IS TO ALTER THE MISSION STATE OF THE DRONES. THE GOAL OF THE BLUE TEAM IS TO IDENTIFY THE ATTACKERS AND TAKE MITIGATING STEPS TO ENSURE THE MISSION IS PROTECTED AND COMPLETED WITHIN THE ALLOWABLE TIME. BY THE END OF THIS PROPOSAL PERIOD, THE CADETS SHOULD HAVE AN AWARENESS OF THE CRITICAL NATURE OF CYBER-SECURITY IN CPS, HOW TO DESIGN AND CONSTRUCT A CPS, HOW TO IDENTIFY THE EXPOSED CYBER-ATTACK SURFACE, AND HOW TO DEFEND A CPS FROM CYBER-ATTACK.

THE C-SCORE PROGRAM WILL ENABLE DOD CONTRACTED RESERVE OFFICER TRAINING CORPS (ROTC) CADETS AND MIDSHIPMEN (COLLECTIVELY "CADETS") AT PARTICIPATING UNIVERSITIES TO TECHNICALLY CONTRIBUTE TO STATE-OF-THE-ART CYBER-SPECTRUM AND ELECTRONIC WARFARE (EW) RESEARCH THROUGH A RIGOROUS, PRODUCT-ORIENTED R&D PROGRAM. CADETS MENTORED BY FACULTY OR SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS AT THEIR RESPECTIVE UNIVERSITIES WILL ENGAGE IN ACADEMIC R&D TO ADDRESS OPERATIONALLY SIGNIFICANT CHALLENGES POSED IN A NOTIONAL OPERATIONAL SCENARIO.

THE IMPACT AND RESULT OF THIS RESEARCH WILL CREATE A TOOLKIT OF PROVEN FUNCTIONAL MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS FOR CYBERSECURITY. THESE ALGORITHMS CAN BE IMPLEMENTED ON LARGE DATA CENTERS OR ON MOBILE SYSTEMS USING NEUROMORPHIC HARDWARE FOR SWAP IMPROVEMENTS. THIS TOOLKIT CAN THEN BE USED TO STUDY COMPLEX PROBLEMS IN CYBERSECURITY AND DATAMINING. SEVERAL DIFFERENT LEARNING ALGORITHMS CAN BE EVALUATED UNDER DIFFERENT CONDITIONS TO DETERMINE THE BEST POSSIBLE OPTIONS FOR CYBERATTACK DETECTION, DATA MINING, AND SENSOR DATA ANALYSIS ON EDGE DEVICES IN THE FIELD.

THE OBJECTIVE OF THE CSPEC DVE EFFORT IS TO IDENTIFY, INVESTIGATE, AND ASSESS POTENTIAL NEW AND EMERGING DISRUPTIVE AND ADAPTABLE TECHNOLOGIES TO ADDRESS FULL SPECTRUM OPERATIONS. AREAS TO BE INVESTIGATED INCLUDE ELECTROMAGNETIC SPECTRUM (EMS) COMMUNICATION, AIRBORNE AND GROUND SENSORS, GUIDANCE AND CONTROL SYSTEMS, INTELLIGENCE GATHERING REQUIREMENTS AND CYCLE PROTECTION AGAINST WEAPON SYSTEMS AND SENSORS.

THIS RESEARCH PROJECT WILL ENGAGE ROTC CADETS AT UHM IN RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT TO ADDRESS RESEARCH ISSUES DEFINED IN THE NOTIONAL OPERATIONAL SCENARIO DEFINED IN THE C-SCORE PROGRAM, HELPING CADETS GRASP SKILLS IN CYBER OPERATIONS, SIGNALS INTELLIGENCE, AND ELECTRONIC WARFARE TECHNOLOGY, AND PREPARING THEM WITH SOLID ANALYSIS SKILLS, SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT EXPERIENCES, AND HARDWARE SKILLS.

HE GEORGIA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY WILL CONTRIBUTE TO RESEARCH THRUSTS 1, 2, AND 3, AND WE SUMMARIZE THESE CONTRIBUTIONS BELOW. THRUST 1 AUTONOMOUS ASSETS OFTEN MINIMIZE A COST, AND, BECAUSE THAT COST ENCODES THEIR OBJECTIVES, WE WILL ENSURE THAT THE ACTIONS TAKEN BY AGENTS PROTECT THE OBJECTIVE THAT DRIVES THOSE DECISIONS. MATHEMATICALLY, A COST IS A FUNCTIONAL THAT MAPS STATE AND INPUT TRAJECTORIES TO REAL NUMBERS, AND WE WILL DEVELOP NEW MECHANISMS THAT APPLY DIFFERENTIALLY PRIVATE PERTURBATIONS TO COSTS WITHIN THE SPACE OF FUNCTIONALS. THEN AN ASSET WILL SYNTHESIZE A CONTROLLER USING THE PERTURBED FUNCTIONAL AND USE THAT CONTROLLER WHEN EXECUTING ITS TASKS. BECAUSE DIFFERENTIAL PRIVACY IS IMMUNE TO POST-PROCESSING, THE USE OF THIS CONTROLLER IS PRIVACY-PRESERVING AS WELL AND HENCE IT DOES NOT REVEAL WHAT THE COST IS. IT IS OF COURSE OF PARAMOUNT IMPORTANCE THAT MINIMIZING THE PRIVATE COST IS STILL USEFUL TO AN ASSET. THEREFORE, WE WILL DEVELOP NEW TECHNIQUES TO PERTURB COSTS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE RULES OF DIFFERENTIAL PRIVACY, AND WE WILL BIAS THESE PERTURBATIONS TOWARD THOSE THAT PRODUCE SIMILAR CONTROLLERS TO WHAT THE UNPERTURBED COST WOULD PRODUCE. THIS WILL ENSURE THAT THE COST IS PROTECTED WHILE ALSO ENSURING THAT ASSETS STILL PERFORM AT A USEFUL LEVEL. WE WILL QUANTIFY TRADEOFFS IN THIS CONTEXT BY COMPARING THE COST INCURRED WITH PRIVACY TO THE COST INCURRED WITHOUT PRIVACY. WE WILL COMPUTE THIS DIFFERENCE IN TERMS OF THE STRENGTH OF PRIVACY PROTECTIONS, AND FROM THIS WE WILL DEVELOP GUIDELINES FOR THE CALIBRATION OF PRIVACY. THRUST 2 THE CONTROLLER USED BY AN ASSET CAN ALSO BE SENSITIVE BECAUSE IT ENCODES HOW AN ASSET MAKES DECISIONS, AND WE WILL DEVELOP DECEPTIVE AUTONOMY TECHNIQUES TO PROTECT IT. WITHOUT ANY PROTECTIONS, A CONTROLLER COULD BE UNCOVERED BY AN ADVERSARY THAT OBSERVES AN ASSET, E.G., THROUGH USING MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES, AND THIS CAN ENABLE AN ADVERSARY TO PREDICT AN ASSET’S FUTURE DECISIONS. MATHEMATICALLY, A CONTROLLER IS A FUNCTION THAT MAPS THE STATE OF AN ASSET TO A CONTROL INPUT. THE PRIVATIZATION OF SUCH A MAPPING WILL THEREFORE BE DONE BY MAKING IT APPROXIMATELY INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM OTHER FUNCTIONS THAT MAP BETWEEN THE SAME SPACES. THIS WILL BE DONE BY ADDING A RANDOM PERTURBATION TO IT. OF COURSE, WE WISH TO PRESERVE CERTAIN USEFUL PROPERTIES OF FEEDBACK CONTROLLERS SUCH AS CONTINUITY OR SMOOTHNESS, AND WE WILL DO SO BY POST-PROCESSING THE PERTURBED CONTROLLER. BECAUSE DIFFERENTIAL PRIVACY IS NOT HARMED BY POST-PROCESSING, THESE OPERATIONS CAN BE FREELY APPLIED, AND WE WILL CO-DESIGN A PRIVACY MECHANISM (FOR PERTURBING THE CONTROLLER) AND POST-PROCESSING TECHNIQUES (FOR IMPROVING ITS MATHEMATICAL PROPERTIES) TO SIMULTANEOUSLY PROVIDE PRIVACY AND ENSURE THE UTILITY OF PRIVATIZED CONTROLLERS. NEXT, WE WILL QUANTIFY TRADEOFFS BETWEEN PRIVACY AND PERFORMANCE BY QUANTIFYING THE COST INCURRED BY A CONTROLLER AND COMPARING THAT TO THE COST INCURRED BY ITS PRIVATIZED FORM. WE WILL BOUND THIS DIFFERENCE IN TERMS OF THE STRENGTH OF PRIVACY TO MAKE THESE TRADEOFFS EASILY TUNABLE. THRUST 3 TO ENSURE THE PRACTICAL APPLICABILITY OF ALL DEVELOPMENTS, WE WILL CONDUCT EXPERIMENTS ON TEAMS OF ROBOTS THROUGHOUT THIS PROJECT. OUR EXPERIMENTS WILL CONSIST OF A SEQUENCE OF RED TEAM VS. BLUE TEAM SCENARIOS. THE MAIN TYPE OF TASK WE WILL IMPLEMENT FOR THE BLUE TEAM IS SURVEILLANCE, IN WHICH THE GOAL IS TO LOCATE AND TRACK A MOVING TARGET. RED TEAM ASSETS WILL OBSERVE BLUE TEAM ASSETS AND ATTEMPT TO INFER THEIR CONTROLLERS AND COST FUNCTIONS. WE WILL IMPLEMENT PRIVACY FOR ONE AND THEN BOTH OF THESE OBJECTS. RED TEAM ESTIMATES OF SENSITIVE DATA WILL BE USED TO VALIDATE THEORETICAL BOUNDS ON WHAT THEY CAN UNCOVER AND DRIVE SUBSEQUENT THEORETICAL ANALYSES AND DEVELOPMENTS IN DECEPTION. BLUE TEAM BEHAVIORS WILL BE USED TO VALIDATE AND IMPROVE TRADE-OFF ANALYSES BETWEEN DECEPTION AND PERFORMANCE. VIDEOS AND LOG FILES OF EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PUBLICLY RELEASED.

INTEGRATED STATIC AND DYNAMIC APPROACHES TO HIGH-ASSURANCE FOR LEARNING-ENABLED CYBER-PHYSICAL SYSTEMS

PI: NICOLA BEZZO UNIVERSITY OF VIRGINIA

THE FOCUS OF THIS WORK IS TO DEVELOP THE FOUNDATIONS FOR THE DESIGN OF HIGH-ASSURANCE LEARNING-ENABLED CYBER-PHYSICAL SYSTEMS (LE-CPS). OVER THE PAST DECADE, SCIENTIFIC ADVANCES IN ROBOTICS, 
CONTROL, SENSING, AND ESPECIALLY MACHINE LEARNING HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO AN INCREASED DEVELOPMENT OF 
AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS CAPABLE OF PERFORMING COMPLICATED TASKS WHILE HARNESSING THE POWER OF DATA TO 
OPERATE IN UNKNOWN ENVIRONMENTS. MACHINE LEARNING PROVIDES A POTENTIALLY REVOLUTIONARY WAY TO 
ENABLE HIGHER-LEVEL AUTONOMY. UNFORTUNATELY, OUR CURRENT LACK OF UNDERSTANDING OF WHEN AND HOW  
MACHINE  LEARNING  WORKS,  MAKES  IT  CHALLENGING  TO  PROVIDE  GUARANTEES  FOR  SAFETY  CRITICAL 
SYSTEMS. DESPITE THIS, GIVEN THE IMPRESSIVE EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS OF MACHINE LEARNING, RESEARCHERS 
HAVE QUICKLY INCORPORATED LEARNING IN PERCEPTION-CONTROL LOOPS EVEN IN DRIVERLESS CARS AND AERIAL 
VEHICLES WHERE THE SAFETY REQUIREMENTS ARE VERY HIGH. THIS HAS RESULTED IN UNRELIABLE AND UNDESIRED 
BEHAVIORS WITH PUBLIC FAILURES AND ACCIDENTS THAT MAY LEAD TO LOSS OF TRUST IN AUTONOMY.

WITHIN THIS WORK, WE AIM TO DEVELOP TECHNIQUES TO MAKE LEARNING-ENABLED AUTONOMOUS VEHICLES SAFE 
AND TRUSTWORTHY. TO THIS END WE WILL DEVELOP MONITORS TO HELP US DERIVE THE CONFIDENCE IN THE 
OPERATION OF VEHICLE COMPONENTS. WE WILL DEVELOP TECHNIQUES TO MONITOR GIVEN SPECIFICATIONS AND TO 
CONSTRUCT THE MONITOR SPECIFICATIONS. PARTICULAR ATTENTION WILL BE GIVEN TO GUARANTEE THAT THE LE- 
CPS IS SAFE DURING RUNTIME OPERATIONS. HERE WE PLAN TO LEVERAGE REACHABILITY ANALYSIS TO PREDICT 
FUTURE STATES OF THE SYSTEM AND ASSESS IF SAFETY-CRITICAL SPECIFICATIONS ARE SATISFIED AT RUNTIME. 
THE MAIN  CHALLENGE  WILL  BE  ON  HOW  TO  PERFORM  RUNTIME  MONITORING  EFFICIENTLY  ONLINE  
MAINTAINING COMPUTATION TIME BOUNDED AND PREDICTABLE. TO SOLVE THIS PROBLEM, WE PLAN TO INVESTIGATE 
THE USE OF MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES LIKE SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINES.

WE WILL ALSO LEAD THE INTEGRATION AND EVALUATION EFFORT FOR THE PROJECT WITH BOTH VIRTUAL 
SIMULATIONS, AND  HARDWARE  EXPERIMENTS  ON  REAL  AUTONOMOUS  UNMANNED  VEHICLES  IN  COMPLEX  
UNSTRUCTURED ENVIRONMENTS.

BACKGROUND:
AS THE AIR FORCE CONTINUES TO EXPAND AUTOMATED INGESTION AND PROCESSING OF HIGH-VOLUME REMOTE SENSING DATA (OVERHEAD PERSISTENT INFRA-RED (OPIR) / ENVIRONMENTAL), HUMAN ANALYSTS AND OPERATORS WILL ALWAYS NEED TO BE KEPT IN THE LOOP. SOPHISTICATED MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS FOR AUTOMATED EVENT DETECTION, TRACKING AND DATA FUSION DO NOT PERFORM PERFECTLY IN ALL SITUATIONS. DOMAIN EXPERT USERS (WHO ARE NOT ALGORITHM EXPERTS) ARE OFTEN UNAWARE OF THESE LIMITATIONS AND ARE CURRENTLY UNABLE TO INTERACT DIRECTLY WITH THESE ALGORITHMS TO MITIGATE THESE ISSUES, E.G. BY UPDATING PRIOR TARGET LOCATION OR BEHAVIOR INFORMATION ONLINE FOR TIME-SENSITIVE OPERATIONS. NEW TECHNOLOGIES THAT BETTER BALANCE BETWEEN AUTOMATION (MACHINE LEARNING) AND HUMAN OVERSIGHT ARE NEEDED TO EXPLOIT THE BEST OF BOTH WORLDS AT VARIOUS LEVELS OF THE FUSION PIPELINE. THE
NEXT GENERATION OF AUTOMATION MUST OPPORTUNISTICALLY LEVERAGE HUMAN REASONING ABILITIES, WHILE STILL ENSURING PERFORMANCE GUARANTEES.

OBJECTIVE:
IN RESPONSE TO RFP, DATED SEPTEMBER 17, 2019, FROM THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO (CU), LOCKHEED MARTIN CORPORATION (LM), THE SUBCONTRACTOR, PROPOSES TO SUPPORT CU, THE CONTRACTOR, TO DEPLOY THE OPERATOR-MACHINE COLLABORATIVE INTERFACE FOR ENHANCED DATA FUSION IN THE SECRET TAP LAB. LM WILL PROVIDE SBIRS EXPERTISE AND TAP LAB INTEGRATION AND TEST ACTIVITIES TO CU IN RESPONSE TO THE REMOTE SENSING APPLICATION, BROAD AREA ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) #4, REQUEST FOR VISUALIZATION AND DISPLAY AND APPLICATION AND AGGREGATION.

THROUGH THE UNITED STATES GOVERNMENTÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) 16-086, THE CONTRACTOR, CU BOULDER, DEVELOPED A PROOF OF CONCEPT DEMONSTRATION FOR ITS COLLABORATIVE ANALYST-MACHINE PERCEPTION (CAMP) INTERFACE TOOL FOR ROBUST ONLINE DATA ANALYSIS AND FUSION. CAMP IS DESIGNED TO LET OPERATORS INTERACT DIRECTLY WITH AUTOMATED DATA FUSION PIPELINES AND MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS, THROUGH USER-FRIENDLY HAND-DRAWN LOCATIVE SKETCHES AND CLICKABLE GRAPHICAL DATA
DISPLAY WINDOWS. CU DEVELOPED THESE FEATURES BASED ON INTERACTIONS WITH SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS AT THE OPIR BATTLE AWARENESS CENTER (OBAC) AND THE SUBCONTRACTOR LM.

BUILDING ON THE SUCCESSFUL YEAR 1 BAA#1 EFFORT, LM WILL SUPPORT THE PROPOSED TO WORK FORMALLY REFINE, VALIDATE, AND ENHANCE THE CAMP TOOL IN SEVERAL SIGNIFICANT WAYS -- RESULTING IN RIGOROUS NEAR-TERM TECHNOLOGY TRANSITION FROM PROOF-OFCONCEPT DEMO TO HIGHER-LEVEL TECHNOLOGY RESEARCH LEVELS (TRLS). SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO: (I) FULLY INTEGRATE AND VALIDATE
THE CAMP TOOL WITH THE SENSOR OPEN FRAMEWORK ARCHITECTURE (SOFA) SIGNAL PROCESSING BACKEND BEING DEVELOPED FOR WIDER USE IN AIR FORCE OPIR APPLICATIONS IN THE TOOLS, APPLICATIONS AND PROCESSING (TAP) LAB AND OBAC, (II) FORMALLY EVALUATE THE CAMP TOOL IN THE U.S. AIR FORCEÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S TAP LAB WITH OBAC SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS (SMES) WORKING WITH AUTOMATION ON (SYNTHETIC) DETECTION/TRACKING SCENARIOS, (III) CONTINUE INTERACTIONS WITH SMES TO RESEARCH TO IDENTIFY, DEVELOP, AND DEMONSTRATE OTHER KEY CAPABILITIES FOR THE CAMP TOOL, SUCH AS DATA CONTEXTUALIZATION (I.E. HIGHLIGHTING INTERESTING AND POSSIBLY NOVEL EVENT TYPES THAT ARE CORRELATED IN SPACE, TIME, AND OTHER DATA DIMENSIONS) AND TWO-WAY ACTIVE QUERYING (I.E.
ABILITY OF HUMANS AND MACHINES TO PRESENT/ANSWER QUESTIONS TO ONE ANOTHER TO CLARIFY THEIR DECISION MAKING)

REQUIREMENTS
4.1 PROGRAM MANAGEMENT
4.1.1 LM SHALL PROVIDE MONTHLY PROGRESS, STATUS AND MANAGEMENT REPORTS TO CU. LM WILL DEVELOP A TEMPLATE FOR THE MONTHLY PROGRESS, STATUS AND MANAGEMENT REPORT IN THE FIRST MONTH OF THE PROJECT. LM WILL SUBMIT MONTHLY UPDATES TO HIGHLIGHT ACHIEVEMENTS AND PROGRESS, TO SUMMARIZE CONTRACT STATUS AND NOTE ANY AREAS OF CONCERN OR ISSUE.
4.2 KEY RESEARCH TASKS
4.2.1 LM SHALL SUPPORT CU IN INTEGRATING CAMP AND SOFA SOFTWARE WHICH WILL INCLUDE PROVIDING OPIR EXPERTISE AND ANALYSIS IN AN UNCLASSIFIED SETTING.
4.2.2 LM SHALL PROVIDE CU UNCLASSIFIED OPIR SIMULATIONS, REP RETURNS AND TRACKS TO

THE GOVERNMENT REQUIRES INVESTIGATIONS FOCUSED TOWARD ASSESSING, AND EXPANDING WHERE POSSIBLE, THE SSA UTILITY OF SENSING IN THE THERMAL INFRARED ALONE, AS WELL AS IN SENSING SIMULTANEOUSLY IN DISCRETE SPECTRAL BANDS SPANNING THE ENTIRE EO SPECTRUM

THE PURPOSE/OBJECTIVE OF THIS CONTRACT IS TO OBTAIN TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATIONS AND GUIDANCE FOR CAPABILITIES ENHANCEMENT OF, IMPROVEMENT OF OPERATIONAL PROCESSES ASSOCIATED WITH, AND CONTINUED SUSTAINABILITY/AVAILABILITY OF THE AMOS LWIR IMAGER.

THE UNIVERSITY OF VIRGINIA WILL FINALIZE ITS WORK DEVELOPING AND EVALUATING A FORMAL LANGUAGES-BASED
SPECIFICATION OF A FRAMEWORK FOR PRECISELY DEFINING THE THE "ILITIES" IN BOEHM'S TAXONOMY OF SYSTEM
NONFUNCTIONAL QUALITIES. THE RESULTS OF THIS EFFORT WILL INCLUDE A FRAMEWORK SUPPORTING SYSTEM AND DOMAIN MODELS, SYSTEM- AND DOMAIN-SPECIFIC, STAKEHOLDER-VALUE-BASED SPECIALIZATION OF DEFINITIONS OF GENERALIZED ILITIES, SUCH AS ACCURACY, RELIABILITY, AND RESILIENCE. NO SINGLE DEFINITION OF ANY SUCH "ILITY" WILL SUFFICE FOR ALL SYSTEMS AND DOMAINS, YET THERE IS GREAT COMMONALITY AMONG VARIATIONS IN DEFINITIONS OF SUCH TERMS ACROSS MANY
SYSTEMS AND DOMAINS. AN IMPORTANT FEATURE OF THE FTESS IS ITS ABILITY TO GENERATE RARE EVENTS. FTESS LEVERAGES TECHNIQUES FOR RARE-EVENT SIMULATION, EDGE COMPUTING, AND RUNS ON A SUPERCOMPUTER. THERE ARE TWO MAIN APPROACHES FOR IMPROVING THE EFFICIENCY OF RARE-EVENT SIMULATIONSÃ¢Â‚¬Â€? IMPORTANCE SAMPLING (IS) AND SPLITTING (SHORTLE
AND LÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢ECQUIER, 2011; ZARE-NOGHABI & SHORTLE, 2017). THE IDEA OF IS IS TO CHANGE THE UNDERLYING SAMPLING DISTRIBUTION SO THAT RARE EVENTS ARE MORE LIKELY. THE IDEA OF SPLITTING IS TO CREATE SEPARATE COPIES OF THE SIMULATION WHENEVER THE SIMULATION GETS "CLOSE" TO THE RARE EVENT OF INTEREST, EFFECTIVELY MULTIPLYING PROMISING RUNS THAT ARE MORE LIKELY TO REACH THE RARE EVENT. SPLITTING IS USEFUL FOR SYSTEMS THAT TEND TO TAKE MANY INCREMENTAL STEPS ON THE PATH TO THE RARE EVENT. IS IS ALSO USEFUL FOR SYSTEMS THAT TEND TO TAKE A
SMALL NUMBER OF "CATASTROPHIC JUMPS" TO THE RARE EVENT.
FTESS IS RUN DURING THE DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING CYCLE TO IDENTIFY EMERGENT SCENARIOS LEADING TO HAZARDOUS OUTCOMES SUCH THAT THEY CAN BE ADDRESSED BY THE DESIGN. MORE IMPORTANTLY, FTESS IS RUN EVEN WHEN THE SYSTEM OF SYSTEMS IS FIELDED AND OPERATING. THIS CAN BE USED TO IDENTIFY HAZARDOUS OUTCOMES THAT HAVE
NOT YET OCCURRED.

QUALIFICATION OF NEEDLED C-SIC BASED STRUCTURAL INSULATOR MATERIALS FOR SOLID ROCKET MOTOR DACS: THE NEED FOR A DOMESTICALLY-SOURCED STRUCTURAL COMPOSITE MATERIAL MORE THERMALLY STABLE THAN THE STATE-OF-THE-ART PHENOLIC COMPOSITES HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED AS A KEY ENABLING TECHNOLOGY THAT WILL ADD BETTER CONTROL AUTHORITY TO PINTLE-BASED DIVERT AND ACS THRUSTERS. BY ESTABLISHING A U.S. SUPPLIER OF THIS TYPE OF MATERIAL, BETTER SOURCE CONTROL AND QUALITY CONTROL OF COMPONENTS CAN BE ACHIEVED. IN ADDITION, STRONG STRUCTURAL INSULATORS POSSESSING THERMALLY INSULATIVE, INNATE EROSION RESISTANT PROPERTIES AND THE ABILITY TO BE MADE INTO MULTI-FUNCTIONAL PARTS WILL REDUCE PART COUNT, VOLUME, WEIGHT, AND COST (UP TO 50% REDUCTION). THE CORE C-SIC STRUCTURAL INSULATOR TECHNOLOGY PROPOSED FOR THIS MDA RAPID INNOVATION FUND (RIF) PROGRAM HAS BEEN PROVEN UNDER MDA-FUNDED SBIR PROGRAMS AT ALLCOMP AS WELL AS UNDER THE MDA FUNDED CKV PROGRAM AT BOTH AEROJET ROCKETDYNE AND ATK. THROUGH THIS RIF PROGRAM, ALLCOMP AIMS TO QUALIFY THE MOST RECENT VARIATION OF NEEDLED-PREFORM BASED STRUCTURAL INSULATOR MATERIAL, AS WELL AS ITS PROCESSING METHODOLOGY, IN A TWO YEAR FAST-PACED TESTING PROGRAM PRODUCING A MATERIAL SYSTEM WITH OPTIMUM THERMO-ELASTIC AND STRENGTH PROPERTIES. VALIDATION OF MANUFACTURABILITY WILL BE CONDUCTED THROUGH FULL MATERIAL CHARACTERIZATION TESTING OF MULTIPLE LOTS TO BRING THIS MATERIAL TOWARDS QUALIFICATION ACCEPTANCE AND INCLUSION IN UPCOMING BALLISTIC MISSILE DEFENSE SYSTEM APPLICATIONS SUCH AS SM-3 CKV AND EVOLVED IIA, AND MORE BROADLY, FOR OTHER INITIATIVES, LIKE THE AIRBORNE WEAPON LAYER DACS

A NOVEL APPROACH TO EFFORTLESSLY EXTEND THE POWERING AND COMMUNICATION RANGE FROM 1 MM TO 1 CM, 10 CM, AND 1 M, WHILE FULLY HARNESSING THE BUILD-IN TRUST AND ANTI-TAMPERING FUNCTIONS OF THE LOW COST SHIELD DIELETS. THE ENGINEERED "RANGE EXTENDER'' CARRY A SHIELD DIELET AND EXTENDS ITS POWERING AND COMMUNICATION RANGE WITHOUT IMPACTING ITS CORE FUNCTION. THE EXTENDERS HAVE VERY LOW COST IN MANUFACTURING AND ASSEMBLY WITH SHIELD DIELETS, VERY HIGH TOLERANCE TO MISALIGNMENT, WHICH GREATLY SIMPLIFY THE AUTHENTICATION PROCESS BY END-USERS. FOR 10 CM RANGE, WE PROPOSE A DISTRIBUTED ARRAY AS READER TO COUPLE TO A 3 OR 4 COIL SYSTEM FOR MORE RANGE EXTENSION. FOR A METER, WE PROPOSE SOUND WAVES EMITTED BY SPEAKERS TO POWER AND COMMUNICATION. THE SHIELD TECHNOLOGY VEHICLES (STV) DEVELOPED IN PHASE I AND PHASE I EXTENSION WILL BE USED FOR TESTING RANGE EXTENDERS.

TOR TASKS

AROUND THE WORLD, PEOPLE ARE TRYING TO SAFELY SPEAK OUT ABOUT THEIR SITUATIONS, AND SAFELY LEARN 
WHAT OTHERS HAVE TO SAY. THIS FREE AND OPEN COMMUNICATION ON THE INTERNET IS CRITICAL TO THE GROWTH 
OF STRONG COMMUNITIES AND SOCIETIES. AT THE SAME TIME, NATION-STATE CENSORS AND OTHERS ATTEMPT TO 
DENY THIS COMMUNICATION, THREATENING THIS GROWTH. IN THIS PROJECT WE WILL LEVERAGE OUR PAST WORK ON 
THE TOR ANONYMITY SYSTEM AND THE PLUGGABLE TRANSPORT ECOSYSTEM TO EXPLORE, DEVELOP, AND DEPLOY 
TECHNIQUES TO DETECT, UNDERSTAND, AND MITIGATE THESE DENIALS OF SERVICE.

SAFE COMMUNICATION ON THE INTERNET REQUIRES MANY COMPONENTS TO COME TOGETHER AT ONCE: (1) A ROBUST 
AND HIGHLY SCALED COMMUNICATIONS INFRASTRUCTURE THAT PROTECTS COMMUNICATIONS METADATA (I.E. TOR); 
(2) MECHANISMS TO GET AROUND BLOCKING OR CENSORSHIP OF CONNECTIONS BETWEEN USERS AND THIS PRIVACY 
NETWORK; (3) SUITABLE PACKAGES DESIGN FOR THE COMPUTING ENVIRONMENTS OF REAL USERS, WITH AN 
EMPHASIS ON USABILITY AND USER EXPERIENCE; AND (4) AWARENESS OF THE CHANGING LANDSCAPE OF THREATS, 
AND ADAPTIVE USER EDUCATION ABOUT THESE THREATS.

WITH THESE COMPONENTS IN MIND, WE WILL FOCUS ON SIX AREAS OF WORK. NOTE THAT EACH OF THESE AREAS IS 
ITSELF AN OPEN-ENDED RESEARCH FIELD, SO WHILE WE WANT TO MAKE SUBSTANTIAL PROGRESS ON EACH OF THEM, 
THERE WILL ALWAYS BE MORE FOLLOW-UP WORK TO DO ON EACH OF THEM.

TOR TASK 1: DEFEND THE TOR NETWORK ITSELF

TOR IS A FREE-SOFTWARE ANONYMIZING OVERLAY NETWORK THAT HELPS PEOPLE AROUND THE WORLD USE THE 
INTERNET IN SAFETY. TORÂ€™S 8000 VOLUNTEER RELAYS CARRY OVER 100GBIT/S OF TRAFFIC FOR SEVERAL MILLION 
USERS EACH DAY. THIS DEPLOYED NETWORK AND DIVERSE USER BASE PROVIDES A GREAT FOUNDATION, BUT WE 
MUST MAKE IT STRONGER. WE WILL:

(A) FOSTER DIVERSITY AND SUSTAINABILITY IN RELAY LOCATIONS AND RELAY OPERATORS,

(B) REACT AS NEEDED TO DENIAL OF SERVICE ATTACKS ON THE TOR NETWORK ITSELF, AND

(C) PROACTIVELY IDENTIFY AND RESOLVE DOS VULNERABILITIES, MAKING USE OF EXISTING RESEARCH 
COLLABO-RATIONS TO ACHIEVE A STRONGER NETWORK AND IMPROVE ROBUSTNESS TO UNKNOWN DOS VECTORS.

TOR TASK 2: DESIGN AND DEPLOY BETTER PLUGGABLE TRANSPORTS THAT WORK IN ACTIVELY CENSORED REGIMES

CURRENTLY, DOMAIN FRONTING SYSTEMS LIKE MEEK WORK IN MOST OR ALL DENIED COUNTRIES, BUT DOMAIN 
FRONTING SCALES POORLY BOTH IN TERMS OF BANDWIDTH AND MONETARY COST. THE MOST PROMIS-ING OF THE 
NEXT GENERATION OF PTS IS SNOWFLAKE, WHICH BUILDS ON FLASH PROXY TO USE IN-BROWSER WEBRTC TO MAKE 
Â€ŒGOOGLE HANGOUTÂ€? STYLE CONNECTIONS TO VOLUNTEER WEB BROWSERS, WHO THEN BRIDGE THE CONNECTIONS ON TO 
THE TOR NETWORK. WE WILL:

(A) RESEARCH AND DESIGN THE MISSING PARTS OF SNOWFLAKE, AND BUILD A PROTOTYPE,

(B) MAKE TOR BROWSER RELEASES THAT INTEGRATE THIS PROTOTYPE,

(C) CONFIRM THAT IT DOES INDEED WORK IN DENIED COUNTRIES,

(D) GET SOME PLUGGABLE TRANSPORTS, INCLUDING SNOWFLAKE, WORKING ON ANDROID TOO, SINCE AN 
INCREAS-ING PERCENTAGE OF THE WORLD IS MOVING FROM DESKTOP TO MOBILE, AND

(E) START RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT ON SOMETHING TO FOLLOW SNOWFLAKE SO WEÂ€™RE PREPARED IF ATTACKERS 
BECOME WILLING TO BLOCK OR DEGRADE THE WEBRTC PROTOCOL.

TOR TASK 3: BUILD CAPACITY AND STRENGTHEN THE RESEARCH COMMUNITY

JUST ABOUT EVERY MAJOR SECURITY CONFERENCE THESE DAYS HAS A PAPER ANALYZING, ATTACKING, OR 
IMPROV-ING TOR. WHILE TEN YEARS AGO THE FIELD OF ANONYMOUS COMMUNICATIONS WAS MOSTLY THEORETICAL, 
WITH RESEARCHERS SPECULATING THAT A GIVEN DESIGN SHOULD OR SHOULDNÂ€™T WORK, TOR NOW PROVIDES AN 
ACTUAL DEPLOYED TESTBED. TOR HAS BECOME THE GOLD STANDARD FOR ANONYMOUS COMMUNICATIONS RESEARCH, 
WHICH IN TURN TRIGGERED AN EXPLOSION OF ACADEMIC PLUGGABLE TRANSPORT DESIGNS. WE WILL:(A) 
COLLABORATE WITH MEMBERS OF THE PETS RESEARCH COMMUNITY TO CONTINUE OPERATION OF THE TOR RESEARCH 
SAFETY BOARD (A GROUP OF RESEARCHERS WHO STUDY TOR, AND WHO WANT TO MINIMIZE PRIVACY RISKS WHILE 
FOSTERING A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE TOR NETWORK AND ITS USERS), WITH THE OUTPUT BEING A GROWING 
SET OF REAL-WORLD CASE STUDIES ON HOW TO SAFELY AND ETHICALLY CONDUCT EXPERIMENTS ON TH LIVE TOR 
NETWORK AND USERS.

TOR TASK 4: CONSIDER MORE USE CASES THAN JUST WEB BROWSING

SMARTPHONE USERS WANT PRIVACY AND CENSORSHIP CIRCUMVENTION FOR MORE THAN JUST WEB BROWSING. 
MILLIONS OF PEOPLE USE CHAT AND SOCIAL MEDIA APPLICATIONS, CREATE AND SHARE MEDIA FILES LIKE IMAGES 
AND VIDEO, AND MORE. IN FACT, IF TORÂ€™S PERFORMANCE PENALTIES ARE MOST VISIBLE FOR LATENCY-SENSITIVE 
APPLICATIONS LIKE WEB BROWSING, WE WOULD BE WISE TO EXPLORE SECURE MESSAGING AND OTHER 
ASYN-CHRONOUS APPLICATIONS. WE WILL:

(A) MAKE SURE THE PROTOTYPES AND TOOLS FROM TASK TWO WORK WITH YOUTUBE AND/OR OTHER POPULAR 
SERVICES, AND

(B) DO A NEEDS ASSESSMENT FOR WHAT OTHER APPLICATIONS ARE POPULAR AMONG USERS BEHIND CENSORSHIP, 
AND HOW WELL WE CAN SERVE THEM, CONSIDERING BOTH SAFETY AND USABILITY. THE FIRST CHALLENGE IS TO 
UNDERSTAND WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY BE USEFUL TO BUILD. OPTIONS TO CONSIDER INCLUDE DESIGNING A VIDEO 
SHARING SERVICE THAT INTEGRATES CHARACTERISTICS OF SECUREDROP OR GLOBALEAKS, OR ADDING AN Â€ŒUPLOAD 
RESUMEÂ€? OR Â€ŒPARALLEL UPLOADÂ€? HELPER TO TOR BROWSER SO USERS CAN UPLOAD CHUNKS AT A TIME AND NOT 
HAVE TO START OVER WHEN THE NETWORK FAILS.

TOR TASK 5: UNDERSTAND TORÂ€™S CLIENT PERFORMANCE ON LIMITED AND/OR INTERMITTENT CONNECTIONS, AND 
NETWORK PERFORMANCE WHILE UNDER ATTACK

SEVERAL FACTORS CONTRIBUTE TO MAKING TOR CONNECTIONS LESS EFFICIENT THAN A DIRECT CONNECTION TO THE 
FINAL DESTINATION, AND WHILE A BIG PART OF THAT DIFFERENCE CAN BE EXPLAINED BY     HOW MUCH 
CAPACITY IS AVAILABLE AT THE TOR RELAYS (SEE TASK ONE), SOME OF THESE PERFORMANCE FACTORS ARE 
PARTICULARLY ACUTE ON BAD NETWORK CONNECTIONS. AT THE SAME TIME, WE NEED TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HOW 
LOAD ON THE NETWORK ITSELF, INCLUDING ADVERSARIALLY-INDUCED OR TARGETED LOAD, CAN IMPACT ALL PARTS 
OF THE SYSTEM. WE WILL:

(A) CONSIDER AND ANALYZE THE END-TO-END PERFORMANCE AND CONGESTION OF TOR CLIENTS BEHIND BAD 
NETWORK CONNECTIONS (HIGH-LATENCY, LOW-BANDWIDTH, SOME PACKET LOSS, ETC),

(B) DESIGN WAYS TO GET AROUND THESE LIMITATIONS, FOR EXAMPLE WITH THE Â€ŒRESUMEÂ€? FEATURE MENTIONED 
ABOVE, OR BY HAVING CLIENTS STRIPE THEIR CONNECTIONS AND/OR CIRCUITS OVER MULTIPLE SNOWFLAKES FOR 
BETTER PERFORMANCE AND BETTER ROBUSTNESS, AND

(C) STUDY THE BEHAVIOR OF TOR CLIENTS AND TOR RELAYS UNDER VARIOUS DENIAL OF SERVICE ATTACKS, AND 
DESIGN COUNTERMEASURES TO TOLERATE THE ATTACKS AND/OR GRACEFULLY DEGRADE SERVICE.

TOR TASK 6: BUILD A NETWORK MEASUREMENT FEEDBACK LOOP SO WE KNOW WHATÂ€™S WORKING AND WHAT SHOULD 
WORK

THIS FEEDBACK LOOP WILL BE CRITICAL TO LETTING US ADAPT TOR BROWSER AND OUR OTHER APPS IN RESPONSE 
TO CHANGES ON THE INTERNET. WE WILL:

(A) RAMP UP OUR OONI-STYLE CENSORSHIP MEASUREMENT TESTS IN DENIED AREAS, SO WE CAN CONFIRM THAT 
VARIOUS PROTOCOLS LIKE WEBRTC DO WORK RIGHT NOW, AND SO WE CAN GET RAPID AND ROBUST NOTIFICA-TIONS 
WHEN THAT CHANGES,

(B) FIGURE OUT HOW TO CONDUCT MORE COMPREHENSIVE TESTS TOO: NOT JUST Â€ŒDOES WEBRTC WORK?Â€? BUT Â€ŒDOES 
TOR BROWSER USING SNOWFLAKE WORK?Â€?, AND

(C) MAINTAIN AND GROW OUR TOR METRICS DATA SETS, WHICH PROVIDE HISTORICAL AND ONGOING TOR NETWORK 
DATA AND PERFORMANCE STATISTICS FOR THE BROADER RESEARCH COMMUNITY.

"CO-PI REXFORDÂ€™S RESEARCH GROUP AT PRINCETON UNIVERSITY WILL CONDUCT RESEARCH AND BUILD PROTOTYPES ON TWO CENTRAL TOPICS IN THE PROPOSAL:

EXPRESSIVE TELEMETRY QUERIES: REXFORDÂ€™S GROUP WILL EXTEND THE SONATA PLATFORM THAT SUPPORTS SPARK-LIKE QUERIES ON NETWORK TRAFFIC AND PERFORMANCE BY SYNTHESIZING P4 CODE THAT PERFORMS DATA REDUCTION IN THE UNDERLYING PROGRAMMABLE NETWORK SWITCHES. THE WORK INVOLVES (I) INTEGRATING THE EXISTING SONATA FUNCTIONALITY INTO THE SWITCH OPERATING SYSTEM (STRATUM) AND THE CENTRAL CONTROLLER (ÂΜONOS) SOFTWARE, (II) EXTENDING SONATA TO SUPPORT TELEMETRY QUERIES WITH WIDER SCOPE (E.G., ACROSS MULTIPLE PIPELINES WITHIN SWITCH, ALONG A PATH, AND ACROSS THE NETWORK), (III) INCORPORATING COMPACT DATA STRUCTURES TO SUPPORT QUERIES IN THE SWITCHES MORE EFFICIENTLY IN THE SWITCHES, AND (IV) AS A STRETCH GOAL SUPPORTING HIGHER-LEVEL NAMES AND METRICS IN SONATA QUERIES. GRADUATE STUDENTS AND THE POSTDOC WILL CONDUCT RESEARCH ON THE NEW FEATURES, WHILE THE SOFTWARE DEVELOPER WILL HARDEN AND INTEGRATE SONATA WITH THE LARGER SOFTWARE PLATFORM---INCORPORATING NEW CAPABILITIES AS THEY BECOME AVAILABLE.

NETWORK APPLICATIONS THAT AUTOMATICALLY ADAPT TO CHANGING NETWORK CONDITIONS. THESE APPLICATIONS INCLUDE (I) PERFORMANCE-AWARE ROUTING (SHIFTING TRAFFIC TO THE BEST PATH BASED ON HIGH-LEVEL POLICIES AND REAL-TIME PROBES OF PATH PERFORMANCE), (II) ALLEVIATING MICROBURSTS (DETECTING THE FLOWS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE SHORT-TERM BUILD-UP OF PACKET QUEUES, AND REROUTING OR RATE- LIMITING THEM ACCORDINGLY), (III) INTRUSION PREVENTION SYSTEM (APPLYING SNORT-LIKE RULES TO NETWORK TRAFFIC AND AUTOMATICALLY BLOCKING, RATE-LIMITING, OR REDIRECTING THE TRAFFIC), AND
(IV) DENIAL-OF-SERVICE ATTACK MITIGATION (DETECTING DISTRIBUTED ATTACKS AND AUTOMATICALLY BLOCKING, RATE-LIMITING, OR REDIRECTING THE UNWANTED TRAFFIC). EACH APPLICATION WILL HAVE A HIGH-LEVEL LANGUAGE FOR EXPRESSING NETWORK POLICIES, AND A COMPILER THAT SYNTHESIZING LOW-LEVEL CODE (E.G., P4 PROGRAMS) TO RUN IN THE NETWORK ELEMENTS. THE GRADUATE STUDENTS AND THE POSTDOC WILL CONDUCT RESEARCH ON THESE APPLICATIONS AND BUILD PROTOTYPE SYSTEMS FOR DEMONSTRATION ON A NETWORK OF PROGRAMMABLE SWITCHES.

TOGETHER, THESE TWO RESEARCH THREADS ENABLE A SAFE AND SECURE NETWORK INFRASTRUCTURE WITH AUTOMATED SUPPORT FOR TELEMETRY AND CONTROL DRIVEN BY HIGH-LEVEL QUERIES AND POLICIES
"

 MACHINE-VERIFIED P4 COMPILER: FOSTERÂ€™S GROUP WILL EXTEND PRIOR WORK ON THE NSF-FUNDED PETR4 PROJECT TO BUILD A MACHINE-VERIFIED COMPILER FROM P4 TO A LOW-LEVEL ABSTRACT MACHINE BASED ON PISA. CONCRETELY THIS WORK INVOLVES (I) MECHANIZING THE OPERATIONAL SEMANTICS OF THE P4 LANGUAGE, (II) DEVELOPING AN OPERATIONAL MODEL OF THE PISA ARCHITECTURE, (III) MODELING THE P4RUNTIME CONTROL-PLANE API, (IV) BUILDING A COMPILER FROM P4 TO PISA, AND (V) VERIFYING THE CORRECTNESS OF THE COMPILER. ALL OF THIS WORK WILL BE CARRIED OUT IN THE COQ PROOF ASSISTANT, YIELDING END-TO-END VERIFIED ARTIFACTS THAT CAN BE EXECUTED ON REAL DEVICES AND DRAMATICALLY REDUCE THE TRUSTED COMPUTING BASE FOR PROGRAMMABLE NETWORKS. THE METRICS FOR EVALUATING THIS WORK INCLUDE THE AMOUNT OF UNVERIFIED CODE IN THE VARIOUS SOFTWARE Â€ŒSHIMSÂ€? NEEDED TO RUN THE CODE EXTRACTED FROM COQ, AS WELL AS THE PERFORMANCE IN TERMS OF THROUGHPUT AND LATENCY OF THE EXTRACTED CODE. AS A STRETCH GOAL, IF TIME PERMITS, WE WILL EXPLORE WHETHER IT IS FEASIBLE TO GO FURTHER AND GENERATE MACHINE-VERIFIED HARDWARE DESIGNS FOR AN FPGA-BASED DEVICE, BUILDING ON THE MIT KAMI PROJECT.COMBINING STATIC AND DYNAMIC VERIFICATION: NETWORK TELEMETRY PROVIDES UNPRECEDENTED VISIBILITY INTO THE DYNAMIC OPERATION OF A NETWORK. FOSTERÂ€™S GROUP WILL EXPLORE HOW TO EFFICIENTLY UTILIZE TELEMETRY DATA TO CHECK NETWORK-WIDE PROPERTIES. THIS WORK WILL ENTAIL: (I) DEVELOPING TECHNIQUES BASED ON INLINE REFERENCE MONITORS TO CHECK SAFETY PROPERTIES SUCH AS WAYPOINTING AND ISOLATION AND (II) DEVELOPING TECHNIQUES FOR EXTENDING FROM SAFETY PROPERTIES TO LIVENESS PROPERTIES SUCH AS CONNECTIVITY AND RELIABILITY BY LEVERAGING FACTS OBTAINED FROM STATIC VERIFICATION, AND (III) DEVELOPING A SOFTWARE PLATFORM THAT REALIZES THESE TECHNIQUES INCLUDING A COMPILER THAT AUTOMATICALLY GENERATES THE P4 CODE AND OFFLINE ANALYSIS FRAMEWORK NEEDED TO EFFICIENTLY DETECT VIOLATIONS OF NETWORK PROPERTIES. THE METRICS FOR EVALUATING THIS WORK WILL INCLUDE THE TIME NEEDED TO DETECT A VIOLATION, THE AMOUNT OF EXTRA DATA THAT MUST BE CARRIED WITH PACKETS OR EXFILTRATED FROM THE NETWORK, AND THE ACCURACY OF THE PROPERTY-CHECKING TOOLS.

TOGETHER, THESE TWO RESEARCH THREADS WILL TAKE A SIGNIFICANT STEP FORWARD TOWARD HAVING VERIFIED NETWORKS THAT ARE GUARANTEED TO BEHAVE AS SPECIFIED BY NETWORK OPERATORS.
"

"RFA-NS-18-009
POPULATION NEURAL ACTIVITY MEDIATING SENSORY PERCEPTION ACROSS MODALITIES
MALA MURTHY, ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR, PRINCETON NEUROSCIENCE INSTITUTE, PRINCETON UNIVERSITY
DESCRIPTION OF THE WORK TO BE PROVIDED.
WE PROPOSE A HIGHLY CROSS-DISCIPLINARY AND AMBITIOUS PROJECT TO CHARACTERIZE MULTIMODAL SENSORY
PROCESSING IN DROSOPHILA, A PROJECT THAT THEREFORE REQUIRES A MULTI-PI TEAM WITH DIVERSE, BUT
COMPLEMENTARY EXPERTISE SPANNING THREE DIFFERENT SENSORY SYSTEMS (VISION, MECHANOSENSATION
AND TASTE), AS WELL AS STRONG QUANTITATIVE MODELING AND DATA ANALYSIS. ALL THREE AIMS OF THIS
PROPOSAL ARE HIGHLY INTEGRATIVE AND COLLABORATIVE IN NATURE. THUS, THE SCIENTIFIC AGENDA AND
DIRECTION FOR THE PROJECT AS A WHOLE WILL BE MADE COLLECTIVELY BY ALL FOUR PIS (INCLUDING PI
CLANDININ). MALA MURTHY WILL TAKE A SCIENTIFIC LEAD ROLE IN AIMS 1.1B AND 1.1C (OPTIMIZATION AND
STANDARDIZATION OF ROI SEGMENTATION METHODS AND BEHAVIORAL MEASUREMENTS), THE PORTION OF
AIM 1 THAT RELATES TO MECHANOSENSORY CODING (AIM 1.2C), AND AIM 2.2 (MULTISENSORY INTEGRATION
IN THE CONTEXT OF COURTSHIP). THESE EXPERIMENTS LEVERAGE STUDIES MY LAB HAS RECENTLY CONDUCTED
INVOLVING VOLUMETRIC TWO-PHOTON IMAGING WITH PRECISE REGISTRATION TO STUDY AUDITORY
REPRESENTATIONS ACROSS TRIALS AND ANIMALS. THEY ALSO LEVERAGE THE WEALTH OF EXPERTISE IN MY LAB
ON SENSORIMOTOR PATTERNING IN THE CONTEXT OF SOCIAL INTERACTIONS (NAMELY DROSOPHILA COURTSHIP).
THESE STUDIES WILL USE THE TWO-PHOTON IMAGING RIGS WE HAVE BUILT IN ADDITION TO BEHAVIORAL DATA
(OF COURTSHIP INTERACTIONS) WE HAVE COLLECTED. WE HAVE CONSIDERABLE EXPERIENCE WITH IN VIVO
RECORDINGS FROM THE DROSOPHILA BRAIN AND WILL ENSURE THAT THE DATA ARE OF THE HIGHEST QUALITY.
BENEFIT TO THE PI AND THE DEPARTMENT
THIS WORK WILL DIRECTLY BENEFIT DR. CLANDININ, AS RESULTS FROM THESE STUDIES WILL INFORM THE ONGOING
WORK IN HIS LAB ON SENSORY PROCESSING AND BEHAVIOR. AT A HIGHER LEVEL, THIS WORK WILL BENEFIT THE
DEPARTMENT OF NEUROBIOLOGY AT STANFORD BY CATALYZING NEW SCIENTIFIC COLLABORATIONS SUPPORTED
BY THIS R01 APPLICATION."

2.1.	THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS DURING THE EXECUTION OF THIS PROGRAM:

2.1.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUBMIT MONTHLY PROGRESS REPORTS, INCLUDING:
2.1.2.1.A DETAILED SUMMARY OF WORK AND TECHNICAL PROGRESS ACCOMPLISHED DURING THE CURRENT REPORTING CYCLE (INCLUDE ANY SUBMISSIONS OF MANUSCRIPTS TO JOURNALS/CONFERENCES, CONFERENCE ATTENDANCE, MEETINGS, ETC.);

2.1.2.3.DETAILED PLANS FOR TECHNICAL RESEARCH DURING THE NEXT REPORTING CYCLE (INCLUDE ANY ANTICIPATED SUBMISSION OF MANUSCRIPTS TO JOURNALS/CONFERENCES, CONFERENCE ATTENDANCE, ETC.);
2.1.2.4. ANY ISSUES THAT MIGHT PREVENT ACCOMPLISHING TECHNICAL RESEARCH DURING THE NEXT REPORTING CYCLE;
2.1.2.5.ANY ANTICIPATED TRAVEL PLANS DURING THE NEXT REPORTING CYCLE.

2.2.	TACTICAL AI FOR MARINE CORPS
2.2.1.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS DURING YEAR 1 OF THE PROGRAM:

2.2.1.1.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT GATHERING AND ANALYZING SYSTEM OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS TO IMPLEMENT A KNOWLEDGE-BASE OF USMC RELEVANT RED AND BLUE UNITS CHARACTERISTICS (UNIT TYPE, WEAPON RANGE RINGS, EMS CAPABILITIES, ETC.).

2.2.1.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT GATHERING AND ANALYZING SYSTEM OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS, FOR AN INITIAL ARCHITECTURE AND TECHNICAL APPROACH TO DEVELOP ANALYTICS TO PREDICT RISK TO FORCE AND RISK TO MISSION FOR DMO AND EABO OR OTHER USMC OPERATIONS.

2.2.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS DURING YEAR 2 OF THE PROGRAM:

2.2.2.1.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONTINUE SUPPORTING GATHERING AND ANALYZING SYSTEM OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS, TO HELP INFORM ANALYTICS TO PREDICT RISK TO FORCE AND RISK TO MISSION FOR DMO AND EABO OR OTHER USMC OPERATIONS.

2.2.2.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE (SME) ON MECHANISMS TO SELECT VISUALIZATION STYLES AND AIDES ON AN OPERATIONS DASHBOARD FOR SEVERAL METRICS AND ASSESSMENT. SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.) 

2.2.3.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS DURING YEAR 3 OF THE PROGRAM:

2.2.3.1.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE (SME) TO EVALUATE A PROTOTYPE AUTOMATING THE TRACKING OF THE STATE OF INFORMATION FLOW MEASURES OF PERFORMANCE AND EFFECTIVENESS (MOPS AND MOES), AND ASSESS THE IMPACT OF SUCH PARAMETERS AND MEASURES TO OUTSTANDING MISSION INFORMATION NEEDS TO ACCOMPLISH OBJECTIVES AND TASKS.

2.2.3.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE (SME) ON THE USE OF MILITARY RELEVANT VIDEO GAMES AND SIMULATORS TO VALIDATE AND DEMONSTRATE CAPABILITIES UNDER DEVELOPMENT.

2.2.4.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS DURING YEAR 4 OF THE PROGRAM:

2.2.4.1.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SME FOR THE DESIGN OF A KNOWLEDGE-BASE OF USMC RELEVANT RED AND BLUE UNITS CHARACTERISTICS (UNIT TYPE, WEAPON RANGE RINGS, EMS CAPABILITIES, ETC.). SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)

2.2.4.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL REVIEW REQUIREMENTS AND PROVIDE FEEDBACK ON THE MODELING OF RISK TO FORCE AND RISK TO MISSION IN SUPPORT OF DMO/EABO OR OTHER USMC OPERATIONS.

2.2.5.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS DURING YEAR 5 OF THE PROGRAM:

2.2.5.1.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONTINUE SUPPORTING THE REVIEW REQUIREMENTS AND OVERALL DESIGN, TO AND PROVIDE SME ON ANALYTICS AND DATA GATHERING TO PREDICT RISK TO FORCE AND RISK TO MISSION BEING DEVELOPED UNDER THIS PROGRAM. 

2.2.5.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE (SME) ON THE DESIGN OF VISUALIZATION STYLES FOR SEVERAL METRICS AND ASSESSMENT AND ADD THEM TO THE OPERATIONS DASHBOARD. SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)

2.2.5.3.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE (SME) ON SCENARIO DEFINITION AND USER CONTROLS TO USE MILITARY RELEVANT VIDEO GAMES AND SIMULATORS WITHIN THE BOW SIMULATION FRAMEWORK. SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)

2.3.	AUTOMATION, AUTONOMIC, AND AUTONOMY
2.3.1. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS DURING YEAR 1 OF THE PROGRAM:

2.3.1.1.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT GATHERING AND ANALYSIS OF SYSTEM OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS AND DESIGN TO RECOMMEND TASK ALTERNATIVES (BRANCHES AND SEQUELS) FOR SMALL UNIT COMMANDERS, INTEGRATING LOW OBSERVABLES SYSTEMS (E.G., EABO, LOCE), TACSIT CONSIDERATIONS, AND KINETIC/NON-KINETIC WEAPONS PAIRING OF TARGETS. 

2.3.1.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL REVIEW REQUIREMENTS AND PROVIDE SME ON THE REPRESENTATION OF ENEMY PATTERN OF LIFE MODELS, UTILIZING DIFFERENT DATA TYPES AND SOURCES SUCH AS, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, TRACK DATA, ENVIRONMENTAL DATA, INTELLIGENCE REPORTS, AND HISTORICAL OPERATIONAL ZONES. SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)

2.3.2. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS DURING YEAR 2 OF THE PROGRAM:

2.3.2.1.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE (SME) AND SUPPORT THE DEFINITION OF SQUAD LEVEL TASKING ALTERNATIVES FOR MANNED-UNMANNED TEAMS BASED ON ORDERS RECEIVED FROM A PLATOON COMMANDER AND CURRENT SITUATIONAL UNDERSTANDING OF THE BATTLESPACE. SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)


2.3.2.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE (SME) AND SUPPORT THE DEFINITION OF COMMUNICATIONS POLICIES FOR SHARING DATA BETWEEN SQUAD LEADERS WHILE MINIMIZING PREDICTED ENEMY MOVEMENTS. SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)

2.3.2.3.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE (SME) AND REVIEW DESIGN TO REPRESENT AND IDENTIFY CONDITIONS AND CRITERIA FROM HISTORICAL, TRAINING AND/OR SIMULATED DATA, TO ALERT/NOTIFY DECISION-MAKERS (FOR EXAMPLE, BASED ON THE CONFIRMATION OR ANOMALY DETECTION OF CONDITIONS/FEATURES ON LEARNED BEHAVIORS). SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)

2.3.3.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS DURING YEAR 3 OF THE PROGRAM:

2.3.3.1.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE (SME) ON THE DEFINITION OF APPROACHES TO REASON OVER ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS SUCH AS TERRAIN AS WELL AS HOSTILE/FRIENDLY ASSET LOCATIONS TO PROVIDE DYNAMIC TASKING ALTERNATIVES TO PLATOON, SQUAD LEVEL ASSETS IN EVOLVING SCENARIOS. SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)

2.3.3.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL REVIEW AND PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE (SME) ON THE DESIGN AND PERFORMANCE TO REPRESENT AND IDENTIFY CONDITIONS AND CRITERIA FROM HISTORICAL, TRAINING AND/OR SIMULATED DATA, TO ALERT/NOTIFY DECISION-MAKERS (FOR EXAMPLE, BASED ON THE CONFIRMATION OR ANOMALY DETECTION OF CONDITIONS/FEATURES ON LEARNED BEHAVIORS). SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)

2.3.4.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS DURING YEAR 4 OF THE PROGRAM:

2.3.4.1.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE ON THE INTERPRETATION OF HIGHER-LEVEL SQUAD LEADER TASKING AND DECOMPOSES IT INTO INDIVIDUAL ACTIONS FOR THE VEHICLE COMMANDER ASSETS TO TAKE. SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)

2.3.4.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE AND SUPPORT THE DEFINITION OF INCLUDE ADDITIONAL BEHAVIORS (RELATIVE TO TASK 2.2.3.2) FOR THE CAPABILITY TO PREDICT ENEMY PATTERN OF LIFE. SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)

2.3.4.3.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL REVIEW ADDITIONAL USE CASES AND DESIGN (FROM TASK 2.2.3.3) AND SUPPORT THE DEFINITION OF ADDITIONAL APPROACHES TO REPRESENT AND IDENTIFY CONDITIONS AND CRITERIA FROM HISTORICAL, TRAINING AND/OR SIMULATED DATA, TO ALERT/NOTIFY DECISION-MAKERS (FOR EXAMPLE, BASED ON THE CONFIRMATION OR ANOMALY DETECTION OF CONDITIONS/FEATURES ON LEARNED BEHAVIORS). 

2.3.5.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS DURING YEAR 5 OF THE PROGRAM:

2.3.5.1.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL REVIEW ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS TO UPDATE DEVELOPED ALGORITHMS (FROM TASK 2.3.4.1) TO PROVIDE A PREDICTION CAPABILITY OF TASKING PLAN PERFORMANCE AS A FUNCTION OF TIME, ORDER OF BATTLE (OOB), DETECTIONS, AVAILABLE ASSETS AND/OR MISSION TASK. FEATURES CONTRIBUTING TO THE PREDICTION MODEL WILL BE EVALUATED DURING EXECUTION AND ALTERNATIVES WILL BE PRESENTED TO THE USER ON HOW TO INCREASE COLLECTION PERFORMANCE. 

2.3.5.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE (SME) AND REVIEW DESIGN AND REQUIREMENTS (FROM TASK 2.3.4.2) TO PREDICT ENEMY PATTERN OF LIFE ALGORITHMS UTILIZING DIFFERENT DATA TYPES AND SOURCES SUCH AS, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, TRACK DATA, ENVIRONMENTAL DATA, INTELLIGENCE REPORTS, AND HISTORICAL OPERATIONAL ZONES. SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)

2.3.5.3.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT THE REVIEW OF THE DESIGN (FROM TASK 2.3.4.3) AND PROVIDE SME ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF ADDITIONAL APPROACHES TO REPRESENT AND IDENTIFY CONDITIONS AND CRITERIA FROM HISTORICAL, TRAINING AND/OR SIMULATED DATA, TO ALERT/NOTIFY DECISION-MAKERS (FOR EXAMPLE, BASED ON THE CONFIRMATION OR ANOMALY DETECTION OF CONDITIONS/FEATURES ON LEARNED BEHAVIORS). SME MAY INCLUDE BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO SUPPORTING MEETINGS, PROVIDE MILITARY RELEVANT DOCUMENTATION, REVIEW DESIGN DOCUMENTATION, COORDINATE MEETINGS, ETC.)

2.4.	EXPERIMENTATION
2.4.1. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS DURING YEARS 1 - 5 OF THE PROGRAM.
2.4.1.1.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF MILITARY SCENARIOS AND IMPLEMENT THEM ON A SIMULATION FRAMEWORK TO TEST THE CAPABILITIES OF THE BOW SYSTEMS.

2.4.1.2.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PARTICIPATE IN TECHNICAL EXCHANGE MEETINGS SUCH AS PROGRESS REVIEWS, PRELIMINARY DESIGN REVIEWS, CRITICAL DESIGN REVIEWS IN SUPPORT OF OPERATIONAL EXPERIMENTS WITH THE GOVERNMENT TEAM.

2.4.1.3.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM ANALYTICAL AND TECHNOLOGY ASSESSMENTS TO AID IN DRIVING FUTURE HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS. 

2.4.1.4.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP DATA AND INFORMATION NECESSARY TO ANSWER SPECIFIC TECHNICAL QUESTIONS AND SUPPORT KEY DECISION MAKING AND PLANNING.

2.4.1.5.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE PRESENTATION MATERIALS, TECHNICAL BRIEFINGS COMMUNICATION TOOLS, POINT PAPERS, TECHNICAL REVIEW/REPORTS AND PLANNING AND OPERATIONAL AIDES.

2.4.1.6.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL EVALUATE AND PROVIDE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF SOFTWARE COMPONENTS FOR TACTICAL AND NON-TACTICAL APPLICATIONS AND MODIFICATIONS AND UPGRADES, AND TRANSITION PLANS FOR SYSTEMS CONVERSIONS.

2.4.1.7.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE PREPARED TO WORK IN AUSTERE TERRAIN/ENVIRONMENTS (I.E. MILITARY RANGES, DESERT TEST FACILITIES, FIELD CONDITIONS) IN SUPPORT OF COMMUNICATION TEST AND EVALUATION EFFORTS. 

2.4.1.8.THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE PREPARED TO SUPPORT THE PREPARATION OR EXECUTION OF TEST EVENTS AND LIVE-FORCE EXPERIMENTAL EXERCISES.

DISCOVERY OF SELF-ENCAPSULATION FOR DEPLOYMENT: THE DEPLOYMENT OF BIOLOGICALLY ACCEPTABLE GLUES (E.G., VETBOND), WHICH ARE ALL CYANOACRYLATES OR THEIR DERIVATIVES, HAS BEEN HAMPERED BY THE FACT THAT THEY POLYMERIZE ALMOST IMMEDIATELY UPON CONTACT WITH WATER. THE RAPID POLYMERIZATION IS AN ISSUE FOR FIELD DEPLOYMENT DUE TO THE VAGARIES OF TAGGING (E.G., SPLASHING WATER) AS WELL AS THE LAYER OF WATER OFTEN ON THE BACKS OF ANIMALS AS THEY ARE TAGGED. THIS FEATURE OF THE CYANOACRYLATES IS NOT AN IMPEDIMENT FOR VETERINARIANS NOR EVEN CAPTIVE TESTING AS THE SURFACES CAN BE APPROPRIATELY PREPARED.  VETBOND AND MANY OFF-THE-SHELF CYANOACRYLATES HAVE A VERY LOW VISCOSITY AND, AS SUCH, ARE DIFFICULT TO WORK WITH AS THEY QUICKLY RUN OFF APPLICATION SURFACES AND, WHEN THEY CONTACT WATER, FORM A VERY THIN LAYER AND POLYMERIZE IMMEDIATELY. ONE OFF-THE-SHELF VARIETY IS MUCH MORE VISCOUS THAN THE VETBOND OR 'SUPER GLUE'. THEY INTRODUCED A FEW DROPS OF THE MORE VISCOUS GLUE INTO THE WATER, AND IT IMMEDIATELY FORMED A SPHERE AS THE OUTSIDE POLYMERIZED, BUT WE DISCOVERED THAT THE INSIDE STILL CONTAINED LIQUID GLUE. KNOWING THIS, WE APPLIED A FEW MILLILITERS OF THE GLUE TO A TAG SURFACE (E.G., SUCTION CUP), THEN CAREFULLY SUBMERSED IT UPSIDE DOWN SO THE OUTSIDE OF THE BLOB WOULD ENCAPSULATE, WHICH IT DID, AND THEN WE WERE ABLE TO ORIENT THE TAG IN THE NORMAL ORIENTATION FOR DEPLOYMENT (ALL OF THIS IN TANKS WITH PIECES OF WOOD FOR TARGETS), AND WHEN WE TRIED TO ATTACH THE TAG WITH A 'SMACK', THE POLYMERIZED SHELL BROKE, EXPOSED THE LIQUID GLUE, WHICH THEN QUICKLY POLYMERIZED IN THE WATER AND FORMED A VERY STRONG ATTACHMENT TO THE WOOD. SO, WE WILL TO RUN MORE TESTS, REFINE THIS STRATEGY, CONDUCT MEASUREMENTS OF ATTACHMENT STRENGTH UTILIZING SKIN/BLUBBER SAMPLES FROM PREVIOUSLY STRANDED ANIMALS, AND GENERALLY EXPLORE THIS STRATEGY FOR USING ADHESIVES DURING FIELD DEPLOYMENTS OF SUCTION CUP TAGS. ASSUMING THAT THE GLUES WILL WORK AND RESULT IN A LONG-TERM ATTACHMENT, DESIGN IS NEEDED FOR A SYSTEM SO THE TAG COULD ALSO RELEASE. ASSUMING THAT THE SUCTION CUPS WOULD HAVE ADHESIVE IN THEM, WE NEED ANOTHER MECHANISM.

THE EMBODIMENT OF A PROSTHETIC LIMB USING PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT SENSORY FEEDBACK IS A METHOD FOR DESCRIBING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF A NEURAL-MACHINE-INTERFACE. PROSTHETIC LIMB INCORPORATION METHODS FOCUS ON QUESTIONNAIRE, PSYCHOPHYSICAL, AND PHYSIOLOGICAL TEMPERATURE MEASUREMENT FOR ASSESSMENT. CROSS-MODAL CONGRUENCY EFFECT (CCE) EXTENDS BEYOND THESE APPROACHES AND WILL PROVIDE A SPECIFIC METRIC FOR QUANTITATIVE INCORPORATION OF A PROSTHETIC LIMB INTO THE BODY SCHEMA AS AN EMBODIED TOOL. PRELIMINARY DATA IN TARGETED REINNERVATION SUBJECTS SUGGESTS THAT SENSORY INCORPORATION DEVELOPS AFTER A TRAINING PERIOD AND THE INCORPORATION LEVEL VARIES DEPENDING ON THE PHYSICAL DISTANCE BETWEEN THE MOTOR OUTPUT AND THE SENSORY FEEDBACK. 
SPEED AND ACCURACY OF PROSTHESIS USE ARE IMPORTANT ASPECTS OF FUNCTIONAL QUANTIFICATION. UNFORTUNATELY, FEW HUMAN-MACHINE INTERFACE METHODS EXIST THAT ARE SENSITIVE ENOUGH TO CAPTURE DIFFERENCES IN EFFICIENCY OF CONTROL AND FEEDBACK SYSTEMS. GAIN MARGIN CROSSOVER FREQUENCY IS AN INDEX USED IN ROBOTICS THAT HAS RECENTLY BEEN APPLIED TO HUMAN-MACHINE-INTERFACES; HOWEVER, IT IS BETTER SUITED TO INDEX CONTROL APPROACHES THAN THE CONTRIBUTION OF FEEDBACK. FITT'S LAW MEASURES SPEED ACCURACY TRADE-OFF OF A GIVEN HUMAN-MACHINE INTERFACE, AND HAS BECOME AN ISO STANDARD FOR MEASURING THE PERFORMANCE OF TOOLS SUCH AS COMPUTER MICE. UNFORTUNATELY, FITT'S LAW IS DEPENDENT ON THE INERTIA OF THE INTERFACE - A FACT ACKNOWLEDGED BY FITTS, BUT UNKNOWN BY MANY CONTEMPORARY SCIENTISTS. DIFFERENT HUMAN-MACHINE INTERFACES HAVE DIFFERENT INERTIA AND THEY WILL OBTAIN DIFFERENT FITTS SCORES EVEN IF CONTROL AND FEEDBACK ARE THE SAME. THIS SOMEWHAT LIMITS THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THIS METRIC FOR COMPARISON ACROSS PROSTHETIC LIMB CONTROL AND FEEDBACK SYSTEMS. FITT'S LAW IS ALSO BASED ON THE ASSUMPTION THAT NOISE IS ADDITIVE. HOWEVER, NOISE IN THE EMG CONTROL INTERFACE IS MULTIPLICATIVE AND DEVIATES TOO MUCH FROM THE MODELING CAPABILITIES OF FITT'S LAW. COMPUTATIONAL MOTOR CONTROL INDEX (CMCI) PROVIDES A COMPARABLE BUT MORE EFFECTIVE PATH FOR QUANTIFICATION OF SPEED AND ACCURACY OF USE IN A PROSTHETIC LIMB SYSTEM. UNLIKE FITT'S LAW CMCI ACCOUNTS FOR MULTIPLICATIVE NOISE AND IS IDEALLY POSITIONED TO TACKLE BIOLOGICAL SYSTEMS SUCH AS EMG CONTROL. IN ORDER TO BEGIN DEVELOPMENT A CMCI THAT ACCURATELY REFLECTS THE MULTIPLICATIVE NOISE FOUND IN PERIPHERAL NERVE CONTROL WE VALIDATED A COMPUTATIONAL MOTOR CONTROL FRAMEWORK TO ACCURATELY ACCOUNT FOR CONTROL AND FEEDBACK. SUBJECTS PERFORMED A BALLISTIC 1D SCREEN POINTING TASK WITH PROSTHETIC ARM DYNAMICS. THREE CONTROL INTERFACES WERE TESTED IN THE PRESENCE OF TWO FEEDBACK CONDITIONS WITH PERTURBATIONS TO VISUAL FEEDBACK. WE FOUND THAT THE CONTROL MODALITY ITSELF(JOYSTICK VS. TORQUE VS. EMG) DID NOT HAVE A STRONG INFLUENCE ON THE RESULTS - THE ERROR OF THE CONTROL MODALITY WAS SUFFICIENT TO CAPTURE THE EFFECT (FIG. 5). THIS RESULT SUGGESTS THAT A CMCI WILL BE ROBUST TO MEASURING THE EFFECT OF VARIOUS PERIPHERAL NERVE CONTROL SOURCES AND FEEDBACK DEVICES, REGARDLESS OF WHICH MODALITY THEY TARGET, AS LONG AS THEY TRULY ADD VALUE TO THE CONTROL AND FEEDBACK OF THE PROSTHESIS.

SPECIFICALLY, THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS SUBCONTRACT IS TO EXPLORE TECHNIQUES FOR GENERATING PATCHES TO DEFECTS IN REALTIME-EMBEDDED SOFTWARE IN CYBER-PHYSICAL SYSTEMS. WE WILL LEVERAGE INSIGHTS FROM GENETIC PROGRAMMING AND EVOLUTIONARY COMPUTATION TO AUTOMATICALLY GENERATE VARIANTS OF A CANDIDATE PATCHED BINARY TO EVALUATE THE QUALITY OF THAT PATCH IN TERMS OF (1) CORRECTNESS WITH RESPECT TO A TEST SUITE, AND (2) ROBUSTNESS AGAINST YET-UNKNOWN DEFECTIVE INPUTS. WE WILL ALSO DEVELOP TECHNIQUES FOR IDENTIFYING PROPERTIES OF AN INPUT PROGRAM THAT ARE RELEVANT TO SUCCESSFULLY DEPLOYING A PATCH IN A LIVE SYSTEM WITHOUT RECOMPILATION AND WHERE SOURCE CODE IS UNAVAILABLE. THIS EFFORT IS RELEVANT TO SEVERAL CIVILIAN AND GOVERNMENTAL PURPOSES: THE ASSURANCE OF BINARY-LEVEL PATCHES CAN INCREASE TRUSTWORTHINESS AND RELIABILITY OF PARTIALLY- AND FULLY-AUTONOMOUS CYBER-PHYSICAL SYSTEMS, AND DECREASE DOWNTIME WHEN DEPLOYING PATCHES TO DEFECTIVE SOFTWARE.

THE GOAL OF THE IRONPATCH PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP RIGOROUS PROGRAM TRANSFORMATION, ANALYSIS, AND VERIFICATION TECHNIQUES TO GENERATED ASSURED MICRO PATCHES FOR MISSION-CRITICAL SOFTWARE. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS SUBCONTRACT IS TO OUTLINE THE STATEMENT OF WORK ITEMS THAT PERTAIN TO THE PHASE III OF THE PROJECT THAT WILL BE CONDUCTED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON. BROADLY, PHASE III WILL ADVANCE SCOPE OF THE EVALUATION TARGETS TO NETWORKED AND DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS THAT EXHIBIT SIGNIFICANT CONCURRENCY. THE INCREASED COMPLEXITY OF THE TARGET SYSTEMS WILL SURFACE NEW SCALABILITY CHALLENGES IN SYMBOLIC PROGRAM COMPARISON THAT WE PLAN TO ADDRESS IN THIS PHASE. IN PARTICULAR, DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS PRESENT A SUBSTANTIAL CHALLENGE TO SYMBOLIC EQUIVALENCE CHECKING DUE TO THE INCREASED NUMBER AND SCALE OF NETWORKED SYSTEMS (E.G., MULTIPLE CONNECTED SYSTEMS AT 1M+ LOC AS MENTIONED IN THE AMP PROGRAM BAA).

THE KEY CHALLENGE IN SYMBOLIC EXECUTION OF DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS IS THAT THE TARGET PROGRAM TO PATCH CAN BE COMMUNICATING WITH DIFFERENT PROGRAMS (E.G., USING SOCKETS). THIS CAN SUBSTANTIALLY COMPLICATE SYMBOLIC ANALYSIS. TO SEE WHY, CONSIDER THE WRITE(FD, BUF, COUNT) SYSTEM CALL WHICH WRITES COUNT BYTES OF DATA FROM BUF INTO THE FILE DESCRIPTOR FD (WHICH CAN BE A NETWORK SOCKET). WRITE CAN RETURN A VALUE BETWEEN -1 AND COUNT. OUR SYMBOLIC EXPLORATION CAN REPLACE THE SYSTEM CALL RETURN VALUEÃ¢Â‚¬Â€?WHICH IS AN INPUT TO THE PROGRAMÃ¢Â‚¬Â€?WITH A SYMBOLIC VALUE BETWEEN -1 AND COUNT, WHICH WOULD ALLOW FOR EXPLORING ALL THE PATHS IN OUR PROGRAM DEPENDING ON THE VALUE ON THE INPUT. SIMILARLY, WE CAN CONSIDER THE EFFECTS OF ALL THE SYSTEM CALL RETURN VALUES (I.E., INPUTS) BASED ON THE INTERFACE SPECIFICATION OF THE SYSTEM CALL AND MARK RETURN VALUES AS SYMBOLIC (WITH APPROPRIATE CONSTRAINTS). OUR SYMBOLIC PROGRAM COMPARISON CAN THEN PROCEED AS DESCRIBED IN TASKS II.1Ã¢Â‚¬Â€ŒII.4.

ALAS, NAIVELY APPLYING SYMBOLIC EXECUTION TO DISTRIBUTED SYSTEMS WILL CAUSE FURTHER PATH EXPLOSION. FOR INSTANCE, THERE ARE NO EXECUTIONS WHERE K BYTES ARE WRITTEN TO A SOCKET AND WRITE RETURNS 0. YET, THE ABOVE NAIVE STRATEGY ACCOUNTS FOR SUCH EXECUTIONS. ANOTHER NAIVE STRATEGY TO SOLVE THIS CHALLENGE IS ATTEMPTING TO SYMBOLICALLY EXECUTE THE CODE OF THE COMMUNICATED PARTY (E.G., AT THE OTHER END OF THE SOCKET). IN THEORY, THIS WOULD ELIMINATE CASES WHERE AN INFEASIBLE SYSTEM CALL RETURN VALUE IS OBSERVED AS IN THE ABOVE SITUATION WITH WRITE. HOWEVER, IN REALITY, SYMBOLICALLY EXPLORING AN ENTIRE OTHER CODEBASE WILL HURT SCALABILITY MORE.
THE PURPOSE OF THIS MODIFICATION IS TO PROVIDE INCREMENTS OF FUNDING.

OBJECTIVE: THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE OF THIS WORK IS TO OPTIMIZE ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING (AM) BUILD QUALITY FOR A NOTIONAL NAVY COMPONENT (OSPREY V-22 LINK) IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE ITS BUILD STRENGTH UPON POST-PROCESS HOT ISOSTATIC PRESSING (HIP) AND HEAT TREATMENT. THE TECHNICAL APPROACH IS TO SYNTHESIZE THE KNOWLEDGE GAINED BY THE COMBINED USE OF INTEGRATED COMPUTATIONAL MATERIALS ENGINEERING (ICME) AND INÃ‚Â­SITU SENSING IN ORDER TO UNDERSTAND HOW THE AM BUILD PROCESS CULMINATES INTO A BUILD DEFECT AND SEEK TO DEMONSTRATE A SCIENTIFIC PROCESS TO METHODICALLY REDUCE THE PEAK % DEFECTS BY A FACTOR OF TWO. IN THIS REGARD, THE INTERIOR AND SURFACE-CONNECTED POROSITY, SURFACE ROUGHNESS, RESIDUAL STRESS AND MICROSTRUCTURE WILL BE UTILIZED AS PROXY MEASURES FOR AM BUILD QUALITY THAT HAVE A DIRECT EFFECT ON THE FATIGUE STRENGTH. ACCORDINGLY, THE PROJECT EFFORT WILL BE TO MAXIMIZE THE BUILD QUALITY WITH RESPECT TO THESE FOUR CRITERIA. 
THE OSPREY V-22 LINK WAS PRODUCED AT PENN STATE AND THERE IS HISTORICAL DATA ON THE PERFORMANCE OF THE AM BUILD PROCESS IN REGARDS TO FATIGUE PERFORMANCE. THE AM PARTS WERE HI PED AND FINISH MACHINED PRIOR TO FATIGUE TESTING. IT WAS OBSERVED THAT DEFECTS NEAR THE SURFACE OF THE MACHINED PARTS MAY HAVE BEEN AN IMPORTANT INFLUENCE IN CREATING A DEBIT IN FATIGUE PERFORMANCE. 
BACKGROUND: AO WILL PERFORM ICME MODELING. THE ICME MODELING WILL BUILD UPON THE PRIOR EXPERIENCE IN AM DEPOSITION OF THE OSPREY V-22 LINK AT PENN STATE. IT WILL BEGIN WITH THE MOST RECENT VERSION OF THE OPTIMIZED PARAMETERS, NOTE THE LOCATIONS OF HIGH DEFECT DENSITY AND TARGET THOSE LOCATIONS FOR BUILD QUALITY IMPROVEMENT WITH RESPECT TO THE FOUR METRICS FOR BUILD QUALITY. 
THIS ICME MODELING WILL UTILIZE THE SCAN VECTOR DATA FROM THE AM BUILD PLAN AS INPUT, AND PROVIDE A DETAILED DEFINITION OF AM BUILD PARAMETERS. THE AM BUILDS WILL BE PRODUCED USING THE PROX DMP 320 SYSTEM. THE IN-SITU SENSING DATA WILL BE COLLECTED BY PENN STATE. THIS DATA WILL INCLUDE INFRARED MEASUREMENT OF BUILD TEMPERATURE ON A LAYER-BY-LAYER BASIS AND THE AO 3D LASER SCANNER DATA TO MEASURE THE BUILD TOP-SURFACE TOPOLOGY, WHICH HAS BEEN IMPLEMENTED UNDER THE NAVY PROJECT NLSA-263 FOR AO. THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE DETAILED SET OF AM BUILD PARAMETERS PREDICTED BY ICME MAY INCLUDE LOCATION DEPENDENT SPECIFICATION OF LASER POWER WITHIN AN INDIVIDUAL LAYER AND ON A LAYER-BY-LAYER BASIS. SUCH LOCATION DEPENDENCE WILL BE DEFINED AS A LIST OF SCALING VALUES FOR THE DEFAULT POWER VS. THE TRACK NUMBER FOR EACH LAYER. PENN STATE MAY NEED TO UTILIZE / MODIFY THE FEEDFORWARD CONTROL (FFC) PROGRAMMING PERFORMED UNDER THE NAVY PROJECT N181-085 FOR AO FOR THIS PURPOSE.
TASK 1) IMPLEMENT LOCATION-DEPENDENT SPECIFICATION OF LASER POWER AND ENABLE THE IN-SITU SENSING.
TASK 1.1) PERFORM FFC PROGRAMMING TO PERMIT LOCATION-DEPENDENT SPECIFICATION OF LASER POWER. 
TASK 1.2) ENABLE THE COLLECTION OF LAYER-BY-LAYER 3D LASER SCANNER DATA. 
TASK 1.3) ENABLE THE COLLECTION OF LAYER-BY-LAYER DATA FOR AM BUILD TOP SURFACE TEMPERATURE. 
TASK 1.4) EVALUATE AND TRANSFER SENSOR DATA TO APPLIED OPTIMIZATION.
TASK 2) SUPPORT STRATEGIES FOR CONTROL AND ALTERATION OF MACHINE SETTINGS. 
TASK 2.1) ADVISE ON CONTROL OF MACHINE SETTINGS AND THE AM BUILD QUALITY OPTIMIZATION. 
TASK 2.2) ASSIST IN IMPLEMENTATION OF AM BUILD PARAMETERS AND THE UTILIZATION OF IN-SITU SENSING. 
TASK 7) TEST ARTICLE BUILDS AND EVALUATION.
TASK 3.1) COORDINATE BUILDUP OF LPBF COMPONENTS. 
TASK 3.2) PERFORM METALLOGRAPHY ON A SELECT NUMBER OF BUILT SAMPLES.

3.2.1. PROCURE THE HARDWARE NEEDED TO REPLACE THE FAMS PITCH AXIS MOTORS.

3.3.2. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE METHOD FOR RECONCILING RENTAL FEES FOR THE COMPRESSED GAS CYLINDERS AND PALLET RENTAL INVOICED BY SUPPLIER(S).
3.4.SUPPORT THE MISSILES STRATEGIC SYSTEMS BRANCH (SIH-MSS) WITH THE INTEGRATION, TEST AND VERIFICATION OF THE SOFTWARE TOOLS (E.G. ICON AND TMSIM) DELIVERED BY THE PRIME CONTRACTORS LOCKHEED MARTIN AND RAYTHEON AS WELL AS THAAD PROGRAM OFFICE. THIS WORK SHALL INCLUDE: (IAW PWS PARA. 2.1.1, 2.1.2)
3.4.1. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROCURE INFORMATION SYSTEMS WHICH WILL HOST THE ICON SIMULATION EXECUTIVE PROGRAM AND THAAD MISSILE SIMULATION (TMSIM).

1.1 PURPOSE

CCDC AVMC HAS A NEED TO PRODUCE NEW AND IMPROVED WEAPON SYSTEMS AND TO IMPLEMENT TECHNOLOGICAL ADVANCEMENTS IN THE MANUFACTURE OF THE WEAPON SYSTEMS. THE CCDC AVMC EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR HAS CHARGED THE CCDC AVMC CIO/G6 WITH TRANSFORMING THE INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY LANDSCAPE ACROSS THE CENTER. 2.0 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE THE MANPOWER AND EXPERTISE TO MEET THE BELOW TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:

2.1 SOFTWARE/SYSTEMS SUPPORT

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SYSTEMS ADMINISTRATION AND SOFTWARE APPLICATION EXPERTISE TO PROVIDE CONTINUED MAINTENANCE, DEVELOPMENT, AND SUPPORT FOR THE FORTIFY SOFTWARE CODE ANALYSIS ENVIRONMENT, TOOL SETS, AND CODE SIMULATORS THAT SUPPORT VARIOUS APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS ACROSS CCDC AVMC. THIS SOFTWARE EXPERTISE SHALL INCLUDE OPERATING THE FORTIFY ENVIRONMENT TO PROVIDE SOFTWARE ANALYSIS REPORTS ON ALPHA AND BETA CODE SETS TO CCDC AVMC DEVELOPERS WHO IN TURN ARE CREATING PRODUCTS OR ARE PROVIDING SOFTWARE ENGINEERING SERVICES TO CUSTOMERS. RESULTS OF THESE EFFORTS SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IAW DI-MCCR- 80700/A004.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SYSTEMS ADMINISTRATION AND SOFTWARE APPLICATION EXPERTISE TO PROVIDE CONTINUED MAINTENANCE, DEVELOPMENT, AND SUPPORT FOR DATABASE DEVELOPMENT ENVIRONMENTS SUPPORTING A VARIETY OF CCDC AVMC CUSTOMER PROJECTS AND DELIVERABLES. THIS SOFTWARE EXPERTISE SHALL INCLUDE SUPPORT FOR SQL AND ORACLE DATABASES AND SHALL INCLUDE MODIFICATION OF THE DATABASE CODING AND DEVELOPMENT ENVIRONMENTS SUPPORTING CUSTOMER REQUIREMENTS WHILE ENSURING DATA INTEGRITY, AVAILABILITY, AND NON-INTERFERENCE. RESULTS OF THESE EFFORTS SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IAW DI-MCCR-80700/A004.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SYSTEMS ENGINEERING, ADMINISTRATION AND SOFTWARE APPLICATION EXPERTISE TO PROVIDE CONTINUED MAINTENANCE, DEVELOPMENT, AND SUPPORT FOR THE SHAREPOINT DEVELOPMENT ENVIRONMENTS SUPPORTING A VARIETY OF CCDC AVMC CUSTOMER PROJECTS AND DELIVERABLES. THIS SOFTWARE EXPERTISE SHALL INCLUDE SUPPORT AND INTEGRATIONS WITH DATABASE SYSTEMS, CAC AND ACTIVE DIRECTORY FEDERATED SERVICES AUTHENTICATION MECHANISMS, ELECTRONIC PROCESS WORKFLOWS, AND VBRICK INTEGRATIONS AND SUPPORTING SERVICES. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ALSO PROVIDE SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT EXPERTISE TO SUPPORT SHAREPOINT APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS ACROSS CCDC AVMC BY DEVELOPERS WHO IN TURN ARE CREATING PRODUCTS OR ARE PROVIDING SOFTWARE ENGINEERING SERVICES TO CUSTOMERS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ALSO PROVIDE A SHAREPOINT OPTIMIZATION PLAN AND TIMELINE BASED UPON REQUIREMENTS STIPULATED BY THE CIO. RESULTS OF THESE EFFORTS SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IAW DI-MCCR-80700/A004.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SOFTWARE & SYSTEMS DEVELOPMENT EXPERTISE IN THE ADMINISTRATION, MAINTENANCE, DEVELOPMENT, AND SUPPORT OF THE INTEGRATED CENTER INFORMATION SYSTEM, WHICH CONSISTS OF MULTIPLE LINUX SERVERS CURRENTLY RUNNING ORACLE APPLICATION SERVER AND ORACLE WEB SERVER IN A LOAD-BALANCED CONFIGURATION. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL HAVE SPECIALIZED KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERTISE IN ORACLE APPLICATION SERVER, ORACLE WEB SERVER, APACHE WEB SERVER, ORACLE INTERNET DIRECTORY AUTHENTICATION, ACTIVE DIRECTORY SERVER SYNCHRONIZATION, SECURE SOCKET LAYER (SSL) WITH SINGLE SIGN ON, TUMBLEWEED VALIDATION AND CAC INTEGRATION, SSL CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION AND WALLET MANAGER INTEGRATION, ORACLE WEB CACHE AND LOAD BALANCING, ENTERPRISE MANAGER CONFIGURATION, JAVA TECHNOLOGY, AS WELL AS EXPERIENCE WITH THE CURRENT INTEGRATED CENTER INFORMATION SYSTEM ENVIRONMENT. RESULTS OF THESE EFFORTS SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IAW DI-MCCR-80700/A004.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PARTICIPATE IN INTEGRATED PROJECT TEAMS TO PROVIDE INPUT INTO SELECTION PROCESSES OF AUTOMATED TOOLS TO SUPPORT IT PROJECT MANAGEMENT, ENTERPRISE ARCHITECTURE, CAPACITY MANAGEMENT, CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT, DATA WAREHOUSING, ENTERPRISE CONTENT MANAGEMENT (ECM) AND KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT, THROUGH COST BENEFIT ANALYSIS, PRODUCT EVALUATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS DEFINITION.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COLLECT, DOCUMENT AND ANALYZE FUNCTIONAL USER REQUIREMENTS, PROCEDURES, AND PROBLEMS IN ORDER TO MAKE SOLUTION ALTERNATIVES ANALYSES & SOLUTION RECOMMENDATIONS; A COST/BENEFIT ANALYSIS OF THESE ALTERNATIVES AND RECOMMENDATIONS SHALL BE PREPARED AND PRESENTED AS A DECISIONAL BRIEFING WHEN REQUIRED BY CCDC AVMC CIO/G6, TO SENIOR LEADERS, TECHNICAL PERSONNEL AND OPERATIONAL CUSTOMERS IN A FORMAT COMPATIBLE WITH THE MICROSOFT OFFICEÂ„¢ SUITE OF SOFTWARE APPLICATIONS. AFTER APPROVAL BY THE GOVERNMENT, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL TRANSLATE THE BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS INTO FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS AND A TECHNICAL DESIGN. SERVICE ORIENTED ARCHITECTURE (SOA). THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE WEB SITE, WEB PAGE AND WEB APPLICATION DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, MAINTENANCE, AND ADMINISTRATION FOR CCDC AVMC AND ITS CUSTOMERS, INCLUDING THE SUPPORT OF CCDC AVMC PUBLIC WEBSITE, SHAREPOINT, TEAM FOUNDATION SERVER (TFS), INTERNET INFORMATION SERVER (IIS) PLATFORMS AND APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT ENVIRONMENTS CURRENTLY APPROVED SUCH AS PAT.  THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ALSO SUPPORT SOFTWARE EFFORTS NOT ORIGINALLY DEVELOPED BY THE CONTRACTOR UPON GOVERNMENT REQUEST AND APPROVAL.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CREATE, UPDATE, AND MAINTAIN LOCAL AND REMOTE DATABASE ENVIRONMENTS TO EFFECTIVELY UTILIZE EXISTING AND SHARED RESOURCES TO ENSURE AVAILABILITY AND INTEGRITY OF DATABASES ACROSS DEVELOPMENT, STAGING, PRE-PRODUCTION, PRODUCTION, AND TRAINING ENVIRONMENTS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL UTILIZE AUTOMATED TOOLS, AS SPECIFIED BY THE GOVERNMENT TO IDENTIFY DATABASE CAPACITY AND AVAILABILITY; OPTIMIZE DATABASE PERFORMANCE AND RESOURCE USAGE; PREDICT IMPENDING DATABASE PROBLEMS; ENSURE DATABASE RELIABILITY AND MAINTAINABILITY; PROVIDE SOLUTIONS TO CORRECT DATA BASE PROBLEMS; AND MAXIMIZE DATABASE THROUGHPUT. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COORDINATE WITH THE GOVERNMENT PRIOR TO SCHEDULING AND IMPLEMENTING DATABASE MAINTENANCE ACTIVITIES.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM DATABASE ANALYSIS, DESIGN, IMPLEMENTATION, SUSTAINMENT AND RETIREMENT ACTIVITIES IN COMPLIANCE WITH THE CCDC AVMC EXISTING SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PARTICIPATE IN WORK GROUPS AND MEETINGS TO ADDRESS DATABASE ADMINISTRATION ACTIVITIES. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL TRACK AND DOCUMENT DATABASE ADMINISTRATION ACTIVITIES THROUGH TECHNICAL SERVICE TICKETS UTILIZING AUTOMATED TOOLS PROVIDED BY THE GOVERNMENT.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL APPLY IAVA SECURITY AND SOFTWARE PATCHES, IMPLEMENT SECURITY REGULATIONS, AND VERIFY COMPLIANCE WITH SECURITY POLICIES IN ACCORDANCE WITH DOD, ARMY AND ORGANIZATIONAL POLICIES, REGULATIONS, AND GUIDANCE, AS DESIGNATED BY THE GOVERNMENT. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COORDINATE WITH THE GOVERNMENT PRIOR TO SCHEDULING AND IMPLEMENTING PATCHES.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE STRATEGIC DATABASE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR IMPLEMENTATION OF FUTURE DATABASE RELEASES, AND REPORTING METRICS ACROSS THE DATABASE ENTERPRISE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ADHERE TO AND IMPLEMENT RECOMMENDED METHODOLOGIES TO ENFORCE STANDARDIZATION AND FLEXIBILITY ACROSS THE DATABASE ENTERPRISE.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP AND MAINTAIN SOURCE CODE IN COMPLIANCE WITH SECURE CODING STANDARDS, APPLICATION STIGS, AND ALL APPLICABLE GOVERNMENT REGULATIONS, GUIDANCE, AND DIRECTIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE AND DELIVER ALL TECHNICAL DATA AND COMPUTER SOFTWARE TO INCLUDE SOURCE CODE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PARTICIPATE IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND EXECUTION OF TEST PLANS, PROCEDURES, AND REPORTS FOR APPLICATION UNIT, INTEGRATION, AND SOFTWARE ACCEPTANCE TESTING. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM SOURCE CODE CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT, ENVIRONMENT MANAGEMENT, AND PRODUCTION CODE DEPLOYMENT UTILIZING THE COTS/GOTS SOFTWARE PROVIDED BY THE GOVERNMENT.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DESIGN, DEVELOP AND DEMONSTRATE COMPUTER- AIDED SOFTWARE ENGINEERING (CASE) TOOLS FOR THE AED TASK TRACKING SYSTEM (TTS), AIRWORTHINESS QUALIFICATION PLAN PROGRAM (AQPP) AND LOCUS SYSTEMS. REQUIREMENTS FOR MODIFICATIONS SHALL BE DEFINED BY SYSTEM ENGINEERING ANALYSIS AND PROCESS REVIEWS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DOCUMENT AND PROVIDE A SCHEDULED TIMELINE FOR EACH SOFTWARE CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT CODE REVISION. THE RESULTS OF THESE EFFORTS SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IAW DI-MISC-80508/A011.

2.2 INFORMATION ASSURANCE/CYBER SUPPORT

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT THE INFORMATION ASSURANCE (IA) ACCREDITATION OF THE AVIATION AND MISSILE RDT&E UNCLASSIFIED LAN INFRASTRUCTURE (AMRULI). THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONDUCT WIRELESS SCANNING, NETWORK SCANNING, AND NETWORK MONITORING TO ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE WITH IA ACCREDITATION REQUIREMENTS. SUPPORT SHALL INCLUDE CONDUCTING AND REVIEWING VULNERABILITY AND COMPLIANCE SCANS, REVIEWING AUDIT RECORDS OF INFORMATION SYSTEMS, AND APPLYING REMEDIATION FOR SECURITY FLAWS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL MAINTAIN STIG CHECKLISTS AND SCAP SCANS FOR ALL SYSTEMS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ALSO PREPARE AND MAINTAIN TECHNICAL DOCUMENTATION ON THE AMRULI REQUIRED BY THE RMF PROCESS AS IT PERTAINS TO SUPPORTING AND MAINTAINING A CONTINUED AUTHORITY TO OPERATE (ATO) AUTHORIZATION FOR THE NETWORK AND ASSOCIATED SYSTEMS CONTINUALLY, AND SYNCHRONIZED WITH EACH ACCREDITATION CYCLE. RESULTS OF THESE EFFORTS SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IAW DI-MISC-80508/A025.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT CCDC AVMC DIRECTORATESÂ€™ & ENTERPRISE IA IN THE INFORMATION ASSURANCE (IA) ACCREDITATION OF SYSTEMS, APPLICATIONS AND PERIPHERALS, INTEGRATION POINTS & NETWORKS. SUPPORT SHALL INCLUDE CONDUCTING AND REVIEWING VULNERABILITY AND COMPLIANCE SCANS OF RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT INFORMATION SYSTEMS HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE, REVIEWING AUDIT RECORDS OF INFORMATION SYSTEMS, AND APPLYING REMEDIATION FOR SECURITY FLAWS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL HELP IN CREATING AND MAINTAINING IA CERTIFICATION AND ACCREDITATION DOCUMENTATION INCLUDING RISK MITIGATION FRAMEWORK (RMF) DOCUMENTATION, MEMORANDUMS OF UNDERSTANDING (MOU), MEMORANDUMS OF AGREEMENT (MOA), AND AUTHORITY TO OPERATE (ATO) DOCUMENTS RESULTS OF THESE EFFORTS SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IAW DI-MISC-80508B/A025.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROTECT CCDC AVMC COMPUTERS SYSTEMS FROM CYBER THREATS USING BEST BUSINESS PRACTICES, GOVERNMENT (DA, DOD, ETC.) REGULATIONS, POLICIES AND PROCEDURES OR AS REQUIRED BY CCDC AVMC. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH THE CCDC AVMC INFORMATION OFFICE AND DIRECTORATE CYBER SECURITY OFFICERS TO IDENTIFY, DIAGNOSE, AND REMEDIATE INFORMATION SYSTEM VULNERABILITIES.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE CLEANUP OF UNCLASSIFIED & CLASSIFIED SPILLAGE DATA WHEN INFORMATION IS SPILLED ONTO MEDIA THAT ARE UNDER THE ADMINISTRATIVE OVERSIGHT OF THE CONTRACTOR.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE AND PRESENT THE ANALYSIS, FINDINGS, AND RECOMMENDATIONS AS A DECISIONAL BRIEFING TO SENIOR LEADERS, TECHNICAL PERSONNEL, AND OPERATIONAL CUSTOMERS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INTEGRATE IT MODERNIZATION EFFORTS ACROSS AVMC AND WILL PROVIDE SURGE TECHNICAL CAPABILITIES, AS NECESSARY, TO SUPPORT THE SOLUTION IMPLEMENTATION PROCESS ENSURING THAT THE FINAL DELIVERED SOLUTION MEETS THE ORIGINAL REQUIREMENTS AND SOLUTION CONCEPT. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL MANAGE AND MITIGATE TECHNICAL RISKS ACROSS ALL WORK STREAMS REQUIRED TO SUPPORT SOLUTION IMPLEMENTATION.
