The Space Vehicles Directorate of the US Air Force and Space Force is interested in image processing on-board satellites for real-time detection of objects of interest. Obviously, such analysis, being on a satellite, must be performed without any human assistance and in a reliable way. Teuvonet has the technology that can provide that capability. That technology is explained using the overall AI technology framework that DARPA has provided over the years through several of its programs. Deep learning models, that are used for image recognition nowadays, are complex, hard to understand and therefore too risky to deploy in defense systems. DARPA launched an Explainable AI (XAI) program in 2016 asking for the development of more transparent and explainable models that can be deployed with confidence in defense systems. For computer vision, DARPA wanted object prediction to be based on the verification of parts of the object. For example, to predict that there is a cat in the image, it wanted the system to verify that it found its claws, whiskers, fur and other unique parts of a cat. So, part-verification based object prediction is DARPAÆs conceptualization of Explainable AI (XAI) for computer vision. Arizona State University (ASU) has developed this type of XAI technology and has filed an international patent application (a PCT) application for it. Teuvonet Technologies, a faculty startup, has licensed this technology from ASU and is currently using it to create a variety of real-time image processing systems based on such transparent models. DARPA is also interested in having AI models that are robust against adversarial attacks and started the GARD (Guaranteeing AI Robustness Against Deception) program. We have found that these parts-verification based XAI models are naturally robust against adversarial attacks. DARPA also started the ANSR (Assured Neuro Symbolic Learning and Reasoning) program. In the ANSR Program, DARPA wants ōnew, hybrid (neuro-symbolic) AI algorithms that deeply integrate symbolic reasoning with data-driven learning to create robust, assured, and therefore trustworthy systems.ö TeuvonetÆs technology supports creating systems that the ANSR program needs. Image processing, in general, whether from satellites, drones, or CCTVs, requires humans to examine them and is, thus, very labor intensive. Using transparent and trusted Explainable AI models, Teuvonet is developing a technology for image processing (1) that would not require humans to continuously observe and verify the content of the images, and (2) where processing and analysis of the images, for object detection, can be done with high-speed in real-time on hardware housed in satellites, drones and CCTVs. Such a capability would also obviate the need to transmit large volumes of unimportant images to an external storage facility such as the cloud. In other words, in this mode of processing, only important images will be transmitted to and stored in an external facility.

The immediate future of U.S. hypersonic vehicle development rests on the capabilities of current DAF/DoD ground-test facilities. One considerable capability gap lies with aerodynamic balances, which are crucial to directly measuring vehicle flight characteristics (e.g., lift, drag, and moment). Many new hypersonic vehicle designs are being equipped with reaction control systems (RCS) or divert attitude control systems (DACS), which produce a dynamic force on the vehicle, as typical aerodynamic control surfaces do not provide enough control authority at hypersonic speeds and altitudes. It is imperative for the vehicle design that the jet interaction with the surrounding hypersonic flow be understood, and the corresponding dynamic forces be accurately quantified. Current ground-test facilities are only equipped with standard static force balances that measure the mean aerodynamic loads. Due to the balance/stingÆs inertial response, these types of balances are not capable of accurately measuring dynamic loads, and no direct measurement alternative exists. To address this critical measurement capability gap, Ahmic proposes to adapt their commercial static balance technology and leverage its experience with calibrations and force reconstruction algorithms to develop a new Dynamic Force Measurement Solution (DFMS), which will allow a new age of hypersonic weapons systems to be accurately tested and characterized.

Corrosion of DoD assets is a continuous problem that seriously impacts cost and availability. We propose to take the Corrosion Modeling Toolset, an existing commercial product by Corrdesa and Siemens, modify it as necessary, and deploy it on the DAF DTO Launchpad for use throughout DAF. Although this Toolset is based on computational corrosion analysis, which typically requires computational specialists, it is designed to work from templates rather than CAD models, so that it can be used by engineers with no computational simulation experience. The Toolset has already been validated and used by the USAF CPCO at Robins AFB to solve a number of serious actual and potential corrosion problems on C-17, U-2 and B-21. This software will be demonstrated by CPCO at various DoD organizations and conferences, where it will be used to solve existing corrosion issues. More templates and materials will be added to solve the different problems that will be encountered in these demonstrations, making it possible to use the approach for almost any DAF corrosion problem. Capabilities will be added to incorporate the effect and degradation of organics such as paint stack-ups and CPCĺs, and to predict corrosion buildup as aircraft fly their missions around the world. A unique aspect of this proposed corrosion simulation deployment is that the tools are not just made available in a cloud platform but also within theáDAF preferred Product Lifecycle Management environment, that is, Siemens Teamcenter. This approach addresses several DAF strategic needs with respect to the digital transformation of the department. DAF staff working at any stage in a weapon system lifecycle will have access to the same data through the digital thread, minimizing repeat of errors and maximizing the benefits of learning and good practice as well as significantly compressing the time from requirements to the fielding of systems.á A number of OEMs have also shown interest in using the software, which will help to ensure that weapon systems are designed to minimize corrosion from the outset, reducing the lifetime cost and non-availability that corrosion commonly causes.
Deploying Consistent Predictive Corrosion Risk Assessment Across the DoD Enterprise

The proposed effort enhances a USSOCOM funded no-emit, vision-based GPS-Denied UAV navigation solution with increased range and altitude, deploys the solution through a software download or modular payload that is compliant with Mod Payload AD1167779 and ASPN/pntOS standards, and adapts the solution to provide robust Alt-PNT to multi-agent systems. The proposed effort demonstrates the solution on a Firestorm Labs, L3Harris, Lockheed Martin UAV, or stakeholder selected UAV and delivers a hardware prototype. The solution is a vision-navigation system that uses a drone’s cameras and IMUs (inertial measurement units). The solution navigates using the features in the environment, no pre-loaded terrain map needed. By combining cameras, IMU data, pixel-movement tracking, and object+feature tracking over time through Rhoman’s unique system, the UAV always knows exactly where it is relative to launch. The UAV can perform any autonomous mission as if it had GPS, and when you know your location at launch, the UAV always knows it’s absolute location. Deploys by Software or Hardware: The solution can deploy by software using the existing cameras and compute on the drone, or through a Mod Payload AD1167779 compliant payload: just mount to the standard payload attachment interface, perform one-time calibration manuevers post install, and the UAV is good to go. Visual Inertial Odometry + Corrector Module: The solution works by using the cameras and IMUs to enact a visual-inertial-odemetry (VIO) system to calculate the flight path of the UAV, then uses an error-correction model to cancel out and correct any drift that occurs in the VIO system. Drift Corrector Module: The drift error correction module detects objects & visual-features in the environment, tracks the relative movement of the drone versus those objects/features over time, and by measuring it’s distance to multiple objects at once, over time, it determines it’s actual exact movement, and corrects the VIO estimate. Object-Location-Maps, Always Return to Launch: The solution allows a UAV to always get back to launch. During flight, when the system detects and tracks objects and visual-features in the environment (bridge, group of trees, mountain ridgeline, rock formation, lake, road- intersection, edge of large farm-field, etc) as part of the drift-correction module, it also saves the description and estimated location of these objects into an ‘object-location-map’. This map provides the UAV with ‘visual-breadcrumbs’ it can use to follow and always get back to launch. The system can also work if the UAV lands at a different location: even if it doesn’t follow the ‘visual-breadcrumbs’ back to launch, it still has its Alt-PNT position estimate throughout the whole mission, and can perform missions and land in new places.

Reinforcement learning (RL) is essential for future autonomous flight systems such as those contemplated by Replicator, Shield AI, and others. Unfortunately, RL is incompatible with safety and airworthiness standards like MIL-STD-882E and DO-178C. In partnership with Carnegie Mellon, we wil bridge this gap with a novel assurance case, massive statistical evidence, calibrated metrics of trust, as well as existing level-of-rigor tasks from safety engineering. We already provide autonomy safety assessment to the U.S. Army’s XM30 and RCV programs, as well commercial developers Aurora, BMW, and Mobileye. We wrote UL 4600, the world’s first standard for autonomy safety. We inform T&E policymaking at the DoD and state- and federal-level departments of transportation. We recently completed a study of metrics for autonomy trustworthiness for the Center for Calibrated Trust Measurement and Evaluation (CaTE) run by Dr. Kim Sablon, the Principal Director for Trusted AI and Autonomy in OUSD(R&E). Our objectives on this project are below. We will document research results for the customer, publish academically, and enhance Edge Case’s nLoop SaaS platform, which we make available to DAF end-users on Azure through our partnership with Microsoft. AI Alignment. Trustworthy RL learns policies that satisfy mission-critical requirements. Primal-dual style approaches suffer from instability issues and lack optimality guarantees. We will apply lessons learned from research on inverse constraint learning, inverse reinforcement learning, and moment-matching frameworks. We will expand our research on an E-M approach for incorporating constraints naturally and decomposing the larger RL problem into a convex optimization phase and a supervised learning phase, for stable training performance. Hazard Assessment. This involves evaluating the safety guarantees of policies generated by RL to identify conditions in which an autonomous system might fail to uphold trust. Encountering all mission-critical scenarios is infeasible, so we seek edge cases using distributionally robust optimization techniques. We will iteratively change the starting state policy to find a potentially unsafe problem instance using multiplicative weights methods. Continuous and high-dimensional spaces can be reduced to simpler optimization problems (e.g., supervised learning) through substructure identification. Assurance and Metrics. We will trace evidence from the above work to claims in our Assurance Framework for Trustworthy Autonomy produced for CaTE. We will employ an eliminative argumentation process to improve our assurance case with feedback from end users, subject matter experts, and stakeholders from DAF and DoD programs of record. We will also incorporate templated metrics of trust from the CaTE assurance framework into the AI Alignment activities, making RL training more successful and efficient in producing models that are worthy of our trust.

A challenge to reducing cost and time in manufacturing these materials lies in a manufacturing process referred to as “densification”, which involves a time consuming sequence of repeat steps that are necessary to reduce the number of voids (tiny air spaces) in the material that can be sources of component failure during operation.  Endeavor Composites, Inc. designs and fabricates novel high-performance composites for customers in building and construction, automotive, energy, consumer goods, and aerospace. Endeavor’s flagship patented technology is a unique process for producing high-performance composites that can be manufactured significantly faster and cheaper than incumbent products. Recently, Endeavor developed a unique “hybrid” composite formulation for customers requiring cost-effective high strength-to-weight solutions in the construction and automotive sectors. Endeavor is proposing the adaptation of its hybrid design to develop a new type of ceramic matrix composite (CMC), consisting of a non-woven ceramic fiber reinforcement, overlaid with a woven skin for enhanced ablation resistance and mechanical performance. If selected for the AFX235-CSO1 Phase II, Endeavor will develop the manufacturing process for its hybrid CMC to meet or exceed requirements for hypersonic and reentry vehicle thermal protection systems, but manufactured at several times the rate and around 50% the cost.

Within the Air Force defense industrial base, industrial equipment supporting maintenance, overhaul and repair (MRO) are critical to meeting the Air Force’s mission needs in the areas of Tactical Air Dominance and Readiness to Deploy and Fight. Production delays due to breakdown of equipment – whether through normal degradation or malicious actions - can severely impact the efficacy and lethality of the Air Force.  Within these MRO operations, many challenges exist around the secure monitoring & diagnostics of machine health, as well as how to prove the efficacy of these monitoring systems such that personnel can trust and respond to them when they indicate an issue. This proposal seeks to improve and further develop OTAware, a "zero-cloud" explainable AI/ML platform to monitor equipment health and status. The OTAware technology is designed to integrate into virtually any kind of machine shop or industrial equipment scenario, and is robustly able to self-train anomaly detection models using a very small amount of computational resources. OTAware enables the deployment of predictive maintenance capabilities to detect emergent issues with equipment health, without needing to deploy cloud-based services, as all information is kept entirely on-device alongside the equipment being monitored.   Sentinel Devices will modify and tailor OTAware to Air Force needs and use cases, and will work with groups supporting MRO within the Air Force to collect data and ensure these adjustments remain performant on Air Force processes. This will take the form of improving portions of the algorithms within OTAware to account for high-variation low-volume production, as well as improvement of the core OTAware software to better meet Air Force user interface needs. Additionally, Sentinel Devices will develop a software interface with existing high-heritage technology developed for the DoD enabling the detection of even extremely sophisticated cyberattacks using physical data. Combined, the total solution developed within this proposal will provide superior protection and coverage for Air Force industrial base assets from normal degradation, faults as well as advanced cyberattacks.

A current TEMP document can consist of 100+ pages of information and require 12+ months to approve, which, once approved, becomes immediately out of date due to its static nature.   The urgency of the situation within the Space Sensing Program Executive Office (PEO) is driven by the imperative to deliver persistent space sensing capabilities across the entire program lifecycle, encompassing prototyping, development, production, fielding, and operational sustainment. Furthermore, the NGP and FORGE programs require integration of their test plans to ensure a successful end-to-end test of the full system delivery. Any changes in a single program must be communicated and reviewed for impact by other integrated systems.  Celeris Systems presents a viable solution with its iRIS test management platform, which will seamlessly integrate essential test functions and data into a high-performance digital engineering environment for the Space Sensing PEO. Given its already established roots in test management, iRIS is well-suited to automate TEMP generation. In this Phase II effort, we will work with the Space Systems Command – Space Sensing PEO to automate the TEMP for the Next-Gen Polar program. With oversight of a substantial $23B portfolio, covering missile warning, tracking, defense, space-based environmental monitoring, and more, the Space Sensing PEO must embrace commercially digital engineering technologies and tools to stay ahead of evolving threats. Introducing Celeris Systems’ technology will accelerate reviews and approvals throughout the agile development lifecycle while delivering new capabilities to benefit the warfighter.
Digital Engineering to Automate the Test and Evaluation Master Plan (TEMP) to Expedite Air Force Acquisitions

Over the past two decades, academic research has significantly advanced wide area network optimization and software-defined networking (SDN), leading to the emergence of Carrier Neutral Facilities (CNF) as a promising commercial opportunity. Optimized SDNs, as suggested by academic literature, promise substantial improvements in traffic management, security, and affordability. Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into SDNs, particularly within CNFs, represents the cutting edge of modern wide area network research. While existing literature has primarily focused on enhancing network throughput, there's a compelling argument for leveraging AI algorithms within SDNs to intelligently route packets for military-specific objectives, such as obfuscating communications to protect against adversaries and enhancing resilience to attacks. However, the adoption of AI in SDNs has been hindered by the need for processing speeds matching fiber optic transmission rates. Recent advancements in Neural Circuit Policies and Liquid Time Constants have led to the development of Liquid Neural Networks (LNNs), capable of achieving explainable performance at fiber optic transmission speeds. This proposal aims to extend LNN research into software-defined military wide area network communication, envisioning LNNs as a key enabler for the OUSD (R&E) Trusted AI & Autonomy Critical Technology Area. The proposed research, named FORTINA, relies on two key enabling technologies: Commercial Solutions for Classified (CSfC) and Carrier-neutral facilities (CNF). CSfC provides NSA Type-I encryption devices, ensuring secure handling, storage, and communication of sensitive data, while CNFs offer redundancy, scalability, and access to multiple carriers, making them ideal hosts for secure military networks. The integration of these technologies with military-grade network management aims to create a commercially available means of communicating classified information. This entails developing bespoke wide area architectures and protocols for edge server communication. Successful implementation would demonstrate the feasibility of an NSA Type-I approved network using entirely Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) hardware and fiber, dynamically routing messages worldwide via ever-changing paths. FORTINA not only enhances communication security but also significantly reduces costs by leveraging CNFs and competing among various commercial offers for connections. This innovative architecture merges state-of-the-art AI research with leading-edge commercial technology, promising a more secure and cost-effective solution compared to government-owned and operated classified fiber optic networks.

Bonding of composite components is a critical process for assembly of complex structures specifically within the aviation and space sector. Aircraft, such as Lockheed Martin’s F-35 Lighting, have extensive composite structures that are assembled together via bonding. To bond these structures together, operators hand sand the composite part in the bond zone region. This process known as “Sand to Black” removes the outside layer of resin, exposing the outermost fiber layer which allows for strong adhesion to the exposed fibers. Being a manual process there is often variability in sanding depth part to part, which can cause non-uniform bond strengths and introduces variability into performance. The labor costs and cycle time penalties paid today for this process are digestible for current platforms, but as the DOD and commercial customers look for more “affordable mass” vehicles built at significantly higher rates manual, long, and variable processes will have to transition to automated, fast, and highly repeatable process. The Composite Laser Ablative Surface Preparation (CLASP) system is able to offer an automated, scalable, and highly repeatable, composite surface preparation process. The CLASP system works by using ultrashort pulsed lasers to remove the thin outside resin layer down to the fibers exposing them, but not damaging them. CLASP can be attached to a robotic arm allowing for automation of high-volume repetitive parts. This technology solves a part of the scalability problem with composite manufacturing process which ultimately needs to be solved to meet the demand from both DOD and commercial customers who are looking at building high volume platforms that rely on composite structures for increased performance.

Hypersonic vehicles are highly expensive crafts that operate at speeds above Mach 5 in low altitude trajectories. In such conditions, rapid heating (e.g., 500 ?C/s) and high heat flux (e.g., 1000 W/cm2) lead to high temperatures (e.g., 1000 ?C) sustained for tens of seconds. While heat concentrates on the exterior and leading edges, other areas of the hypersonic craft also experience significant ambient thermal loads. Indeed, these harsh conditions can lead to heat damage to critical internal subsystems (e.g., sensors and avionics equipment) onboard the hypersonic vehicle.   To resist the punishing thermal environment, ultra-high temperature ceramics and composite materials have been used to shield external structures. However, while these advanced materials survive the high heat load, they fail to prevent heat transfer to the interior of the hypersonic vehicle, which threatens the sensitive equipment onboard.   Currently, thermal blankets are widely used to insulate internal components; however, these bulky blankets can add significant weight and occupy significant amounts of space on a relatively small vehicle. An advanced coating system is needed to provide a lightweight, low-profile thermal protection system for the interior of hypersonic vehicles.  IBC Materials & Technologies, LLC (IBC) proposes Plasma Electrolytic Oxidation (PEO) coating technology as a unique solution for thermal protection of interior systems on hypersonic vehicles. PEO coatings are applicable to lightweight alloys such as titanium alloys, a key material for hypersonic vehicles. PEO coatings are relatively thin (e.g., 30 microns), have exceptionally strong adhesion to the substrate, boast low thermal conductivity (<0.2 W/m.k), and have extreme high temperature durability, resisting thermal shock and degradation.   As a lightweight, low-profile thermal barrier, PEO coating will provide superior thermal protection, reducing weight and reducing the burden on thermal management systems. PEO coatings will improve performance and allow increased range and capability for hypersonic vehicles, which may lead to increased field advantage for US defense systems.  IBC uniquely provides both machining and PEO coating. IBC manufactures and PEO-coats large, complex USAF parts (e.g., LAU-12X rails) in quantities of hundreds per year. In this way, IBC is uniquely positioned for vertical integration of both manufacturing and coating for hypersonic vehicles, improving logistics and mitigating supply chain issues.?  Key target markets for PEO coating on hypersonic vehicles include aerospace, defense, and space industries. IBC has received customer interest from USAF and MDA for PEO technology for hypersonics. Additionally, IBC has support from Lockheed Martin and Raytheon RTX, world leaders in hypersonics, to assist with transitioning PEO coating to hypersonic vehicles.

The development of MEDAL aligns with the USSF's strategic goals of asset longevity, mission success, and technological superiority. One of the greatest challenges to operating in a space environment is tolerating the constant bombardment by cosmic radiation. Radiation causes mutations to humans at the cellular level, and can wreak havoc on electronic hardware by flipping bits of digital logic and causing integrated circuits to burn-out. Today most radiation protection is afforded through thick metallic shields that reflect many larger particles and can absorb or at least slow down higher energy smaller particles. Radiation shielding is commonly found on the spacecraft outer structure for a layer of global protection, but much space electronics is further placed inside of metallic boxes for added protection to ensure reliable operation. As mass and volume come at a premium for all space applications, lightweight conformal radiation protection is desired. Under this STTR we will investigate the use of Boron Nitride Nano Tubes (BNNT) as an effective means for radiation mitigation. When combined with an appropriate polymer binder using the right mix ratios and layer thicknesses, BNNT laminates can be conformally applied to electronics to provide effective self-healing radiation shielding and absorption. If compounded with a non-structural polymer, this technology also has the potential to be applied as a textile for human radiation protection.

Parasitic radar, a passive radar system, represents a highly advanced solution for austere air traffic control, especially in low-visibility and contested environments. This technology will utilize electromagnetic signals generated by jamming in GPS-denied environments, transforming potential threats into valuable data sources for air traffic control and situational awareness. By integrating parasitic radar with Thrust AI's Hybrid AI-Driven Radar and Optical Sensor Platform (“Harpo”) multi-spectral sensor suite, we enhance situational awareness through continuous, real-time tracking of airborne and ground targets, thereby improving safety and efficiency in terminal airspace at austere airfields. Parasitic radar systems exploit existing electromagnetic signals, such as commercial broadcasts and cellular networks. When jamming signals are introduced, they increase the ambient electromagnetic signals available for passive radar use. These signals, typically meant to disrupt GPS, can be harnessed by parasitic radar to detect and track objects, autonomously tasking Harpo’s optical sensors for operators.Harpo will utilize parasitic radar to detect reflections of ambient signals off objects like aircraft and vehicles. In GPS-denied environments with prevalent jamming signals, Harpo processes these strong signals, analyzing time delay, Doppler shift, and other characteristics to determine the position and velocity of objects accurately. The system can track multiple targets simultaneously by distinguishing between various jamming signal sources and their reflections, crucial for managing air traffic in terminal airspace at austere airfields. Harpo enhances its capabilities by integrating parasitic radar with electro-optical infrared (EOIR) sensors, computer vision (CV), and natural language processing (NLP). This fusion provides a comprehensive situational awareness solution, allowing for precise object identification and tracking even in GPS-denied conditions. The hybrid integration ensures robust detection, classification, and real-time tracking of targets, enhancing operational readiness and safety. Research has demonstrated the feasibility and effectiveness of parasitic radar in various applications. Advanced jamming techniques, such as smart noise convolution jamming, can be countered by parasitic radar, which uses signal processing to extract useful information from the noise. Additionally, methods like convolutional neural networks and fractional Fourier transform-based techniques improve the recognition and utilization of jamming signals for radar systems. Harpo will incorporate these advanced techniques to enhance its performance in complex electromagnetic environments.

A Bloomberg News investigation in September 2023 discovered that a little-known company, AOG Technics Ltd., in England, is the source of a catalog of bogus products, including components like nuts, bolts, and friction dampers, which could find their way into critical military equipment. The use of counterfeit parts, driven by a desire to cut costs or adversaries intentionally creating issues within the supply chain, has the potential to create safety vulnerabilities in military systems, allowing adversaries to exploit these weaknesses. Incidents involving fake parts persist, affecting a wide range of defense equipment, from electronic systems to basic hardware items. For the military, the risk is bigger than monetary loss. “Parts and materials that could present an adversary with a specific strategic advantage are a target to be counterfeit,” reads a US Army pamphlet published in January. “Malicious insertions can result in system data being reported to an adversary, monitoring of a system by an adversary, or enabling an adversary to control the system.” In one case involving more than 400 displays installed in US C-130J and C-27J military aircraft, failure rates escalated to almost a third of all units tested, including one incident while the plane was in use. A similar example occurred with more than 300 semiconductors used in systems to detect icing on aircraft wings purportedly made by San Jose, California-based Xilinx Inc., but which were actually found to be knockoffs, again originating from China. To address the United States Air Force’s need for efficient and cost-effective transformation of certification documents to MBSE-ready digital models, RedShred proposes to continue developing the AIRworthiness Model Automation for cerTification Evaluations system (AIRMATE) based on the latest advances in generative AI and Redshred’s existing document AI platform. Specifically, the innovation in automatically extracting digital certification artifacts for digital models from legacy documents will enable the technology to accelerate certification processes, eliminate the need to manually search across multiple documents, increase transparency, reduce cost and labor, and empower downstream tasks that depend on the successful parsing of the certification documents (e.g., modification description alignment with relevant criteria). As a result, this system offers a scalable, lightweight technology and does not require large datasets to support domain adaptability. In addition, AIRMATE supports multiple formats, which directly addresses the customer requirements to be compatible with popular third-party MBSE tools. Redshred will fulfill all Phase II requirements established by relevant stakeholders and demonstrate the feasibility of using advanced generative AI to transform certification documents to MBSE-ready digital models in multiple domains with cross-reference linking. In Phase II, Redshred will 1) Review the System Architecture and Requirements, 2) Acquire & Process Documents, Update SysML Mapping, 3) Prompt Refinement & Development of Quality Evaluation Models 4) Cross-Document Linking & Extraction, 5) Modification Specification & Criteria Alignment Pipeline, 6) UI Development for Easy User Interaction, and 7) Develop SysML Outputs and Testing of Feasibility.

“We have to get the cost down for hypersonic weapons – if we don’t, the services will move to adopt less effective but lower cost solutions” – a statement made in April 2024 by a senior leader within the Joint Hypersonic Transition Office (JHTO) is a keen reminder of the challenge to the national security industrial base. The DOD needs performance AND affordability, otherwise great inventions will be relegated to libraries of history where countless DAF and NASA hypersonic demonstrators from the 60s and 70s remain. This translates to an opportunity to enable truly performance-increasing solutions through new, advanced manufacturing technologies. Canopy Aerospace (“Canopy”), a veteran-owned, venture-backed company, aims to develop and commercialize innovative transpiration-cooled silicon carbide (SiC) thermal protection systems (TPS) for hypersonic and space applications. The company's primary objective is to address critical gaps in  the U.S. supply base for high-temperature materials and TPS, benefiting both national security and commercial space markets. This innovation leverages advanced additive manufacturing (AM) techniques to produce high-performance, reusable TPS materials suitable for the extreme conditions of hypersonic flight and space reentry. The AM process allows for rapid, cost-effective production of complex ceramic components. Canopy's 18,000 sq. ft. facility in Colorado houses next-generation ceramic 3D printers and scalable manufacturing solutions. The company's expertise and equipment enable the rapid development and production of state-of-the-art TPS. Previous funding from NASA and the USAF has supported advancements in these manufacturing techniques. The projected market for advanced TPS is estimated to reach $2.5 billion by 2030. Canopy’s primary customers include the USAF, United States Space Force (USSF), NASA, and commercial space companies. The company's innovative manufacturing techniques are expected to capture significant market share due to favorable unit economics and superior product performance. In Phase II, Canopy will collaborate with AFRL/RVBN, Texas A&M, and NASA Langley Research Center to advance its TPS technology over a 19-month period of performance that will conclude with projected flight readiness, including alignment with mission requirements and funding for Phase III technology transition. The transition strategy involves engaging with partners like AFLCMC Propulsion Directorate, Arnold Engineering Development Complex, AFRL, and demonstrating progress to facilitate integration into defense and commercial programs. Canopy Aerospace is set to transform the high-temperature materials and TPS market with its innovative transpiration-cooled SiC TPS. Supported by strong technical expertise, strategic partnerships, and significant funding, Canopy is well-positioned to meet the needs of both defense and commercial aerospace sectors, driving advancements in space exploration and national security.

The F-35 Lightning II, developed by Lockheed Martin, is one of the most advanced and widely used fifth-generation fighter jets globally. The aircraft's intricate supply chain involves an extensive network of over 1,700 suppliers providing approximately 300,000 components. This complexity has highlighted vulnerabilities, as seen in the recent discovery of a tiny magnet sourced from China, prompting concerns about the integrity of the entire supply chain. As a result, the DoD halted the entire $6.5 billion shipment, emphasizing the critical  importance of Air Force Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) units. These units play a pivotal role in monitoring and safeguarding the supply chains of essential weapons systems. Also, An Air Force investigation of a fatal fighter jet crash in 2020 quietly discovered that key electronic components of the pilot’s ejection seat may have been counterfeit. First Lt. David Schmitz, an F-16 Fighting Falcon pilot at South Carolina’s Shaw Air Force Base, died June 30, 2020, when his ejection seat malfunctioned as he tried to escape from a failed nighttime landing. In the case of the F-35, the incident with the Chinese-origin magnet raises questions about whether it was a deliberate act of manipulation or the result of negligence by a subcontractor. Counterfeit semiconductors represent a staggering $200 billion annual threat to the worldwide electronics supply chain. These fake chips not only have the potential to halt or impede multi-billion dollar projects but also carry the risk of premature failure. A Senate Armed Services Committee investigation uncovered over a million suspected counterfeit electronic parts within the U.S. defense supply chain, highlighting the severity of the issue. The most counterfeited product in the global microelectronics market is not always a fake, often it is a true OEM original but has been altered and is not suitable for the full requirements of system performance. Moreover, counterfeit electronic components pose grave dangers, including the interception of classified data and the sabotage of critical weapons systems, ultimately endangering the safety of military personnel. Chiplytics Power Spectrum Analysis, a fast, non-invasive electrical testing technique licensed from Sandia National Laboratories captures a unique multi-pin frequency response to reveal subtle differences between components. Because the current state-of-the-art for this kind of component testing takes minutes, the Air Force can only test a small fraction of units through sample testing. Chiplytics' technology reduces this time to seconds, allowing 100% testing of all critical components. Chiplytics has four successful external pilots totaling more than 100 hours of external testing and includes validation from Sandia National Lab. Chiplytics has more than 2000 hours of internal testing.

Avalanche Energy is developing a high-throughput, tailored-to-requirement process (“solution”) for discovering, developing, and deploying refractory multi-principal element alloys (MPEA) for extreme environments at scale within 12 months. The solution is designed to facilitate the rapid development of plasma-facing components (PFCs) and structural materials for the company’s compact fusion reactor. The proposed Phase II solution will adapt the non-defense commercial solution to the development of MPEAs for hypersonic leading edges, specifically for reusable hypersonic aircraft and space access vehicle applications. The solution is achieved by integrating the following critical design aspects into a single, end-to-end process: An innovative AI-supported prediction system that incorporates novel performance parameters, markers (including manufacturability), and a performance-based scoring system to accelerate material down-selection.Advanced material synthesis and characterization techniques developed by partner universities, followed by the test and evaluation of select MPEAs in both relevant and operational environments in collaboration with industry partners. An adaptive MRL assessment approach that seeks to eliminate poor MPEA candidates early in the prediction process and rapidly screen prospective MPEA candidates during development by continuously evaluating the manufacturability and scalability of each candidate as part of the down-selection process.The overall objective of the Phase II effort is to demonstrate a process for identifying and developing advanced MPEA systems that can be fielded at scale within a year of discovery. To validate the solution, at least three MPEA prototypes will be developed, tested, and qualified as TRL 6+ per the key performance parameters, including manufacturability, which will be assessed using the adaptive MRL assessment process. Each material will address one of three applications—fusion PFCs and hypersonic leading edges at Mach 5 and Mach 20+ conditions. The proposed solution addresses the following critical technology areas (CTA):Advanced Materials: Accelerates the discovery-to-deployment timeline of MPEAs, targeting the CTA’s goal of “reducing the development cycle by >100x” and supporting the Defense Industrial Base rapidly by maturing advanced materials and manufacturing capabilities. Rapidly fields MPEAs into systems at scale and reduced cost. Hypersonics: Supports CTA priorities of “demonstrating and delivering transformational capabilities through rapid design, build, test, and learn” and “reducing the cost of hypersonic systems and increasing industrial capability to build warfighting inventories” by rapidly developing and fielding MPEAs for hypersonic leading edges.Energy Resilience: Enables the development of fusion and advanced nuclear reactors via the development of materials that improve reactor performance and extend operational lifetimes.
Multi-Principal Element Alloys for Extreme Environments

These platforms operate in extreme conditions where conventional materials face performance limitations, particularly in protecting sensitive radar systems. The project will provide critical insights into SiN’s potential to protect radar systems in the next generation of hypersonic platforms and will advance the technology towards TRL 5.

The rapid military modernization efforts of adversaries, particularly the People’s Republic of China, necessitate significant advancements in the U.S. Air Force’s Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to maintain strategic superiority and ensure national security. Lovelace AI proposes the Phase I SBIR project, “Left-of-Launch Early Warning via AI-Enabled Anticipatory Tipping and Cueing,” aimed at conducting a feasibility study and developing an initial SBIR-adapted product definition and requirements. This project seeks to automate the collection management process, specifically focusing on the tipping and cueing of high-value maritime entities within a multimodal sensor environment, thereby aligning with AFRL’s MAINSAIL Program and demonstrating the potential to enhance maritime domain awareness. Our existing product, Elemental, currently at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 7, employs advanced data fusion techniques by integrating multimodal sensor inputs such as Automatic Identification System (AIS) data, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery, and commercial adtech. Utilizing hybrid Bayesian inference and generative models, Elemental processes and fuses billions of data points in near real-time, delivering predictive analytics that enhance situational awareness and decision-making for tracking high-value maritime entities, including “dark vessels” that evade traditional detection methods. This research proposal aligns with AFRL’s MAINSAIL project and addresses critical technological challenges, including sparse observation tracking, contextual reasoning, automated sensor tasking, and rapid multimodal data fusion. By overcoming these hurdles, Elemental aims to improve the Air Force’s ISR capabilities, enabling more accurate and timely tracking of maritime targets. Lovelace AI is supported by $7M in venture capital and led by CEO Andrew Moore, former Dean of Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon and leader of the AI Division at Google Cloud. Our team comprises seasoned hyperscaler engineers, machine learning scientists, and defense veterans, equipping Lovelace AI to deliver impactful ISR solutions. Elemental has demonstrated operational success at the Pacific Air Forces (PACAF) 613th Air Operations Center during Valiant Shield 2024 and is actively participating in the US Space Force TacSRT Initiative to track objects using commercial data, as well as the NSIN Propel Hawaii 2024 accelerator, focused on the Air Operations Center of the future. This proposal aims to establish the foundational requirements and demonstrate the feasibility of integrating Elemental into existing Air Force systems, ultimately contributing to Programs of Record such as the Command, Control, and Battle Management (C3BM) system and the Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) initiative. The anticipated outcomes include enhanced situational awareness, improved target prioritization, and sustained custody of high-value maritime targets.

SSCI proposes RAMMS: Robust and Autonomous Management of Mission Systems. RAMMS incorporates autonomy into drive Defensive Mission Systems, tasking these systems to improve operator survivability and lethality while simultaneously reducing operator workload by switching from an “operator in the loop” paradigm to an “operator on the loop” paradigm. The RAMMS system is architecturally aligned with the USAF Autonomy Government Reference Architecture (A-GRA), ensuring an ability to rapidly deploy software from this R&D effort to the DAF.

Acute combat pain (ACP) from battlefield injuries has adverse effects, including (1) diminished operational effectiveness, (2) consumption of limited medical resources, and (3) heightened PTSD risk. Current Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC) pain management guidelines include the use of opioids, such as oral transmucosal fentanyl citrate or parenteral morphine, and ketamine. Opioids are effective but increase the risk of respiratory depression, drowsiness, confusion, impaired mobility, gastrointestinal side effects, and addiction. Ketamine is increasingly preferred owing to its strong analgesic effect, rapid onset of action, and lower respiratory depression risk. However, ketamine has a short duration of action and an increased risk of dissociation, hallucinations, anxiety, cardiovascular effects, and addiction.  Peripheral nerve blocks (PNB) offer a superior alternative to opioids or ketamine for managing ACP. They provide localized and effective pain relief without the systemic side effects, rendering them particularly suitable for use in field settings where maintaining cognitive and physical capacities is crucial. The adoption of PNBs also aligns with the strategic goals of military medicine by preserving medical resources and improving the relative operational readiness of personnel. Unfortunately, the use of PNBs in austere environments is limited by the high level of technical skill required for their administration, which is outside of the training of almost all medics and many other military healthcare providers. Given the modest cost and size of ultrasound, this limitation is primarily due to the challenges of ultrasound image interpretation and coordinated needle guidance; skills that require significant training to master and are typically in the purview of subspecialist anesthesiologists. To help personnel rapidly overcome this skills gap, AutonomUS’s Artificial Intelligence-Guided Ultrasound Intervention Device (AI-GUIDE) integrates ultrasound, machine learning, and hand-held robotics. The on-device machine learning algorithms interpret the ultrasound imagery in real time and guide the user where to place the device via a simple targeting display. The robotics perform the needle insertion and anesthetic delivery. By enabling medics with fundamental medical training to safely and effectively perform PNB, AI-GUIDE extends the accessibility of advanced pain management techniques to austere environments. The result would be a fighting force with increased operational effectiveness, reduced PTSD, and better preparedness for prolonged field care.
Handheld Robotic Medical Device for Semi-automated Nerve Block Administration in Austere Environments

Launchspace has created an advanced spacecraft shielding solution with the dual-use capability of active debris removal (ADR) under the only NASA Space Act Agreement to develop materials for a commercial company for this purpose. Shielding can protect USSF spacecraft from counter-space kinetic ASAT threats, while reducing the collateral damage from backward splatter from debris object impacts. Embedded sensing allows for characterization of orbital debris in LEO, GEO and beyond, and are part of Launchspaceĺs overall space domain awareness (SDA) sensor architecture. The threat of an ASAT attack has been demonstrated numerous times in the 21st century, and can come in the form of a simple kinetic collision from a basic ballistic missile launching a low-tech cloud of pellets into the path of the target LEO satellite. Protection against such attacks by small pellets is gained from Launchspace satellite shielding. Additionally, the temperature resistant material may offer other protective measures. This shielding offers the USSF both protection and sustainment via capitalizing on the dual-use properties of a product intended to benefit civilian and commercial sectors.

The DAF currently relies on rare earth magnets for its most critical applications including fighter jets, drones, and satellites. Today, the U.S. has virtually no domestic manufacturing capacity for magnetics, creating a significant supply chain vulnerability for the U.S. and its allies. Further, there have been few to no innovations in magnet chemistries over the last 30 years. Vulcan Elements, in collaboration with the University of Central Florida (UCF), is proposing an innovative, software-enabled hardware development platform designed to optimize and scale the synthesis of a novel magnetic chemistry—a promising green, high-temperature alternative to the widely-used Neodymium-Iron-Boron magnets in motor applications. The proposed magnets offer significant potential for next-generation motors, especially under demanding environmental conditions. Past work in this area has been impeded by technical issues including scale, chemical property control, and crystal structure alignment. To address these challenges, Vulcan Elements will build upon the recent advancements made by UCF in developing magnetic thick films. By leveraging the capabilities of thick-film technology, combined with Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE) techniques, Vulcan will enable precise, real-time magnetic property measurements crucial for larger-scale production processes. The proposed solution is a significant step toward establishing commercial viability for next-generation magnetic technologies into DAF systems. This effort has the potential to expand into other material systems across the DoD and commercial sectors that are more cost effective and provide an asymmetric advantage to future warfighting capabilities.

Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) has impacted over 417,000 service members since 2000, significantly degrading operational effectiveness and costing the Department of Defense (DoD) $76.5 billion annually. Despite annual Air Force investments exceeding $50M in TBI research, no field-deployable neuroregenerative treatment exists. StellarNotch’s Neural EV Regenerative Therapy (NEV-RT) presents a first-in-class, field-deployable, intranasal treatment utilizing extracellular vesicles (EVs) to deliver neuroprotective and regenerative cargo directly to the brain, bypassing the blood-brain barrier (BBB). This lyophilized EV-based therapy ensures stability in austere environments, allowing immediate administration at the point of injury. Unlike current approaches, NEV-RT actively repairs neural damage, reduces inflammation, and mitigates cognitive decline. Phase II will focus on optimizing EV cargo loading, ensuring formulation stability, and validating therapeutic efficacy through in vitro testing. The work will establish a scalable, reproducible bioprocess for military and civilian applications. By accelerating cognitive recovery and reducing disability separations, StellarNotch’s solution enhances warfighter resilience, ensuring sustained mission readiness in future combat operations.

The Daedalus ATL system delivers a resilient, GPS-independent Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) capability that directly addresses the Department of Defense’s urgent need to mitigate the threat of GPS jamming, spoofing, and signal disruptions. By harnessing “signals of opportunity” from non-cooperative Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, Daedalus provides warfighters with uninterrupted PNT data in contested environments where adversaries target GPS vulnerabilities. Unlike conventional solutions, Daedalus’s phased-array antenna and software-defined radio (SDR) architecture eliminate reliance on large, dish-shaped antennas or extensive terrestrial infrastructure. This low size, weight, and power (SWaP) design seamlessly integrates with existing systems via standard GPS interfaces, providing a drop-in replacement for critical missions. Leveraging advanced signal-processing techniques—such as Time-Difference of Arrival (TDoA) and robust error-correction algorithms—the system continuously calibrates for Doppler shifts, atmospheric variations, and hardware offsets. The result is reliable and highly accurate timing and  navigation in the face of jamming or spoofing attacks. Key Competitive Advantages for DoD Missions:Assured Operations in Contested Domains: By drawing on multiple LEO constellations, Daedalus maintains full operational capability—even if GPS is fully denied—ensuring continuity for ISR, cyber, special operations, and command-and-control assets.Rapid, Scalable Deployment: The flat-panel phased-array antenna is compact, easily concealed, and can be fielded quickly across forward bases or integrated into diverse platforms without major hardware overhauls.Alignment with DoD Operational Imperatives: Daedalus enhances space resilience, supports advanced battle management systems, and provides assured PNT for agile basing and readiness to fight, meeting the Secretary of the Air Force’s top priorities.Future-Proof Architecture: Built on SDR technology and open standards, Daedalus can adapt to emerging threats, new satellite constellations, and evolving mission requirements with minimal hardware modifications.Having reached Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 5–6, Daedalus is already validated through prototype field tests and is poised for rapid transition to Phase III procurement. Backed by strong partnerships within DoD and a clear commercialization pathway, the Daedalus ATL system stands ready to deliver a decisive operational advantage—protecting mission-critical capabilities in the most challenging and dynamic threat environments.

PrisAM proposes the development of Lattice Core Sandwich Panels (LCSP) as an advanced solution for micrometeoroid and orbital debris (MMOD) shielding in space vehicles. Current shielding technologies, such as honeycomb-core sandwich panels (HCSP) and traditional Whipple shields, face limitations in impact dissipation due to their structural constraints. LCSPs, by contrast, utilize a multi-shock effect that disperses impact energy more efficiently, reducing penetration risk and structural damage.The proposed Phase II effort will optimize LCSP designs for MMOD shielding applications, leveraging advanced additive manufacturing techniques to create lightweight, structurally resilient panels. The project builds on a successful Phase I feasibility study that demonstrated the effectiveness of LCSPs in high-velocity impact scenarios. Key results included experimental validation of LCSPs' superior impact resistance compared to HCSPs, with enhanced debris dispersion and improved energy dissipation.In collaboration with AFRL/RX and AFRL/RV, the Phase II objectives include:Numerical Modeling & Design Optimization – Developing hydrocode models to predict LCSP performance under hypervelocity impacts.Manufacturing & Prototyping – Producing LCSP configurations with graded-density lattice structures to maximize shielding efficiency.High-Velocity Impact Testing – Conducting controlled impact tests at the University of Dayton Research Institute to validate experimental and computational results.PrisAM’s technology aligns with multiple Department of the Air Force operational imperatives, particularly in enhancing space resilience, supporting rapid mission reconstitution, and enabling lightweight, cost-efficient structural solutions. Beyond defense applications, LCSPs offer significant commercial potential in aerospace, heavy vehicles, and infrastructure.This effort will position LCSPs as a next-generation MMOD shielding solution, offering a scalable and manufacturable alternative to traditional space shielding technologies.

Problem:As adversaries develop sophisticated space threats, mastering remote and autonomous Rendezvous and Proximity Operations (RPO) is critical to U.S. space dominance and security. However, today’s RPO systems face key challenges. They are designed for specific missions, limiting scalability, and lack real-time visual feedback, reducing situational awareness. Without a scalable, intelligent, real-time Full Motion Video (FMV) intelligence solution, adversaries may gain a first-mover advantage, exploiting gaps in surveillance and maneuverability.Solution:TRL11’s Quadclops Pro is a modular, intelligent low-delay FMV RPO sensor suite (sensors + compute platform) supporting Space Mobility & Logistics (SAML) and Space Domain Awareness (SDA) for USSF. The low SWaP-C system enables precise RPO navigation from stereo imagery while enhancing operator awareness to detect threats and characterize objects within 20km. TRL11’s VIPOnly software delivers low-delay FMV, providing continuous on-orbit recording and real-time oversight with ‘human-on-the-loop’ situational awareness. Additionally, threat assessment software analyzes FMV to assess a target’s behavior and intent, identifying nearby threats for autonomous decision-making or alerting ground operators with a live video feed for analysis and response. Built on TRL11’s flight-proven RPO technology, Quadclops Pro features TRL-9 heritage components with prior on-orbit success, enabling dual-use capabilities for expanded mission execution.Objectives and Approach:This Phase II effort matures Quadclops Pro hardware, culminating in an Engineering Model, alongside VIPOnly and threat assessment software. The goal is to achieve Critical Design Review (CDR) and build Engineering Models. Software objectives include superior video compression and threat detection capabilities.DoD Benefits:Quadclops Pro enhances USSF’s ability to conduct on-orbit servicing, transportation, life extension, situational awareness, threat recognition, and SDA characterization in a contested orbital environment. It aligns with DoD goals to maintain operational superiority, reduce surprises, protect U.S. space assets, and enable confident maneuvering.Expertise and Team Strength:TRL11’s team includes ultra-low-latency video pioneers with Technical Oscar and Emmy awards, space domain intelligence experts, and leaders in state-of-the-art space optics. The team has engaged with USSF to drive the requirements of their Quadclops Pro solution and assess its feasibility.Commercialization Potential:Beyond military applications, Quadclops Pro and its VIPOnly software have strong commercialization potential in commercial space services, spacecraft health monitoring, own-ship awareness, and space surveillance, enhancing orbital asset management for government and commercial operators.
Quadclops Pro: Dual-Use, Intelligent, Low Delay Full Motion Video RPO System for Space Mobility & Logistics and Space Domain Awareness

Technical Abstract (SBIR Proposal)This SBIR Phase II proposal develops an AI-driven Adaptive Mixed Reality (MR) training platform to enhance tactical readiness, decision-making, and operational effectiveness for the Air Force Security Forces Center (AFSFC). Unlike static training, this system employs real-time AI-driven scenario evolution, dynamically adjusting mission parameters, adversary tactics, and environmental conditions based on trainee performance. This ensures a personalized, continuously evolving training experience, addressing instructor shortages, inconsistent standards, and resource constraints affecting 38,000 Total Force Defenders.Technical Approach & Key InnovationsThe proposed solution integrates M4 and M18 replica weapons with realistic recoil, precise ammunition tracking (±2 rounds per magazine), and configurable malfunction simulation to create a highly immersive, responsive MR training environment. Upon Phase II completion, the solution will transition to Phase III commercialization through:Air Force Enterprise-Wide Deployment – Transitioning to a Program of Record (PoR) with AFSFC for DoD-wide implementation.Expansion into Other DoD Branches & Foreign Military Sales (FMS) – Targeting Army, Navy, Marine Corps, and NATO/allied forces.Law Enforcement & Private Sector Adoption – Expanding to federal, state, and local agencies (FBI, DHS, ATF) and private security.With strong government and commercial interest, this AI-driven MR training system is positioned to redefine tactical training, enhance force readiness, and drive adoption across defense and security sectors.

The United States Air Force faces increasing challenges related to high operational tempo, sustained stress exposure, and musculoskeletal injuries, leading to reduced warfighter readiness, prolonged recovery times, and cognitive impairment. Current recovery solutions—such as cold plunges, red light therapy, and float tanks—are impractical for field deployment and require trained personnel, limiting their scalability.Shiftwave presents an innovative, field-deployable solution that leverages Pulsed Pressure Wave (PPW) technology to accelerate recovery, reduce stress, and enhance cognitive function without requiring medical personnel. The system integrates whole-body vibration (WBV) principles and has been scientifically validated in clinical trials and operational testing with elite U.S. military personnel, professional athletes, and special operations forces.This Phase II effort will focus on military-specific adaptations, testing, and integration to ensure Shiftwave meets the rigorous demands of Air Force personnel. Key objectives include:Field testing Shiftwave with Air Force Operational Support Teams (OSTs) to refine protocols for stress mitigation, pain reduction, and autonomic nervous system regulation.Conducting controlled scientific studies in collaboration with AFRL STRONG Lab and Ohio State University to validate Shiftwave’s physiological benefits using biomarkers, self-reported stress data, and sleep tracking metrics.Ruggedizing Shiftwave for austere environments, ensuring durability under extreme operational conditions (heat, sand, water, and high-intensity use).Addressing cybersecurity compliance for safe integration into Air Force networks.With over $7.3M in commercial sales and existing adoption by NFL, UFC, and corporate wellness programs, Shiftwave has demonstrated strong market traction. A $2M funding commitment from SOCOM S&T further supports its transition into the TACFI, STRATFI, and AFWERX Phase III procurement pathways.By the end of Phase II, Shiftwave will deliver a fully optimized, Air Force-ready recovery system, positioning it for wide-scale DoD adoption to enhance warfighter resilience, operational performance, and mission readiness.

SensXR addresses a critical Department of Defense (DoD) capability gap in warfighter protection from chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) threats. Most fielded detectors are limited to identifying single threats, forcing operators to carry multiple bulky devices, which increases the size, weight, and power (SWaP) burden, slows decision-making cycles, and reduces situational awareness. These challenges conflict with the DoD’s Human-Machine Interface (HMI) and Trusted AI & Autonomy Critical Technology Areas (CTAs), which emphasize the need for integrated, lightweight sensing systems capable of providing trusted, edge-based intelligence.SensXR proposes a wearable, low-SWaP platform integrating chemical and radiological sensor fusion, TinyML-powered edge inference, and a human-machine interface (HMI) optimized for use with standard PPE (e.g., SCBA and M50 masks). The system provides automated hazard classification with confidence scores, real-time shared data-mapping and alerts over encrypted LoRa mesh, and intuitive AR visual cues via a flip-down display. This design minimizes cognitive load, accelerates perception-to-action cycles, and ensures mission continuity even in contested electromagnetic environments.Phase I demonstrated successive prototypes, evolving from helmet-mounted units with COTS smartglasses to a compact belt-worn module with custom PCBs and an integrated sensor array. Trials at events like CBOA 24 and RDAX 24 validated system feasibility, highlighting improvements in form factor, power efficiency, and network resilience. Field tests confirmed reliable edge inference, high-confidence alerts, and user-preferred HMI features under realistic operational conditions.Phase II will further mature SensXR through structured warfighter workshops and field trials at Ellsworth AFB, incorporating user feedback to refine enclosure ergonomics, validate LoRa mesh communications, and implement federated learning pipelines to adapt inference models against adversarial inputs. The program’s objectives include achieving measurable decision-cycle compression, improving situational awareness, and enhancing the safety and effectiveness of CBRN response operations.With a multidisciplinary team experienced in sensor fusion, embedded AI, radiological science, electronics engineering, and field operations, SensXR is poised to deliver a scalable, mission-ready solution. The effort supports a clear path to commercialization and DoD adoption while offering dual-use potential in non-Defense markets.
SensXR: Accelerating Decision Cycles with Low-SWaP Wearable Edge-AI Sensor Fusion & PPE-Compatible HMI for Multi-Threat Detection

MCT Industries proposes the development of two next-generation aerospace platforms—the WORKHRZ-UV (Self-Propelled Universal Platform) and the WORKHRZ-EX (Expeditionary Platform)—to respond to what senior Department of the Air Force (DAF) leadership has identified as one of the most critical and immediate threats to mission readiness. The WORKHRZ-UV is designed for in-garrison operations, enabling launching, inspection, component upgrades, and scheduled maintenance. The WORKHRZ-EX is a lightweight, collapsible, and stackable system optimized for resilient bases, supporting rapid deployment, acute repair, and battle damage assessment in contested environments. AFMC HQ/A4 Military Deputy Director Col Barnard’s support letter underscores the Platforms’ urgency: “the proposed next-generation MCT stands will play a crucial role in home station and contingency operation locations by ensuring our aircraft remain mission-ready. With ACE in mind, MCT’s proposal will consolidate multiple legacy variation capabilities/sizes into a single lighter and durable stand, occupying minimal space within our mobility aircraft. MCT will also include advanced corrosion prevention to meet the stringent demands of the Pacific theater of operation thereby saving the Air Force millions in lifecycle and replacement costs.” Seven MAJCOMs have deemed these platforms a critically urgent need and prioritized buy. MCT brings over 52 years of manufacturing expertise and is ranked in the top 5% of all DoD contractors by SPRS. Operational Testing at Edwards AFB in coordination with AFLCMC/ROZ and AFMC leadership. Eudia is an AI-powered acquisition augmentation platform purpose-built to modernize Department of the Air Force Contracting workflows, accelerate acquisition timelines, and strengthen mission readiness. Designed for the unique regulatory and operational complexity of federal contracting, Eudia automates key aquisition functions including contract review, clause logic selection, compliance verification, and source selection scoring, reducing regulatory risk and empowering contracting teams to move faster with greater precision. At its core, Eudia leverages proprietary machine learning and natural language processing models trained specifically on federal acquisition language and workflows. The platform's "contract brain" layer allows for the encoding of institutional knowledge, enabling each deployment to be tailored to the mission-specific needs of Air Force contracting units. Unlike black-box LLM-based tools or rule-based RPA systems, Eudia delivers transparent, auditable outputs with a human-in-the-loop design that maintains decision authority with contracting officers while enhancing their capacity through intelligent automation. The solution integrates seamlessly with existing government systems such as digital contract file repositories and contract writing tools, ensuring minimal disruption to ongoing operations. Combat Casualty Care (CCC) continues to face a deadly challenge: the inability to detect internal bleeding and physiologic deterioration early enough to enable timely, life-saving intervention.  According to the Joint Trauma System, uncontrolled hemorrhage accounts for nearly 90% of potentially survivable battlefield deaths, making it the leading cause of preventable mortality in combat. Further, 87% of combat fatalities occur before the casualty reaches a medical treatment facility, underscoring the urgent need for rapid assessment and advanced physiologic monitoring in prehospital and en route care environments. Traditional vital signs—such as blood pressure (BP), heart rate (HR), and oxygen saturation (SpO?)—have long been the foundation of trauma triage, yet they are lagging indicators of hemodynamic collapse. In combat scenarios like blast events, bodily compensatory mechanisms can maintain normal blood pressure despite significant blood loss, giving medics a false sense of stability and delaying urgent intervention. These limitations are particularly dangerous in Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC) settings, where early detection of shock is essential for accurate triage, targeted resuscitation, and survivability during prolonged field and aeromedical evacuation. Flosonics’ FDA-cleared FloPatch, a wireless, wearable Doppler ultrasound sensor, was developed to address this exact gap. FloPatch enables continuous, real-time monitoring of central blood flow, offering a clearer and earlier view of physiologic compromise than conventional vital signs. Data from a hemorrhage model co-developed by Flosonics and the Mayo Clinic demonstrates that blood flow parameters like stroke volume (SV) and flow time corrected (FTc) decline significantly before blood pressure (MAP) drops—proving FloPatch’s value in identifying early-stage shock. The core innovation of this proposal is FloPredict—an AI-powered trauma severity score that elevates the proven clinical foundation of FloPatch to a new level of decision support. While FloPatch already delivers unparalleled real-time visibility into central blood flow via Doppler ultrasound, FloPredict takes the next evolutionary step in vital sign technology by applying Trusted AI and Autonomy to transform raw physiologic data into predictive insights. This enhancement is specifically designed to address the demands of high-stakes environments like TCCC and en route care.
FloPredict - DOPPLER INTELLIGENCE: ADVANCING AI-POWERED HEMODYNAMIC MONITORING FOR EARLY DETECTION OF CLINICAL DETERIORATION

Human-in-the-loop sessions in Months 8–14 will capture edge-case annotations to improve model precision over 93 percent. Months 12–18 focus on security accreditation—RMF Step 4, vulnerability scans, and CUI compliance—culminating in a formal Authority to Operate. Pilot demonstrations in Months 16–20 will validate system readiness, operator training, and deployment workflows. Phase II concludes in Month 21 with a technical report and Phase III transition plan.This platform addresses Air Force imperatives for “Digital Advantage at the Tactical Edge” and “Agile Combat Employment” by enabling Security Forces to reduce incident response times by up to 60 percent, cut post-incident reporting time by 50 percent, and lower compliance errors by 25–35 percent. By fielding a scalable, mobile-ready solution that bridges complex threat doctrine with real-time guidance, Kilsar paves the way for enterprise-wide adoption across Security Forces, BDOC units, and allied security organizations, enhancing base defense and force protection in garrison and expeditionary settings.

Star Catcher Industries proposes a novel thermal management solution to enable high duty cycle optical power beaming in space, addressing a persistent capability gap in the Department of the Air Force (DAF): insufficient onboard power for advanced satellite functions. Spacecraft in low Earth orbit (LEO) frequently lack the power necessary to support high performance computing, directed energy systems, electric propulsion, and advanced sensing capabilities. This limits mission uptime, operational flexibility, and responsiveness, particularly during eclipse periods or in contested environments. The Star Catcher Network is a scalable space based optical power beaming architecture that delivers concentrated solar energy to unmodified satellite solar arrays. The architecture comprises Power Nodes, satellites equipped with modular Fresnel lens collectors, solar pumped lasers, steerable optics, and passive tracking systems, and Relay Sats, which transfer power during eclipse. This enables persistent on demand energy delivery without requiring hardware modifications to client satellites. Phase I validated key subsystems and demonstrated energy beaming over 100 meters and autonomous satellite tracking at 1,500 kilometers, achieving TRL 5. Phase II focuses on maturing the Network’s thermal management system (TMS), a critical enabler for sustained power transmission. The TMS captures, dissipates, and recycles heat from high power subsystems using heat sinks, cold plates, phase change materials, and thermoelectric generators to maintain thermal stability and convert waste heat into additional usable power. Tasks include modeling heat flow in key components, building a compact modular prototype, conducting laboratory testing, and demonstrating integrated subsystem performance under simulated space conditions. The proposed solution advances critical technology areas identified by OUSD(R&E): Space Technology, Energy Resilience, and Directed Energy. It supports DAF objectives for energy independent operations, enhanced maneuverability, and resilient satellite support. Operationally, the system enables longer duty cycles, better radar tracking, and real time optical characterization of space objects, contributing to missions such as space domain awareness (SDA), maneuver support, and orbital ISR. Star Catcher has secured five power purchase agreements and over $14 billion in nonbinding commercial LOIs, indicating strong dual use commercial demand. The company has raised $12 million in private capital, received $2 million in non-dilutive support, and is supported by AFRL and SSC as committed stakeholders. The proposed Phase II effort will culminate in a validated TMS prototype supporting transition to STRATFI and Phase III deployment. This effort directly contributes to resilient U.S. space infrastructure and supports the long term strategic goals of the U.S. Space Force.
Thermal Management for High Powered Energy Beaming Systems

full_descriptions: Combat-Ready Brain Health: Mobile AI Diagnostics for TBI

Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) is the signature injury of modern military service—widespread, underdiagnosed, and operationally debilitating. Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) is the signature injury of modern military service—widespread, underdiagnosed, and operationally debilitating. Since 2000, the DoD has reported over 485,000 diagnosed TBIs, with studies estimating that up to 50% of mild cases (mTBI) go unreported. These injuries degrade cognition, impair decision-making, and elevate the risk of PTSD, depression, suicide, and early separation—without obvious physical signs. Current diagnostics rely on subjective methods, lack scalability, and are unavailable at the point of need.This Direct-to-Phase II proposal adapts Senseye’s clinically validated, AI-powered mental health platform into the first objective, mobile diagnostic for TBI. The technology analyzes involuntary ocular and autonomic biomarkers—gaze stability, saccadic latency, pupil response, heart rate variability—using only a smartphone camera. It delivers sub-10-minute, offline-capable assessments without the need for connectivity or clinical supervision. Senseye’s platform has been used by over 3,000 patients, is advancing toward FDA approval for PTSD and MDD, and is commercially deployed in healthcare and pharma applications.The Phase II effort, backed by AFRL, the 59th Medical Wing, and BAMC, will expand Senseye’s biometric models to identify TBI-specific disruptions. Tasks include AI model training, prototype development, field testing across Air Force units, and iterative refinement based on user feedback. The result will be a deployable, secure, CMMC-compliant diagnostic tool fully aligned with military operational needs and ready for Phase III transition.Senseye’s adaptation addresses a critical readiness gap. Undetected mTBI contributes to degraded performance in high-risk roles such as aviation, cyber, and special operations. The tool empowers commanders and medics with real-time physiological insights for triage, post-blast evaluation, and return-to-duty decisions—enabling earlier intervention and reducing long-term disability costs. Integration with Air Force platforms such as BATDOK and MHS GENESIS will streamline deployment.The commercial potential is equally strong. With over 2.8 million TBIs annually in the U.S., and a $10B+ neurodiagnostics market, Senseye offers a scalable solution for urgent care, sports medicine, telehealth, and behavioral health sectors. The firm has raised $30M, generated $1.8M in 2024 revenue, and is projected to reach $8M in 2025. With robust IP, active commercial pilots, and government validation, Senseye is uniquely positioned to transform brain health diagnostics across defense and civilian markets.
